general_translation: (Everything) from...to..., From…up until..., Starting with...ending with...
formation: (Noun (A) + から(1)）+ Noun (B) + に至（いた）るまで(Noun (A) + から(1)）+ Noun (B) + に至（いた）るまで + の + Noun (C)(1) より
casual_structure: (Noun (A) + から(1)）+ Noun (B) + に至（いた）るまで(Noun (A) + から(1)）+ Noun (B) + に至（いた）るまで + の + Noun (C)(1) より
explanation: A phrase indicating a wide range of something. From (A) right up until the climax of (B). (B) often being surprising information.

example_sentences.japanese: にしまさんはバーテンダーから大企業の社長にいたるまでいろいろな仕事を歴任した。
example_sentences.english: Nishima-san held various positions, from a bartender to a president of a large company.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は成人してから退職にいたるまで、ずっと同じ会社で働いてきた。
example_sentences.english: My grandfather has worked for the same company, from when he became an adult until retirement.

example_sentences.japanese: このライトノベルは子供から大人にいたるまで、幅広い層で人気がある。
example_sentences.english: This light novel is popular with a wide range of audiences, from children to adults.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は大阪から福岡にいたるまで、一日中雨が降るようです。
example_sentences.english: Apparently it is going to be raining all day tomorrow, from Osaka to Fukuoka.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日では、ＣＰＵはパソコンから歯ブラシにいたるまで、さまざまな装置に見られる。
example_sentences.english: Nowadays, CPUs can be found in various kinds of devices, from computers to toothbrushes, etc.

example_sentences.japanese: 総理大臣から一般人にいたるまであらゆる市民は法のもとで平等である。
example_sentences.english: All citizens are equal under the law, from the prime minister to an ordinary person.

example_sentences.japanese: 航海の初めから事故そのものにいたるまでの難破船の航海日誌が見つかった。
example_sentences.english: A shipwreck's logbook covering everything from the beginning of the voyage to the accident itself has been found.

example_sentences.japanese: アジアでは、箸は昔より現在にいたるまで長きに渡って、食べるために使われている。
example_sentences.english: In Asia, chopsticks have been used to eat for a long time, from long ago to the present.

example_sentences.japanese: ふじはらたくみはローターからハンドル操作にいたるまで車にかけてはすべてを知っている人物です。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to cars, Takumi Fujihara is a person that knows everything, from rotors to operating a steering wheel.

example_sentences.japanese: 石川県にある「法師」旅館は７１８年から今にいたるまで１３００年以上商いし続けている。
example_sentences.english: The Japanese-style inn called 'Houshi' that is located in Ishikawa prefecture has been operating continuously for over 1300 years from 718 right up until now.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社はスマートフォンの販売から大学の経営にいたるまで、たくさんのビジネスを運営している。
example_sentences.english: This company is running numerous businesses, from selling smartphones to owning a university.

example_sentences.japanese: 手足から髪の毛一本にいたるまで身体中のすべてが震えていた。そのとき、それくらい怖かった。
example_sentences.english: My whole body was shaking, from my hands and feet to the individual strands of my hair. That's just how scared I was then.

example_sentences.japanese: ​‎バブル景気崩壊にあって、小企業から大企業にいたるまでいろいろな会社が倒産を余儀なくされている。
example_sentences.english: Due to the bursting of the bubble economy, various companies were forced into bankruptcy, from small ones to major ones.

example_sentences.japanese: この自動車修理工場では、修理はもちろん、洗車からチューニングにいたるまで、あなたの車を安全にお取り扱いします。
example_sentences.english: This auto repair shop will not only make repairs, but will take good care of your car, doing everything from cleaning to tuning it.

example_sentences.japanese: 国税庁に調べられるとき、銀行口座のお金の額から１０年前の金曜の朝にお弁当にいくらで買ったかにいたるまで何でもチェックされる。
example_sentences.english: When you are investigated by a national tax agency everything is checked, from money in your bank account to how much you spent on a bentou, Friday morning 10 years ago.

general_translation: Even if ~ cannot or will not, Even though ~ not
formation: Verb［た］+ ところで +Phrase［ない］
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ ところで +Phrase［ない］
explanation: A hypothetical structure, highlighting that even in the situation or location of (A), the result will not be as expected. Even though (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 徹夜で勉強したところで、合格しない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I studied all night, I would not pass.

example_sentences.japanese: 今更勉強を始めたところで、合格はできないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if I were to start studying now, I would not be able to pass.

example_sentences.japanese: もう電車は発車してしまったから、急いだところで間に合わないよ。
example_sentences.english: The train has already left, so even if you hurry, you won't make it.

example_sentences.japanese: 少し走ったところで、すぐには痩せないよ。
example_sentences.english: Just merely by running, you won't lose weight that quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: 「いまごろ車にのっていったところで間に合いようがない。」
example_sentences.english: Even if you went by car right now, you would not to be on time.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あやまってみたところで、彼女が許してくれるわけじゃないけど。」
example_sentences.english: 'Even if I try to apologize, it doesn't mean she will forgive me.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「たとえ失敗してしまったところで、 問題はありません。」
example_sentences.english: 'Even if you fail, there will not be a problem.'

example_sentences.japanese: 私が告白したところで、彼女は応じないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if I confessed my love, she wouldn't respond.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなにお金をかせいだところで使い切れないでしょうから、募金してみてはどうですか？
example_sentences.english: Even if you made that much money, since you surely wouldn't be able to use it all, why don't you try donating them?

example_sentences.japanese: すみませんが、今注文をキャンセルしたところで、お金は返金できませんよ。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry, even if you cancel the order now, we cannot refund your money.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっとやそっと妻に優しくしたところで妻が機嫌を直してくれるとは思わない。
example_sentences.english: Just merely by going out of your way for your wife, I don't think that she'll cheer up.

example_sentences.japanese: 五分の運動を三日間つづけたところで直ぐに成果が見られるとは限りません。
example_sentences.english: Even if you continued to exercise for 5 minutes daily for three days, it is not certain that any positive results would immediately be visible.

example_sentences.japanese: 今更焦って勉強をはじめたところであなたが志望する大学に受かる見込みはないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if you started studying in a rush at this late point, you probably have no chance of being accepted by the university that you're hoping for, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 冷房の設定温度を一度あげたところで節約できる電力はあまり多くないが、そのような小さな積み重ねが大事なのである。
example_sentences.english: Even if you raise the temperature setting of the air-con one degree, you won't be able to economize much on electricity output, but even small accumulations like that are important.

example_sentences.japanese: 真犯人を追及したところで遺族の悲しみが消えることはありませんが、刑事として何としてでも真犯人を見つける所存であります。
example_sentences.english: It is not like the bereaved family's sadness will disappear even if the true culprit is sought out, but as a detective, I have the intention of doing whatever it takes to find them.

general_translation: Like, Similar to, As if, The same as
formation: Noun + の(1) + ごとし。Noun +  の(1) + ごとくNoun + の(1) + ごとき + NounVerb + が(2) + ごとし。Verb + が(2) + ごとくVerb + が(2) + ごとき + Noun,(1)であるが(2) かの
casual_structure: Noun + の(1) + ごとし。Noun +  の(1) + ごとくNoun + の(1) + ごとき + NounVerb + が(2) + ごとし。Verb + が(2) + ごとくVerb + が(2) + ごとき + Noun,(1)であるが(2) かの
explanation: A formal construction, highlighting that something is in the likeness of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の動きはバレリーナのごとし。
example_sentences.english: Her movements are like those of a ballet dancer.

example_sentences.japanese: ことわざ：「 竜に翼を得たるごとし。」
example_sentences.english: Proverb: 'It is as if a dragon had wings.'

example_sentences.japanese: 主婦の私には休みなんかはあってなきがごとし。
example_sentences.english: As a housewife, it's like I don't have any days off.

example_sentences.japanese: 高橋先生は鬼のごとく怖いと言う噂を聞いた。
example_sentences.english: I have heard rumors that Mr. Takahashi is as scary as a demon.

example_sentences.japanese: 生まれてきたばかりの赤ちゃんが天使のごとくかわいい。
example_sentences.english: The baby that was just born is cute like an angel.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のごとき頭がいい人でも失敗することはあるに決まっている。
example_sentences.english: Even a smart person like her is bound to make mistakes.

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪ごときで休んでいる余裕など私にはない。
example_sentences.english: I can't afford to take a break just because of something like a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: ガンダルフのごとき英雄はたんと無い。
example_sentences.english: There are not many heroes like Gandalf.

example_sentences.japanese: ウサイン・ボルトのごとく走る。
example_sentences.english: He runs like Usain Bolt.

example_sentences.japanese: サービス業のマネージャーを任されている私にとって、休日などはあってなきがごとし。
example_sentences.english: For me, who has been entrusted as the manager of the service sector, something like days off are virtually nonexistent.

example_sentences.japanese: 忍者についての小説：「カツラが疾風のごとく庭を駆け巡り、塀を飛び越えていった。」
example_sentences.english: A novel about ninja: 'Katsura ran through the garden like a swift wind and jumped over the wall.'

example_sentences.japanese: 古い小説：「何かを思い出したかのような顔をして、悪夢を見ているがごとき目つきで問うた。」
example_sentences.english: Old novel: 'He seemed to have remembered something, with his face looking like something out of a nightmare, he asked....'

example_sentences.japanese: 懐かしい香水の匂いを嗅いで、十年前の青春時代の事が今さらのごとく思い出されました。
example_sentences.english: Smelling a nostalgic perfume's aroma, as if it were right this moment, it brought back memories from the prime of my youth, 10 years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 葬儀のスピーチ：「子供の頃、おじさんが「光陰矢のごとし」とよく言っていました。その意味が、今やっとわかるようになってきた気がします。」
example_sentences.english: Funeral speech: 'When I was a kid, my uncle used to say 'time flies like an arrow.' Now I feel like I'm finally starting to understand the meaning of it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒の一人が授業を終えて風のごとく教室を去っていきましたが、一体何故あんなに急いでいたのでしょうか…。
example_sentences.english: Like the wind, one of the students left the classroom after finishing the lesson, but why the heck they were in such a rush, I have no idea.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済について長年研究している知人の言うがごとく、経済は忽ち回復し始めた。
example_sentences.english: In a way similar to what a friend of mine who has been researching economics for many years said, the economy suddenly started to recover.

example_sentences.japanese: あの頃は彼のごとき人はこの世に二人といないと思っていたが、年をとって彼のような人は沢山いる事を知った。
example_sentences.english: Around that time, I thought there were no two people similar to him in this world, but as the years passed, I learned that there are actually many people just like him.

example_sentences.japanese: 獲物に追われている兎のごとく私の側から放れる同僚を見て、彼女が私を避けている事を確信した。
example_sentences.english: Seeing my colleague distance herself from me like a rabbit being chased as prey, I was convinced that she was avoiding me.

general_translation: To be worthy of, To be enough, To be sufficient
formation: Verb［る］+ に足（た）る + NounNoun (A) + に足（た）る + Noun (B)
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ に足（た）る + NounNoun (A) + に足（た）る + Noun (B)
explanation: A formal expression, showing that (B) is worthy or enough for (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「これは多くの人の興味を引くにたるものではない。」
example_sentences.english: 'This is not enough to interest a lot of people.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はこの試合に勝つにたる能力はないだろう。
example_sentences.english: He is probably not worthy to win in this competition.

example_sentences.japanese: 信頼にたる友達に、家族のことをすべて話した。
example_sentences.english: I told my trustworthy friend everything about my family.

example_sentences.japanese: 信頼にたる友達に、腕のいい歯医者を紹介してもらった。
example_sentences.english: A skilled dentist has been introduced to me by a trustworthy friend.

example_sentences.japanese: 功績から考えると、その専門分野では尊敬にたる研究者だ。
example_sentences.english: Judging from his achievements he is a researcher that is worthy of respect in that field.

example_sentences.japanese: テスラ・モデルＳは語るにたる電気自動車であり、その技術は世界に認められる。
example_sentences.english: Tesla Model S is an electric car that is worthy of being talked about, and its technology is recognized worldwide.

example_sentences.japanese: 地検：「捜査を尽くしましたが、起訴するにたる証拠を掴むことができませんでした。」
example_sentences.english: Public Prosecutor's office: 'We thoroughly investigated, however, we were unable to find enough evidence to prosecute.'

example_sentences.japanese: 確かに彼女にはおっちょこちょいな部分があるが、それでも信頼にたる友人である。
example_sentences.english: There are certainly scatterbrain parts to her, but even with that, she is a trustworthy friend.

example_sentences.japanese: 「実際のところ、信頼するにたる先生なんてほんの一握りしかいないと思う。」
example_sentences.english: 'I think there is only a handful of trustworthy teachers.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の両親に僕が彼女の夫にたる人物だと認めてもらうにはどうしたら良いだろうか…。
example_sentences.english: I wonder what I should do in order to get her parents to acknowledge me as someone that would be a worthy husband.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに分厚い本を読む気になれないあなたの気持ちも理解できますが、これは読むにたる参考書です。
example_sentences.english: I also understand your feeling of not being able to become interested in reading such a massive book, but this is a reference book worthy of reading.

example_sentences.japanese: 意地悪な上司に一生懸命に用意した原稿は読むにたるものではないとケチをつけられ、落ち込んでいます。
example_sentences.english: I’m feeling down because my mean boss nitpicked the manuscript I worked so hard on, saying it wasn’t even worth reading.

example_sentences.japanese: プレゼンテーションの冒頭で聴衆の興味を引くにたる導入をする事が出来なかったため、聴衆の関心を集める事が出来なかった。
example_sentences.english: Since I couldn't give an introduction that was sufficient to draw the attention of the audience at the beginning of the presentation, I wasn't able to rouse the listener's interest.

example_sentences.japanese: ニュース下部の欄外注記事項：「記事は信頼にたる情報源への取材等に基づいて記述しておりますが、我が社はその正確性、及び信頼性を保証いたしかねます。」
example_sentences.english: A note at the bottom of the news section: 'The report is created based on data obtained from trustworthy sources, however, we DO NOT guarantee their accuracy and reliability.'

example_sentences.japanese: お腹はいっぱいにならなかったものの、満足に足る量だった。
example_sentences.english: Even though I did not get full, it was enough to satisfy me.

example_sentences.japanese: お腹はいっぱいにならなかったものの、満足するに足る量だった。
example_sentences.english: Even though I did not get full, it was enough to satisfy me.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生は尊敬に足りない先生だと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that teacher is not worthy of respect. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生は尊敬に足る先生ではないと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that teacher is not worthy of respect.

general_translation: Extreme, Extremely
formation: ［な］Adjective + （な + こと）  +  極（きわ）まりない［な］Adjective + （な + こと）  +  極（きわ）まりない + Noun［な］Adjective + 極（きわ）まる［な］Adjective + 極（きわ）まる + Noun ［い］Adjective + こと + 極（きわ）まりない［い］Adjective + こと + 極（きわ）まりない + Noun
casual_structure: ［な］Adjective + （な + こと）  +  極（きわ）まりない［な］Adjective + （な + こと）  +  極（きわ）まりない + Noun［な］Adjective + 極（きわ）まる［な］Adjective + 極（きわ）まる + Noun ［い］Adjective + こと + 極（きわ）まりない［い］Adjective + こと + 極（きわ）まりない + Noun
explanation: An somewhat old expression, indicating that something is extremely (A). To the polar limits of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 犯罪を犯すのは愚劣きわまりないことだ。
example_sentences.english: It is extremely foolish to commit a crime.

example_sentences.japanese: 傘をさしながら自転車を運転することは危険きわまる行動なので、もっと厳しく取り締まるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Riding a bicycle while holding an umbrella is extremely dangerous behavior, so the police should more strictly enforce the law.

example_sentences.japanese: 理不尽きわまるクレームを言われるたびにノイローゼになりそうになる。
example_sentences.english: Every time I get an extremely unreasonable complaint, I feel like I'm going to have a mental breakdown.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社ではＦＡＸを使わなくてはいけないので、不便なこときわまりない。
example_sentences.english: Since we have to use fax at my company, things are extremely inconvenient.

example_sentences.japanese: この展望台から見る景色は美しいこときわまりない。
example_sentences.english: The view from the observatory is extremely beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: 目上の人に向かってその口の聞き方はなんだ。失礼きわまりないやつだな、お前は。
example_sentences.english: Why are you talking in such a manner to a person that is in a higher position than you? You are an extremely rude person, aren't you?

example_sentences.japanese: 当初、ベジータは残忍きわまる人だった。
example_sentences.english: At first, Vegeta used to be an extremely cruel person.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官は危険きわまりない仕事です。
example_sentences.english: Police officers have an extremely dangerous job.

example_sentences.japanese: ひらさわ・すすむさん：「さすがにグレープフルーツはサワーきわまる味があるわよ。」
example_sentences.english: Susumu Hirasawa-san: 'As expected from grapefruit juice, it has an extremely sour taste.'

example_sentences.japanese: ブログの投稿：「食べながら話すことは、失礼きわまりない行為だと考えられている。」
example_sentences.english: Blog post: 'Talking while eating is considered to be an extremely rude act.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「結婚してください。」ヒキガヤの声を聞いて、ユキノは感きわまって手を取って、握りしめた。
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Please, marry me.'Hearing Hikigaya's voice, Yukino was overcome with extreme emotion, she took his hand and grasped it tightly.

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルの従業員の不誠実きわまりない態度に飽き足らず、支配人に苦情を出した。
example_sentences.english: I was so dissatisfied with the hotel personnel's extreme insincerity, that I complained to a manager.

example_sentences.japanese: その皇帝は征服欲きわまりないため、次々と周辺の国へ侵攻した。
example_sentences.english: Due to his extreme lust for conquest, that emperor invaded surrounding countries one after the other.

example_sentences.japanese: 容疑者が取り調べ中に退屈きわまる話をする狙いは、刑事たちの気を逸らす事でしょう。
example_sentences.english: The suspect’s aim in talking about such extremely boring things during the interrogation was probably to distract the detectives.

example_sentences.japanese: 大胆きわまりない戦術を提案する彼は武士として尊敬されていたが、その分敵も多かった。
example_sentences.english: Suggesting an extremely bold strategy, he was respected as a warrior, but with that being the case, there were many enemies.

example_sentences.japanese: 失礼きわまりない態度で取引先を怒らせてしまったため、僕は近々首にされるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Due to making our trade partners angry with my extremely rude behavior, I am probably going to get fired before too long.

example_sentences.japanese: 怠慢な態度で仕事をしている同僚の無責任きわまる発言を聞き、真面目に働く事が馬鹿らしく思えてきました。
example_sentences.english: Hearing the extremely irresponsible remarks of my colleague who works with a negligent attitude, I began to think that working earnestly was just foolish.

general_translation: Even (if), Although, Even though
formation: Verb + といえどもNoun + といえども［な］Adjective + (だ) + といえども［い］Adjective + といえども
casual_structure: Verb + といえどもNoun + といえども［な］Adjective + (だ) + といえども［い］Adjective + といえども
explanation: A formal, very old-fashioned way of saying although. But even if (A) were said to be the case, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ヒジカタが恐るべしといえども、スギモトの敵ではない。
example_sentences.english: Even though Hijikata is incredible, he is no match for Sugimoto.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらお金に困っているといえども、闇金には絶対手を出さないよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if I was really troubled about money, there is no way I would turn to a loan shark.

example_sentences.japanese: 前は一回で成功したといえども、毎回一回で成功できる訳ではない。
example_sentences.english: Even though we were able to succeed before on our first try, that doesn't mean that we can succeed in one try every time.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女がどれだけ優しいといえども、そんなことばかりやってたら別れられるぞ。
example_sentences.english: Even though she is super nice, if you keep doing such things she is going to break up with you.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ犯罪者といえども、動物みたいに扱ってはいけない。
example_sentences.english: Even if they are criminals, you must not treat them like animals.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転が上手だといえども、シートベルトは必ず着用しなくてはならない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are good at driving, you must wear a seatbelt.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら有名だといえども、なんでも好き勝手やっていいと言うことではない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are famous, it doesn't mean that you can just do whatever you wish.

example_sentences.japanese: 手術中は一瞬といえど気が抜けない。
example_sentences.english: During an operation you cannot lose focus, not even for a second.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ囚人といえどもときどき刑務所を出ることができる。
example_sentences.english: Even a prisoner can leave prison from time to time.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨天といえども、ゴミ拾いのボランティアをしないわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is rainy weather, there is no way that I can not volunteer for the litter clean up.

example_sentences.japanese: 王様といえども、法律を犯すことは出来ません。
example_sentences.english: Although he is the king, he cannot break the law.

example_sentences.japanese: 弁護のためといえども、暴漢を撃つべきではないという意見もある。
example_sentences.english: There are also opinions that one should not shoot a hoodlum, even in self-defense.

example_sentences.japanese: 対戦相手が子供といえども、気を抜くことは出来ない。
example_sentences.english: Even if my match opponent is a child, I cannot let my guard down.

example_sentences.japanese: 人間はいくら手練れといえども生きている限り間違いをすることがある。
example_sentences.english: Although humans are skilled, as long as they live they will make mistakes.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは双子といえども、見た目も性格も全く違います。
example_sentences.english: Even though we are twins, both our looks and our personalities are completely different.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらイケメンだといえども、それだけで付き合おうとは思えない。
example_sentences.english: Even if he is that much of a stud, I don’t think that I could date him just on that.

example_sentences.japanese: 不況下で損失が出ているといえども、我が社は遅滞無く給与を支払う。
example_sentences.english: Even when taking losses during a recession our company pays salaries without delay.

example_sentences.japanese: 親を説得するためといえども、そのためにネットから嘘の情報を引っ張ってくるのは卑怯だろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is in order to persuade your parents, hauling in false information from the internet for that purpose is pathetic, isn't it?

general_translation: By means of, With, By, Via, In view of
formation: Noun + をもって
casual_structure: Noun + をもって
explanation: A formal phrase expressing something done or caused by the means of (A). Often when that means is important, or leads to a final result.

example_sentences.japanese: 以上、本状をもって辞表と致します。
example_sentences.english: Moreover, I resign by means of this document.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の家族を持ってから、親である大変さを身をもって感じた。
example_sentences.english: After having my own family, I felt through personal experience how difficult it is to be a parent.

example_sentences.japanese: お客様の順番になりましたら、アプリをもって通知いたします。
example_sentences.english: When it is your turn, you will be notified via the app.

example_sentences.japanese: 検査の結果は電話をもって連絡させていただきます。
example_sentences.english: The results of the examination will be communicated by telephone.

example_sentences.japanese: 当選は賞品の発送をもって発表に代えさせていただきます。
example_sentences.english: The winner will be notified by means of the shipment of the prize. (Literally - The announcement of the winner will be replaced with the shipment of the prize)

example_sentences.japanese: ライトノベル：「どうしてヒメジの料理がみんなに避けられるか、身をもって知ったばかりだ。」
example_sentences.english: Light novel: 'I just learned with my own body why everybody avoids Himeji's cooking.' (by means of)

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんは多数決をもって労働組合の代表として選出されました。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san has been elected as a labor union representative with a majority vote. (by means of)

example_sentences.japanese: 採用担当者：「面接の結果は電話をもってご連絡いたします。」
example_sentences.english: Recruiter: 'The results of the interview will be communicated to you by phone.' (by means of・in view of)

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚式、新郎新婦の入場、神父：「皆さん、拍手をもってお迎えください。」
example_sentences.english: A wedding ceremony, the entrance of the bride and groom, priest: 'Everybody, please welcome (the bride and groom) with applause.' (by means of)

example_sentences.japanese: ホストファミリーから好意をもって迎えられ、緊張で強張った体が少し楽になりました。
example_sentences.english: I was greeted by my host family with kindness, so my body that had become stiff with nerves relaxed a little bit.

example_sentences.japanese: デジタル化が進むこの時代にまだ紙媒体の書類をもって契約しなければならないなんて、信じられない！
example_sentences.english: In this generation of continuing digitization, I cannot believe something like the need for a contract via the medium of paper.

example_sentences.japanese: うちのエースをもってもこの試合に勝つことが出来なかったのだから、エースなしでは少しも希望が見出せない。
example_sentences.english: Since we couldn't win this match with our star player, in their absence, not even a tiny bit of hope is detectable.

example_sentences.japanese: 死をもって罪の償いをしたところで、被害者やその遺族が報われることはありません。
example_sentences.english: Even if a crime is atoned for via death, there is no reward for the victim or their bereaved family.

example_sentences.japanese: 陽極のグラフェンという物質の塗布をもって作られる、新たな種類の電池は翌年導入される予定である。
example_sentences.english: A new kind of battery, made with graphene-coated anodes, is expected to be introduced next year. (by means of)

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩から取引先との契約が成立した事を告げられ、誠意をもって交渉に臨んだ甲斐があったと感じた。
example_sentences.english: When I was informed by my senpai that the contract with our client was successful, I felt that dealing with the negotiations with sincerity had been worth it.

example_sentences.japanese: 最新の技術をもってすれば、運転を完全に自動化することは可能だと思います。
example_sentences.english: With recent technologies, I think it will be possible to fully automate driving.

example_sentences.japanese: 君みたいな忍耐をもってすれば、どんなことでも乗り越えられるだろう。
example_sentences.english: With your perseverance, you will probably be able to overcome anything.

general_translation: Have a tendency to, Tend to, Be slightly~
formation: Verb［る］+ きらいがあるVerb［ない］+ きらいがあるNoun + の + きらいがある
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ きらいがあるVerb［ない］+ きらいがあるNoun + の + きらいがある
polite_structure: Verb［る］+ きらいがありますVerb［ない］+ きらいがありますNoun + の + きらいがあります
explanation: An expression often used to imply negative tendencies. The hateful (A) exists.

example_sentences.japanese: 近頃の親は過保護のきらいがある。
example_sentences.english: Parents these days tend to be overprotective.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は三日坊主だから、何かを始めてもすぐに辞めるきらいがある。
example_sentences.english: Since she is a quitter, she tends to quit things as soon as she starts them.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は自分の意見を言わないきらいがある。
example_sentences.english: He tends to not share his own opinions.

example_sentences.japanese: お盆休みの間は浅草に行く観光客の数が上昇するきらいがある。
example_sentences.english: The number of tourists visiting Asakusa tends to rise during Obon.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんは少し強い言い方をするきらいがあるけど、あまり気にしないでね。
example_sentences.english: My father tends to use harsh words, but please don't take it personally.

example_sentences.japanese: 斉藤さんはどうも冬になると家に引きこもるきらいがあるので、今年の冬は斉藤さんとたくさんお出かけに行く予定です。
example_sentences.english: Apparently, Saito-san tends to become a hermit during winter, so I made plans to go out a lot with her this winter.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は彼の気持ちを尊重しないきらいがある。
example_sentences.english: She has a tendency to not respect his feelings.

example_sentences.japanese: ある人は、民族だけで人の性格を判断してしまうきらいがある。
example_sentences.english: A certain person tends to judge a person's nature just by their ethnic group.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんは、困っている人のためには人助けをする。しかし助けてもらった人は、されたことを忘れるきらいがある。
example_sentences.english: Father always helps people in need. However, the people who received help tend to forget about it.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「高血圧のきらいがあることを除けばほとんど健康だった３４歳の男性はバクテリアの感染により重体に陥った。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'A 34-year-old man, who was mostly healthy, aside for a tendency to have high blood pressure, has fallen seriously ill due to a bacterial infection.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「日本のような先進国では出生率低下のきらいがあり、その結果として諸問題が発生する。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'In developed countries such as Japan, there is a tendency for a declining birth rate, and as a result, various problems arise.'

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は何でも独断するきらいがあるため、僕は度々信頼されていないのではないかと悩んでしまう。
example_sentences.english: Since my wife has a tendency to decide everything on her own, unfortunately I am frequently troubled as to whether I am trusted.

example_sentences.japanese: 考えすぎるきらいがある患者にある薬を処方したところ、患者は心の状態が良くなった事を報告した。
example_sentences.english: After prescribing a certain medication for a patient that has a tendency to overthink, they reported that their mental condition had gotten better.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆から慕われている上司の一言で、業績を鼻にかけるきらいがある同僚の態度が一変しました。
example_sentences.english: With the brief comment from our boss who is deeply admired by everyone, my colleague who tends to be boastful about his achievements had a complete change in attitude.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の思い通りにいかないと機嫌を損ねるきらいがある息子をどう教育するべきか夫婦で話し合う。
example_sentences.english: We talk together as husband and wife about how to raise our son who tends to feel bad when things don't go his way.

example_sentences.japanese: 少数派の意見を無視するきらいがあるその政治家が首相になっては大変なので他の政治家に投票しよう。
example_sentences.english: Since that politician who tends to ignore the opinions of minorities would be problematic if they became the prime minister, let's vote for another politician.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は自分が研究している分野の話になると話し過ぎるきらいがあるので、その分野の話は避けるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: If it becomes a conversation about my mom's field of research, since she has a tendency to talk too much, you should avoid conversations about that topic.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はなんでもすぐ飽きる嫌いがある。
example_sentences.english: I have a tendency to get bored easily with everything. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: A is fine...but B is not, If it's ~ then it is ok...but ~ is not, It's different when...but, It's not so bad when...but
formation: Phrase (A) + ならまだしも + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Phrase (A) + ならまだしも + Phrase (B)
explanation: A hypothetical expression, stating that even if it is still (A), that's fine, but not (B). It's different if it's (B).

example_sentences.japanese: すみませんが、付き合うぐらいならまだしも、結婚は無理な注文です。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry, if it is just going out then it is ok, but marriage is out of the question. (is not okay)

example_sentences.japanese: 暑いだけならまだしも、湿度も高いからどこにも行きたくない。
example_sentences.english: If it was hot, that would be fine, but because it is also humid, I don't want to go.

example_sentences.japanese: 二、三日ならまだしも、二週間なんて待てませんよ。
example_sentences.english: If it was 2 or three days, we could wait, but 2 weeks? We can't wait that long.

example_sentences.japanese: 一回だけならまだしも、毎日同じことで怒られて何にも思わないの。
example_sentences.english: If it was only once, okay, but don't you feel any sort of way being scolded for the same thing everyday?

example_sentences.japanese: すごく恥ずかしい！お父さん、ビーチでならまだしも、半裸で外に出るのはやめてほしい！
example_sentences.english: This is so embarrassing! Papa, if it is a beach, it is ok, but going half naked outside? I want you to stop! (it is not okay)

example_sentences.japanese: 「ねぇ、歩いて行こうよ。」「自転車ならまだしも、そんな遠くまで歩いて行くのは無理だよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'C'mon, let's go on foot!''If it was on a bicycle, then it would be ok, but it is impossible to go that far on foot!' (is not okay)

example_sentences.japanese: 隣人がうちの駐車区域にたまに車を止めるならまだしも、いつも止めているから、いい加減腹が立つよ。
example_sentences.english: If my neighbor uses my parking spot from time to time then it's ok, but because he is always parking there, I get pissed. (it is not okay)

example_sentences.japanese: ツイート：「自分が感染するだけならまだしも祖父母や親などが病気になってしまうのがとても恐ろしいです。」
example_sentences.english: Tweet: 'If it is just me becoming infected, then it is ok, but my grandparents or parents becoming ill is really scary.' (is not okay)

example_sentences.japanese: ただ寒いだけならまだしもこんなに雪が降っているなら外でのピクニックは中止か延期にするべきだ。
example_sentences.english: It's not so bad if it's just cold, but if there's this much snow falling, you ought to cancel or postpone your picnic outside.

example_sentences.japanese: 一度や二度ならまだしも三日間続けて遅刻をしてきた社員には何かしらの罰を与えよう…。
example_sentences.english: It's different if it's one or two times, but for an employee that has continued to come in late for three days in a row, let's give them some kind of punishment.

example_sentences.japanese: 待ち合わせに１０分遅れてくるくらいならまだしも、２時間も遅刻して謝らないなんてどうかしているよ！
example_sentences.english: It is not so bad if it is coming around 10 minutes late for a meeting time, but something like being 2 hours late and not apologizing means they are not right in the head!

example_sentences.japanese: ただ風が強いだけならまだしも、台風並みに強いこの風の中で飛行機が飛ぶことはないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It's fine if it is merely just a strong wind, but not when a plane is flying through wind that's strength is in line with that of a typhoon, right? (it is not okay)

example_sentences.japanese: ３人や４人ならまだしも、１０人も友達を家に呼んでパーティーをするなんて、隣人から文句を言われるに違いない。
example_sentences.english: If it is 3 or 4 people then it is ok, but something like calling 10 or so friends over to your house for a party, there's no mistake that the neighbors will complain. (it is not okay)

example_sentences.japanese: カロリーが高いだけならまだしも、材料に沢山の添加物まで入っているのならそれを食べるのは遠慮しておくよ。
example_sentences.english: It's not so bad if it is just high calorie, but if it's something where there are even lots of additives in the ingredients, I will hold back from eating it.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に出荷遅延について苦情を言う：「１週間とか２週間ならまだしも、出荷まで３ヶ月も待つなんて全く受け入れられない！」
example_sentences.english: Complaining to a friend about a shipment delay: 'If it was one or two weeks, that would be fine, but waiting something like 3 months until the shipment? That is completely unacceptable!' (not okay)

example_sentences.japanese: 今しも家を出ようとしていたところだった。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to leave the house.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰しも長年使ってきた釣り竿には愛着がある。
example_sentences.english: Everyone has an attachment to a fishing rod they have used for many years.

general_translation: There is no need to, Do not have to, It is not necessary to, Needless to
formation: More common patterns:Verb［る］+ までもないVerb［る］+ までもなく + PhraseLess common patterns:Verb［る］+ までもなくて + Phrase
casual_structure: More common patterns:Verb［る］+ までもないVerb［る］+ までもなく + PhraseLess common patterns:Verb［る］+ までもなくて + Phrase
polite_structure: More common patterns:Verb［る］+ までもありませんVerb［る］+ までもなく + PhraseLess common patterns:Verb［る］+ までもなくて + Phrase
explanation: A construction indicating (A) as unnecessary. There's no need to even go until (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「今さら訂正するまでもなく、明らかに間違っている。」
example_sentences.english: 'There is no need to correct it, it is clearly wrong.'

example_sentences.japanese: 痛いけど、指は全部ちゃんと動くから病院に行くまでもないと思う。
example_sentences.english: Although it hurts, all my fingers move properly so there is no need to go to the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子を見て、何か悪いことをしたと分かった。聞くまでもなかった。
example_sentences.english: I could tell that my son did something bad by just looking at him. It was not necessary for me to ask anything.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人ならなんとかしてくれるよ。心配するまでもないよ。
example_sentences.english: Knowing that person, they would probably do something about it. There is no need to worry.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は、すでに全て解説したので聞くまでもない。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to ask questions because the teacher has already explained everything.

example_sentences.japanese: これはただの打撲で骨にヒビが入っているわけではないので病院に行くまでもない。
example_sentences.english: Since this was just a body-blow, and it is not the case that there is a fracture to the bone, there is no need to go to the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: あのね......そんごくうはクリリンなんかとは比べるまでもなく、それどころかベジータよりもずっと強いんだから。
example_sentences.english: Hey, there is no need to compare Goku to someone like Krillin, because he is far stronger than Vegeta.

example_sentences.japanese: この試験の難しさから考えると、試験の結果発表は見るまでもなく明らかだ。
example_sentences.english: Judging from this exam's difficulty, the results are clear without the need to see them.

example_sentences.japanese: ゆきちゃん：「さきちゃん、あれはひどかったよ。」さきちゃん：「あんな奴なら、優しくするまでもない。」
example_sentences.english: Yuki: 'Saki, that was cruel.'Saki: 'If it's a guy like that, there is no need to be friendly.'

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家はここから徒歩五分圏内なので、わざわざ私を家に送るまでもないよ。
example_sentences.english: As for my house, since it is within the range of a 5 minute walk by foot from here, there is really no need to go out of your way to escort me home.

example_sentences.japanese: その問題なら私一人で解決できるから、わざわざ他の部署から助っ人を呼ぶまでもない。
example_sentences.english: If it is just that issue, since I can resolve it by myself, it is not necessary to go out of the way to call for a helper from another department.

example_sentences.japanese: 全身に返り血を浴び、犯行に使われた凶器を持った彼が殺人犯である事は確かめるまでもなく明らかです。
example_sentences.english: Being that he was completely covered in the blood of his victim, and had the murder weapon, there is no need to confirm that he is the killer. It is plain as day!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の事なら心配するまでもないよ。だって誰よりも賢くて体力も精神力もあるんだから。
example_sentences.english: If it is him, then you don't need to worry! You know, because he is more clever, more resilient, and has a stronger will than anybody else!

example_sentences.japanese: 母親が社長で父親が医者である生徒の家庭に金銭的な余裕がある事は言うまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It is needless to say that a student who has a managing director as a mother and a doctor as a father has a financially abundant household.

example_sentences.japanese: コーラの瓶を開けようとしているとき、Ａ：「待っててよ。栓抜きをすぐ持ってくるよ。」テーブルの端っこで瓶を開ける、Ｂ：「わざわざ持ってくるまでもないよ。」
example_sentences.english: When trying to open a bottle of coke, A: 'Wait a sec! I'll quickly bring a bottle opener.'*Opens the bottle with the edge of the table* B: 'No need to bother bringing it!' ('You don't need to go to the trouble of getting it!')

example_sentences.japanese: 言うまでもなく、不法投棄で近所の人が迷惑しています。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that illegal disposal of garbage is causing troubles to the people in this neighborhood.

general_translation: When, If, Once, As
formation: Noun + と(1) + （も） + なると(2)Verb［る］+ と + （も） + なると(2)(1) に(2) なれば
casual_structure: Noun + と(1) + （も） + なると(2)Verb［る］+ と + （も） + なると(2)(1) に(2) なれば
explanation: A strong hypothetical phrase, indicating that once something becomes (A), (B) will result. Often about rare events or important milestones.

example_sentences.japanese: 大人ともなると、幼馴染との友情は弱くなりつつあるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Once you become an adult, the bond with childhood friends gets weaker and weaker.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたも行くともなると、席が足りないので、車３台ではなく４台で行くことにしましょう。
example_sentences.english: If you are also coming, there will not be enough seats, so let's take 4 cars instead of 3.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社のウェブページを作成するともなれば、優秀なプログラマーが必要になるだろう。
example_sentences.english: We would probably need good programmers, once we start working on the company website.

example_sentences.japanese: ゴールデンウィークともなると、遊園地などは混む。
example_sentences.english: Amusement parks get crowded once Golden week starts.

example_sentences.japanese: 社会人ともなれば、色々な社会的ルールを守らなければいけなくなる。
example_sentences.english: Once you become a member of society, there are various societal rules that you need to start following.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなつまらない観光地も、週末ともなると観光客で賑わう。
example_sentences.english: When the weekend starts, even the most boring tourist attractions are crowded.

example_sentences.japanese: チームリーダーに就任するともなると、自分の仕事に限らずチームメンバーの仕事に責任があるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Once you become a team leader, you will be responsible not only for your own but also for the work of team members.

example_sentences.japanese: 普段は貪欲ではない人でも、莫大な金額ともなると貪欲になるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Even people who are generally not greedy might become greedy when it comes to huge amounts of money.

example_sentences.japanese: この辺りでは１１月ともなると中々寒さも厳しくなってくるため、これからの時期はヒートテックが必須だろう。
example_sentences.english: Once it becomes winter around here, since the cold becomes quite harsh, it's probably necessary to buy some thermal clothing as of now.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは普通の漁村だが、夏休みともなると大勢の客が来て、賑やかになります。
example_sentences.english: This is an ordinary fishing village, but when the summer vacation starts, a large number of visitors come and it becomes lively.

example_sentences.japanese: 絶叫系のアトラクションも今日で３個目ともなると体もだんだんと慣れてくるみたいです。
example_sentences.english: As it's also the third thrill-type ride of the day, it seems like my body is gradually getting used to it.

example_sentences.japanese: 最初の頃は妻の愚痴も辛抱強く聞いていたが結婚５年目ともなると、そうはいかない。
example_sentences.english: In the beginning stages, I even listened to my wife's complaints patiently, but once it got to the 5th year of marriage, I could no longer do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんは普通のサラリーマンだが、危なくて後が無い状況ともなると獅子のように他の人を守る。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san is just an ordinary office worker, but when the situation is dangerous and there is no way out, he will protect others like a lion.

example_sentences.japanese: 数年に渡って海外の支店で仕事をするともなると、流石にその地域の言語や文化を学ばないわけにはいきません。
example_sentences.english: Once passing a number of years working in an overseas branch office, as expected, not learning that region's language or culture is hardly possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 若い頃は体力に自信がありましたが四十代ともなると今までのようには体が動きません。
example_sentences.english: I had confidence in the power of my body in my younger days, but once I reached my forties, my body could not move in the way that it did up until now.

example_sentences.japanese: 親が娘に話している：「今は大丈夫だけど、運動をしないと３０代になれば健康問題が一つずつ現れるよ。」
example_sentences.english: Parent speaks to daughter: 'It is alright now, but if you don't exercise, once you get to your thirties, health problems will appear one by one!'

example_sentences.japanese: 新入社員の頃は上の指示に従って動くだけで評価してもらえたが、入社十年目ともなると流石にそれだけでは評価してもらえない。
example_sentences.english: As a new-entry, I was able to get approval by acting in line with the directions of my superiors. Naturally however, once in my tenth consecutive year with the company, simply just doing that will not get any acknowledgement.

example_sentences.japanese: ５０代となると体が思うように動かなくなる。
example_sentences.english: Once you turn 50, your body stops working like how you want it to. (Unavoidable due to age)

example_sentences.japanese: ５０代になると体が思うように動かなくなる。
example_sentences.english: Once you turn 50, your body stops working like how you want it to. (Simply stating that once you turn 50, your body won't be the same as it was before)

general_translation: To take advantage of
formation: Verb + の + をいいことに（して）Noun + （なの）+ をいいことに（して）［い］Adjective + の + をいいことに（して）［な］Adjective + なの + をいいことに（して）
casual_structure: Verb + の + をいいことに（して）Noun + （なの）+ をいいことに（して）［い］Adjective + の + をいいことに（して）［な］Adjective + なの + をいいことに（して）
explanation: A structure that highlights (A) as being taken advantage of negatively. Making a good thing out of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私が稼いでいるのをいいことに、遊んでばかりいます。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of that I am turning a profit; he is doing nothing but having fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 顔が見えないのをいいことにひどいことを書き込む人は最低だと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that people who write terrible things on the internet, taking advantage of anonymity, are the worst.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が優しいのをいいことに、クラスメイトたちは彼をいじめた。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of his niceness, his classmates bullied him.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は美人であるのをいいことに、色々な男からお金を騙し取った。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of her great looks, she swindled many men out of their money.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みなのをいいことに、友達と一日中ゲームをした。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of my day off, I played video games all day with my friend.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の耳が遠いのをいいことにして、授業中に友達と話していた。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of my teacher being hard of hearing, I was talking with my friends during class.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の目が悪いのをいいことに試験中にカンニングしていた。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of the teacher's bad sight, I cheated during the exam.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はお母さんが忘れっぽいのをいいことに、責任から逃れようとした。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of that my mom is forgetful, I tried to evade taking responsibility.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は新入社員なのをいいことに、仕事が出来ないふりをしている。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of that she is a new recruit; she is pretending that she doesn’t know how to do the work.

example_sentences.japanese: 敵が罠にはまったのをいいことに、全力で総攻撃をしかけた。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of the enemy being trapped, he launched an all-out attack.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏休みのうちは住人の留守をいいことに泥棒が増えるばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: During summer vacation, taking advantage of absent residents, thefts only increase.

example_sentences.japanese: その男は力が強いのをいいことに、色々な人からお金を奪った。
example_sentences.english: Taking advantage of his strength, that man has robbed various people of their money.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんってば自分が大臣なのをいいことに姪を省で縁故採用した。
example_sentences.english: That Tanaka-san... He took advantage of his position as a minister, and got his niece a job in ministry.

example_sentences.japanese: コンマンはうちの子供が幼いのをいいことに家の鍵や携帯を詐欺で巻き上げた。
example_sentences.english: A con man took advantage of my child's young age and swindled (him) of (his) house keys and cellphone.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「この期間に多くの家族が親類を訪れる。それをいいことに空っぽの家に泥棒にはいる人もいる。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'During this period, many families visit relatives. Some people take advantage of it and steal from empty households.'

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の不在をいいことに自主学習の時間に遊んでいたばかりいた生徒は後に後悔する事となりました。
example_sentences.english: For the students that took advantage of the teacher's absence, doing nothing but mucking around in their free-study time, they came to regret it afterwards.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日が休日なのをいいことに散々飲み歩いていたら翌日に酷い二日酔いに襲われました。
example_sentences.english: When taking advantage of the next day being a holiday, going bar hopping all over the place, I was assailed by a wicked hangover the day after.

general_translation: Depending on
formation: Noun + （の）+ 如何（いかん） + で（は） (1)Noun + （の）+ 如何（いかん） + だ(2)。(1) によって（は）(2) である
casual_structure: Noun + （の）+ 如何（いかん） + で（は） (1)Noun + （の）+ 如何（いかん） + だ(2)。(1) によって（は）(2) である
explanation: A formal word, expressing that (B) depends on (A). By something that's one in the same likeness as (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 入学試験の成績いかんで、私の将来が決まる。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the exam results, my future will be decided.

example_sentences.japanese: 嵐の状況のいかんで、来週のイベントが中止されるかされないかが決まる。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not next week's event will be canceled will depend on the status of the storm.

example_sentences.japanese: 前回の試験の結果いかんでどの大学に入れるかが決まる。
example_sentences.english: Which college I can get into will depend on the result of my last exam.

example_sentences.japanese: 東大に入学できるかは、君たちの努力のいかんだ。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not you guys can get into Tokyo University would depend on your efforts.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月昇進できるかは自分の業績いかんだ。
example_sentences.english: Whether I get a promotion next month depends on my performance.

example_sentences.japanese: 実験の結果いかんによっては、最初からやり直さないといけなくなる可能性もあります。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the results of the experiment, we may have to start over from the beginning.

example_sentences.japanese: 中東情勢いかんでは石油価格が急上昇しかねない。
example_sentences.english: The oil prices might surge depending on political tension in the Middle East.

example_sentences.japanese: 衝突事故ならば傷の状態いかんによっては入院する場合もありうる。
example_sentences.english: In the case of an accident, depending on the severity of the wound, hospitalization is also possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 「応募者の採用・不採用は書類選考の結果いかんです。」
example_sentences.english: 'The acceptance or rejection of the applicants depends on the results of the document screening.'

example_sentences.japanese: 相手の対応いかんでは、今回の件を裁判沙汰にしようと思っている。
example_sentences.english: Depending on what way the other party responds, I am thinking that today's incident shall be a matter for the courts.

example_sentences.japanese: 必要な最少参加者数の到達いかんによってコース開催かどうか決定される。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not the course will be held all depends on the minimum number of required participants being reached.

example_sentences.japanese: 実験の結果のいかんで研究資金が決まる。中止の場合もあります。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the experiment's results, funding will be decided. Cancellation is also a possibility.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い友人に「このプロジェクトの成否はあなたの協力いかんによる」と言われてしまっては、申し出を断る事は出来ない。
example_sentences.english: Being told that 'the outcome of this project will depend on your cooperation' by an old friend, It's a request that I cannot turn down.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学の教授：「私の授業では基本公欠は認めていませんが、理由のいかんによっては認める場合もあります。」
example_sentences.english: University professor: 'Basically, I don't recognize authorized absences in my classes, but depending on the reason, there are times that I will acknowledge it.'

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルのサイト：「今後の状況いかんでは予約の取り消しが不可避の場合もございます。その際はメールをもって告知させていただきます。」
example_sentences.english: Hotel website: 'Depending on future circumstances, we may have to cancel your reservation. In that case, we will notify you with an email.'

example_sentences.japanese: 上司が部下に：「今後の君の働き方いかんでは、君を首にする事や他の部署に移す事になる。」
example_sentences.english: Boss to a subordinate: 'Depending on the way that you work from now on, it will end up that you are fired, or moved to another department.'

example_sentences.japanese: 大学が募集する留学のプログラムに参加できるかどうかはその費用等の詳細いかんである。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not I will be able to participate in the university's currently being recruited for exchange program is something that will depend on the particulars of the cost and such.

general_translation: Just, Merely, Simply, Only
formation: (Negative Situation) Verb［ば］(1) + Verb［る］+ まで(2) + だ(1) Phrase［たら］、Phrase［ても］(2) までのこと
casual_structure: (Negative Situation) Verb［ば］(1) + Verb［る］+ まで(2) + だ(1) Phrase［たら］、Phrase［ても］(2) までのこと
polite_structure: (Negative Situation) Verb［ば］(1) + Verb［る］+ まで(2) + です(1) Phrase［たら］、Phrase［ても］(2) までのこと
explanation: An expression showing that the negative thing which is (A) will only last until (B). If (A), simply (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 「問題が起きても、かいけつするまでだよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'If a problem arises, I will just solve it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 誰にも教えてもらえないなら、ネットで調べてみるまでだ。
example_sentences.english: If no one is going to teach me, I will just search it online.

example_sentences.japanese: もし失敗したのなら、もう一回挑戦するまでだ。失敗しても諦めないことが大切だ。
example_sentences.english: If you made a mistake, you just have to try again. It is important to not give up even if you fail.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰も迎えにきてくれないのなら、電車で帰るまでのことだ。
example_sentences.english: If no one is going to come pick me up, I will simply go home by train.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社に入社できなかったら、別の会社を探すまでのことです。
example_sentences.english: If I can't join this company, I will simply look for a different one.

example_sentences.japanese: もしＪＬＰＴに落ちたら、もう一度ためしてみるまでのことだ。
example_sentences.english: If I fail the JLPT, I will simply try it once again.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車に乗り遅れたら、次のをまつまでのことだ。
example_sentences.english: If I miss the train, I will simply wait for the next one.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫婦の話：「やめなくちゃならないというなら、やめるまでのことだ。」
example_sentences.english: A conversation between a couple: 'If you say I have to quit, then I will simply quit.'

example_sentences.japanese: 祖国で就職できなかったら、外国へ移住することになるまでだ。
example_sentences.english: If I can't find work in my motherland, I will simply move abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: ファンタジー小説：「峠を越えるのが不可能ならば、モリアの坑道をとおりぬけるまでのことだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Fantasy novel: 'If passing through the mountain pass is impossible, we will simply go through the mines of Moria!' (just)

example_sentences.japanese: 飲み会のせいで終電を逃してしまったのなら、タクシーを拾って帰るまでだ。
example_sentences.english: If I miss the last train due to the drinking party, I'll simply just grab a taxi and go home.

example_sentences.japanese: 一度試験に失敗してもまた受けるまでのことなので、そこまで思い詰める必要はありません。
example_sentences.english: Even if you fail the examination once, since you just need to take it again, there's no need to torment yourself about it.

example_sentences.japanese: 元彼が「君と別れなくちゃいけないなら死ぬまでだ。」と言った時はゾッとしました。
example_sentences.english: I was horrified when my ex-boyfriend said 'if we must break up, I will just die'.

example_sentences.japanese: 確かにその会社と提携を結びたいのは事実だが、不公平な条件を提示されたら断るまでだ。
example_sentences.english: Certainly, while it is true that I want to form a bond with that company, if any imbalanced conditions are suggested, I will simply refuse.

example_sentences.japanese: 心の健康ほど大事なものは無いのだから、そんなに今の仕事をやりたくないなら辞めるまでです。
example_sentences.english: Since even mental health is not something that is valued, if you really do not want to do your current work that much, simply resign.

example_sentences.japanese: 性格や食の好みが合わないとなれば別れるまでだ。結婚を考えないうちはそうやって場数を踏むつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: If our personalities or tastes in food are not compatible, we can simply break up. Doing that while we're still not thinking about marriage is something that I intend to gain experience from.

general_translation: At, In the (place or situation), Under ~ conditions or circumstances, During, Suited to
formation: Noun + にあってに + ある ￫ にあって
casual_structure: Noun + にあってに + ある ￫ にあって
explanation: A phrase showing that under the circumstances or situation of (A), (B). When in the existing situation of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 好況にあっても破産を申請している企業がある。
example_sentences.english: Even during a boom, there are companies applying for bankruptcy.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は校長先生という立場にあって、いつも生徒たちのために一生懸命働いている。
example_sentences.english: In the position of a principal, she is always working hard for the students.

example_sentences.japanese: インフルエンザが流行っているという状況にあって、外にいる人はみんなマスクをしている。
example_sentences.english: In a situation where the flu is spreading, everyone outside is wearing masks.

example_sentences.japanese: 緊急事態宣言にあって、県を跨ぐ移動が制限された。
example_sentences.english: Under the state of emergency, movements across prefectures were restricted.

example_sentences.japanese: 緊急時にあっても、常に冷静を保つようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: Even under emergencies, please stay calm at all times.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな厳しい状況にあっても、諦めずに営業を続けていたから彼は儲けることができた。
example_sentences.english: Even under difficult circumstances like this, they were able to make a profit because they kept running their business without giving up.

example_sentences.japanese: 危険な非常時にあっては、安全確保が第一だ。
example_sentences.english: Under emergency conditions, ensuring safety is the most important.

example_sentences.japanese: このような状況下にあって、医療機関へのアクセスは限定されているかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Under conditions like this, access to the medical institutions might be limited.

example_sentences.japanese: ＣＥＯのスピーチ：「混乱期にあっても心配せずに将来を見据えます。」
example_sentences.english: CEO's speech: 'Even in this chaotic time, without fear, we look into the future.' (under...circumstances)

example_sentences.japanese: 歴史の教科書：「総理大臣という立場にあって、言論の自由のみならず動物の権利も提唱した。」
example_sentences.english: History textbook: 'In the position of Prime Minister, she advocated not only for the freedom of speech but also for animal rights.'(under...circumstances)

example_sentences.japanese: 警告サイン：「被災地にあっては、破片から目を保護するため安全メガネを必ず着用して下さい。」
example_sentences.english: Warning sign: 'In the disaster zone, be sure to wear safety glasses to protect your eyes from debris.'(under...circumstances)

example_sentences.japanese: 逆境という状況にあっては、何があっても諦めないという強い意志が必要になります。
example_sentences.english: During adverse situations, having the strong intention to not give up no matter what happens is necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら後輩を指導する職にあっても、指導の中で暴力を振るう事や暴言を吐く事は禁止されています。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much you are in the situation of guiding juniors, lashing out with violence during direction, or spitting abuse is forbidden.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行会社のパンフレット：「紛争が続いている地域にあっては、我が社の保険は適用されませんのでご注意下さい。」
example_sentences.english: Travel agency's pamphlet: 'Since our company's insurance is not suitable for zones that are in an ongoing conflict, please take heed.' (under...circumstances)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は長年に渡って社員の教育係という立場にあって、そのおかげで人を指導する事には自信があります。
example_sentences.english: In the position of being in charge of staff training for many years, I have self confidence in guidance thanks to that.

example_sentences.japanese: 家庭環境や金銭的に恵まれた環境にあってそれに感謝できていない人は、社会に出て苦労する事になるだろう。
example_sentences.english: For a person that cannot be thankful toward being blessed environmentally and financially within the household, they will surely suffer upon going out into society. (under...circumstances)

example_sentences.japanese: 我が党内にあって唯一原発についての専門知識を持っている彼女は、党内からも党外からも厚い支持を得ている。
example_sentences.english: Within the party, having unique specialist knowledge about nuclear power generation, she receives warm reception from both inside and outside of the party. (under...circumstances)

grammar_point: を余儀（よぎ）なくされる
general_translation: To be forced to do something
formation: Noun + を余儀（よぎ）なくされる
casual_structure: Noun + を余儀（よぎ）なくされる
polite_structure: Noun + を余儀（よぎ）なくされます
explanation: A structure showing that one is being forced to do something, due to being in the excessively unalterable situation of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 景気悪化のため、会社は閉鎖をよぎなくされた。
example_sentences.english: Due to the economic downturn, the company has been forced to close down.

example_sentences.japanese: パーク内での迷惑行為が悪化し始めたため、人気撮影スポットの封鎖をよぎなくされた。
example_sentences.english: Due to the worsening nuisance caused by guests in the park, they were forced to close off the popular photo spot.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲食店はコロナの影響で、営業の自粛をよぎなくされた。
example_sentences.english: Restaurants were forced to refrain from continuing business due to Covid.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近大きな地震があったため、この地域の人たちは避難所での生活をよぎなくされた。
example_sentences.english: Due to a recent major earthquake, people in the area were forced to live in shelters.

example_sentences.japanese: 津波が接近したため、野外コンサートは中止をよぎなくされた。
example_sentences.english: Because of the approaching tsunami, outdoor concerts were forced to be canceled.

example_sentences.japanese: 少子化により学生が減れば、多くの学校は閉校をよぎなくされるだろう。
example_sentences.english: If the number of students decreases due to declining birth rates, many schools will be forced to close down.

example_sentences.japanese: 国民による反発が強まったために、政府は補助金の配布をよぎなくされました。
example_sentences.english: Because of the intensified backlash from citizens, the government was forced to distribute relief subsidies.

example_sentences.japanese: 津波によって家を流されてしまった被災者達は、避難所での生活をよぎなくされた。
example_sentences.english: As for the natural disaster victims whose homes were washed away as a result of the tsunami, they were forced to go about their daily lives at the evacuation site.

example_sentences.japanese: 戦闘は６月まで続き、この頃には、反乱軍の大半はすでに国外への退避をよぎなくされた。
example_sentences.english: The fights continued until June, and around that time most of the rebels had already been forced to take refuge abroad.(against their will)

example_sentences.japanese: 根岸総理大臣は初め拒否していた。しかし結局、数日後に、大衆の抗議により辞任をよぎなくされた。
example_sentences.english: Prime Minister Negishi resisted in the beginning. But in the end, he was forced to resign by mass protests anyway a few days later.(against his will)

example_sentences.japanese: 三ヶ月前に異国の地で生活を始めた美波さんは身内の不幸により早々での帰国をよぎなくされた。
example_sentences.english: 3 months ago, having started life in a foreign land, Minami-san was forced to return home due to the loss of a family member.

example_sentences.japanese: コロナウイルスの影響でオリンピックの開会の延期をよぎなくされた日本政府は経済的に大きなダメージを背負うことになりました。
example_sentences.english: As for the Japanese government being forced to delay the opening of the Olympics due to the effects of the Coronavirus, economically they were burdened with extensive damages.

example_sentences.japanese: 違法薬物の使用や過剰なアルコール飲料の摂取により入院をよぎなくされた父は誰からも同情されませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Due to things like the use of illegal drugs, and excessive intake of alcohol, my father who was forced to be hospitalized was pitied by nobody.

example_sentences.japanese: この試験に合格しなかったら一年間の浪人生活をよぎなくされるため、何としてでも合格したいと思っている。
example_sentences.english: Because of failing this exam leading to me being forced to live the life of a student waiting to get into university for one year's time, I will do no matter what it takes to succeed.

example_sentences.japanese: ２０〇〇年５月には降着装置の故障により緊急着陸をよぎなくされた飛行機が飛行活動に復帰した。
example_sentences.english: In May 20XX, the plane that was forced to make an emergency landing due to a failure of the landing gear returned to flying operations.(no choice but to...)

general_translation: That..., (Surprised) that..., (Never expected) that..., (Shocked) that...
formation: Verb + （など）+ とはNoun + （だ(1)）+ （など）+ とは［い］Adjective + （など）+ とは［な］Adjective + （だ(1)）+ （など）+ とは(1) だった
casual_structure: Verb + （など）+ とはNoun + （だ(1)）+ （など）+ とは［い］Adjective + （など）+ とは［な］Adjective + （だ(1)）+ （など）+ とは(1) だった
explanation: An expression used to emphasize surprise or shock. One never expected that the general situation of (A) could happen.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなところでキアヌ・リーブスに出会ったとはねぇ！
example_sentences.english: I (never expected) that I would come across Keanu Reeves in a place like this!

example_sentences.japanese: こんな簡単なことで失敗するなどとは思っていなかったが、あいつに任せた俺が悪い。
example_sentences.english: I was not expecting him to fail at something so simple, but it was my fault for leaving it to him.

example_sentences.japanese: まさか彼が私の知らないところでそんなひどいことを言っていたなどとは...
example_sentences.english: I had no idea that he was saying such horrible things behind my back…

example_sentences.japanese: こんな安く家が買えるとは思わなかったよ。
example_sentences.english: I did not think that I would have been able to buy a house this cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: 君があんなに速く走れるとは...なんで今まで黙っていたんだい？
example_sentences.english: I had no idea that you could run that fast… Why did you keep this from us?

example_sentences.japanese: まさかこんな場所でなつみちゃんに会うとは！元気にしてた？
example_sentences.english: I would have never expected to see you at a place like this! How have you been?

example_sentences.japanese: 「一戸建てに住むってこれほどまでに大変だったとは驚きだよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I'm shocked that living in a single family home would be this hard!'

example_sentences.japanese: まさか二ヶ月で１０キロも痩せるとは！このダイエットは効果的だ！
example_sentences.english: I (never expected) that I would lose 10kg in two months! This diet is super effective!

example_sentences.japanese: メアリーさんとたけしさんが去年もう一度新婚旅行に行ったとは驚いた。
example_sentences.english: I was surprised that Mary-san and Takeshi-san went on another honeymoon last year.

example_sentences.japanese: 病弱で内気だった田中さんがボクシングチャンピオンになるとは夢にも思わなかったよ！
example_sentences.english: I would never have even dreamed that sickly and reserved Tanaka-san would become a boxing champion. (never expected)

example_sentences.japanese: 「ついこの間彼と話したばかりなのに、今日が彼の葬式だとは信じられないよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'It's unbelievable that I spoke with him just recently, and yet today is his funeral.' (never expected)

example_sentences.japanese: 「中古のいいパソコンが安く買えると知っていたけどこんなに安いとは思ってもみなかった。」
example_sentences.english: 'I knew that you could buy a good, second hand computer cheaply, but I never expected that it would be this cheap!'

example_sentences.japanese: 少し前までヨチヨチ歩きをしていた甥っ子が今年の四月から小学校に入学するとは…！
example_sentences.english: My nephew, who was tottering along until just a while ago, I cannot believe that they are entering primary school from April this year! (never expected)

example_sentences.japanese: 優勝間違いなしと世間で言われていた体操選手が演技の序盤で基本的なミスをするとは…。
example_sentences.english: That such a world renowned, undeniably excellent gymnastics competitor would make such a basic mistake from the outset of their performance, I am shocked.

example_sentences.japanese: 地球温暖化による気候変動が問題になっている事は知っていましたが、桜が咲いた後に雪が降るとは…！
example_sentences.english: I knew that climate change was becoming a problem due to global warming, but I never expected that snow would fall after the cherry blossoms bloomed!

example_sentences.japanese: あの真面目な生徒が実は芸能活動をしていたとは、担任の先生を務める僕にとって意外でした。
example_sentences.english: I'm shocked that that serious student was actually doing performing arts, as their homeroom teacher, it was unexpected.

example_sentences.japanese: まさかあんなに勉強をサボっていた涼太が先日受けた日本語能力試験に満点で合格するとは驚いたよ！
example_sentences.english: Unbelievable, I am shocked that Ryota, who neglects studying so much, would pass the JLPT with a perfect score yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 高橋さんがもう結婚していたとは驚いた。
example_sentences.english: I was surprised to hear that Mr. Takahashi was already married.

general_translation: You are not ~ so..., it isn't ~ so...
formation: Noun + じゃある(1) + まいしVerb + ん + じゃある(1) + まいしVerb + わけ + じゃある(1) + まいし(1) ではある、でもある
casual_structure: Noun + じゃある(1) + まいしVerb + ん + じゃある(1) + まいしVerb + わけ + じゃある(1) + まいし(1) ではある、でもある
explanation: A slightly formal phrase, criticising that something is not (A), so it shouldn't (B). Negative volitional.

example_sentences.japanese: 減るもんじゃあるまいし車を貸してくれ。
example_sentences.english: You are not going to lose out or anything, so lend me your car, man.

example_sentences.japanese: 減るわけではあるまいし、少しぐらい貸してくれてもいいじゃん。
example_sentences.english: It's not like it's going to decrease, so why don't you just let me borrow some?

example_sentences.japanese: 親に止められているのではあるまいし、好きに自分が行きたいところに行けばいいんじゃないの？
example_sentences.english: You are not being stopped by your parents, so why don't you just go wherever you want to?

example_sentences.japanese: もう子供じゃあるまいし、行動する前に少しでも考えたらどうなの？
example_sentences.english: You aren't a child anymore, so why don't you think a little before taking action.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供じゃあるまいしお菓子を見つけた途端に全部食べるな！
example_sentences.english: You are not a child, so don't instantly eat every sweet you stumble upon!

example_sentences.japanese: アニメじゃあるまいし、かわいい女の子は急に空から落ちてこない。
example_sentences.english: This is not an anime, so a cute girl won't suddenly fall out of the sky!

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さん！新入社員でもあるまいし！そんな簡単なミスはすべきじゃないよ。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san! You are not a new employee, so you should not make such simple mistakes.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん、結婚するわけじゃあるまいし、ただの学校のパーティーだよ。泣かないで。
example_sentences.english: Papa, I am not getting married. It is just a school party, so please don't cry!

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ: 「野菜好きじゃない！」Ｂ: 「赤ちゃんでもあるまいしもう駄々をこねるのはよして！」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I don't like veggies!' B: 'You are not a baby, so stop whining already!'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「行ってきます！」 Ｂ: 「待って、砂漠じゃあるまいし、外に出たら厚着をしろよ！」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I am heading out!' B: 'Wait, it's not a desert (outside), so if you go out then dress warmly!'

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪を引いているわけじゃあるまいし、毎日お昼過ぎまで寝るのはどうかと思うよ...
example_sentences.english: It is not like you caught a cold, so I wouldn't be so sure about sleeping in until after midday every day…

example_sentences.japanese: 狩猟時代じゃあるまいし、自分で狩りをする事が出来なくても全然問題にならないよ。
example_sentences.english: It isn't the era of hunting, so even if I can't really go hunting by myself, it will not be a problem!

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生や中学生じゃあるまいし、将来の夢が未だにスーパーヒーローっていうのはちょっとね...
example_sentences.english: You're not a junior or middle schooler, so still having the dream of becoming a superhero in the future, c'mon…

example_sentences.japanese: 隕石が落ちてくるわけじゃあるまいし、明日や明後日等の近い内にこの世界が滅びるという噂は到底信じられません。
example_sentences.english: It isn't like a meteorite is going to fall, so a rumor like the world being destroyed tomorrow or the day after, I absolutely cannot believe it.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔じゃあるまいし、女性は早々に結婚をして子供を産んで専業主婦になるという考えは古臭いと思います。
example_sentences.english: It isn't ancient times, so I think that immediately getting married, having kids, and becoming a housewife stinks of the past.

general_translation: After, Since, Ever since then
formation: Verb［て］ + から + というものPhrase (A)。 それから + というもの + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Verb［て］ + から + というものPhrase (A)。 それから + というもの + Phrase (B)
explanation: A strong, formal structure, showing that ever since (A), (B). (B) is a thing which can be said to be from (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんが生まれてからというもの、もっと本気で働くようになった。
example_sentences.english: Ever since the baby was born, I have come to take my job more seriously.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社に入社してからというもの、日付が変わる前に家に帰ったことがない。
example_sentences.english: Ever since I joined this company, I have not been home before the clock ticks over midnight.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事に行く前に散歩に行くようにしてからというもの、どんどん体重が減ってきたのでこれからも散歩を続けようと思っている。
example_sentences.english: Ever since I started to go on walks before work, I have been steadily losing weight, so I am thinking of continuing to go on walks.

example_sentences.japanese: ファイナルデスティネーションという映画を見てからというもの、木材を運んだトラックの後ろを走るのを避けるようになった。
example_sentences.english: Ever since watching the movie 'Final Destination', I have been avoiding driving behind trucks carrying lumber.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は社長にみんなの前でものすごく怒られた。それからというもの彼は別人になったかのように性格が変わった。
example_sentences.english: He was yelled at in front of everyone by the boss. Ever since that event, he became a different person.

example_sentences.japanese: 先月彼女が痴漢にあった。それからというもの、満員電車を避けるようになった。
example_sentences.english: She was groped last month. Ever since then, she has been avoiding packed trains.

example_sentences.japanese: あやうく溺れかけてからというもの、泳ぎ方を習い始めました。
example_sentences.english: Ever since I almost drowned, I started learning how to swim.

example_sentences.japanese: ツイート：「娘が生まれてからというもの、一日たりともろくに眠れていない。」
example_sentences.english: Tweet: 'Ever since my daughter was born, I haven't been able to get a good night's sleep one single day.'

example_sentences.japanese: スペースＸのファルコンヘビーの離陸を観てからというもの、宇宙が頭から離れない。
example_sentences.english: Ever since watching the launch of SpaceX's falcon heavy, I cannot stop thinking about space.

example_sentences.japanese: 親友が鬱で自殺してからというもの、心理学を勉強してカウンセラーになりたいとずっと夢見ている。
example_sentences.english: Since my best friend commited suicide due to depression, I have constantly been studying psychology, and had the dream of wanting to become a counselor.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子はパートナーができてからというもの、私たち両親と出かける事がめっきりなくなった。
example_sentences.english: Ever since my son was able to get a partner, going out with us, his parents, has ceased noticeably.

example_sentences.japanese: 妊娠してからというもの、頻繁に気持ち悪くなったり腰が痛くなったりするので毎日よく眠れていません。
example_sentences.english: After becoming pregnant, since there are things like my mood incessantly becoming bad, and my lower back starting to hurt, I have not been able to sleep well.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に留学をしに来てからというもの毎日和食を食べているので体重が大幅に減りました。
example_sentences.english: Since I have been eating Japanese food ever since coming to Japan on a student exchange, my weight has drastically decreased.

example_sentences.japanese: 社会に出て一人暮らしを始めてからというもの、コンビニ弁当ばかりで食事が楽しくなくなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Since stepping out into society and starting to live by myself, eating nothing but convenience store bentos has unfortunately lost its fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画ナレーター：「３０年前、ロボットが反旗を翻した。それからというもの人生のために戦わない日はなかった。」
example_sentences.english: Movie narrator: '30 years ago robots revolted. Ever since then, a day has not passed where we have not fought for our lives.'

example_sentences.japanese: 伝記：「彼はとても元気な人だったが、パラシュートの落下事故にあってからというもの、身体が目に見えて弱っていった。」
example_sentences.english: Biography: 'He used to be a very lively man, but ever since he had the parachute accident, his health has clearly declined.'

example_sentences.japanese: ジムに行き始めてからというもの順調に体脂肪率が下がっているので、これからも通い続けようと思っている。
example_sentences.english: Since my body fat percentage has reduced after having started going to the gym, I reckon I will keep going.

general_translation: While, Besides, In addition to
formation: Verb［る］+ かたわらNoun + の + かたわら
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ かたわらNoun + の + かたわら
explanation: A formal phrase which emphasizes in addition to (A), (B). Beside or alongside the more important (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 本業のかたわらバイトなどの副業をしている多数の人々がいる。
example_sentences.english: Besides working their main jobs, there are many people that also work part-time jobs on the side.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は子育てのかたわら、近所の子供達にそろばんを教えている。
example_sentences.english: My wife teaches abacus to kids in the neighborhood in addition to raising our children.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は飲食店を経営しているかたわら、鳶職人としても働いている。
example_sentences.english: Besides running a restaurant, he also works as a steeplejack.

example_sentences.japanese: グレッググラフィンは大学の教授をしているかたわら、歌手として活動している。
example_sentences.english: In addition to being a college professor, Greg Graffin is also active as a singer.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の妹は本業のかたわら、英会話教室で英語を教えている。
example_sentences.english: My sister teaches English at an English conversation class in addition to her day job.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は大学で教えるかたわら、家でも個人指導をしている。
example_sentences.english: Besides teaching at university, she gives private lessons at home.

example_sentences.japanese: さらに大学での国語の教授をしているかたわら、漫画家として活躍している。
example_sentences.english: Moreover, besides holding the position of a Japanese professor at the university, he is also active as a manga artist.

example_sentences.japanese: ブルースは、昼は財閥を経営するかたわら、夜はバーマンとして危険地域を見回っている。
example_sentences.english: During the daytime, Bruce manages his family corporation, while at night he patrols dangerous areas as BARMAN.

example_sentences.japanese: いくつかの国では、女性は仕事のかたわら、苦労をいとわず子供を育てている。立派なことだと思う。
example_sentences.english: In some countries, women work in addition to raising their children, not minding the hardships. I think that is quite praiseworthy.

example_sentences.japanese: 指導医として病院に務めるかたわら、コンサルタントと専門医として企業でも業務を行っています。
example_sentences.english: In addition to working as the preceptor at the hospital, she also engages in business as a consultant and a medical specialist.

example_sentences.japanese: 歌手として活動するかたわら女優業も立派にこなす彼女は、一体一年でいくら稼いでいるのだろう…。
example_sentences.english: In relation to her, who in addition to getting along as a singer, is also doing well as an excellent actress, I wonder how much she earns in a year.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は美容の専門学校に通うかたわらアルバイトを通して自分で学費を賄っているので感心している。
example_sentences.english: In addition to my daughter going to a beauty school, she is also paying her own tuition fees through part-time work, so I'm thankful.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が務める会社は釣りに関する製品を製造するかたわら、環境保全のために木を植える活動もしています。
example_sentences.english: In addition to manufacturing fishing-related products, the company I work for also engages in tree-planting activities for environmental preservation.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の父は製薬会社で新薬の開発をするかたわら僕たち三人兄弟の子育てにも奮闘しています。
example_sentences.english: My father, who in addition to developing novel drugs at a drug manufacturing company, is also putting strenuous efforts into raising us three siblings.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の将来の夢は主婦として子育てに全うするかたわら、自分の芸術の才能を生かして少しお金を稼ぐ事です。
example_sentences.english: As for my future dream, in addition to carrying out the raising of children as a housewife, I'd also like to make the most of my performance abilities and earn a bit of money.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学に通うかたわら自身の壮絶な幼少期に関する自叙伝を執筆するなんて、彼には相当体力があるのだろう。
example_sentences.english: In addition to going to university, something like writing an autobiography about the prime of their youth, that guy has a considerable amount of stamina.

general_translation: Beginning of, Starting with
formation: Noun + を皮切（かわき）りにして(1)Verb［る］(2) + の + を皮切（かわき）りにして(1)(1) を皮切（かわき）りとして(2) Verb［た］
casual_structure: Noun + を皮切（かわき）りにして(1)Verb［る］(2) + の + を皮切（かわき）りにして(1)(1) を皮切（かわき）りとして(2) Verb［た］
explanation: A construction that presents (A) as the beginning of (B). (A) broke the skin, and now (B) keeps happening.

example_sentences.japanese: 店の移転をかわきりとして、売上げがどんどんと上がっています。
example_sentences.english: Starting with the shop relocation, sales are rapidly increasing.

example_sentences.japanese: 藤田先輩がやめたのをかわきりに、他の人たちもどんどんやめていった。
example_sentences.english: Starting with Fujita senpai quitting, others quit in quick succession.

example_sentences.japanese: あの俳優はテレビ東京に出演したのをかわきりに、色々な局に出演することになった。
example_sentences.english: That actor started by appearing on TV Tokyo and then went on to appear on various stations.

example_sentences.japanese: 佐々木さんの発言をかわきりに、賛成する人が出てきた。
example_sentences.english: Starting with Sasaki-san's comment, some people began to agree with him.

example_sentences.japanese: クラスメイトの高橋さんをかわきりに、クラスみんな風邪になってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Starting with Takahashi-san, my classmate, everyone in my class caught a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が社長に文句を言ったのをかわきりにして、みんな社長に文句を言い始めた。
example_sentences.english: Starting with her making a complaint to the boss, everyone started to make complaints to the boss.

example_sentences.japanese: あのグループは名古屋をかわきりとして、全国でライブを行った。
example_sentences.english: Starting with Nagoya, that group performed throughout the country.

example_sentences.japanese: それをかわきりとして、コンビニは相次いで出店し始めた。
example_sentences.english: Starting with that, convenience stores started opening one after the other.

example_sentences.japanese: 俳優の伝記：「『Ｙ-ＭＥＮ』に出演したのをかわきりにして、多数出演。」
example_sentences.english: Actor's biography: 'Starting with his appearance in Y-MEN he appeared in numerous performances.'

example_sentences.japanese: 皆川さんが監督として選ばれたのをかわきりにして、うちのチームは次々とスポーツの成功を掴んだ。
example_sentences.english: Starting with Minagawa-san being chosen as our trainer, our team continued to be successful.

example_sentences.japanese: 「レオナルド・ディカプリオはタイタニックの主人公になったのをかわきりにしてスターへの道を歩み始め、大ヒット映画に出演している。」
example_sentences.english: 'Starting with his leading role in Titanic, Leonardo DiCaprio embarked on the road to stardom and has appeared in many hit movies.'

example_sentences.japanese: その二十歳のシンガーソングライターは東京をかわきりに全国、そして全世界でライブを行った。
example_sentences.english: As for that 20 year old singer songwriter, starting with Tokyo, they went on to hold live events nationally, and then globally.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京をかわきりに、明治時代を舞台にした演劇「〇〇」が全国３０劇場で公演されます。
example_sentences.english: Starting with Tokyo, the play XX, which is set in the Meiji era, will be performed at 30 theaters nationwide.

example_sentences.japanese: この学習塾は関西地方をかわきりに、全国に兄弟塾や姉妹塾を作りました。
example_sentences.english: As for this private tutoring school, starting with the Kansai region, they went on to make things like brother and sister cram schools nationally.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長が反対意見を言ったのをかわきりに、社内からその改革に対してどんどん反対意見が出てきた。
example_sentences.english: Starting with the section manager stating an opposing opinion, there came to be more and more opposing opinions from within the company in relation to that reformation.

example_sentences.japanese: 元々出勤日数が少なかった川瀬さんをかわきりに、優秀な成績を収めていた谷口さんまで次々に社員が首になっていった。
example_sentences.english: Starting with Kawase-san, who had a low number of working days from the beginning, to even Taniguchi-san, who had been accruing stellar results. One after the other, employees were getting fired.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の勇気ある告発をかわきりに、芸能界で蔓延するパワハラや性的搾取の問題が明るみになってきました。
example_sentences.english: Starting with his brave accusation, the problem of things like rampant power harassment and sexual exploitation within the performance industry began to come to light.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は趣味で作った釣り道具がＳＮＳで売れた事をかわきりに、その趣味を仕事にする事を決めたようだ。
example_sentences.english: Starting with dad being able to sell fishing accessories on social media, which were made as a pastime, it appears as though he has decided to turn that hobby into a job.

general_translation: When it comes to, As for, In particular, What is worse or more
formation: Noun + に至（いた）っては
casual_structure: Noun + に至（いた）っては
explanation: A structure showing that when it comes to (A), (B). In the climactic example of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 父親はパソコンならともかくスマートフォンにいたってはまるでお手上げらしい。
example_sentences.english: My father isn't too bad if it is a PC, but when it comes to smartphones he seems to have given up.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家族は全員機械音痴です。母にいたってはインターネットさえ使えないです。
example_sentences.english: My whole family is mechanically illiterate. What's more, my mother can't even use the internet.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近ここにいる社員みんなのやる気がない。藤田さんにいたってはパソコンもつけていない。
example_sentences.english: Recently, employees here are unmotivated. As for Fujita-san, their computer isn't even turned on.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字テストは４９点だった。リスニングにいたっては２０点だった。
example_sentences.english: My kanji test's score was 49. What's worse is that my listening score was 20.

example_sentences.japanese: ２０〇〇年は非常に乾燥していた。４月にいたっては２回しか降らなかった。
example_sentences.english: The year 20XX was a very dry one. April in particular, as it rained only twice.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近の子供は、かろうじてＣＤは知っているが、フロッピーにいたっては全く知らない場合が珍しくない。
