example_sentences.english: Children these days barely know CDs, but when it comes to floppy disks, it is not unusual if they know nothing at all about them.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人暮らしをしている息子の生活は荒れているようです。食生活にいたっては、毎日カップラーメンを食べていると聞きました。
example_sentences.english: It appears as though my son's independent lifestyle is tumultuous. When it comes to his eating habits, I heard that he has been eating cup-ramen every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家族はみんな方向音痴です。母にいたってはナビゲーションアプリを使っても道に迷ってしまいます。
example_sentences.english: As for my family, everybody has no sense of direction. What's more, mom gets lost even if she uses a navigation app.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回の定期テストでは化学の点数が１００点満点中６０点でした。物理にいたっては３０点でした。
example_sentences.english: In this period's exam, for chemistry, there were 60 marks out of a perfect score of 100. When it comes to physics, there were 30.

example_sentences.japanese: 今どきの若者はよく転職をするらしい。姪っ子にいたってはまだ３０歳なのにもう４度も転職をしている。
example_sentences.english: It seems like young people in these modern times often change jobs. When it comes to my niece, even though she's only 30, she's already changed jobs 4 times.

example_sentences.japanese: ネット調査によると、将来結婚をしたいと思う人の割合は約４０％、子供がほしいと思う人にいたっては９％以下だった。
example_sentences.english: According to an internet survey, the percentage of people who want to get married in the future is about 40%, and as for those who want children, it was less than 9%.

example_sentences.japanese: コロナウイルスによる不景気のせいで新卒を採用する会社がガクンと減った。旅行業界にいたっては、新卒を採用する会社がほぼないらしい。
example_sentences.english: Due to the recession stemming from the Coronavirus, companies that will accept new graduates have markedly decreased. What is worse, there are practically no travel industry companies that will accept them.

example_sentences.japanese: 二年前の出生率は女性一人あたり１．８、去年にいたっては女性一人あたり１．３３と歴史上最低の結果となった。
example_sentences.english: The birthrate two years ago was 1.8 per woman, as for last year it was 1.33 per woman, which was the lowest (result) in history.

example_sentences.japanese: 「不景気によりガソリン車の売上げが７％、電子自動車の売上げが３０％減少。バイクにいたっては、売上げはほぼ止まっている始末だった。」
example_sentences.english: Due to the recession, the sales of gasoline cars decreased by 7%, the sales of electric cars by 30%. When it comes to motorcycles, the sales ended up almost completely stopping.

example_sentences.japanese: 近年は異常気象のせいで夏の気温が極めて高く、去年にいたっては東京でも最高気温３８度を観測した。
example_sentences.english: Due to abnormal weather in recent years, Summer's air temperature has been incredibly high, in particular last year, the highest air temperature observed in Tokyo was 38 degrees.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのお宅の次男は留年するらしいですよ。長男に至っては学年トップだったらしいですよ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the second son of the family over there flunked. As for their eldest son, I heard that he was at the top of his grade. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: As soon as, The moment, When
formation: Verb［る］+ なり
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ なり
explanation: An expression showing that (B) happened as soon as (A) changed. While (A) was still in its just completed state, (B) became, or arose.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が出張からかえるなり母は泣きだした。
example_sentences.english: The moment father returned home from a business trip, mother started crying.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が家に上がるなりトイレへと駆け込んだ。
example_sentences.english: My son ran to the toilet as soon as he entered the house.

example_sentences.japanese: ママ友が私の家に入るなり、冷蔵庫の中を物色し始めた。
example_sentences.english: As soon as my mom-friend came into my house, she started to go through my refrigerator.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は机に座るなりすぐスマホをいじり始めたから注意した。
example_sentences.english: I warned him because he started playing on his phone as soon as he sat down.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はジョークをきくなり笑い出してしまった。
example_sentences.english: As soon as she heard the joke, she bursted out laughing.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの奥さんは毎日おきるなりスマホで電子メールを見ている。
example_sentences.english: As soon as my wife wakes up, she checks mail on her smartphone.

example_sentences.japanese: 踊りをやめるなり、彼女が急にキスしてくれたんだ。気持ちいい。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I stopped dancing, she suddenly kissed me. I feel great.

example_sentences.japanese: 実家のお母さんからの電報がくるなり、山田さんは青ざめた。
example_sentences.english: As soon as the telegram from his mother came, Yamada became pale.

example_sentences.japanese: 故郷にかえるなり灰燼に帰した家を見て、驚き、悲しんだ。
example_sentences.english: The moment I returned to my home town, I saw my house reduced to ashes. I was shocked and saddened.

example_sentences.japanese: 自宅に訪問してきた男性が指名手配犯だと気づくなり、妻は警察へ通報した。
example_sentences.english: As soon as my wife realized that the man who came to visit our house was a wanted criminal, she reported it to the police.

example_sentences.japanese: 教授は授業開始を告げるチャイムが鳴るなり直ぐに授業の本題へ入りました。
example_sentences.english: As for the professor, the moment the chime that signifies the beginning of class rang, he immediately went straight into the main topic of the lesson.

example_sentences.japanese: 以前会った時に彼に失礼な事を言ったのは確かだが、彼に会うなり罵られるとは…。
example_sentences.english: When I met him previously, it is indeed true that I said something rude, but to think that he would hurl abuse at me the moment he saw me…

example_sentences.japanese: 普段は深夜にお風呂に入る夫が家に着くなり急いでお風呂に入ったのを見て妻は首を傾げた。
example_sentences.english: When seeing her husband, who usually has a shower in the middle of the night, enter the shower hurriedly upon arriving home, the wife became quite puzzled.

example_sentences.japanese: 夕食を食べ終わるなり自室へ篭ってしまった息子を見て、息子がストレスを抱えている事に気づきました。
example_sentences.english: When they saw their son shut himself in his room the moment he finished eating dinner, they realized that he was harboring some stress.

example_sentences.japanese: 自他ともに認める雨女である私と旅行へ行くと、どんな場所へ旅行に行っても宿から出るなり雨に降られる事になりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you're going on a trip with me, who is generally accepted as a woman that takes the rain with her everywhere, no matter where we go, from when we settle in, til as soon as we depart, we'll get rained on.

general_translation: Absentmindedly, Mindlessly, Unconsciously, Without paying attention
formation: Verb［る］(A) + ともなく(1) + Verb［たら］(2)(A)(1) ともなしに(2) Verb + と
casual_structure: Verb［る］(A) + ともなく(1) + Verb［たら］(2)(A)(1) ともなしに(2) Verb + と
explanation: A phrase highlighting that the action of (A) was happening absentmindedly. While not even sure that (A) was happening, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: この曲は行きつけのバーでいつも流れているため、覚えるともなく覚えてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Since this song is always playing at my favorite bar, I unconsciously memorized it.

example_sentences.japanese: 話を聞くともなく、先生と黒板の方向をぼーっと見ていた。
example_sentences.english: I absentmindedly listened while spacing out in the direction of my teacher and the blackboard.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日テレビを見るともなく見ていたら、急にお母さんが出てきたから驚いた。
example_sentences.english: When I was absentmindedly watching TV yesterday, I was surprised when my mother suddenly appeared.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲み会で上司の話を聞くともなしに聞いていたら、「お前はどう思う」と聞かれたから適当に返事した。
example_sentences.english: When I was at a drinking party and was absentmindedly listening to my boss, he asked what I thought, so I gave him a random response.

example_sentences.japanese: 暇だったから近所を歩くともなしに歩いていたら、高校の同級生にばったりあった。
example_sentences.english: When I was mindlessly walking in my neighborhood because I had nothing to do, I met my classmate from high school.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣人の窓を見るともなく見ると、驚いたことに裸の人がいた。
example_sentences.english: I looked at my neighbor's window without paying attention, and, to my surprise, there was a naked person.

example_sentences.japanese: 勝者の発表を聞くともなく聞いていたら、なんと私の名前が挙がっていた。
example_sentences.english: I listened absentmindedly to the announcements of the winners, when, to my disbelief, my name came up.

example_sentences.japanese: ノベル：「彼は夜遅くテレビを見るともなく見ているうちにいつのまにか寝入ってしまったようだ。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'It seems that he fell asleep while he was mindlessly watching TV late at night.'

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、考えるともなく考えているところに、スズメバチにひどく刺されて「痛っ！」思わず叫んでしまった。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, when I was thinking about nothing in particular, I was badly stung by a wasp, and without thinking shouted: 'Ouch!' (mindlessly)

example_sentences.japanese: 見るともなくテレビを見ていると、ビールの広告に友達が出演していて驚きました。
example_sentences.english: While watching TV without paying too much attention, I was surprised to see a friend appear in a beer commercial.

example_sentences.japanese: 「何も無い」とはどういう事なのか、考えるともなく考えてしまう事がたまにあります。
example_sentences.english: There are occasionally times where I unconsciously contemplate what 'there being nothing' means.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌な事があると、その事を考えるともなく考えてしまうので、そういう時は早く寝るようにしている。
example_sentences.english: If there is something that I dislike, since I'll absentmindedly think about it, I do my best to go to sleep quickly at those times.

example_sentences.japanese: カフェでぼんやりしていると気づけば隣に座っている主婦たちの会話を聞くともなく聞いていました。
example_sentences.english: When lazing around in a cafe, upon reflection, I was listening to the conversation of the couple sitting next to me without paying attention.

example_sentences.japanese: 山田さんと晩御飯を食べるともなく食べていたら、急に彼が告白してきて驚いた。
example_sentences.english: When I was absentmindedly eating dinner with Yamada-san, he suddenly confessed (his feelings for me) and it really surprised me.

example_sentences.japanese: ライトノベル、あまくささん：「家に帰るともなく帰っていたら、突然美少女が空から落ちてきてびっくりした。」
example_sentences.english: Light Novel, Amakusa: 'When I was absentmindedly on my way back home, a beautiful girl fell from the sky and startled me.'

example_sentences.japanese: 学生の頃は親友と何を話すともなく話す時間が好きだったが、今はそんなに暇な時間が無い。
example_sentences.english: When I was a student, I loved the times when I would mindlessly talk about something with my best friend, but now I don't have that much free time.

general_translation: Stained, Covered in, Smeared, Dirty with, Soaked in
formation: Noun + まみれNoun + まみれ + の + NounNoun + まみれ + になって + Phrase
casual_structure: Noun + まみれNoun + まみれ + の + NounNoun + まみれ + になって + Phrase
explanation: A structure implying that something is drenched or soaked in (A). Completely painted with (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 床は泥まみれになった。
example_sentences.english: The floor became covered in mud.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん：「服泥まみれじゃん！どうしたの？！」
example_sentences.english: Mother: 'You are covered in mud! What happened?!'

example_sentences.japanese: 家に帰ったら犬が血まみれになっていたと思ったら、どうやらいちごジャムを食べて寝たみたい。
example_sentences.english: When I got home, I thought my dog was covered in blood, but it seems like he ate some strawberry jam and fell asleep.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな借金まみれの男とは付き合わない方がいいよ！
example_sentences.english: I don't think you should date a guy like that, who is drowning in debt!

example_sentences.japanese: ストップ！そんな泥まみれの服を洗濯機に入れないで！
example_sentences.english: Stop! Don't put clothes covered in mud in the washing machine!

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は泥まみれのまま遊んでいる。
example_sentences.english: 'Children are playing while covered in mud.'

example_sentences.japanese: 頭から汗まみれになって、走っている選手はすごいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that players running with their heads covered in sweat are amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事で油まみれになったら、家に帰ってからシャワーを浴びると気持ちがいいよね。
example_sentences.english: After getting soaked in oil at work, there's nothing better than having a shower after coming back home, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の田中さんは氷で滑って雪の塊で転び、雪まみれになってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Tanaka slipped on ice and fell on a lump of snow. He was completely covered in snow.

example_sentences.japanese: 血まみれになって帰ってきた妹を見て、直ぐに警察へ１１０番通報をした。
example_sentences.english: When I saw my little sister come home smeared with blood, I immediately reported it to the police via 110.

example_sentences.japanese: ずっと放置していた漢和辞典が埃まみれになっていたので捨てる事にしました。
example_sentences.english: Since my kanji dictionary that I have been constantly neglecting got absolutely covered in  dust, I decided to throw it away.

example_sentences.japanese: 風の強い日に窓を開けると部屋が砂まみれになってしまうのでやめた方がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: When you open your window on a day with strong wind, since the room will become covered in sand, you should hold off.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女：「キモイ！机がよだれまみれだわ！」彼氏：「勉強中に寝ちゃったもので...」
example_sentences.english: Girlfriend: 'Gross! The desk is covered in drool!'Boyfriend: 'I fell asleep while studying, so…'

example_sentences.japanese: 所詮人間は欲まみれなのだから、それほど禁欲を推奨しなくても良いと思います。
example_sentences.english: Since humans are all defiled with greed in the end, I think that not endorsing abstinence so much is fine. (smeared with)

example_sentences.japanese: テレビ業界はパワハラやセクハラまみれだと聞き、アナウンサーに憧れる気持ちが無くなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Hearing that the entertainment industry is stained with things like power abuse and sexual harassment, my fond feelings toward presenters disappeared.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に助言する：「借金まみれの現状を変えない限り、誰も君と付き合ってくれないと思うよ。」
example_sentences.english: Giving advice to a friend: 'As long as you don't change your current state of drowning in debt, I don't think anyone is going to date you.' (covered in)

grammar_point: う・よう + が～まいが
general_translation: Even if, No matter what, Whether or not, [Emphatic], Volitional + が
formation: Even if / No matter whatVerb ［おう］ + が(1)Verb［まい］ + が(1)Noun + だろう.(2) + が(1)［な］Adjective + だろう(2) + が(1)［い］Adjective［い］+ かろう + が(1)Whether or notVerb ［おう］ + が(1)  +  Verb［まい］ + が(1)Noun (A) + だろう(2) + が(1) +  Noun (B) だろう(2) + が(1)［な］Adjective１ + だろう(2) + が(1)  +  ［な］Adjective２ + だろう(2) + が(1) ［い］Adjective［い］+ かろう + が(1)  +  ［い］Adjective［い］+ かろう + が(1)(1) と(2) であろう
casual_structure: Even if / No matter whatVerb ［おう］ + が(1)Verb［まい］ + が(1)Noun + だろう.(2) + が(1)［な］Adjective + だろう(2) + が(1)［い］Adjective［い］+ かろう + が(1)Whether or notVerb ［おう］ + が(1)  +  Verb［まい］ + が(1)Noun (A) + だろう(2) + が(1) +  Noun (B) だろう(2) + が(1)［な］Adjective１ + だろう(2) + が(1)  +  ［な］Adjective２ + だろう(2) + が(1) ［い］Adjective［い］+ かろう + が(1)  +  ［い］Adjective［い］+ かろう + が(1)(1) と(2) であろう
explanation: A slightly formal construction which highlights the speaker's strong will to disregard (A). No matter what (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 何年がかかろうと、ドラゴンボールを見つけるつもりだ！
example_sentences.english: Even if it takes many years, I intend to find the dragon balls!

example_sentences.japanese: 忘年会に出席しようが出席するまいが、会費はみんなからもらっています。
example_sentences.english: Whether you attend the year-end party or not, we will collect the admissions fee from everyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が降ろうが降るまいが、明日は絶対に釣りに行くと決めた。
example_sentences.english: Whether it rains or not, I have decided to go fishing tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 楽しかろうが楽しくなかろうが、学校は子供の仕事だから学校には行かなくてはだめだ。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is fun or not, school is a child's job, so you must go to school.

example_sentences.japanese: 安全だろうが安全でなかろうが、２メートル以上の場所に上がる場合は安全帯を必ず装着してください。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is safe or not, always wear a safety belt when you climb to a place higher than 2 meters.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬であろうが猫であろうが、どちらにしても動物なので軽い気持ちで買ってはいけない。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is a dog or a cat, they are both animals, so they must not be bought on a whim.

example_sentences.japanese: 人が何といおうが、ずっとあなたを愛しています！
example_sentences.english: No matter what people say, I will always love you!

example_sentences.japanese: 商品は上質であろうが悪質であろうが、よく売れるものはよく売れる。
example_sentences.english: Whether the product is of good quality or low quality, if it sells well, it sells well.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が生きていようがいきていまいが、私は彼らのために歌い続ける。
example_sentences.english: Whether my friends are alive or not, I will still sing songs for them.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒が授業に出席しようが出席するまいが、私はきちんと授業を進めていく。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not students attend, I will proceed with my lecture as planned.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強が難しかろうが易しかろうが、流暢に話せるようになるまで勉強する。
example_sentences.english: Whether learning Japanese is difficult or easy, I will learn until I become fluent.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰に反対されようが、僕は同性婚を支持する気持ちを変えないつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: No matter who I am opposed by, I intend to not change my feelings of endorsing same-sex marriage.

example_sentences.japanese: 出発時にどんなに晴れていようがいまいが、夏の沖縄へ行くなら台風への対策もするべきです。
example_sentences.english: No matter how clear it is when you depart, if you're going to Okinawa in summer, you ought to take measures against typhoons.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のルームメイトは動物が大嫌いだ。犬だろうが猫だろうが、動物を飼うのに猛反対してくる。
example_sentences.english: My roommate hates animals. No matter whether it is a dog or a cat, she will fiercely oppose owning one.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が幼い頃に蒸発してしまった父が今再婚していようが再婚していまいが、僕には関係ない。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether my father, who disappeared without a trace in my youth, is now getting remarried or not, it is none of my business.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘が離婚しようが離婚しまいが、私は娘が幸せならそれ以上は何も求めません。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not my daughter gets a divorce, as long as she is happy, I do not wish for anything more than that.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験のために沢山の参考書をかおうと、それを実際に使いこなさないなら意味が無い。
example_sentences.english: Even if you buy heaps of reference books for the JLPT, if you don't actually use them until you get the knack of it, there is no meaning.

general_translation: About, Or more, Over, Starts at
formation: Number + Counter + からするNumber + Counter + からする  +  NounNumber + Counter + からの + Noun
casual_structure: Number + Counter + からするNumber + Counter + からする  +  NounNumber + Counter + からの + Noun
polite_structure: Number + Counter + からしますNumber + Counter + からする  +  NounNumber + Counter + からの + Noun
explanation: A formal expression indicating a minimum where a number or amount starts. To go from (A) and up.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕には１００万円からの腕時計を買う余裕はない。
example_sentences.english: I don't have the surplus to buy a watch that goes from 1 million yen.

example_sentences.japanese: この辺だと家賃は１５万からする。
example_sentences.english: Around here, rent costs 150,000 yen or more.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の大地震で十人からの人が行方不明になった。
example_sentences.english: 10 or more people have gone missing due to the big earthquake that happened yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 父から三百万円からする時計をもらった。
example_sentences.english: I received a watch that costs 3,000,000 yen or more from my father.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品を製造するには、１億からのお金がかかる。
example_sentences.english: In order to manufacture this product, it will cost 100 million yen or more.

example_sentences.japanese: その靴買ったの？それって１５万からするやつでしょ？やばいね。
example_sentences.english: You bought those shoes? Those are the ones that cost 150,000 yen or more, aren't they? That's nuts.

example_sentences.japanese: スタジアムに１０万人からの人が集まったそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that over 100,000 people gathered at the stadium.

example_sentences.japanese: この辺りはとても高いよ。家賃は１０万円からする。
example_sentences.english: This neighborhood is awfully expensive. The rent is around 100,000 yen or more.

example_sentences.japanese: ビルさんは彼女に２００万ドルからする車を買ってあげたらしいわ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Bill gave his girlfriend a car that is worth over 2 million dollars.

example_sentences.japanese: アーノルドさんはもう７２歳なのに１００キロからのダンベルを持ち上げられるよ。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Arnold can lift over 100 kg of dumbbells even though he is 72!

example_sentences.japanese: ミユ：「見てよ。このバッグをたった１０万で買ったの！」アヤ：「えぇ？羨ましいね。普通は３０万円からするのに…｡」
example_sentences.english: Miyu: 'Look! I only paid 100,000 yen for this bag!'Aya: 'Wha? I'm jealous. Usually, it is over 300,000 yen, and yet...'

example_sentences.japanese: 先月の大地震以降、都内では十万人からの市民が学校などで避難生活を続けている。
example_sentences.english: Ever since last month's large earthquake, 100,000 or more citizens in the city have continued to be taking refuge within schools and such.

example_sentences.japanese: 私立の医学部が一千万円からの学費がかかると聞いて、おったまげた。
example_sentences.english: I was blown away when I heard that the tuition fee for a private medical university starts at about 10 million yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物園はエミューの脱走によって十人からの人が怪我を負った事を受け、謝罪会見を開きました。
example_sentences.english: Regarding the zoo, accepting that over 10 people incurred injuries due to the emu's escape, they held a public apology press conference.

example_sentences.japanese: ２トンからのカバが民家に向かって突進したと聞き、その民家が崩れた事を確信した。
example_sentences.english: Hearing that a hippo that was about 2 tons charged toward a residential home, I was confident that the house was demolished.

example_sentences.japanese: この国では婚約指輪や結婚指輪を買う際は百万円からする指輪を買うのが普通だと言われて驚いた。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of buying something like an engagement or wedding ring in this country, I was surprised to be told that it's normal that they start from about 1,000,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 最高裁判所が下した判決に納得がいかなかった人達によるデモが行われ、当日は一万人からの人々が集まりました。
example_sentences.english: Due to the people who did not accept the judgment handed down by the supreme court holding a demonstration, over 10,000 people gathered on the day.

example_sentences.japanese: １０５円からするライトを買ったらすぐ壊れた。
example_sentences.english: When I bought a light that went from 105 yen, it broke immediately. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: At, Over, In, Only (after, when, or because)
formation: Number + Counter + にしてNoun + にして
casual_structure: Number + Counter + にしてNoun + にして
explanation: An expression which emphasizes a specific phase or time. Going off (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はバブルがはじけたことにより一夜にして破産者となった。
example_sentences.english: Due to the bubble burst, he went bankrupt overnight. (only (after/when/because))

example_sentences.japanese: ３０歳にして初めて海外旅行に行った。
example_sentences.english: At the age of 30, I traveled abroad for the first time.

example_sentences.japanese: 五回目にしてやっと資格を取ることができた。
example_sentences.english: I was finally able to get my qualification only after my fifth try.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人たちは道を曲がって、一瞬にして暗闇の中へと消えた。
example_sentences.english: The perpetrators turned off the road and disappeared into the darkness in an instant.

example_sentences.japanese: ５０歳にしてようやく、イタリアに住んでいる従兄弟の家に行くことができた。
example_sentences.english: At age 50, I was finally able to visit my cousin who lives in Italy.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は６０歳にして初めて、コンサートに行ったらしい。
example_sentences.english: My mother went to a concert for the first time at the age of 60.

example_sentences.japanese: 釈迦は２９歳にして初めて、宮殿を出た。
example_sentences.english: Buddha left the palace for the first time at the age of 29. (only (after/when/because))

example_sentences.japanese: これは西尾維新のような文豪にして初めて書ける名著だ。
example_sentences.english: This is a masterpiece that could only be written when a literary giant like Nishio Ishin did it for the first time.

example_sentences.japanese: ふうかはあきつき氏夫妻の結婚２０年目にして初めて授かった長女だった。
example_sentences.english: Fuuka was the first daughter that the Akitsuki couple was blessed with in the 20th year of their marriage. (only (after/when/because))

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじに当たって一夜にして大金持ちになった彼が、お金の価値を理解する事は無いでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Having won the lottery and becoming incredibly rich overnight, he cannot understand the value of money, can he?

example_sentences.japanese: 五十歳にして、もう孫が二人もいるなんて、あなたはとんでもなく若いおじいちゃんですね！
example_sentences.english: To think that at 50 years old you would already have something like 2 grandchildren, you're an absurdly young grandpa, right!

example_sentences.japanese: 今にして思えばあの頃５ドルでビットコインを売るのは間違った決定だったかも。
example_sentences.english: When I think about it now, selling bitcoin for 5 dollars at that time might have been a bad decision. (only (after/when/because))

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、語り手：「ミステリアスなその見知らぬ人は、一瞬にして二人の暗殺者を同時に殺してしまった。」
example_sentences.english: A novel, narrator: 'The mysterious stranger, in a moment, killed two assassins at once.' (only (after/when/because))

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚５０年目にして離婚をするなんて、一体どんな理由があったのか気になって仕方がありません。
example_sentences.english: To think that they would do something like divorce only after 50 years of marriage, I cannot help but to wonder what the heck kind of reason there was.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強を始めて１１年目にしてようやくＪＬＰＴのＮ１に合格する事が出来ました。
example_sentences.english: From when I started studying Japanese, it was only in  my 11th year that I was finally able to pass the JLPT N1.

example_sentences.japanese: ６０歳にして初めて海外で生活する事になった叔母の話を聞き、海外へ移住する勇気が湧いてきました。
example_sentences.english: Hearing my aunt's story of how she is only now living abroad for the first time after turning 60, my courage to migrate has been welling up.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学一年生にして起業した友達の木村はお金に余裕があるらしく、一緒に食事をするといつも奢ってくれる。
example_sentences.english: As for my friend Kimura, who started his own enterprise in the first year of university, it appears as though he has an abundance of cash, and he always treats me if we eat together.

general_translation: But, Although, If only, I wish I had
formation: Verb［ば］(1) + Verb + ものを(2)Verb［ば］(1) + ［い］Adjective + ものを(2)Verb［ば］(1) + ［な］Adjective + な + ものを(2)Verb［ば］(1) + Noun + の + ものを(2)(1) Verb［たら］、Verb + と(2) もんを
casual_structure: Verb［ば］(1) + Verb + ものを(2)Verb［ば］(1) + ［い］Adjective + ものを(2)Verb［ば］(1) + ［な］Adjective + な + ものを(2)Verb［ば］(1) + Noun + の + ものを(2)(1) Verb［たら］、Verb + と(2) もんを
explanation: A strong phrase, meaning if only (A), presenting (A) as an object of desire. The thing which is (A), if only it had occured.

example_sentences.japanese: 「嫌いなものがあったなら、そう言ってくれればいいものを...」
example_sentences.english: 'If there was something you didn't like, you should have said so, but…'

example_sentences.japanese: もっと早くに歯医者に行けば歯を抜かずに済んだものを...
example_sentences.english: If you went to the dentist earlier, they wouldn't have had to remove your tooth, but…

example_sentences.japanese: 目を合わせなかったら止められなかったものを、なんで警察なんかと目を合わせちゃうんだ。
example_sentences.english: If only you didn't make eye contact with the police, we wouldn't have been stopped, so why did you have to go and make eye contact with them?

example_sentences.japanese: アレルギーなどがあったなら、さきに言ってくれればいいものを...
example_sentences.english: If you had an allergy, you should have let me know beforehand, but…

example_sentences.japanese: 「手伝って」って言えばいいものを、一人でやるからこう言う目に遭うんだよ。
example_sentences.english: If you have just asked for help, but because you did it alone, it ended up like this.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなでやれば簡単なものを...
example_sentences.english: It would have been easy if we all worked on it together, but…

example_sentences.japanese: 道具を使えば楽なものを、わざわざ自分の力でやろうとするから怪我をするんだよ。
example_sentences.english: It would have been easier if you used tools, but because you went out of your way to try it without any tools, you ended up getting hurt.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は息子に言う：「ＲＩＮＥでメッセージをしてくれたら迎えに行ってあげたもんを...」
example_sentences.english: Father speaking to his son: 'If you had messaged me on Rine, I would have picked you up, but… (you didn't).'

example_sentences.japanese: 犯罪コメディ映画、トニー：「まったく、ボリス、おとなしく死んでおればいいものを...」
example_sentences.english: Crime comedy movie, Tony: 'Dear God, Boris, it would have been good if you had just shut up and died, but…'

example_sentences.japanese: 「もっと早くタバコをやめれば健康問題なしに済んだものを、手遅れになってしまった。」
example_sentences.english: 'If I had quit smoking much earlier I would have ended up without any health problems, but now it is too late.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼が君に謝ったのなら許すべきものを、子供じゃあるまいし、無視するなんてひどすぎるよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'You are not a child! If he is apologizing, you should forgive him, but ignoring him is too cruel!'

example_sentences.japanese: 素直に従っていればいいものを、反抗的な態度をとったために仕事を首になった。
example_sentences.english: I wish I had just obediently complied, but due to my insubordinate behavior, I got fired.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で自殺すればいいものを周りの人を巻き込んで自殺するなんて、身勝手が過ぎる。
example_sentences.english: If only they had just killed themselves, but to involve all of the surrounding people in their suicide, it is far too selfish.

example_sentences.japanese: 日頃から片付けをしていれば直ぐに片付いたものを、サボっていたために業者に頼む羽目になった。
example_sentences.english: If only I had habitually tidied, then I could have cleaned straight away, but since I have been neglecting it, I am in the bind of having to request a professional.

example_sentences.japanese: 機嫌が悪いなら早く寝ればいいものを、起きていたために家族に八つ当たりしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I wish that I had gone to sleep early due to my poor mood, but because I was unfortunately awake, I took it out on my family.

example_sentences.japanese: 早く病院へ行っていれば治療が出来たものを、行かなかったために彼女の体は治療が不可能なほど弱っていました。
example_sentences.english: If she had gone to the hospital early, it could have been handled with therapy, but because she didn't, her body had become weak to the extent that treatment was not possible.

example_sentences.japanese: かみやま：「その不良学生が僕の鉛筆を食わなかったら入学試験を受けていたはずのもんを...（食ったから、受けられなかった）」
example_sentences.english: Kamiyama: 'If that delinquent hadn't eaten my pencil, I would have taken the school entrance exam for sure, but… (He has eaten it, so I couldn't)'

example_sentences.japanese: 不満があるのならその都度言ってくれればいいものを、君が溜めておくから喧嘩になってしまったじゃないか...。
example_sentences.english: If you have complaints, it would have been fine if you told me at those times, but it becomes a fight because you let it get all pent up, doesn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 素直に認めていればいいものを...
example_sentences.english: I should have just been honest, but… (I should have just been honest, but instead I continued to lie)

example_sentences.japanese: 政治ポスター： 「日本を前へ。」
example_sentences.english: Political poster: Japan forward. (Verb omitted but obvious from context, the positive improvement of Japan)

general_translation: Even if, Even, No matter
formation: Noun + であれ［な］Adjective + であれWH-Word + であれ
casual_structure: Noun + であれ［な］Adjective + であれWH-Word + であれ
explanation: A formal, imperative phrase, indicating that whether something exists as (A) or not, nothing will change.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰であれ全ての人々は同様に死ぬ。
example_sentences.english: No matter who you are, all people die similarly.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供であれ、法律は守らなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are a child, you still need to obey the law.

example_sentences.japanese: 理由が何であれ、家族や友達を裏切るのはよくないと思う。
example_sentences.english: No matter the reason, I don't think it is right to betray your family and friends.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらあなたが年上であろうと、ここでは一応私が先輩なので私の言うことに従ってください。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much older you are, I am your superior here so please do as I say.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司からのメール：「インフルエンザであろうと、会社には来てください。」
example_sentences.english: Email from one's boss: 'Even if you have the flu, please come to work.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「どのような状況であれ、逃げることは許されない。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'No matter the circumstances, running away is unforgivable.'

example_sentences.japanese: 何であれ、両親にとっては我が子はいつも愛する我が子。
example_sentences.english: No matter what, from a parent's point of view, their child is always their beloved child.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ小さなものであれ検察官は賄賂を受け取るわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is just a small thing, the public prosecutor must not accept a bribe.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ氷のように純粋であれ、世界の悪からは免れられないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if one is as pure as ice, it seems that one cannot avoid the evil of the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 大人であれ、時にお菓子でお腹を一杯にしたい時もあるものだ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you're an adult, it's just a fact that you sometimes want to completely stuff yourself with snacks.

example_sentences.japanese: 友人の家であれ、訪問時は靴を脱ぐことが、基本的な礼儀です。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is a friend's house, taking shoes off when visiting are basic manners.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人が未成年であれ、そのような凶悪な犯罪を犯したのなら罰するべきです。
example_sentences.english: No matter whether the perpetrator is underaged, if they committed such a brutal crime, they must be punished.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな理由であれ、大切な人を裏切るような行為をしたのなら許されないと思うべきだ。
example_sentences.english: No matter what kind of reason there is, if you've been conducting yourself in a way that betrays those important to you, you ought to assume that you won't be forgiven.

example_sentences.japanese: 何歳であれ褒められると嬉しいのは変わらない。だからどんどん僕の事を褒めて欲しい。
example_sentences.english: No matter what age, that I will be happy upon getting complimented will not change. Because of that, I want you to compliment me more and more.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに真っ当に生きている人であれ、人に言えない秘密が一つや二つはあるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Even if they are a person that lives respectably, they still have one or two secrets that they can't tell anyone, right?

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ十年以上の付き合いであれ、自分以外の人には常に敬意を持って接するべきである。
example_sentences.english: Even if you were dating for over 10 years, for instance, you must always treat someone other than yourself with respect.

grammar_point: を措（お）いて他（ほか）に〜ない
general_translation: No...but, Nothing else but, None other than
formation: Noun + をおいてほか + には(1) + … + ない(1)に
casual_structure: Noun + をおいてほか + には(1) + … + ない(1)に
explanation: A formal construction, emphasizing that nothing beats (A). Setting aside (A), there are no others.

example_sentences.japanese: 長年付き合ってきたパートナーに別れを切り出すのなら明日をおいてほかにはない。
example_sentences.english: If you're going to broach the subject of breaking up with a long-time partner, there's nothing like tomorrow. (no choice but)

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに人類学に詳しい人は高橋教授をおいてほかにいない。
example_sentences.english: No one knows anthropology better than Professor Takahashi.

example_sentences.japanese: 最初のライブは、大阪をおいてほかにない。
example_sentences.english: The first concert will be held in none other than Osaka.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の文法を習いたいなら、文プロをおいてほかにない。
example_sentences.english: If you want to learn Japanese grammar, there is none other than Bunpro.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が子の世話を安心して任せられるのは、実の両親と妻をおいてほかにはいません。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to entrusting the care of my child with peace of mind, there's none other than my parents and my wife.

example_sentences.japanese: もう今年で四十歳になる事だし、結婚を本気で考えているのなら次の機会をおいてほかにはないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Since you're already going to be 40 years old this year, if you're going to seriously think about marriage, then the next chance is all there is, right? (nothing but)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強を始めたばかりの初心者の方におすすめするアプリを一つあげるとするなら、「文プロ」をおいてほかにありません。
example_sentences.english: If I were to mention an app that I would recommend for beginners that have just started learning Japanese then it would be none other than 'Bunpro.'

example_sentences.japanese: 探偵は容疑者に言う：「とぼけないでください。これほど事件について知っているのは犯人自身をおいてほかにいないでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: Detective speaking to the suspect: 'Don't play dumb. No one but the murderer himself knows this much about the murder.'

example_sentences.japanese: 社長は副社長に言う：「私は引退しようと思う。次期社長は君をおいてほかにふさわしい人は思い浮かばない。」
example_sentences.english: The company president speaks to the vice president: 'I am planning to retire. No one but you comes to my mind as a suitable successor.'

example_sentences.japanese: 先月から問題になっている円安について分かり易く解説を出来るのは、加藤教授をおいてほかにはいません。
example_sentences.english: As for explaining about the weakening yen problem since last month in an easy to understand way, there's none other than professor Katou.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が若い頃は結婚するなら当時の彼女をおいてほかには考えられないと思っていたが、それは間違いだった。
example_sentences.english: In my younger days, if I was going to get married, I thought that I could not even contemplate someone other than my girlfriend at the time, but that was wrong.

example_sentences.japanese: 不動産を購入するにあたって、長年不動産の売買に携わってきた叔父をおいてほかにはいないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of purchasing real estate, there's no one like your uncle, who has been involved in the buying and selling of real estate for many years, don't you think? (none other than)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が退職した後の後任としてあなたをおいてほかには考えられないのですが、引き受けてくれませんか？
example_sentences.english: After retiring, I can't think of anyone other than you as my successor, but… Would you assume the responsibility for me?

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話、こまり：「東京で観光するつもりよ。」ほたる：「東京で観光するなら東京タワーをおいてほかにないと思うの。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends, Komari: 'I plan to go to sightseeing in Tokyo.'Hotaru: 'If you are going sightseeing in Tokyo, then I can think of nothing but Tokyo Tower.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「日本人監督といえば、現代の映画撮影技術に最も大きな影響を与えたのは、もちろん黒沢明をおいてほかにいない。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'When I mention Japanese directors, the one that has the greatest influence on modern cinematography is of course none other than Akira Kurosawa.'

general_translation: As of, With, Effective from
formation: Time-Related Expression + をもって以上（いじょう）(1) + をもって(1) これ
casual_structure: Time-Related Expression + をもって以上（いじょう）(1) + をもって(1) これ
polite_structure: Time-Related Expression + をもちまして以上（いじょう）(1) + をもちまして(1) これ
explanation: A formal phrase expressing something done or caused by the means of (A). (A) is often a time from when something comes into effect.

example_sentences.japanese: 以上をもちまして、私のスピーチは終わりとさせて頂きます。
example_sentences.english: 'With this, I would like to conclude my speech.' (effective from)

example_sentences.japanese: このゲームのオンラインサービスは２０２３年８月１０日をもって終了することに決定しました。
example_sentences.english: It has been decided that the online service for this game will end as of August 10, 2023.

example_sentences.japanese: 本日をもって、受付を終了いたします。
example_sentences.english: As of today, we will no longer be accepting applications.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のツアーをもって、解散することになりました。
example_sentences.english: We have decided to disband as of this tour.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもご来店ありがとうございます。この店舗は本日をもちまして閉店いたします。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for always visiting our shops. As of the day of writing, this store location will be closed.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は４月２日をもて、４０年間勤めていた会社をやめることにした。
example_sentences.english: As of April 2nd, my father decided to quit the company he had worked for for 40 years.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議、問いかけに答えた後：「これをもちまして質疑応答を終わります。ありがとうございます。」
example_sentences.english: The conference, after answering a question: 'With this, I will end the question-answer session. Thank you very much.' (effective from)

example_sentences.japanese: 辞令：「一条蛍殿。令和２年５月１日をもって経理部第５課勤務を命ずる。」
example_sentences.english: Appointment notice: 'Ichijou Hotaru, we appoint you to a position in the fifth section of the accounting department, effective (from) May 1st, 2020.'

example_sentences.japanese: 誠に勝手ながら「可愛い店」は本日をもちまして閉店いたします。長きに渡りご愛顧、誠にありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: We regret to inform you that 'KawaiiMise' will close as of today. We are truly thankful for the long-lasting patronage. (effective from)

example_sentences.japanese: 司会：「以上をもちまして、２０２１年度の運動会を閉会致します。」
example_sentences.english: Master of ceremonies: 'With this, I will bring a close to the 2021 sports carnival.'

example_sentences.japanese: テレビＣＭ：「本日２３：５９分をもって、キャンペーンへの応募を締め切らせて頂きます。」
example_sentences.english: Television commercial: 'Effective from 11:59pm tonight, entries to the campaign will close off.'

example_sentences.japanese: お笑い芸人の独り言：「こんなに精神的に辛い仕事は今年をもって終わりにしたいな...。」
example_sentences.english: The monologue of a comedian: 'Work that is this mentally tough, I want to stop as of this year.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のプロジェクトをもちましてチームが解散となったため、メンバー全員で打ち上げを開く事にしました。
example_sentences.english: As of this project, since it has been decided that the team will dissolve, we have decided to hold a completion party with all the members.

example_sentences.japanese: 体操選手としてはまだ若手の草彅選手が来月をもって引退すると聞き、多くのファンが悲しみに暮れている。
example_sentences.english: Upon hearing that Kusanagi, who is still young for a gymnastics competitor, will retire effective as of next month, many fans sunk into despair.

example_sentences.japanese: ファイナルファンタジー ７のＸｂｏｘ Ｓｅｒｉｅｓ Ｘ版及びＰｌａｙＳｔａｔｉｏｎ ５版のサービスは２０２１年７月１６日（金）をもちまして終了させていただくことになりました。
example_sentences.english: It has been decided that Final Fantasy 7's services for the Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5 will be shut down as of July 16th, 2021 (Friday).

example_sentences.japanese: キャンパスツアーのガイド：「本日はこれをもちましてツアーは終わりとなります。ご参加して下さり有難う御座いました。」
example_sentences.english: Campus tour guide: 'For today, this will bring the tour to a finish. Thank you so very much for participating.' (effective from)

example_sentences.japanese: 社長の退社の辞：「本年７月をもちまして社長の立場を退任することに致しました。今まで大変お世話になりましたことを心より御礼申し上げます。」
example_sentences.english: Company president's retirement speech: 'I decided to retire from the position of President effective from the month of July this year. I sincerely appreciate your continued patronage.'

example_sentences.japanese: ２０２３年７月２７日をもって、人気映画の続編が公開されます。
example_sentences.english: The sequel to the popular film will be released on July 27, 2023. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Though, Although (I admit that), Be that as it may, Nonetheless
formation: Verb + とはいえ + Phrase［い］Adjective + とはいえ + PhraseNoun + （だ）+ とはいえ + Phrase［な］Adjective + （だ）+ とはいえ + PhrasePhrase (A)。とはいえ + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Verb + とはいえ + Phrase［い］Adjective + とはいえ + PhraseNoun + （だ）+ とはいえ + Phrase［な］Adjective + （だ）+ とはいえ + PhrasePhrase (A)。とはいえ + Phrase (B)
explanation: A formal, imperative expression, showing that (A) may be said, but nonetheless (B). Go ahead and say (A), but (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 馬は肉を食べることができる。とはいえ、普通は食べない。
example_sentences.english: Horses are perfectly capable of eating meat. Having said that, they generally do not eat it. (be that as it may)

example_sentences.japanese: この事件の犯人が分かったとはいえ、犯人はまだ捕まっていないからまだ油断はできない。
example_sentences.english: Although the culprit in this case is known, we can't let our guard down yet because the culprit has not been caught yet.

example_sentences.japanese: このパソコンは新しいといえ、今持っているパソコンより性能がいいと言うわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Although this computer is new, it does not mean that it has better features than the computer that I already own.

example_sentences.japanese: この国は安全だといえ、日本ではないので子供から目を離さないようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: Although this country is safe, it is not Japan, so please keep an eye on your child.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人とはいえ、スペインで育ったから日本語があまり話せない。
example_sentences.english: Although I am Japanese, I grew up in Spain so I can't speak much Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人は逮捕されたとはいえ有罪と宣告されるまで時間がかかるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Although (I admit that) the criminal has been caught, it will be some time before they are declared guilty. (be that as it may)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は社長とはいえ名前ばかりだ。権限は取締役会にある。
example_sentences.english: Although he is admittedly the company president, it is in name only. It is the board of directors that holds the power. (be that as it may)

example_sentences.japanese: 今では、パンデミックの進行状況は遅いとはいえ、まだ安心するわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Although (I admit that) the progress of the pandemic is slow, we cannot afford to feel at ease just yet. (be that as it may)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女があなたにとって実の母親であるとはいえ、礼儀を欠くべきではない。
example_sentences.english: Although she is, for you, your real mother, you should not lack manners.

example_sentences.japanese: 容疑者がまだ未成年だとはいえ、残忍な事件を犯した事には何ら変わりはない。
example_sentences.english: Although it may be that the suspect is not of age, It does not in any way change the fact that he committed such a brutal act.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょうどその時に急いでいたとはいえ、友達からの挨拶を無視するのはどうかな...。
example_sentences.english: Although you were in a rush at precisely that moment, ignoring your friend's greeting, I don't know about that…

example_sentences.japanese: 妹が犠牲となった交通事故から十年経ったとはいえ、未だに立ち直る事は出来ていません。
example_sentences.english: Although 10 years have passed since my little sister ended up as the victim of a traffic accident, I still have not been able to get back on my feet.

example_sentences.japanese: 体重が五キロ減ったとはいえまだまだ健康的な体型とは言えないため、食事制限を継続するつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: Although I lost 5 kilos, since it still cannot be said that I have a healthy figure, I intend to continue with calorie restriction.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は日本語が話せるとはいえ日常会話止まりで、ビジネスとして使うにはまだまだ勉強が必要です。
example_sentences.english: Although I am able to speak Japanese, that stops at daily conversation. To use it for business, study is still necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「この場合、「ようだ」と「ごとし」のどちらを使ってもよいということである。しかしながら、どちらも使えるとはいえ、実際には意味合いが異なる。」
example_sentences.english: Thesis: 'In this case, one can use both 'ようだ' and 'ごとし.' However, although I say you can use both, their meanings actually have different nuances.' (be that as it may)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「キャッシュレス決済手段を日常的に使う人が増えたとはいえ、２０ＸＸ 年時点における日本での決済に占めるキャッシュレスの比率は僅か約２０％程度です。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Although (I admit that) the number of people using cashless payments on a daily basis has increased, as of 20XX, they only account for about 20% of all payments made in Japan.' (be that as it may)

general_translation: Unique to, Only, Impossible if not, Expected only of
formation: More common patterns:Noun + ならでは + の + NounNoun + ならでは + だ。Less common patterns:Noun + ならでは + Verb［できる］［ない］+ Noun
casual_structure: More common patterns:Noun + ならでは + の + NounNoun + ならでは + だ。Less common patterns:Noun + ならでは + Verb［できる］［ない］+ Noun
polite_structure: More common patterns:Noun + ならでは + の + NounNoun + ならでは + です。Less common patterns:Noun + ならでは + Verb［できる］［ない］+ Noun
explanation: A hypothetical expression indicating that, in general, if it's (A), then (B). Not possible if not (A). Often showing high evaluation of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: このクリーミーで且つ重くない絶品のカルボナーラは地元の名店ならではだ。
example_sentences.english: This exquisite, creamy, and moreover light carbonara is expected only of a famous shop in our region.

example_sentences.japanese: 味噌カツは名古屋ならではの食べ物です。
example_sentences.english: Misokatsu is a food unique to Nagoya.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカならではの観光地といったらどこを連想しますか。
example_sentences.english: Where do you think is a tourist attraction that is unique to the States?

example_sentences.japanese: この祭りはこの地域ならではの祭りです。
example_sentences.english: This festival is unique to this area.

example_sentences.japanese: 食品広告：「おばあさんの手作りならではなかなか出せない味だ。」
example_sentences.english: Food product advertisement: 'Unique flavor that can only be found in grandma's homemade cooking.' (unique to)

example_sentences.japanese: 求人のサイト、求人情報：「小さいカフェならではの良さが溢れています。」
example_sentences.english: Job search website, job information: 'The charm unique to a small cafe is overflowing.'

example_sentences.japanese: 広告ポスター：「沖縄ならではの、普段は見られない透明度の高い青い海は必見だ。」
example_sentences.english: A poster ad: 'The extremely clear blue waters that can usually only be seen in Okinawa are a must-see.' (unique to)

example_sentences.japanese: 求人のサイト、店員コメント：「こうした社風の良さは当社ならではだと思います。」
example_sentences.english: Job search website, employee comment: 'I think that the good quality of our corporate culture is unique to this company.'

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は海外へ旅行に行く時は必ずその土地ならではの料理を食べるようにしています。
example_sentences.english: When going on an overseas trip, without fail, I try to eat the cuisine unique to that region.

example_sentences.japanese: 雪山で遭難するという絶体絶命な状況でもユーモアを欠かさないのは父ならではだ。
example_sentences.english: Even in a desperate, life-or-death situation like being stranded on a snowy mountain, not losing his sense of humor is something only my father would do.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が通う大学は少人数ならではの実践的な英語教育で人気が高まっています。
example_sentences.english: As for the university that I go to, with a small number of students unique to it, it is becoming popular for its practical English education.

example_sentences.japanese: 新年に年賀状を送り合うという日本ならではの文化は、インターネットの登場を機に衰退し続けている。
example_sentences.english: The culture of sending new year's cards to each other on New Year, unique to Japan, is something that has been waning since the appearance of the internet.

example_sentences.japanese: 折角日本へ旅行をしに行くのなら、神社やお寺、アニメをコンセプトにしたカフェ等の日本ならではの場所へ行きたいです。
example_sentences.english: If I'm going to put in the effort to go to Japan, then I want to go to places that are expected only of Japan like shrines, temples, and cafes that have been styled after anime.

example_sentences.japanese: 本のおすすめ記事：「そのようなマンガやアニメなどの小ネタっぽいライトノベルを書き上げるのはさすが西尾維新先生ならではです。」
example_sentences.english: A book recommendation article: 'The one who can write a light novel filled with small joke references to manga and anime is unique to Nishio Ishin.'

example_sentences.japanese: お茶の広告：「ハイクオリティな紅茶ならではの味わい！〇〇紅茶ティーバッグ３０バッグ入」「すっきりと香り高く澄み切った味です！」
example_sentences.english: Tea advertisement: 'A flavor only possible with high-quality black tea! XX tea bags, 30 bags included.''A serene, refreshing, and aromatic taste!'

example_sentences.japanese: こんな綺麗な作品を作れるのは、藤田さんならではだ。
example_sentences.english: Only you, Fujita-san, can create such an amazing piece.

example_sentences.japanese: 車なしで生活できるのは都会ならではだ。
example_sentences.english: Only in the city can one live without a car.

general_translation: It's all well and good but...
formation: Verb［た］+ はいいがVerb［た］+ の + はいいが
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ はいいがVerb［た］+ の + はいいが
explanation: An expression used to convey the speaker’s dissatisfaction, describing a situation where something has been done with positive intent at first but was followed by an unexpected negative outcome.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みの日に早くおきたはいいが何もすることがない。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I woke up early on my day off, but I have nothing to do.

example_sentences.japanese: 晩ご飯をつくったはいいが大量に作りすぎて困っている。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I made dinner, but I made way too much and don't know what to do.

example_sentences.japanese: ジムに通いはじめたはいいが３日で飽きてしまった。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I started going to the gym, but I got bored of it in three days.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長にほめられたはいいが上司から妬まれそうだ。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I was praised by the company president, but it seems my boss is going to be jealous.

example_sentences.japanese: 満員電車で席にすわれたはいいが、降りたい駅で立ち上がるのが大変だ。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I managed to get a seat on the crowded train, but it's hard to stand up at the station where I want to get off.

example_sentences.japanese: 無事就職できたはいいが入社前と入社後のギャップに疲れ果てている。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I successfully got a job, but I am exhausted by the gap between my expectations before joining and the reality after.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はオリンピックで１位をとったはいいが燃え尽き症候群に悩まされているそうだ。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that she took first place at the Olympics, but I hear she is suffering from burnout syndrome.

example_sentences.japanese: 脱毛した部分から毛がはえてきたはいいが白髪しか生えてこない。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that hair started growing back in the area where I got laser hair removal, but only white hairs are growing.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘が私立大学に合格したはいいが今後４年間の学費が心配でならない。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that my daughter got accepted into a private university, but I am endlessly worried about the tuition fees for the next four years.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の苦しそうな様子を見て黙ってはいられないと思い声をかけたはいいが、うまく言葉が出てこなかった。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I called out to him because I couldn't bear to stay silent seeing him in pain, but the words just wouldn't come out right.

example_sentences.japanese: 婦人服セールで安くなっているのをいいことにたくさんかったはいいが、結局ほとんど着ていない。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I bought a lot taking advantage of the cheap prices at the women's clothing sale, but in the end, I hardly wear any of it.

example_sentences.japanese: キャンプ用品を何から何までそろえたはいいが、当日は豪雨で結局使わずじまいだった。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I gathered together absolutely all the camping gear, but there was a heavy downpour on the day of the trip and it ended up going unused.

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越したはいいが、まだ荷物が届いていない。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I moved, but my stuff hasn't arrived yet.

example_sentences.japanese: ３ヶ月で１５ｋｇも痩せたはいいが、すぐにリバウンドして体重が戻ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I lost 15kg in three months, but I immediately rebounded and gained the weight back.

example_sentences.japanese: ５０歳にして初めて海外旅行に行けたのはいいが、実際は英語が話せなくて苦労した。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I was able to travel overseas for the first time at 50 years old, but in reality, I struggled because I couldn't speak English.

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじに当たったはいいが、情報が漏れていないかと不安で怯える毎日である。
example_sentences.english: It's all well and good that I won the lottery, but every day I am terrified and anxious that information about it might have leaked.

general_translation: Even
formation: Noun + （Particle）+ すら（も）
casual_structure: Noun + （Particle）+ すら（も）
explanation: A strong, formal expression, highlighting that even the extreme example of (A) applies to a statement, so is obviously true for other things.

example_sentences.japanese: マンガの迷った主人公：「何日たったのかすら...」
example_sentences.english: A lost manga protagonist: 'I don't even (know) how many days have passed…'

example_sentences.japanese: 子供ですらできることをできないのか。お前よくここまで生きてこれたな。
example_sentences.english: You can't do what even a child can do. How have you managed to live this long?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼にすら話してないのに、親と話すわけがない。
example_sentences.english: I haven't even talked to my boyfriend about it, there is no way I'm telling my parents.

example_sentences.japanese: ガラケーすらも使えないのに、パソコンが使えるわけないじゃん。
example_sentences.english: I can't even use a flip phone, there is no way I can use a computer.

example_sentences.japanese: 鉛筆すら持ってきてないの？本当にやる気あるの？
example_sentences.english: You didn't even bring a pencil? Do you actually want to do this?

example_sentences.japanese: 南極大陸では夏ですら気温が０度以下である。
example_sentences.english: In Antarctica, temperatures are below zero even in summer.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「カラスは道具を使用する能力を示したことすらあります。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Crows have even demonstrated the ability to use tools.'

example_sentences.japanese: ノベル、語り手：「負傷により、走るどころかベッドから立ち上がることすらもできない。」
example_sentences.english: A novel, narrator: 'Due to her injuries, let alone running, she can't even stand up out of bed.'

example_sentences.japanese: ノベル、語り手：「友達どころか家族にすら説明せずに旅に出た。」
example_sentences.english: A novel, narrator: 'Without even explaining to his family, let alone friends he embarked on a journey.'

example_sentences.japanese: ビジュアルノベル、キャラクターの紹介：「牧瀬紅莉栖。子供ですら知っている、この世界的研究者。」
example_sentences.english: Visual novel, character introduction: 'Kurisu Makise. The world-famous researcher, whom even children know.'

example_sentences.japanese: まだ平仮名や片仮名すらうろ覚えなのに日本語能力試験を受けるのは無理があります。
example_sentences.english: There's no way you can take the JLPT, despite only having a vague grasp of even hiragana and katakana.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生ですら出来るような掛け算九九の計算を間違えてしまい、大恥をかいた。
example_sentences.english: Miscalculating a times table multiplication that can be done even by a primary school student was very embarrassing.

example_sentences.japanese: 連絡先どころか本名すら知らないなんて、本当に彼女とは友達なんですか...？
example_sentences.english: Let alone her contact details, something like not even knowing her real name, is she even your friend?

example_sentences.japanese: イギリスに十年も住んでいて日常会話すら出来ないなんて、今までどうやって生活をしていたの...？
example_sentences.english: Something like not even being able to have a daily conversation after 10 years of living in England. What kind of lifestyle have you been leading up until now…?

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに元気だった祖母が今は家の中の掃除すら出来ないと聞き、老いる事に恐怖を感じています。
example_sentences.english: Hearing that my grandmother, who had been so energetic, can now not even do chores around the house, I am dreading getting old.

example_sentences.japanese: ネイティブですら満点を取ることが出来ない試験を作るなんて、この言語能力試験の制作者は一体何を考えているのだろうか...。
example_sentences.english: Creating a language test that not even a native speaker can get a perfect score on, what on earth were the creators thinking…

example_sentences.japanese: そこさえ乗り越えれば、あとは楽になるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you can overcome that, everything will be a breeze.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなことすら乗り越えることができないのなら、この先何もできませんよ。
example_sentences.english: If you can't even overcome something so simple, you won't be able to do anything beyond this point.

general_translation: Exist only because of or due to, Owe everything to
formation: Noun (A) + （が）+ あっての + Noun (B)
casual_structure: Noun (A) + （が）+ あっての + Noun (B)
explanation: A structure emphasizing that (B) is only possible because (A) exists. (B) owes everything to (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が大学をやめるのは、何か理由があってのことだろう。
example_sentences.english: I guess he is dropping out of university only because some sort of reason exists.

example_sentences.japanese: お客様あっての仕事だと思うのですが、理不尽なクレームを言われるとちょっとイラっときます。
example_sentences.english: My job only exists because of the customers, but I get a little annoyed when people make unreasonable complaints.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回は皆様の努力あっての結果です。皆様本当にありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: This time, the results are because of your efforts. Thank you very much.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はお金がなかったら愛もない、お金があっての幸せだと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that without money, there’s no love and happiness is something that exists only due to money.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あなたあってのわたしです。あなたがいなければ私の人生は無意味ですよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I can only exist because of you. My life would be meaningless without you.' (owe everything to)

example_sentences.japanese: 支配人、社員に：「ゲストあっての遊園地だということを忘れてはいけません。」
example_sentences.english: Manager to employees: 'You must not forget that the amusement park exists only because of the customers.'

example_sentences.japanese: 恋愛は相手あってのことだから一人だけでは無理だ...と思っていませんか？
example_sentences.english: Love only exists because you have a partner, so it is impossible to love when you are alone… don't you think? (owe everything to)

example_sentences.japanese: 部員あってのクラブ活動なんだから、部員に対してもっと優しくするべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Since club activities exist only because of our club members, we must be nicer to them.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘：「お金と愛、どっちが大事だと思う？」母：「そうね〜、お金あっての幸せだと思うわ。」
example_sentences.english: Daughter: 'Money and love, which do you think is more important?'Mom: 'Hmm, happiness exists only because of money I think.'

example_sentences.japanese: 兄が一人暮らしを始め、私たちの家族は兄あっての家族だった事が分かった。
example_sentences.english: When he started living independently, I realized that my family existed only because of my older brother.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が志望校に合格したのは君の努力あっての成果で、僕はただ側にいただけさ。
example_sentences.english: Successfully getting your first-preference school was only possible due to your own efforts, all I did was stay by your side. (owe everything to)

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚という契約は愛あってのものであって、愛の無い結婚など全く意味を成しません。
example_sentences.english: The contract of marriage owes everything to love, and something such as a loveless marriage will amount to nothing.

example_sentences.japanese: お客様や取引先相手あってのビジネスなので、ビジネスにおいて礼儀を欠く事は命取りになります。
example_sentences.english: Since we are a business that owes everything to our customers and clients, lacking manners in business would prove fatal.

example_sentences.japanese: ベストセラー作者の演説：「 私の本は、家族の支えあってのものです。息子と夫がいなければここまでやってこれなかったと思います。」
example_sentences.english: Best Selling author's speech: 'My books exist only because of the support from my family. I believe, if it was not for my son and husband, I would not have gotten this far.' (owe everything to)

example_sentences.japanese: 切手のコレクションが火事で全焼して悲しいのは分かっているけどさ、生きて逃げられたのは何よりだよ。「命あっての物種」だね。
example_sentences.english: I understand that you are sad because your stamp collection was destroyed in the fire, but getting out of there with your life is more important than anything. 'While there is life, there is hope,' right? (only exist because of)

general_translation: Just, Merely, Simply, Only
formation: Verb［た］+ まで(1) + だ(1)までのこと
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ まで(1) + だ(1)までのこと
polite_structure: Verb［た］+ まで(1) + です(1)までのこと
explanation: A construction emphasizing the reason for an action. Doing up until (A) was the only motive. Merely (A).

example_sentences.japanese: なんで怒っているの？私の意見をいったまでのことだ。
example_sentences.english: Why are you angry? I merely stated my opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: なんで俺が悪者扱いされないといけないんだ？俺はただ自分の意見を言ったまでだ。
example_sentences.english: Why do I have to get blamed for this? I only expressed my opinions.

example_sentences.japanese: お婆さんが困った顔をしていたから、助けたまでだ。
example_sentences.english: I just helped because the old lady looked like she needed help.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近学校にも行かないし部屋からも出ないから、聞いたまでのことだ。
example_sentences.english: I merely asked because recently, you haven't left your room and haven't gone to school.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなお礼とかはやめてください、人として当たり前のことをしたまでです。
example_sentences.english: Please, don't thank me. I just did something expected as a human.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「助けてくれてありがとうございます！」Ｂ：「いや、当然のことをしたまでのことです。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Thank you very much for helping me!' B: 'Not at all. It was just the obvious thing.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「わぁ、日本語上手だね！」Ｂ：「ただ趣味で勉強してたまでのことで、まだまだだけどね。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Wow, your Japanese is good!'B: 'I was merely learning it as a hobby. I still have a ways to go.'

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はただ伝言を頼まれたからつたえたまでで、それは僕の考えではないからね！
example_sentences.english: Since I was just requested to have a word with you, that's merely all I did, it's not like they were my thoughts.

example_sentences.japanese: 真実をはなしたまでのことなのに、なぜかクラスメイトから嘘つきと言われてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: When I just told the truth, I was accused by my classmate of being a liar for some reason.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫：「君は本当に世界で一番美しいよ。」妻：「もう、お世辞はやめてよ！」夫：「本心をいったまでのことだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Husband: 'You are honestly the most stunning woman in the world.'Wife: 'Ok, ok, quit it with the lip service!'Husband: 'I just spoke my mind is all.'

example_sentences.japanese: 娘：「どうしてそんな事を聞くの？」父：「ちょっと気になったからきいたまでのことだ。」
example_sentences.english: Daughter: 'Why would you ask such a thing?'Dad: 'It was bothering me, so I just asked.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女：「あなたは本当に優しいね。」彼氏：「そうかな？彼が困っていたからたすけたまでだ。」
example_sentences.english: Girlfriend: 'You are honestly so nice!'Boyfriend: 'You think? He was in trouble, so I simply helped.'

example_sentences.japanese: お年寄りを助けるという基本的な事をしたまでのことなのでお礼は要りません。
example_sentences.english: Since I just did something as fundamental as helping the elderly, thanks is not required.

example_sentences.japanese: 気分が悪い人を助けるという人として当然の事をしたまでのことです。褒めないで下さい。
example_sentences.english: As someone that would help a person feeling ill, it is just the obvious thing to do. Please don't praise me for it.

example_sentences.japanese: 香奈：「どうして秘密をバラしたりなんかしたの？」由紀恵：「聞かれたからこたえたまでだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Kana: 'Why did you have to do something like spill secrets?'Yukie: 'Because I was asked, I simply answered.'

example_sentences.japanese: どうして怒っているんだい？君が本音を聞かせてと言うからそうしたまでのことだ！
example_sentences.english: Why are you mad? Because you always ask to let you hear my real opinion, I did just that.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私が困っていたから、助けてくれたまでだ。
example_sentences.english: Because I looked like I was in need, he merely helped me. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Via, Through, After (experience at job, university, etc.), Pass through
formation: Noun + を経（へ）て
casual_structure: Noun + を経（へ）て
explanation: A formal construction, showing that through (A), (B). By passing through the time period of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ベルリンからローマをへてブエノスアイレスに向かいます。
example_sentences.english: From Berlin, via Rome, to Buenos Aires. (through)

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは２０１９年に出会って、約２年間の交際をへて結婚しました。
example_sentences.english: We met in 2019, and married after going through two years of dating.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本への留学をへて、日本の文化などを学ぶことができました。
example_sentences.english: Through my study in Japan, I was able to learn about Japanese culture and other aspects of the country.

example_sentences.japanese: 人は色々な経験をへて、成長していく。
example_sentences.english: People grow through various experiences.

example_sentences.japanese: 数世代をへてもなお争議が続いている。
example_sentences.english: Even after several generations, the dispute still continues. (through・via・experience)

example_sentences.japanese: ちとげとらくは、約１０年の交際をへて結婚した。
example_sentences.english: Chitoge and Raku finally married after going through about ten years of dating. (through・via・experience)

example_sentences.japanese: 略歴：「早稲田大学理学部卒業後Ｇｏｏｇｌｅ勤務をへて２０２〇年独立。」
example_sentences.english: Short bio: 'Graduated from the department of science, Waseda University. After (having the experience of) working at Google, he started his own business in 202X.' (through・via)

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞：「今後必要な手続きをへて、鉱山買収は完了します。」
example_sentences.english: Newspaper: 'After going through all of the necessary procedures, the mine acquisition will be complete.' (through・via・experience)

example_sentences.japanese: 私の妹は大学卒業後に三年間に渡るイギリス留学をへて高校の英語教師になった。
example_sentences.english: After my little sister's graduation, through her experience of studying abroad in England for 3 years, she became a high school English teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 様々な手続きをへてやっと離婚が成立し、今は清々しい気持ちでいっぱいです。
example_sentences.english: After a slew of proceedings, our divorce was finally realized, and now I am full of refreshed feelings.

example_sentences.japanese: 一年間の休養をへて仕事に復帰する事になったが不安で押し潰されそうになっている。
example_sentences.english: After recuperating for one year, I was reinstated at work, but it feels like I will be crushed with anxiety.

example_sentences.japanese: 新入社員として五年間に渡る本社での経験をへて、今月から地方でリーダーとして働く事になった。
example_sentences.english: Through my experience spanning 5 years at the head office as a new arrival, it has been decided that I will work as a regional leader from this month.

example_sentences.japanese: 流行りの疫病で直行便が減っているため、私たちは日本からシンガポールをへてオーストラリアへ渡りました。
example_sentences.english: Due to direct flights decreasing with the prevalence of the epidemic, we crossed from Japan, via Singapore, and to Australia.

example_sentences.japanese: 人は多くの失敗をへて成長するのだから、一つや二つ失敗をしたからといって落ち込み過ぎないでね。
example_sentences.english: Since people will grow after going through many failures, don't get depressed just because of one or two mistakes.

example_sentences.japanese: 教科書の筆者の紹介：「日本語研修所講師をへて現在はＪａｐａｎｅｓｅ Ｉｎｓｔｉｔｕｔｅ ｏｆ Ｌａｎｇｕａｇｅ ＆ Ｈｉｓｔｏｒｙ代表。」
example_sentences.english: Introduction of a textbook author: 'After working as a lecturer at a Japanese language training institute, she is now the representative of the Japanese Institute of Language & History.' (through・via・experience)

general_translation: While being, Born (with), Traditional (old-fashioned, as it was long ago), As always, While crying or in tears, (Burned) alive
formation: Verb［stem］+ ながら（に）Noun + ながら（に）Verb［stem］+ ながら + の + NounNoun (A) + ながら + の + Noun (B)生（い）きる ￫ 生（い）きながら（にして）生（う）まれる ￫ 生（う）まれながら（にして）昔（むかし） ￫ 昔（むかし）ながらいつも ￫ いつもながら毎回（まいかい） ￫ 毎回（まいかい）ながら涙（なみだ） ￫ 涙（なみだ）ながらに溜（た）め息（いき） ￫ 溜（た）め息（いき）ながらいる ￫ いながら（にして）
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ ながら（に）Noun + ながら（に）Verb［stem］+ ながら + の + NounNoun (A) + ながら + の + Noun (B)生（い）きる ￫ 生（い）きながら（にして）生（う）まれる ￫ 生（う）まれながら（にして）昔（むかし） ￫ 昔（むかし）ながらいつも ￫ いつもながら毎回（まいかい） ￫ 毎回（まいかい）ながら涙（なみだ） ￫ 涙（なみだ）ながらに溜（た）め息（いき） ￫ 溜（た）め息（いき）ながらいる ￫ いながら（にして）
explanation: A phrase highlighting that while (A), (B). In the ongoing, unchanging state of (A), (B). Born with (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: いきながら焼かれるところだった。
example_sentences.english: She was almost burned alive. (while alive)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供ながらにして、なんで親がいつも喧嘩をしていたかは理解していた。
example_sentences.english: Even as a child, I understood why my parents were always fighting.

example_sentences.japanese: 自由権は人が生まれながらに持っている権利の一つだ。
example_sentences.english: Freedom is one of the rights that people are born with.

example_sentences.japanese: 家に居ながらにして仕事ができるから、職場までわざわざ行かなくても良くなった。
example_sentences.english: I can work while being home, so I don't have to go all the way to my workplace anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は涙ながらに彼を見送った。
example_sentences.english: She sent him off while crying.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもながらあなたたちと話すのは楽しいですよ。
example_sentences.english: It is a pleasure to talk with you, as always.

example_sentences.japanese: コナンはうまれながらのすぐれた名探偵だそうだ。
example_sentences.english: They say that Conan is a great detective by nature. (by birth).

example_sentences.japanese: テレワークというのは家にいながら働くということだ。
example_sentences.english: Telework means to work while being at home.

example_sentences.japanese: コウタはカエデからの手紙を手に取りつつ、なみだながらに喜んだ。
example_sentences.english: While crying with joy, Kouta held the letter from Kaede in his hands. (in tears)

example_sentences.japanese: このカフェはその昔ながらの内装で、常連さんから長い間に渡って愛されています。
example_sentences.english: With upholstery as it was long ago, this cafe has been loved by faithful customers for a long time.

example_sentences.japanese: 生まれながらに孤独だった彼女は、そのせいで今も人との交流に苦手意識を持っている。
example_sentences.english: Having been alone from birth, she was self conscious of the fact that she was bad at interactions with people due to that. (born with)

example_sentences.japanese: 行きつけの居酒屋の店主は、いつもながら私たち家族にサービスをしてくれました。
example_sentences.english: As always, the proprietor of my regular izakaya provided some freebies for my family.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな人にも生まれながらの使命があると言われているが、君はどんな使命を背負っていると思う？
example_sentences.english: It is said that every person has a mission that they are born with, but what kind of task do you think you have been burdened with?

example_sentences.japanese: 人は私が生まれながらにしてフルートの才能を持っていたと言いますが、これは努力の結果です。
example_sentences.english: People say that I was born with a talent for the flute, but this is the result of effort.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖母が涙ながらに広島での被曝体験を語る姿を見て、二度と核兵器が使用されない事を祈らずにはいられなかった。
example_sentences.english: Seeing my grandmother talk about her experience of being bombed in Hiroshima while crying, I couldn't help but pray that atomic weapons are never used again.

example_sentences.japanese: 料理レシピサイト：「むかしながらのオムライスの作り方を簡単で分かりやすい動画で紹介しています。」
example_sentences.english: A site with cooking recipes: 'With this simple and easy-to-understand video, we will introduce a traditional omuraisu recipe.' (as it was long ago)

general_translation: While... ~ing, Remaining, Not or ever since, Keep or leave
formation: Verb［た］+ なり + （で）+ Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ なり + （で）+ Phrase
explanation: A formal expression highlighting that while (A) remains in its completed state, (B) became, or arose.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は腰かけたなりじっと考えていた。
example_sentences.english: While remaining seated, he has been pondering intently.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟は彼女に振られて部屋に入ったなり、全然部屋から出てこなくなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Ever since my brother locked himself in his room after his girlfriend broke up with him, he hasn't come out of his room at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が釣りにいったなりまだ帰ってこない、大丈夫かな...
example_sentences.english: My father hasn't come back home since he went out fishing. I wonder if he is okay…

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は上京したなり、帰ってこない。
example_sentences.english: My older brother hasn't come back, ever since he moved to Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: 町を離れたなり消息は途絶えた。
example_sentences.english: We haven't heard from her ever since she left the city.

example_sentences.japanese: ３年前に涙ながらに家出したなり、帰ってこない。
example_sentences.english: She ran away three years ago in tears, and hasn't come back (ever) since.

example_sentences.japanese: レース後、草の上に横になったなり、泣き続けた。
example_sentences.english: After the race, he cried while lying down on the grass.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿泊客の一人がドアを開けたなりにしてあります。
example_sentences.english: One of the hotel guests left the doors open.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は写真を見つめたなり、まばたきせずに目を見開いていた。
example_sentences.english: She kept staring at the picture intently, without blinking, with her eyes wide open.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと叱っただけで息子は自室に入ったなり、一向に出てこなくなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: After scolding my son just a little bit, ever since entering his room, he will not come out at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校に出かけたなり夜になっても帰ってこない娘を家族総出で探しています。
example_sentences.english: After not returning home even late at night ever since heading to school, the whole family has been searching together for my daughter.

example_sentences.japanese: 核心に迫る質問を投げかけると、夫は下を向いたなり黙り込んでしまいました。
example_sentences.english: After throwing out a question aimed right at the heart of the issue, while looking down, my husband was completely silent.

example_sentences.japanese: 子猫は背の高い木の枝から落ちたなりピクリとも動かなくなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Ever since falling from the branch of a high tree, my kitten started to not even move an inch.

example_sentences.japanese: これから一人暮らしを始める息子が家から出たなり、妻は声を出して泣き始めました。
example_sentences.english: While our son was leaving home to start living independently from now on, my wife called out and began crying.

example_sentences.japanese: 部活から帰ってきた弟が玄関に倒れ込んだなり寝てしまった姿を見て、弟が相当疲れている事がわかりました。
example_sentences.english: Seeing the figure of my little brother remain asleep in the entrance to our house ever since having fallen over after returning home from club activities, I realized that he was considerably worn-out.

general_translation: Ultimate, Extreme, Utter, Epitome, Peak
formation: Noun + の + 極（きわ）み
casual_structure: Noun + の + 極（きわ）み
explanation: A formal phrase showing that (A) is the ultimate something. (A) is the polar extreme.

example_sentences.japanese: タイトル：「シンプルのきわみ！絶品『ハンバーグ』の作り方」
example_sentences.english: Title: 'The epitome of simplicity! The recipe for a perfect Hamburg steak.'

example_sentences.japanese: あと５分待って居れば私が大好きなアイドルに会えていたとは...痛恨のきわみだ。
example_sentences.english: If only I had waited five more minutes, I would have met my favorite idol... It's the peak of despair.

example_sentences.japanese: 今までこんなに良くしてくれて、感激のきわみです。
example_sentences.english: I am beyond thrilled that you have been so good to me so far.

example_sentences.japanese: 有給は取るなとか鬼畜のきわみだ。
example_sentences.english: Telling us to not take paid time off? That's the epitome of being evil.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな景色がいいところで、こんな美味しい料理を食べられるなんて、なんて贅沢のきわみだ。
example_sentences.english: It's the ultimate luxury to be able to eat such delicious food in such a scenic place.

example_sentences.japanese: この曲の歌詞は感動のきわみで、聞くたびに涙が溢れ出てくる。
example_sentences.english: The lyrics of this song are the peak of emotion and bring tears to my eyes every time I listen to it.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震によってビルに閉じ込められた人々は混乱のきわみにあった。
example_sentences.english: The people trapped in the building due to the earthquake were in extreme (utter) turmoil.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「ダイモス王はこの報道を聞いて、驚きのきわみに達しました。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Hearing the news, the King Daimos reached the very peak of surprise.'

example_sentences.japanese: 目上の人にはじめて出会う時：「お目に掛かることができ、光栄のきわみです。」
example_sentences.english: When meeting a superior for the first time: 'It is an extreme honor to be able to meet you.'

example_sentences.japanese: 釈迦様は当初贅沢のきわみを尽くした生活をしていた。
example_sentences.english: At first, Buddha lived an utterly luxurious life.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫カフェで癒しのきわみを体験し、仕事での疲れが全て取れました。
example_sentences.english: Experiencing the ultimate therapy of being at a cat cafe, all of my weariness from work was completely removed.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行で立ち寄ったお寺であの歌手にバッタリ会えるとは感激のきわみです！
example_sentences.english: Bumping into that musician while stopping by a temple on holiday was the epitome of being overwhelmed with emotion.

example_sentences.japanese: あと一問でも合っていれば試験に合格していたとは…痛恨のきわみだ。
example_sentences.english: To think that I would have passed the examination if only one more question was right, it's the peak of despair.

example_sentences.japanese: 客室にプライベートの露天風呂とプールが付いているなんて、なんて贅沢のきわみなのだろう…。
example_sentences.english: Something like a guest room equipped with a private open air bath and pool, it's the ultimate luxury, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 疲労のきわみに達している父を元気付けるため、マッサージと居酒屋に連れて行く事にしました。
example_sentences.english: Having reached the extreme exhaustion, in order to cheer dad up, I decided to take him with me to get a massage and to an izakaya.

example_sentences.japanese: 少し前までヨチヨチ歩きしか出来なかった姪が今となっては学校で学級委員長を務めているなんて、感激のきわみです。
example_sentences.english: To think that my niece, who until just a while ago could do nothing but toddle around, is now serving as the class president, it is the peak of emotion.

example_sentences.japanese: レストランサイト：「寿司 - 日本のきわみ、主に米飯に魚介類など組み合わせた和食です。」
example_sentences.english: Restaurant website: 'Sushi - the epitome of Japan. This Japanese-style meal is made by combining fish and shellfish with cooked rice.'

general_translation: For (A), In the case of (A), From (A)'s point of view, In the eyes of (A)
formation: Noun + にしてみれば(1)(1) にしてみたら
casual_structure: Noun + にしてみれば(1)(1) にしてみたら
explanation: A hypothetical construction, examining something from (A)'s point of view. If going off how (A) would see it, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ハリーにしてみれば、優しくしてもらうなど、初めての経験だった。
example_sentences.english: For Harry, it was the first time he had ever been treated kindly.(From the perspective of Harry)

example_sentences.japanese: 上級者には簡単かもしれないが、初心者にしてみればかなり難しいと思う。
example_sentences.english: For someone who is experienced it may be easy, but for someone new, I think it would be difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人の私にしてみれば、日本語は簡単だけど英語は難しい。
example_sentences.english: As a Japanese person, Japanese is easy, but English is hard.

example_sentences.japanese: アニメをあまり知らない人にしてみれば、ポケモンもデジモンも同じアニメだ。
example_sentences.english: From the point of view of someone who doesn't watch anime, Pokemon and Digimon are the same anime.

example_sentences.japanese: 傍から見ればただの安っぽいペンダントだろうが、ラクにしてみれば貴重な思い出の品になっている。
example_sentences.english: It might appear to be a mere cheap pendant from the side, but for Raku, it has become a precious memento.(From the perspective of Raku)

example_sentences.japanese: 大人には非常に簡単だが、小さな子供にしてみればかなり困難なことかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: For an adult, it is very simple, but for a small child, it might be quite hard.(From the perspective of a small child)

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちにとっては危険すぎるようにみえる彼の生活は、彼自身にしてみればごく普通のことなのでしょう。
example_sentences.english: His life that seems too dangerous to us, is likely quite ordinary for him.(From his perspective)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１は失敗した友達２を励ます、友達１：「たいしたことじゃありませんよ。」友達２：「いや、わたしにしてみたら、たいしたことなんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Friend 1 reassuring Friend 2 who has made a mistake, Friend 1: 'Come on, it's not a big deal!'Friend 2: 'No, this is a big deal FOR me!'(From my perspective)

example_sentences.japanese: 先生にしてみれば、三十人もいる生徒の名前と顔を覚える事は一苦労だろう。
example_sentences.english: For a teacher, remembering the names and faces of 30 students has to be a pain, right?

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんにしてみたら、商品の値段が上がる事はただのマイナスでしかない。
example_sentences.english: For a customer, the rising price of a product is nothing more than a negative.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者にしてみれば出鱈目だと分かる嘘の健康法も、一般人には見分けられません。
example_sentences.english: Even health methods that are recognizably garbage lies for a doctor are indiscernible for a regular person.

example_sentences.japanese: 母のように綺麗好きの人にしてみれば、私の家はまるでゴミ屋敷のように見えるのでしょう。
example_sentences.english: For a person that loves cleanliness like my mom, my house must appear almost as though it were a hoarder's shack, don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は冗談のつもりだったが、彼にしてみれば笑い事ではなくて３週間彼女と話さなかった。
example_sentences.english: She intended it as a joke, but for him, it wasn't a laughing matter, and he didn't talk to her for three weeks.(From his perspective)

example_sentences.japanese: 滅多に怒らない仏のような彼にしてみれば、少しの事で怒る私は別の人種に見えるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: From his point of view as someone who rarely gets angry, just like a Buddha, I, who gets angry at even a small thing, must appear as a different species of human.

example_sentences.japanese: 大金持ちの木下さんにしてみたら、私達が悩むような家電や車の買い物も全て即決してしまうのだろう。
