formation: Noun + （の(1)) + ゆえ + （に）Noun + （の(1)) + ゆえ + の + Noun［な］Adjective + （な(1)）+ ゆえ + （に）［な］Adjective + （な(1)）+ ゆえ + の + Noun［い］Adjective + （が）+ ゆえ + （に）［い］Adjective + （が）+ ゆえ +  の + NounVerb + （が）+ ゆえ + （に）Verb + （が）+ ゆえ +  の + NounPhrase (A)。（その(2)）+ ゆえ + に+Phrase (B) (1) である、が、であるが(2) それ、それが
casual_structure: Noun + （の(1)) + ゆえ + （に）Noun + （の(1)) + ゆえ + の + Noun［な］Adjective + （な(1)）+ ゆえ + （に）［な］Adjective + （な(1)）+ ゆえ + の + Noun［い］Adjective + （が）+ ゆえ + （に）［い］Adjective + （が）+ ゆえ +  の + NounVerb + （が）+ ゆえ + （に）Verb + （が）+ ゆえ +  の + NounPhrase (A)。（その(2)）+ ゆえ + に+Phrase (B) (1) である、が、であるが(2) それ、それが
explanation: A formal structure, highlighting that something is due to (A). As a consequence of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ラテン語のフレーズ：「不合理ゆえにわれ信ず 」
example_sentences.english: Latin phrase: 'I believe just because it is absurd.'

example_sentences.japanese: お巡りさんたちが夜も眠らずにパトロールしているがゆえに、夜でも安心して散歩できる。
example_sentences.english: Due to the police officers patrolling the area at night without sleep, it makes it safe for us to go on walks at night.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のおじいちゃんは目が悪いがゆえに、運転免許証を返納した。
example_sentences.english: My grandpa had to give up his driver's license because of his bad eyesight.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の接客は丁寧なゆえに、お客さんからの評判がいい。
example_sentences.english: His customer service is courteous and therefore well received by his customers.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本ではまだ女性のゆえに差別されることがある。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, women are still discriminated against because of their gender.

example_sentences.japanese: あの国では高齢化が深刻な問題になってきている。ゆえに、海外から若者を呼び込み始めた。
example_sentences.english: Aging is becoming a serious problem in that country. Due to that, they have started to attract young people from abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 若さゆえの過ちであったとしても必ず許さなければならないということでもない。
example_sentences.english: Just because something was done due to a young age, doesn't mean that it should be forgiven.

example_sentences.japanese: 手紙：「季節の変わり目ゆえ、くれぐれもご自愛くださいませ。」
example_sentences.english: Letter: 'Since the seasons are changing, please take good care of yourself.' (due to)

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「ベンジャミンのわかさゆえの自信過剰も無知もミセス・ロビンソンの目からすれば、可愛らしい。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'From the perspective of Mrs. Robinson, Benjamin's overconfidence and naivety, due to his youthfulness, is charming.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ⇒Ｂ、Ｂ⇒ＣゆえにＡ⇒Ｃ (Ａが真ならばＢも真、Ｂが真ならばＣも真。ゆえにＡが真ならばＣも真である）
example_sentences.english: A⇒B、B⇒C therefore A⇒C (If A, then B, if B then C. Therefore if A, then C)

example_sentences.japanese: ファンタジー小説：「 ドワーフ族が滅んだのは富に対する飽くなき欲望ゆえであった。」
example_sentences.english: Fantasy novel: 'The reason for the dwarves' undoing was their untiring desire for wealth.'

example_sentences.japanese: セリアック病や小麦アレルギーを持っているゆえに菓子パンのような甘いものすら食べられない人も存在する。
example_sentences.english: There are some people who cannot even eat sweets like 'kashipan' because they have celiac disease or a wheat allergy.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の美春に彼氏が出来ないのは、彼女の自分勝手さゆえである。
example_sentences.english: The reason my friend Miharu cannot get a boyfriend is her self-centeredness.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は旧友からからかわれる事が多いが、それは僕の人当たりの良さゆえだ。
example_sentences.english: There are many things that I was made fun of by my old friends about, but they were due to my attitude.

example_sentences.japanese: 叔母は完璧主義で理想が高すぎるゆえに、完璧ではない自分が嫌になり自殺してしまった。
example_sentences.english: As a consequence of my auntie's too-high ideals with perfectionism, she began to hate her imperfect self and unfortunately took her own life.

example_sentences.japanese: 貧しさゆえに窃盗を繰り返してしまう人を見る度に、この社会の不公平さが嫌になります。
example_sentences.english: Every time I see people that repeatedly burgle due to their poorness, I begin to dislike this society's injustice.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はあなたを愛しているので、あなたが過去に若さゆえの過ちを犯してしまった事を受け入れます。
example_sentences.english: Because I love you, I accept the things that were your indiscretions in the past as a consequence of your youth.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機は船や車とは違って短時間で長距離を移動できるがゆえに、旅行シーズンになると多くの人に利用される。
example_sentences.english: Unlike things like boats or cars, as a consequence of planes being able to traverse long distances in a short time, they are utilized by many people in the travel season. (due to)

general_translation: Every single, Each and every, Emphasis, Everything that could be called
formation: Noun (A) + という + Noun (A)
casual_structure: Noun (A) + という + Noun (A)
explanation: A grammar point implying each and every (A). All (A)'s that can be called (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「今日という今日は許さん。」
example_sentences.english: 'I absolutely will not allow it TODAY.' (emphasis)

example_sentences.japanese: 空き家に入ったら床という床が全てゴミに覆われていたのでびっくりした。
example_sentences.english: When I entered the vacant house, I was surprised because the entire floor was covered in garbage.

example_sentences.japanese: この街の電柱という電柱に広告の張り紙が沢山貼られてあったので、街の人たちが張り紙を全て撤去した。
example_sentences.english: There were so many advertising posters on every single telephone pole in this city that the people of the city removed all the posters.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界各国の偉い人たちが来るということで、サミットの近くの道という道は閉鎖されている。
example_sentences.english: Every single road near the summit was closed due to the fact that important people from all over the world are coming.

example_sentences.japanese: 政治家という政治家はみんな口ばっかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Every single politician is nothing but talk.

example_sentences.japanese: それを聞いて、人という人が一斉に頷いた。
example_sentences.english: Every single person nodded in unison when they heard that.

example_sentences.japanese: 山々に生えた木という木は地すべりのため根こそぎ倒れていた。
example_sentences.english: Every single tree that was growing on the mountain collapsed due to the landslide.

example_sentences.japanese: 名古屋に生まれて名古屋で育った。だから、町中の道という道、家という家を、すっかり知っている。
example_sentences.english: (They were) born and raised in Nagoya. Therefore, (they) know every single street and each and every house in the city.

example_sentences.japanese: この間の大地震で学校の壁という壁にヒビが入ってしまい、校舎の建て直しが決まった。
example_sentences.english: Cracks appeared in every single wall with the recent large earthquake, and the school building's reconstruction was decided.

example_sentences.japanese: 教授は生徒の顔という顔が曇っている事に気づき、同じ説明をもう一度繰り返しました。
example_sentences.english: Noticing that each and every student's face was gloomy, the teacher repeated the same explanation one more time.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生：「ウイルスが部屋に溜まらないように、窓という窓を開けて換気をしましょう！」
example_sentences.english: Sensei: 'In order to prevent accumulation of the virus, let's open every single window.'

example_sentences.japanese: ゴールデンウィークの最終日は帰宅ラッシュのせいで道路という道路が混んでいました。
example_sentences.english: Due to the homecoming rush on the last day of Golden Week, each and every road was congested.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕がセナの部屋に入ると、壁という壁にヨゾラの写真があるのを見てショックを受けた。
example_sentences.english: When I went into Sena's room, I was shocked to see that every single wall was decorated with photos of Yozora.

example_sentences.japanese: ある調査によると、若者という若者がこの国の将来には希望が無いと思っているそうだ。
example_sentences.english: According to a certain study, it is thought that every single young person has no hope for this country's immediate future.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名人になってから通りですれ違う人という人が私にサインを求めてくるので、もはや気軽に外を出歩く事は出来ません。
example_sentences.english: Due to each and every person I pass on the street wanting my signature since becoming famous, I am no longer able to heedlessly go for a walk outside.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日という今日は絶対あいつを許さない！
example_sentences.english: I will not forgive him today of all days!

example_sentences.japanese: 今度という今度は優勝してみせる！
example_sentences.english: I will win THIS TIME!

general_translation: Not limited to, Not only...but also, Not stopping at
formation: Verb + にとどまらずNoun + （である）+ にとどまらず［な］Adjective + である + にとどまらず
casual_structure: Verb + にとどまらずNoun + （である）+ にとどまらず［な］Adjective + である + にとどまらず
explanation: A formal structure, showing that something is not limited to (A). Not stopping at (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 共感は人間にとどまらず、動物にも見られるものである。
example_sentences.english: Compassion is not only limited to humans but is something that can also be observed in animals.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は会社の経費を管理するにとどまらず、社員の給料も管理している。
example_sentences.english: He not only manages the company's expenses, but also the salaries of its employees.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は授業を行うにとどまらず、部活の指導などもしなくてはならない。
example_sentences.english: Teachers must not only teach classes, but also supervise club activities.

example_sentences.japanese: 寿司は日本にとどまらず、世界中で人気がある。
example_sentences.english: Sushi is popular not only in Japan but all over the world.

example_sentences.japanese: この漫画は子供にとどまらず、大人の間でも話題になっている。
example_sentences.english: This manga is not limited to children, but has become a topic of conversation among adults as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 先日の悪夢が夢にとどまらず、まさか現実になってしまうとは…。
example_sentences.english: It is unbelievable that yesterday's nightmare was not only a dream, but would actually happen in reality…

example_sentences.japanese: ボックスステーション７、日本国内にとどまらず、海外でも普及しています。
example_sentences.english: Boxstation7 is not only popular in Japan, but also abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の学習によって語学力にとどまらず、日本風の考え方も身に着ける。
example_sentences.english: By studying Japanese, one does not only acquire linguistic ability but also a Japanese way of thinking.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社ウェブサイト：「当社は製品を販売するにとどまらず、その商品の設計もいたします。」
example_sentences.english: Company website: 'Our company is not only selling products but also designing them.'

example_sentences.japanese: 間博士の研究分野は遺伝学にとどまらず、微生物学にまで及ぶ。
example_sentences.english: Doctor Hazama's field of research is not limited to genetics, but it also extends to microbiology.

example_sentences.japanese: 近年ではＫ-ＰＯＰは韓国内にとどまらず、世界中で大人気となっています。
example_sentences.english: Limited not only to within Korea, K-pop has become popular worldwide as of late.

example_sentences.japanese: 飼い猫の癌が足にとどまらず全身に転移している事を受け、急いで治療を受けさせる事にした。
example_sentences.english: Accepting that my pet cat's cancer is not limited to her leg, but has moved to her whole body, I quickly decided to make her undertake treatment.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が運営しているフィットネスの利用者は若い男女にとどまらず、高齢者や障害者にまで及びます。
example_sentences.english: Among my fitness operation’s consumers, not limited to young men and women, they also extend to the elderly and handicapped.

example_sentences.japanese: そのアイドルは外見の良さにとどまらず歌唱力やコミュニケーション能力も高い。
example_sentences.english: Not stopping at her good looks, that idol also has things like high singing skills and communication ability.

example_sentences.japanese: 大雨による被害は洪水だけにとどまらず、山岳地方では多くの場所で地滑りが発生した。
example_sentences.english: With damages not only limited to flooding due to the heavy rain, there were also many areas in the mountain region where landslides occured.

example_sentences.japanese: このＮＧＯは絶対的貧困の撲滅にとどまらず、相対的貧困の削減にも取り組んでいます。
example_sentences.english: This NGO not only works to eliminate absolute poverty, but also addresses the reduction of relative poverty.

example_sentences.japanese: 国内で一位を争うほどの人気を誇るテーマパークは、休日にとどまらず平日も混雑しているそうです。
example_sentences.english: Among the national theme parks that boast popularity to the degree of fighting for the number one spot, I heard that they are crowded not only on the weekends, but also weekdays.

example_sentences.japanese: このコンサートのチケットにとどまらず、限定グッズなども高かった。
example_sentences.english: Not only were tickets to this concert expensive, but also limited edition merchandise. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Thought...but, When...thought that...but, Despite having thought...
formation: Verb + （か）+ と思（おも）いきや + Phrase［た］［い］Adjective + （か）+ と思（おも）いきや + Phrase［た］［な］Adjective + (か(1)）+ と思（おも）いきや + Phrase［た］Noun + (か(1)）+ と思（おも）いきや + Phrase［た］(1)（だ）
casual_structure: Verb + （か）+ と思（おも）いきや + Phrase［た］［い］Adjective + （か）+ と思（おも）いきや + Phrase［た］［な］Adjective + (か(1)）+ と思（おも）いきや + Phrase［た］Noun + (か(1)）+ と思（おも）いきや + Phrase［た］(1)（だ）
explanation: A strong expression, implying that just when (A) was thought, unexpectedly it was actually (B).

example_sentences.japanese: いよいよ晴れるだろうとおもいきや、たちまち雨が降り出してしまった。
example_sentences.english: I thought that the weather would finally clear up, but it suddenly started raining.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女たちは姉妹だとおもいきや、親子だった。
example_sentences.english: I thought that they were sisters, but they were mother and daughter.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日も残業するかとおもいきや、４時になったと同時に上司が「みんな、毎日お疲れさん、今日は早めに帰って、ゆっくりしてくれ」と言ってくれたから定時前に帰ることができた。
example_sentences.english: I thought I would have to work overtime again today, but as soon as it hit 4:00, my boss said, 'Hey guys, thanks for working hard every day, go home early today and relax,' so I was able to leave before the regular time.

example_sentences.japanese: 木村くんのピアノの先生は優しいとおもいきや、見学してみたらめちゃくちゃ怖くて厳しいということが分かった。
example_sentences.english: I thought that Kimura-kun's piano teacher was nice, but when I went to observe the class, I found out that she is very scary and strict.

example_sentences.japanese: 家を建てるのは簡単かとおもいきや、建てる前に色々土地の調査など測量などをしないといけなかったから思っていたより面倒だった。
example_sentences.english: I thought building a house would be easy, but it was more trouble than I expected because I had to do things such as survey and inspect the land before building.

example_sentences.japanese: 「やっぱり、今度も失敗したか...」とおもいきや、見事合格だった。
example_sentences.english: Despite having thought, 'As expected, I failed again,' I passed with flying colors.

example_sentences.japanese: うたげさんが小さいから同級生とおもいきや、驚くことに先生だった。
example_sentences.english: Because she was small (like me), I thought Utage-san was (my) classmate, but, to my surprise, she was (my) teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆はまずそうに見えるから、間違いなくまずいとおもいきや、実際は、そうではなかった。
example_sentences.english: I thought for sure that natto would be gross since it looks unappetizing, but that was not the case.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は部屋がとても静かだからきっと寝ているとおもいきや、意外にも勉強していた。
example_sentences.english: I thought that my daughter was sleeping because it was very quiet, but to my surprise she was studying.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は定時で帰れるとおもいきや、やはり定時の直前に新たな仕事を任されてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Despite having thought that I could return home at the regular time today, as expected, just before that I was requested to do some new work.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は二年も日本で留学したので日本語が話せるのかとおもいきや、全く話せなかった。
example_sentences.english: I thought that my older sister would be able to speak Japanese due to her 2 year study abroad in Japan, but she couldn't speak at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 十分も待った末にようやく電車が来たとおもいきや、その電車はここで折り返すそうだ。
example_sentences.english: After waiting for a suitably long time, just as I thought that the train was finally going to come, but I heard that that train was turning back around from here.

example_sentences.japanese: 確実にボールがゴールに入ったかとおもいきや、背が高い相手チームにブロックされてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Despite having thought that the ball had definitely gone in the goal, it was blocked by the tall opposing team.

example_sentences.japanese: 非常によく似ているので兄弟とおもいきや、実際には、単なる友達と知って驚きました。
example_sentences.english: I thought they were brothers because they were remarkably similar, but I was shocked to learn that they were just friends.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度の実習先の看護師達は怖いとおもいきや、見た目とは裏腹に非常に優しい人達でした。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought that the nurses here on placement would be scary, but contrary to their appearances, they were extraordinarily nice people.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間に余裕を持って問題を全て解き終わったとおもいきや、裏のページにもまだ沢山の問題が残っていました。
example_sentences.english: Having plenty of time, just when I thought that I had solved all of the problems, there were still lots of questions that remained on the reverse page.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は日本に１０年も住んでいるもんだから日本語をペラペラに話せると思いきや、少しも話せない。
example_sentences.english: He had lived in Japan for 10 years, so I thought that he could speak Japanese fluently, but he can't speak a word of it. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Cannot, There is no way one can, Nothing one can do, Cannot possibly not by any means, Cannot do no matter how hard one tries, Nothing will come out, It is meaningless to
formation: どうにも（こうにも） + (Negative)Verb［できる］どうにも（こうにも） + Verb［stem］+ ようがないどうにもできないどうにも（こうにも）ならない
casual_structure: どうにも（こうにも） + (Negative)Verb［できる］どうにも（こうにも） + Verb［stem］+ ようがないどうにもできないどうにも（こうにも）ならない
explanation: A strong phrase, emphasizing that no matter even how (A) is handled, nothing will come of it. (A) is meaningless.

example_sentences.japanese: あたしがいなきゃどうにもならないでしょ？
example_sentences.english: It seems that there is nothing you can do if I am not around?

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で読むだけじゃどうにも理解できないので、先生に聞くことにした。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't manage to understand it just by reading it myself, so I decided to ask my teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなことを言われてもどうにもこうにもなりません。
example_sentences.english: No matter what you say, nothing will come out of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 説明してあげたいけど、どうにもこうにも説明できない。
example_sentences.english: I would love to explain it for you, but there is no way I can explain it.

example_sentences.japanese: 今更頑張ってもどうにもならないよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you try your best now, nothing will come out of it.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなこと急に言われても、どうにもできないよ。
example_sentences.english: Nothing could be done, even if you suddenly tell me that.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「後悔したってもうどうにもなんない。」
example_sentences.english: Chat with a friend: 'Even if you regret it, nothing can be done now.'

example_sentences.japanese: どうにもできない事態に陥ったので手を借りるしかない。
example_sentences.english: I got trapped in a situation about which nothing could be done so I have no choice but to ask for help.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は人の言うことを聞かないからアドバイスしたところでどうにもならないよ。
example_sentences.english: She doesn't listen to what people say, so even if you give her advice, nothing will come out of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 「都心に向かう電車の中は、人でいっぱい。どうにも身動きしようがない。」
example_sentences.english: 'Trains heading downtown are packed with people. There is no way for one to move.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達のバイクを修理した後で：「やれるだけのことはやったけど、武田さんのバイクはどうにも修理できない。」
example_sentences.english: After repairing a friend's bike: 'I did all I could, but I couldn't repair Takeda's bike no matter what.'

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの夫が自分から態度を改善したいと思わない事には、どうにもならないよ。
example_sentences.english: Nothing will come of the situation if your husband doesn't want to improve his own attitude.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校の授業だけではどうにも理解できないので、塾へ通う事にしました。
example_sentences.english: Since there is no way I can understand classes just with school, I decided to start going to cram school.

example_sentences.japanese: 知識と技術を持った医師達がどうにも出来ないと言うのだから、もう僕は死を待つ事しか出来ないのだろう…。
example_sentences.english: Since the doctors who have skill and knowledge say that there is nothing they can do, I guess there is nothing left to do but wait for my death.

example_sentences.japanese: その患者は「どうにも寝付く事が出来ない」と病院に来たが、お昼まで寝ていて夜に寝付けないのは当然の事である。
example_sentences.english: That patient came to the hospital saying 'I cannot fall asleep no matter how hard I try', but since they sleep until midday, of course they cannot sleep at night.

example_sentences.japanese: 過去について「もしこうだったら…。」と考えてもどうにもならない事は理解していますが、考えずにはいられない時もあります。
example_sentences.english: I understand that nothing will come out of thinking that 'if only it was like this' about the past, but there are times where I cannot go without thinking about it as well.

general_translation: (And) so, Because, Since
formation: Verb + ことだし  ［い］Adjective + ことだし  ［な］Adjective + な(1)  + ことだし  Noun + の(1) + ことだし     (1) である
casual_structure: Verb + ことだし  ［い］Adjective + ことだし  ［な］Adjective + な(1)  + ことだし  Noun + の(1) + ことだし     (1) である
explanation: A construction used for listing reasons. It's the thing which is (A), amongst other things.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機代も安いことだし天気もいいから沖縄に行こうよ。
example_sentences.english: Since plane tickets are cheap and the weather is nice, let's go to Okinawa.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく君のお父さんとお母さんが来ることだし、どっかいい焼肉屋さんにでも行こう。
example_sentences.english: Since your father and mother are coming all the way (to see us), let's go to a nice yakiniku restaurant.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気もいいことだし、みんなで公園にでも行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: Since the weather is nice, let's all go to the park together.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が勤めている会社は有名なことだし、給料もいいんだろう。
example_sentences.english: Since the company he works for is famous, his salary must be good.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のことだし、また遅れてくるんじゃないの。
example_sentences.english: Knowing him, I bet that he will come late as usual.

example_sentences.japanese: 割引クーポンもあることだし、明日映画を一緒に観に行かない？
example_sentences.english: I also have discount coupons, so why don't we go watch a movie together tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: もう夜も更けてくることだし、今日のパーティはこれでお開きにしよう！
example_sentences.english: It's getting late, so let's call it a night with this!

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪を引いていることだし、今日くらいは何もしないでゆっくり休んだら？
example_sentences.english: Since you have caught a cold, at least for today, how about you rest without doing anything?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のことだし、きっと次の試合には勝つとわたしは信じているよ！
example_sentences.english: Knowing her, I am convinced that she will surely win the next match.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼も十分反省していることだし、今回はもうこの辺で許してあげたら？
example_sentences.english: I'm sure he's also sufficiently remorseful, so why won't you already let him off the hook this time?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は朝から重い物は嫌だ。それに徹夜しちゃったことだし軽い物が食べたいな。
example_sentences.english: I dislike eating heavy things in the morning. Plus, I have pulled an all-nighter so I want to eat something light.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気も悪いことだし、今日は外に出ずに家の中で勉強とか仕事をする事にしよう。
example_sentences.english: The weather is bad today, so I decided not to go outside, but to do things like study and work inside.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏が彼女に：「もう長年付き合ってきて互いを十分に理解していることだし、近々結婚するのはどう？」
example_sentences.english: A boyfriend to his girlfriend: 'Since we have been together for many years, and we both sufficiently understand what is going on, why don't we get married soon?'

example_sentences.japanese: まだ入社して三週間しか経っていないことだし、彼の失敗を大目に見ることにしよう。
example_sentences.english: Since it has only been 3 weeks since he entered the company, let's overlook his mistake.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学受験も終わったことだし、今日からは目一杯マンガを読んだりアニメを見たりして夜更かしするぞ！
example_sentences.english: Since the university acceptance exams are also finished, I am going to sit up all night doing things like reading manga and watching anime as much as possible!

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく高い学費を払って大学に通っていることだし、興味のある分野だけでなく他の分野の授業もとってみようかな〜。
example_sentences.english: Since I went to the effort of paying expensive tuition and am going to university, not only fields that I am interested in, but I will also try taking classes in other fields.

general_translation: Totally, Seriously, Completely, Furiously, Majorly
formation: ガン見ガン + Verb［stem］
casual_structure: ガン見ガン + Verb［stem］
explanation: A slangy prefix that emphasizes a verb and turns it into an irregular verb (する verb).

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が主人公の映画を見たら、過去に飼っていた愛犬とその犬を重ねてしまって、がんなきした。
example_sentences.english: When I watched a movie that had a dog as a main character, I imagined my old dog in its place and completely bawled my eyes out.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰も見ていないと思って、カーテンを開けたまま着替えていたら、向かいの部屋の人にがんみされてて、恐怖を覚えたよ。
example_sentences.english: I thought no one was watching so changed with the curtains open, but then I realized I was being majorly stared at by the person in the room across the way and felt terrified.

example_sentences.japanese: 残業を４時間もしたせいで、家に帰った途端に、ソファでがんねしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Because I worked four hours overtime, the second I got home, I completely conked out on the sofa.

example_sentences.japanese: 顧客の個人情報リストを失くしてしまって、上司にがんづめされた。
example_sentences.english: I lost the customer’s personal information list and got majorly pressed on it by my boss.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の帰りが遅くなった理由を、妻にがんづめされた。
example_sentences.english: My wife completely hounded me about why I came home late yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかくキャンプ用品を揃えたのに、雨なんてがんなえなんですけど。
example_sentences.english: I finally got all my camping gear together, but the rain is just a total buzzkill.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜ご飯いるよって言ってたから用意したのに、急にいらないなんて、がんぎれだわ。
example_sentences.english: I made dinner since you said you wanted it and now suddenly you say you don’t? I’m gonna totally lose it.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の娘がいじめられていたなんて、もう学校にがんぎれしに行くしかない。
example_sentences.english: You’re saying my daughter has been bullied? There’s nothing left for it but to go absolutely ballistic at the school.

example_sentences.japanese: あれだけ彼に会えることを楽しみにしていたのだから、彼女ががんなえするのも無理はないと思う。
example_sentences.english: Since she had been looking forward to seeing him that much, it’s understandable that she’s totally down.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女に振られたことがショックだったとはいえ、目の前でがんなきをしたら最後、もう復縁の望みなんて、１ミリもないよ。
example_sentences.english: Even though getting dumped by your girlfriend is a shock, once you completely bawl your eyes out right in front of her, there is not even a slither of hope of getting back together.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっとした冗談のつもりだったのに、彼女にとっては地雷だったみたいで、いきなりがんぎれされた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I’d meant it as a little joke, apparently it was a crazy sensitive topic for her and she furiously snapped at me.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、カラオケで深酒をした後に、そのままがんねをしてしまったので、起きた時には、２４時間も滞在したことになっていた。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday, after some heavy drinking at karaoke, I completely went out cold and, when I woke up, it turned out that I’d been there for 24 hours.

example_sentences.japanese: 最後までジュースを飲みたかったから、ストローで勢いよく吸ったんだよね。そしたら思いの外、大きい音が出ちゃって、周囲の人にがんみされたよ。
example_sentences.english: I wanted to drink my juice all the way to the end, so I sucked it up hard through the straw. But then, unexpectedly, it made a loud noise and I was totally gawked at by the people around me.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹に１日中がんむしされ続け、今日は一言も会話を交わしていない。
example_sentences.english: I was completely ignored by my little sister continuously today, so I am not chatting with her even a bit.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画館で大きなあくびをして、隣の人にがんみされて恥ずかしかった記憶がある。
example_sentences.english: I was majorly stared at by the person next to me when I let out a large yawn at the cinema, so it is an embarrassing memory.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車の中で転んで、周りの人たちにガン見されたときは恥ずかしさのあまり、泣いてしまった。
example_sentences.english: When I fell while on the train and everyone majorly stared at me, I cried from embarrassment.

example_sentences.japanese: 両親の電話をガン無視していたら家まで来られた。
example_sentences.english: When I completely ignored my parents' phone calls, they came to my house.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日も先輩にガン切れされたよ。
example_sentences.english: I was majorly scolded by my senpai again today.

general_translation: Whether or not
formation: Verb + か否（いな）か［い］Adjective + か否（いな）か［な］Adjective + （である）+ か否（いな）かNoun + （である）+ か否（いな）か
casual_structure: Verb + か否（いな）か［い］Adjective + か否（いな）か［な］Adjective + （である）+ か否（いな）かNoun + （である）+ か否（いな）か
explanation: A formal grammar point. Indicating that whether or not (A), (B). Although uncertain about it being (A) or not (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の人生に満足できるかいなか、それはあなたの頑張り次第である。
example_sentences.english: Whether you are satisfied or not with your own life is a result of your effort.

example_sentences.japanese: この授業を楽しむかいなかは自分次第だ。
example_sentences.english: Whether you enjoy this class or not is up to you.

example_sentences.japanese: 怖いかいなかは別として、この映画はとても面白かった。
example_sentences.english: Putting aside whether this movie was scary or not, it was really enjoyable.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人が貧乏であるかいなかは私たちには関係のないことです。
example_sentences.english: Whether that person is poor or not is none of our business.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人がこの子の父親かいなか、ＤＮＡ検査をしなくてはわからない。
example_sentences.english: We will never know if that man is the father of this child or not without a DNA test.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の会社を辞めて転職するかいなか、もう少し悩む事にしよう。
example_sentences.english: Whether I will resign from my current company and get a new job or not, I'll ponder on it a bit more.

example_sentences.japanese: イベントのサイト：「参加資格： 登録ユーザーであるかいなかを問わず、どなたでもご参加可能」
example_sentences.english: Event website: 'Entry qualifications: Regardless of whether you are a registered user or not, anyone can participate.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事のタイトル：「プロゲーマーは真のスポーツ選手かいなか。ｅスポーツ業界が直面するビザの問題」
example_sentences.english: Article title: 'Are pro gamers real athletes or not? The visa problem that eSports faces.' (whether or not)

example_sentences.japanese: サイト、クッキーファイルについて：「利用者はそのクッキーを受け入れるかいなかを決めることができますし、また、全部のクッキーを削除することもできます。」
example_sentences.english: Website, about cookie files: 'Users can decide whether or not they accept cookies. Users are also able to delete all accepted cookies anytime.'

example_sentences.japanese: 過去の間違いを気にしない事が長所であるかいなか、人によって意見が分かれるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Whether not caring about the mistakes of your past is a strong point or not is divided based on people's opinions.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当にこの男が殺人犯であるかいなか、もっと証拠を集めないと断定は出来ません。
example_sentences.english: Whether this man is really a murderer or not cannot be determined without gathering more evidence.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、語り手：「スウォン王は武力で反乱を鎮圧すべきかいなか、について迷っていた。」
example_sentences.english: A novel, narrator: 'King Su-won was hesitant about whether or not he should put the rebellion down by force.'

example_sentences.japanese: サイト：「我々のシステムは質問への回答が正しいかいなかは照会とデータベースとの比較によって決める。」
example_sentences.english: Website: 'Our system determines whether the answer to the question is correct (or not) by comparing the query with the database.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女からの交際の申し出を受け入れるべきかいなかを早く決めないといけないのは分かっているけど、もう少し時間が欲しいなぁ…。
example_sentences.english: I know that I have to quickly decide whether I ought to accept her relationship proposal or not, but I really want a bit more time.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が就職活動を早く終える事が出来るかいなかは君がそれにどの程度真剣に臨むかで決まるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not you will be able to quickly finish job hunting will be decided by the degree to which you seriously confront it.

example_sentences.japanese: サイバーセキュリティ会社のサイト：「怪しいかいなかの判断に迷うメールを受け取った場合は、どうぞそれを開かずにＬａｉｎ＠ｃｙｂｅｒｌａｎｄ．ｘｙｚまでご連絡をお願いします。」
example_sentences.english: Cybersecurity company website: 'In the event that you receive an email in which you are unable to determine whether or not it is suspicious, do not open it and please contact us at Lain＠cyberland.xyz.'

example_sentences.japanese: 君に全てを話すべきかいなか、夜通し考えていたんだ。
example_sentences.english: Throughout the night I was thinking about whether or not I ought to tell you everything.

example_sentences.japanese: イロハ銀行は、国内居住者かいなかを問わず、口座開設に対応しています。
example_sentences.english: Iroha Bank will deal with account openings whether or not you are a domestic resident or not.

example_sentences.japanese: それが真実であるかいなかにかかわらず、噂は広まっていった。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether that was the truth or not, the rumors continued to spread.

general_translation: Even if, If
formation: Verb［たら］(1) + Verb［た］+ で［い］Adjective［たら］(2) + ［い］Adjective(3) + で［な］Adjective + なら + ［な］Adjective + で(1) Verb［ば］(2) ［い］Adjective［ば］(3) ［い］Adjective［た］
casual_structure: Verb［たら］(1) + Verb［た］+ で［い］Adjective［たら］(2) + ［い］Adjective(3) + で［な］Adjective + なら + ［な］Adjective + で(1) Verb［ば］(2) ［い］Adjective［ば］(3) ［い］Adjective［た］
explanation: A hypothetical expression, implying that when doing (A), (A) comes with (B). (B) is usually a negative or unwanted truth about (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「もし失敗したらしっぱいしたで、また最初からやり直そうと思う。」
example_sentences.english: 'Even if I fail, I will do it again from the beginning.'

example_sentences.japanese: ニートになったらなったで大変だと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you become a NEET, I think it would still be tough.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日雨が降れば降ったでなんとかすればいい。
example_sentences.english: If it rains tomorrow, we can do something about it.

example_sentences.japanese: 大きい方が荷物とかいっぱい積めるけど、大きかったら大きいでデメリットがある。
example_sentences.english: The bigger the car, the more luggage it can carry, but if the car is big, there are many disadvantages.

example_sentences.japanese: 力がなくてもできる仕事は沢山あるから、弱ければ弱いでいい。
example_sentences.english: There are plenty of jobs that can be done even if you are weak.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌なら嫌で大丈夫！田中くんに頼むこともできるし。
example_sentences.english: If you hate it that's fine! Since you could also just request Tanaka-kun to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 「結婚したい。」「結婚したらしたで大変だよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I want to marry…''Even if you get married, it's (still) tough.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「また子供になりたいな。」「けど、子供になったらなったで子供なりの苦労があるよ」
example_sentences.english: 'I want to be a child again…''But, children have problems of their own even if you become (are) one.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「金は沢山あったらあったで悩みも増えるものだよ。」「それはそうだけど、でも、なかったらないで困るでしょ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Even if you have a lot of money, problems will also multiply.''That might be right, but even if you don't have any, then it's (still) troublesome.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「スーパーとかで高い棚に手が届けばいいんだけど、背が低ければひくいで、なんとかなるはずだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'It'd be nice if I could reach the high shelves in the supermarket and such, but I should be able to manage one way or the other even if I'm short.'

example_sentences.japanese: 遠く離れた場所に住む家族のことが恋しいけれど、あったら会ったで喧嘩をするはずだ。
example_sentences.english: I miss my family that lives far away, but even if I saw them, we are bound to just fight.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動をするのは確かに億劫だが、運動をしたらしたで気分も体調も良くなるのは事実だ。
example_sentences.english: While working out is indeed bothersome, it is a fact that if you exercise, your mood and condition will improve.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が欲しいとは思っていますが、子供がいたらいたで、時に子供がいない人を羨ましく思ってしまうでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I think that I want kids, but even if I had kids, I would sometimes be jealous of those that do not have them, right?

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに授業中は眠かったのに、休み時間に入ったらはいったで途端に眠気が覚めてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Despite being that tired during class, when it was break time, my tiredness went away instantly.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ったく、いつも、彼は、雨が降ったら降ったで『外に出かけられない』と文句を言うし、晴れたら晴れたで「暑い暑い」と文句を言う。」
example_sentences.english: 'Good grief, if it rains, he always complains that he cannot go outside, and if it's sunny he always complains that it's really hot.' (even if)

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋が寒かったのでエアコンの設定温度を一度上げたが、あげたら上げたで今度は部屋がムシムシしてきた。
example_sentences.english: I raised the temperature setting on the aircon in my room by one degree because it was cold, but even when I raised it just a bit, it got hot and humid this time.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は「試験に落ちたらおちたで浪人すればいい」と言うけど、僕は何としてでも浪人だけは避けるつもりです。
example_sentences.english: Although mom says 'even if you fail your exams, you can just have a gap year', I intend to avoid that no matter what it takes.

example_sentences.japanese: 難しい文法を見ると怯んでしまうけど、簡単なら簡単でやりがいはない。
example_sentences.english: It's daunting to see difficult grammar, but if it's easy then it's not worth doing. (This grammar point's meaning)

example_sentences.japanese: 辞めるなら辞めるでいいけど、後からやっぱりやめなければよかったとかって言わないでね。
example_sentences.english: If you want to quit, then go ahead and quit, but don't say later that you wish you hadn't quit after all. (The other なら～で meaning)

general_translation: As expected, Meant to, Supposed to, Destined to, Sure to
formation: (Intransitive) Verb［る］+ べくして + (Intransitive) Verb［る］(1)Verb［られる］［る］+ べくして + Verb［られる］［る］(1)(1)Verb［られる］［た］
casual_structure: (Intransitive) Verb［る］+ べくして + (Intransitive) Verb［る］(1)Verb［られる］［る］+ べくして + Verb［られる］［る］(1)(1)Verb［られる］［た］
explanation: A formal expression, showing that (A) is as expected, or destined to be. Going off that (A) ought to be the case, (A) happened.

example_sentences.japanese: タイトル：「俺の青春ラブコメはまちがいになるべくしてなった。」
example_sentences.english: Title: 'As expected, my romantic youth comedy was a blunder.' (meant to・supposed to・destined to)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女らはここ２年間毎日文句を言わずにトレーニングしてきたから、大会で勝つべくして勝ったんだ。
example_sentences.english: These girls have trained every day for the last two years without complaint, so as expected they won the competition.

example_sentences.japanese: 役所には何回もここに止まれの標識を設置するように訴えたが対応してくれなかったので、この事故は起こるべくして起こった。
example_sentences.english: We have asked the city office multiple times to install a stop sign here, but they never listened to us, so this accident was expected.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、彼女とは出会うべくして出会ったと感じることが多い。
example_sentences.english: Recently, I have been feeling that we were destined to meet.

example_sentences.japanese: 壊れた一時停止標識を放置した結果、起こるべくして起こった交通事故だ。
example_sentences.english: As expected, the result of neglecting a broken stop sign was a traffic accident. (meant to・supposed to・destined to)

example_sentences.japanese: 「これらの二人は、専門分野も年齢も共に近いゆえに出会うべくして出会ったと言えるだろう。」
example_sentences.english: As expected, one can say that these two met because they both shared fields of expertise and were close in age. (meant to・supposed to・destined to)

example_sentences.japanese: 不景気か否かにかかわらず、高品質で適正価格の商品は売れるべくして売れている。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether there is a recession or not, products of good quality and reasonable price are sure to sell. (meant to・supposed to・expected to)

example_sentences.japanese: 好景気が遅かれ早かれ終わるのは経済学者にとって当然のことであったし、そうなるべくしてなった。
example_sentences.english: To the economists, it was only natural that prosperity will end sooner or later, and, as expected, that's what happened. (meant to・supposed to・destined to)

example_sentences.japanese: 今回、ユーザーさんはＪＬＰＴ Ｎ１に合格すべくして合格した。なぜなら、毎日のように勉強したからだ。
example_sentences.english: User-san passed the JLPT N1 exam, as expected. It is because they studied hard enough every day. (meant to・supposed to・destined to)

example_sentences.japanese: 全ての人が生まれるべくして生まれたと言う人がいるが、では私はなぜ生まれたのだろうか…。
example_sentences.english: There are people that say everyone that is born as supposed to be, but I wonder why I was born…

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のプレゼンの準備にはそれほど時間をかけなかったし、この失敗は起こるべくして起きました。
example_sentences.english: Because I didn't put much time into preparing this presentation, as expected it was a failure.

example_sentences.japanese: その社員の自殺は起こるべくして起こった。なぜなら誰もが会社の環境が劣悪だと知っていたからだ。
example_sentences.english: That employee was sure to take his own life. It's because everybody knew that that company's work environment was inadequate.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日喧嘩ばかりで落ち着いて話し合いをする事が出来なかった二人だ。彼らは別れるべくして別れたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: They were a couple that fought every day and could not calmly talk with each other. They were destined to break up.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の息子は寝る間も惜しんで毎日必死に勉強した結果、受験に合格するべくして合格しました。
example_sentences.english: As a result of my son studying furiously every day without sparing any time for sleep, he passed his exams as expected.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の彼氏の事を知るほど、そして共通点を見つけるほど、私達は出会うべくして出会ったのだと思う。
example_sentences.english: As far as I know my current boyfriend, and mutual points that I have found, I think that we were destined to meet.

general_translation: As (one likes, feels or pleases), Spur of the moment, Wherever one fancies, Spontaneously, On a whim
formation: Verb［る］+ （が）+ まま（に）
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ （が）+ まま（に）
explanation: A phrase emphasizing that (A) is done as is, without any alteration caused by unnecessary thought. On a whim, or as one pleases.

example_sentences.japanese: 足の向くままにバイクで駆けていたら公園に行き着いてしまったのだ。
example_sentences.english: I was biking where my feet took me and ended up in a park.

example_sentences.japanese: これはもうあなたのものだから、自分が思うままに使えばいいよ。
example_sentences.english: This is yours now, so you can use it as you see fit.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はしばらくの間一人で、足の向くままに旅をする。
example_sentences.english: I will be alone for a while, traveling wherever my feet take me.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法とかは気にしなくていい！ただ思いつくままに書いてくれればいい。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to worry about grammar! Just write whatever comes to mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 抽象画家は深く考えずに形や色を気の向くままに選ぶ。
example_sentences.english: Abstract painters choose shapes and colors as they please, without thinking deeply about them.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「ジラヤさんはどこ？」Ｂ：「わからん。どこかに行ったんだ。」Ａ：「相変わらず、風の吹くまま、赴くなぁ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Where is Jiraya?'B: 'Dunno. He went somewhere.'A: 'As always, he goes wherever the wind takes him.'

example_sentences.japanese: ふぶき：「そのあと、どうするつもり？」さいたま：「ただ心の欲するまま、自由に生きる。」
example_sentences.english: Fubuki: 'What are you going to do after that?'Saitama: 'I will simply live freely, as I desire.'

example_sentences.japanese: モーガンさん、クリスチャンさんに：「あなたのものですから気兼ねなく自分の思うままに扱ってもいいです。」
example_sentences.english: Mr. Morgan to Mr. Christian: 'It belongs to you, so feel free to handle it as you please.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「彼女は特に行き先も目的も考えず足の向くままに歩き続けた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'She kept on going as her feet led her, without any particular goal or destination in mind.'

example_sentences.japanese: 暇なので足の向くままに散歩をしていたら、気づかないうちに隣町までやって来ていた。
example_sentences.english: When I was walking wherever my feet lead me because I had spare time, I had come to the neighboring town without even noticing.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分が思うままに夢を追いかける事が出来たのは、父と母が支えてくれたからです。
example_sentences.english: Being able to pursue my dreams as I pleased was due to the support of my mother and father.

example_sentences.japanese: 他の社員が遠慮する中で思うままに意見を言ったところ、社長に気に入られました。
example_sentences.english: When I spontaneously said my opinion among other employees who hold theirs back, I started to be liked by the boss.

example_sentences.japanese: 他人を思うままに操ろうと心理学を学び始めたが、結果としてそのような事は出来ないと学んだ。
example_sentences.english: I started to study psychology so that I could manipulate others as I please, but it just ended up with me learning that something like that is not possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 筆者とのインタビュー：「これまで、思いつくままにいろいろと書いてきましたが、出来が良くないような気がしましたので出版しないことに決めました。」
example_sentences.english: Interview with an author: 'Previously, I wrote many things as they spontaneously came to my mind, but because I felt the end product was not very good, I decided not to publish them.'

example_sentences.japanese: 老後は時間やお金の心配をせずに気の向くままに旅行に行きたいと考えているので、そのために今は必死にお金を貯めています。
example_sentences.english: Since I think that I would like to travel wherever I fancy in my old age, without worrying about things like time or money, I am currently frantically saving money to that end.

general_translation: Or, Either or
formation: ［い］Adjective［い］+ かれ + ［い］Adjective［い］(Antonym) + かれ遅（おそ）かれ早（はや）かれ - sooner or later多（おお）かれ少（すく）なかれ - more or lessto a greater or lesser extent良（よ）かれ悪（あ）しかれ - good or badfor better or worse
casual_structure: ［い］Adjective［い］+ かれ + ［い］Adjective［い］(Antonym) + かれ遅（おそ）かれ早（はや）かれ - sooner or later多（おお）かれ少（すく）なかれ - more or lessto a greater or lesser extent良（よ）かれ悪（あ）しかれ - good or badfor better or worse
explanation: An old-fashioned construction, contrasting opposite adjectives. Although it is uncertain whether it will be via (A) or (B), (C) will still happen.

example_sentences.japanese: 「こんなにタバコを吸い続けてはおそかれはやかれ病気になるだろう。」
example_sentences.english: 'If you keep on smoking like this, sooner or later you will get sick.'

example_sentences.japanese: どんな人でも多かれ少なかれ悩みを抱えて生きている。
example_sentences.english: Whether it be to a higher or lesser extent, everyone lives burdened by troubles.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑かれ寒かれ、脱水症状は起こりうるので水分補給はこまめにしてください。
example_sentences.english: Dehydration can occur in hot or cold weather, so please hydrate frequently.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅かれ早かれ提出させないといけないのであるならば、早めに提出した方がいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: If it has to be submitted sooner or later, I think it is better to submit it as soon as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: この発見はよかれあしかれ、大きな変化をもたらすだろう。
example_sentences.english: For better or worse, this discovery will bring great change.

example_sentences.japanese: 好奇心はおおかれすくなかれ誰もが持っているものだろう。
example_sentences.english: Curiosity is something that everybody has, to a greater or lesser extent.

example_sentences.japanese: おそかれはやかれ有人火星探査の時代はやってくるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: I am sure that sooner or later, the era of manned missions to Mars will come.

example_sentences.japanese: よかれあしかれ、確かに社会がキャッシュレス化する傾向が続いている。
example_sentences.english: For better or worse, the trend of society turning cashless continues.

example_sentences.japanese: おおかれすくなかれ、どんな親も子育てに対して常に悩みを持っているものです。
example_sentences.english: To a greater or lesser extent, all parents constantly have concerns about bringing up their children.

example_sentences.japanese: 研究によるとあらゆる頭部外傷はおおかれすくなかれ脳に影響を及ぼすということだ。
example_sentences.english: According to research, all kinds of head trauma affect the brain to a greater or lesser extent.

example_sentences.japanese: 違法薬物の使用を続けている彼女は、おそかれはやかれ後悔する事になるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Continuing to use unlawful drugs, she will probably start to regret it sooner or later.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、誰もがおおかれすくなかれ人には言えない秘密を隠し持っていると考えています。
example_sentences.english: I think that everyone to a greater or lesser extent has hidden secrets that they will not tell anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: ストレスをアルコールで発散するような生活を続けていたらおそかれはやかれ病院送りになってしまうよ。
example_sentences.english: If you continue to lead a lifestyle of shaking off stress with alcohol, sooner or later you will end up in the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日必死に日本語の勉強をしているのだから、おそかれはやかれあなたが日本語を習得する日が来るでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Because you continue to fervently study Japanese every day, sooner or later the day will come where you have acquired the skill, right?

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが他人に対してとる態度は、 よかれあしかれ、いずれ自分に返ってくるものだと思いなさい。
example_sentences.english: In regard to the attitude that you adopt toward other people, you better believe that for better or worse it will all come back to you at some point.

example_sentences.japanese: この発明は、良かれ悪しかれたくさんの人に影響を与えるだろう。
example_sentences.english: This invention will affect a lot of people, for better or worse.

general_translation: Cannot even...if wants, Would like to...but cannot, Wants to...but cannot
formation: Verb［る］(A) + に + Verb［できる］［ない］(A)
casual_structure: Verb［る］(A) + に + Verb［できる］［ない］(A)
explanation: A structure implying that one cannot (A) even if they wanted to. Even toward (A), (A) cannot possibly be done.

example_sentences.japanese: 親友から土下座をしながら頼まれては、ことわるにことわれません。
example_sentences.english: Being requested something while my friend is on their hands and knees, I cannot refuse even if I want to.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は色々と悩み事が多くて、集中するにできない。
example_sentences.english: A lot has been on my mind recently that I haven't been able to concentrate even if I wanted to.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒が言った冗談は面白かったが内容が下品だったので笑うに笑えなかった。
example_sentences.english: The joke the student told was funny, but it was inappropriate so I could not laugh even if I wanted to.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当は時間はあんまりなかったが、先輩に頼まれたから断るに断れなかった。
example_sentences.english: I actually didn't really have too much time, but since my senpai asked me I couldn't refuse even if I wanted to.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子には明日までに滑り台を作ってあげると約束してしまったので、どんな忙しくても引くに引けない。
example_sentences.english: I promised my son that I would build him a slide by tomorrow, so I can't back out no matter how busy I am.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が一晩中泣いていて寝るに寝れず徹夜をしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: My son cried all night and because of that I couldn't sleep even if I wanted to and stayed up all night.

example_sentences.japanese: にげるににげられない状況から救ってくれたのは、いつもは厳しい先輩だった。
example_sentences.english: The one who saved me from a situation that I wanted to escape from but could not, was my senpai who is always strict.

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌われている上司が見事に転んでしまった。従業員がわらうにわらえない、という顔をしてた。
example_sentences.english: The boss that everyone hates had a spectacular fall. The employees' faces looked as though they wanted to laugh but were unable to.

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼はどうして学校に戻ろうとしないのかな？」「何があったか知らないけど、いうにいえない事情があるのかな。」
example_sentences.english: 'Why is he not willing to go back to school?''I'm not sure if something happened or not, but maybe he is in a situation where he cannot talk about it (even though he may want to).'

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼女が断れば殺すと言って突然ことわるにことわれない状態になった。」
example_sentences.english: 'She said, 'If you refuse, I will kill you,' so the situation suddenly turned into one where I couldn't refuse even if I wanted.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は妻との約束があるのに、先輩たちが残業しているからかえるにかえれない。
example_sentences.english: Even though I have plans with my wife, my seniors are working over time so I can't leave even if I want to.

example_sentences.japanese: ドラマ、女主人公：「なら、やめてよ。」男性主人公：「ひくにひけないんだ。俺は知り過ぎてるから、引いたらやられる。」
example_sentences.english: TV drama, the female protagonist: 'If that's the case, then just stop!'Male protagonist: 'Even if I wanted to, I can't pull out. I know too much. If I stop now, I'll be done for.'

example_sentences.japanese: お互いに意地を張ってひくにひけない状態なのは分かりますが、それでは時間の無駄ですよ？
example_sentences.english: I understand that our stubbornness put us in a situation where even if we wanted to, we cannot fold, but doesn't that just make it a waste of time?

example_sentences.japanese: 部長のその高圧的な態度のせいで、周りの従業員は部長に不満をいうにいえないでいる。
example_sentences.english: Due to that oppressive attitude of my boss, the surrounding employees cannot express their dissatisfaction to him even if they want to.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当はモラハラの夫と一刻も早く離婚をしたいですが、実家にもかえるにかえれないのでどうにも出来ずにいます。
example_sentences.english: Honestly, I want to divorce from my psychologically abusive husband this very instant, but because I cannot return to my parent's house even if I wanted to, there's nothing that can be done.

example_sentences.japanese: 中学生の頃、好きな子に告白して断られた。周りに人がいたからなくになけない状況だった。
example_sentences.english: During my junior high school days, I confessed to a girl I liked and was rejected. There were some people nearby, so I was in a position where I could not cry even if I wanted to.

example_sentences.japanese: 周りの人は「寝られる時に寝なさい」と言うが、ワンオペで育児をしていては常にねるにねられない状況なのだ。
example_sentences.english: The people around me say 'you should sleep when you're able to', but because I do all of the child rearing and housework, I am in the situation of never being able to sleep, even if I want to.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の練習で足の怪我をしてしまったので歩こうにも歩けない。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't walk even if I wanted to because I injured my foot in yesterday's practice.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の仕事を辞めようと思っているが、次のところが見つからないから今の仕事を辞めようにも辞められない。
example_sentences.english: I'm thinking of quitting my current job, but I can't find another one, so I couldn't quit my current job even if I wanted to.

general_translation: Without, If not for
formation: Noun + なくして(は)Verb + ことなくして(は)
casual_structure: Noun + なくして(は)Verb + ことなくして(は)
explanation: A formal structure, indicating that if not for (A), (B) is impossible. Going off (A) not being a thing in general, neither would (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 名言：「努力なくして成功なし。」
example_sentences.english: Wise saying: 'There is no success without hard work.'

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼女なくしては生きていけないと思います。
example_sentences.english: I don't think that I can live without her.

example_sentences.japanese: 努力なくしては、日本語は上達しません。
example_sentences.english: Without hard work, your Japanese won't improve.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗することなくしては、成功できないと言われているが本当なのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: It is said that, without failure you cannot succeed, but I wonder if that is true.

example_sentences.japanese: 相手の気持ちを考えることなくしては、友情は続かない。
example_sentences.english: Friendship cannot last without considering the feelings of the other person.

example_sentences.japanese: この国ではエアコンなしには夏を乗り越えられません。
example_sentences.english: In this country you cannot survive summer without air conditioning.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたなしでは生きていけません！
example_sentences.english: I can't live without you!

example_sentences.japanese: 愛なくしては生きられないというが、それが苦痛になることもある。
example_sentences.english: They say that one cannot live without love, but sometimes it becomes a significant burden.

example_sentences.japanese: トランジスタの開発なくして、現在の世界は成立しえない。
example_sentences.english: The world we know today is not possible without the development of transistors.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ノーベル賞受賞はノーベル委員会に是認されることなくしては、ありえないことであろう。」
example_sentences.english: Receiving the Nobel prize is impossible without the approval of the Nobel Committee.

example_sentences.japanese: スピーチ、ＣＥＯ：「消費者の皆様との協力なくしてはこの商品開発は不可能であります。」
example_sentences.english: Speech, CEO: 'The development of this product is impossible without the cooperation of all of our consumers.'

example_sentences.japanese: 先生：「皆さんの協力なくしては、こんなに早く掃除を終えることが出来ませんでした。」
example_sentences.english: Sensei: 'Without everyone's cooperation, we would not have been able to finish the cleaning this quickly.'

example_sentences.japanese: 両親からの金銭的、そして精神的な支えなくしては、ここまで立派になれなかったと思う。
example_sentences.english: Without your parents' financial and emotional support, I don't think you would have been able to become such a tremendous person.

example_sentences.japanese: 若い頃は当時の彼氏なくしては生きていけないと思っていましたが、それは間違いでした。
example_sentences.english: In my younger days, I thought that I couldn't live without my boyfriend at the time, but that was a mistake.

example_sentences.japanese: ライバルでもある彼女と和解することなくしては、私達はお互いを高め合うことが出来ないと思います。
example_sentences.english: If not for accommodating her, who was also my rival, I think that neither of us would have been able to elevate each other.

example_sentences.japanese: パートナーなくしては子育てなど出来ないのに、私のパートナーは私一人に育児を押し付けている。
example_sentences.english: Despite not being able to do something like raising a child without your partner, my partner imposes all of that on me.

example_sentences.japanese: 努力なくしては何も達成出来ないと言うが、どんなに努力をしてもその努力が実らない事だってある。
example_sentences.english: I say that nothing can be attained without effort, but there are also things that will bear no fruit no matter how much effort you put in.

example_sentences.japanese: スピーチ：「何よりまず我が友人トトロに感謝します。彼なくしては今日の私はなかったと言えるでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: Speech: 'First and foremost, I would like to thank my friend Totoro. It can be said that without him, I wouldn't be the person I am today.'

general_translation: So much that, Extremely, Very
formation: Verb + のなんのって［い］Adjective + のなんのって［な］Adjective + な + のなんのって
casual_structure: Verb + のなんのって［い］Adjective + のなんのって［な］Adjective + な + のなんのって
explanation: A very casual phrase, used to emphasize a huge degree of (A). Especially when that degree cannot be expressed with simple words.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんが「勉強しろ」ってうるさいのなんのって、もう家に帰りたくないよ…。
example_sentences.english: My mom is extremely annoying with comments like 'study!', and I don't want to go home anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな痩せているのにあの量一人で食べちゃうなんて、びっくりしたのなんのって。
example_sentences.english: I was extremely surprised that such a skinny guy could eat that amount of food all by himself.

example_sentences.japanese: 名古屋の夏は暑いのなんのって、外に出た瞬間シャツが汗でびっしょりになるんだよ。
example_sentences.english: It is so hot in Nagoya in the summer that the moment you step outside, your shirt will be drenched in sweat.

example_sentences.japanese: あの建物は丈夫なのなんのって、去年あった震度７の地震までも耐えたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: That building is so sturdy that it even withstood last year's earthquake that measured 7 on the Japanese seismic scale.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は食べるの食べないのって、三十分で三キロも肉を一人で食べた。
example_sentences.english: He eats so much that he ate 3 kg of meat in 30 minutes all by himself.

example_sentences.japanese: あのジェットコースターは大人でも失神するほど怖いの怖くないのって。
example_sentences.english: That rollercoaster is so scary that even an adult would pass out.

example_sentences.japanese: あの旅館の女将さんは愛想が悪いのなんのって、もう二度と行くもんか！
example_sentences.english: That ryokan's proprietress' amiability was so bad that there is no way I would ever go there again!

example_sentences.japanese: ジャングルの中でワニと出くわした時は焦ったのなんのって、もう死ぬかと思ったよ！
example_sentences.english: I was extremely startled when I happened upon a crocodile in the jungle that I thought I was going to die!

example_sentences.japanese: 東京の夏は蒸し暑いのなんのって、少し歩いただけで気持ち悪くなるくらいです。
example_sentences.english: Tokyo's summer is extremely humid, so much so that it feels gross even if you just walked around a little bit.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫の実家は広いのなんのって、庭には沢山の木が植えられていてプールもあるんだよ！
example_sentences.english: My husband's family home is extremely spacious. There are lots of trees planted in the garden, and even a pool!

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「疲れた顔だね。」Ｂ：「昨日は騒音で眠れなかったから、もう眠いのなんのって・・・」
example_sentences.english: A: 'You look tired!'B: 'I couldn't sleep yesterday because it was noisy, so I am already extremely sleepy…'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「今買ったケーキはどう？食べてみたい。」Ｂ：「ケーキおいしいのなんのって、もう完食しちゃったほど。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'How is the cake we bought today? I want to try.'B: 'It was so delicious (to the point) that I ate it all already.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「田舎はどうだった？」Ｂ：「よかったよ。静かなのなんのって虫の音が聞こえる。とてもリラックスできた。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'How was the countryside?'B: 'Great! It was so quiet that one could hear the insects chirping. I was really able to relax.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達は日帰り旅行について話す、Ａ：「で、お腹がすいてなかった？」Ｂ：「そりゃお腹がすいたのなんのって、一人でご飯三杯も食べたよ。」
example_sentences.english: Friends talking about a day trip, A: 'And then? Weren't you hungry?'B: 'I was extremely hungry. I ate three bowls of rice by myself!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「あそこのエンジニアが下手クソでさ。修理が上手くないのなんのって。修理から一日経っただけでまた壊れたんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'That engineer is absolutely terrible (at his job). He is extremely unskillful! Only one day after 'repairs' it broke again.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「おにづか先生って、強いんだって。」Ｂ：「強いのなんのって一人で十人ほどを倒しちゃいましてね。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I heard that Onizuka-sensei is strong.'B: 'He is so strong that he took down ten people by himself...'

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の部活の顧問の先生の態度は酷いのなんのって、体罰と暴言が原因で解雇させられました。
example_sentences.english: My club's advisory teacher's behavior was so cruel that he was discharged because of physical punishment and verbal abuse.

general_translation: To depend on
formation: Noun + （如何（いかん））+ にかかっているPhrase + かどうか(1) + （如何（いかん））+  にかかっているWH-Word + Phrase + か + （如何（いかん））+  にかかっている(1) か否（いな）か
casual_structure: Noun + （如何（いかん））+ にかかっているPhrase + かどうか(1) + （如何（いかん））+  にかかっているWH-Word + Phrase + か + （如何（いかん））+  にかかっている(1) か否（いな）か
polite_structure: Noun + （如何（いかん））+ にかかっていますPhrase + かどうか(1) + （如何（いかん））+  にかかっていますWH-Word + Phrase + か + （如何（いかん））+  にかかっています(1) か否（いな）か
explanation: An expression emphasizing that something depends on (A). It's all riding on (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ほむら：「すべてが一人の少女の選択にかかっている。」
example_sentences.english: Homura: 'Everything depends on one girl's choice.'

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で立ち上げた会社が成功するかどうかは自分の努力にかかっている。
example_sentences.english: Whether your company will succeed or not depends on your own efforts.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品の売れ行きはマーケティングが成功するかどうか如何にかかっている。
example_sentences.english: The sales of this product will depend on the success of the marketing.

example_sentences.japanese: 地球の未来は若者にかかっているから、若者を教育しなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: We must educate the youth because the future of this earth depends on them.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月旅行に行けるかは、部長が僕に休みをくれるかにかかっている。
example_sentences.english: Whether I can go on the trip next month depends on whether my boss will give me time off.

example_sentences.japanese: みなさんが合格できるかできないかは、皆さんが努力するかどうか如何にかかっている。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not you will be able to pass the exam depends on how hard you are going to work.

example_sentences.japanese: コーチ：「勝つも負けるも我々の協力にかかっているから頑張ろう。」
example_sentences.english: Coach: 'Whether we win or lose depends on our cooperation, so let's do our best!'

example_sentences.japanese: 明日予定通りにピクニックに行けるかどうかは明日の天気にかかっている。
example_sentences.english: Whether we can go on a picnic tomorrow as planned depends on tomorrow's weather.

example_sentences.japanese: 成功するかどうかは才能よりむしろどれだけ頑張るかにかかっていると言えるだろう。
example_sentences.english: 'It is fair to say that whether or not one succeeds depends on how hard one can work rather than one's ability.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「帝国の運命はターニャの作戦が成功するか否かにかかっている。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'The fate of the empire depends on whether Tanya's strategy succeeds or not.'

example_sentences.japanese: この国の未来は若者にかかっているのに、若者の教育のレベルが下がっているそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Despite the future of this country depending on young people, I heard that the education level of youth is declining.

example_sentences.japanese: 指定校推薦を勝ち取る事が出来るかどうかは今学期の評定にかかっている。
example_sentences.english: Whether I am able to gain priority admission into university or not depends on this semester's assessment.

example_sentences.japanese: ずっとラブラブでいられるかどうかは、お互いの思いやりや正直さ、そして誠実さにかかっている。
example_sentences.english: Whether you're always able to have a love filled relationship or not depends on your mutual consideration, frankness, and honesty.

example_sentences.japanese: この手術が成功するか否かは主治医である僕の腕にかかっていると聞き、重いプレッシャーを感じている。
example_sentences.english: Hearing that whether this operation will be a success or not depends on my, the attending physician's ability, I am feeling immense pressure.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「田中社長は当社の将来が、政府からの貸付けを受けられるかどうか如何にかかっている、ということを確信しました。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Company President Tanaka believes that the company's future depends on whether or not it is able to acquire a government loan.'

example_sentences.japanese: ずっとおねだりしていた犬を買ってもらえるかどうかは、私がマラソン大会で首位を獲得できるかどうかにかかっている。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not I am able to have the dog bought for me that I have constantly been begging for depends on whether I can get first place in the marathon or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社のサイト：「当社は、会社の発展、即ち業績の持続的拡大の成否は、従業員各員の主体的なやる気と活動量にかかっているものと信じています。」
example_sentences.english: Company website: 'At our firm, we believe that company development, i.e. the end result of our expansion with sustained growth in performance, depends upon the determination and actions taken by each employee.'

general_translation: Never cease to, Always, Sincerely, Greatly, From the bottom of one's heart
formation: Verb［て］+ やまない
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ やまない
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ やみません
explanation: A formal grammar point, indicating that (A) never ceases. The act of (A) will not desist. Often about unfading emotions.

example_sentences.japanese: 献辞：「あいしてやまない妻と息子へ」
example_sentences.english: Dedication: 'To my wife and son, whom I will always love.' (never cease to)

example_sentences.japanese: 私が愛してやまない犬が急に体を壊したから心配でしょうがない。
example_sentences.english: The dog that I love from the bottom of my heart got sick suddenly, so I am worried.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなことを親にさせてしまって後悔してやまない。
example_sentences.english: I never cease to regret letting my parents do that for me.

example_sentences.japanese: １日も早く普通の生活に戻れる様に祈ってやみません。
example_sentences.english: I will never cease to pray for them to be able to return to their normal lives as soon as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: スピーチ：「飢餓がこの世界から駆逐されることを、いのってやみません。」
example_sentences.english: Speech: 'I will never cease to pray for the eradication of hunger and starvation from this world.' (always・deeply・sincerely)

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「彼は人をひきつけてやまない何かを持っていると言えるだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'One could say that he has something that greatly fascinates people.' (never cease to)

example_sentences.japanese: どうして科学的な証拠もないのに幽霊をしんじてやまない人がこんなに沢山いるのかな…。
example_sentences.english: I wonder why there are lots of people that never cease to believe in ghosts, despite there being no scientific evidence.

example_sentences.japanese: 賛辞：「友達としても人としても心の中に生涯存在する尊敬してやまない人でした。」
example_sentences.english: Eulogy: 'She was a person I greatly respected throughout my life both as a friend and as a human being.' (never cease to)

example_sentences.japanese: スピーチ：「今日こちらにお集まりになった皆様には、当社の製品紹介をお楽しみいただけるようねがってやみません。」
example_sentences.english: Speech: 'To all who have gathered here today, I sincerely hope that you will be able to enjoy the presentation of our new product.' (never cease to)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕があいしてやまない妻を傷つけた奴に対しては、倍でやり返すつもりだ！
example_sentences.english: Regarding the man who hurt my wife, whom I love from the bottom of my heart, I plan to repay the favor twofold.

example_sentences.japanese: そのスポーツ選手の輝かしい功績の裏には血のにじむような努力があったと知り、尊敬してやまない気持ちになった。
example_sentences.english: Knowing that behind that athlete's brilliant results was blood sweat and tears, I began to sincerely have respect for him.

example_sentences.japanese: あの時の一つの行動がこれからも永遠にパートナーを傷つけるのだと思うと、それを後悔してやまない。
example_sentences.english: Thinking that that one action of mine that time would forevermore cause pain for my partner, I will never cease to regret it.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の結婚式でスピーチをする：「お二人が末永く、幸せで安定した生活を送る事をねがってやまない。」
example_sentences.english: Giving a speech at a friend's wedding: 'I wish that the couple will never cease to lead a happy and stable life, as long as they both shall live.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今回の土砂災害で避難を余儀なくされている被災者の皆様が、一刻も早く元の生活に戻れることをいのってやまない。
example_sentences.english: From the bottom of my heart, I pray that everyone who was forced to evacuate with the recent landslide disaster will be able to return to their normal lives, even if only a moment sooner.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「巨大なピラミッドの信じられないほどの大きさと美しさは、建設以来何千年経っても人の心を魅了してやみません。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Despite thousands of years passing since their construction, the incredible size and beauty of the great pyramids will never cease to capture the hearts of people.' (always・greatly)

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に子供や妻のことを悪く言われて、腹が立ってやまない。
example_sentences.english: I was sincerely mad at my boss for saying such things about my wife and kids. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Would rather...than, Rather than, Better off
formation: Verb［る］+ ぐらいなら(1) + Phrase(1) くらいなら
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ ぐらいなら(1) + Phrase(1) くらいなら
explanation: A hypothetical grammar point, showing that if something were to the extent of (A), (B) would be preferable. (A) is almost always negatively evaluated.

example_sentences.japanese: 「やらずに後悔するくらいなら、いっそやってみなさいよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Rather than regret not doing it, try it!'

example_sentences.japanese: あの地域に引っ越すくらいなら、死んだ方がマシだ。
example_sentences.english: I would rather die, than move to that neighborhood.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先輩の下で働くぐらいなら、一人で働いた方がいいと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I think you would be better off working alone, than working under that senpai.

example_sentences.japanese: 何十万もかけて直すくらいなら、もう少し出して新しい車を買った方がいい。
example_sentences.english: I would rather buy a new car that is a little expensive than pay thousands of dollars to fix this car.

example_sentences.japanese: 「 こんなクソゲームを買うくらいならお金をドブに捨てたほうがよかった・・・」
example_sentences.english: 'I would have been better off throwing money away than buying this gosh darn game…'

example_sentences.japanese: 「その仕事は絶対に嫌だ。それに戻るくらいなら死んだほうがましだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I really hate that job. I would rather die than go back.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「小さなことに目くじらを立てる人と一緒に生活するくらいならホームレスになったほうがましだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I would rather become homeless than live together with a person who nitpicks every little thing I do.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「愛Ｐｈｏｎｅの画面の修理は３万円からするよ。どうしようかな？」Ｂ：「とっても高いよね！修理するくらいなら新しいのを買っちゃった方がいいかなあ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'My aiPhone screen repair cost starts at about 30000 yen! What should I do?'B: 'Wha, that's super expensive! You would be better off buying a new one rather than repairing it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 失恋してこんなに悲しい気持ちになるくらいなら、最初から恋なんかをしなければよかった…。
example_sentences.english: If a broken heart was going to cause this much sadness, I would have been better off without something like love in the first place.

example_sentences.japanese: あのクソみたいな彼女ともう一度付き合うくらいなら、一生独身でもいいです。
example_sentences.english: I would rather be single for the rest of my life than date that blasted woman again.

example_sentences.japanese: そのコートを捨てるくらいなら、私に譲ってくれない？リメイクして着たいからさ。
example_sentences.english: Rather than throwing away that coat, why don't you give it to me? I want to alter it and then wear it.

example_sentences.japanese: その仕事を嫌々するくらいなら、とっとと転職した方が長期的にみていいんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Rather than just hating that job, wouldn't it be better in the long run if you thought about changing jobs straight away?

example_sentences.japanese: 頼れない友達を何人も持つくらいなら、数人でも頼れる友達を作る方が意味があると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that you would be better off making even just a few reliable friends, than having lots of unreliable ones.

example_sentences.japanese: あの息も吸えないほどの満員電車に乗るくらいなら、あえて一時間くらい早く家を出た方がマシだ。
example_sentences.english: Rather than riding on a train that is so packed that I cannot even breathe, I would rather deliberately leave home about an hour early.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「彼に助けを求めたらどう？」Ｂ：「彼に助けを求めるくらいなら、むしろピラニアだらけの池を泳いだほうがましだぞ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'What about asking him for help?'B: 'I would rather swim through a pond full of piranha than ask him for help.'

example_sentences.japanese: え、前使ってたパソコン捨てちゃったの？捨てるくらいなら俺が買ったのに。
example_sentences.english: What… You threw away the computer you were using? I would have bought it from you rather than you throw it away.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな奴に頼むぐらいなら、自分でやればよかった。
example_sentences.english: I should have done it myself, rather than asking a person like that to do it.

general_translation: I said...!, I told you...!, !
formation: Verb + ってば(1)。［い］Adjective + ってば(1)。［な］Adjective + （だ）+ ってば(1)。Noun + （だ）+ ってば(1)。(1) ったら
casual_structure: Verb + ってば(1)。［い］Adjective + ってば(1)。［な］Adjective + （だ）+ ってば(1)。Noun + （だ）+ ってば(1)。(1) ったら
explanation: A hypothetical, very casual grammar expression, emphasizing that (A) has already been said. I told you (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 親：「もっとお姉ちゃんを見習いなさい！」子供：「見習いたくないったら！」
example_sentences.english: Parent: 'You need to better follow your sister's example!Child: 'I said I don't wanna!'

example_sentences.japanese: 分かったってば！何回も言われると本当むかつくからちょっと黙ってて。
example_sentences.english: I said I got it! You telling me the same thing (repeatedly) is getting on my nerves so can you please be quiet for a little bit?

example_sentences.japanese: 痛いったら！なんでずっと痛いって言ってるのに何回も何回もフォークでつついてくるの？
example_sentences.english: I said that hurts! Why do you keep poking me with a fork even when I say that it hurts?

example_sentences.japanese: 嫌いだってば！あんな奴なんて大嫌いだ！
example_sentences.english: I said I don't like them! I don't like such people!

example_sentences.japanese: だから、俺は大人だったら！背が低いからってひどいぞ本当に。
example_sentences.english: For the last time, I said that I am an adult. It is kind of mean to say such things just because I am short.

example_sentences.japanese: 親：「宿題やりなさいよ！」イライラした子供：「今からやるったら！」
example_sentences.english: Parent: 'Do your homework!'Irritated child: 'I said I'm gonna do it!'

example_sentences.japanese: 配偶者１がケーキを食べようとしている配偶者２に「ケーキを夕食の前に食べちゃダメったら！」
example_sentences.english: Spouse to spouse that is about to eat cake: 'I told you not to eat cake before dinner!'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「俺と一緒バンジージャンプ、やってみない？」友達２：「興味ないんだ。」友達１：「本当に？」友達２：「やだってば、もう！」
example_sentences.english: Friend1: 'Won't you go bungee jumping together with me?'Friend2: 'Not interested.'Friend1: 'Are you sure?'Friend2: 'I said no, Jeez!'

example_sentences.japanese: 父：「宿題やったのか？」息子：「やったよ〜。」父：「ふむ…本当か？」息子：「本当だってば！」
example_sentences.english: Dad: 'Have you done your homework?'Son: 'Done.'Dad: 'Hmmm, is that true?'Son: 'I said it's true!'

example_sentences.japanese: 娘：「お母さん、遊びに行ってもいい？」母：「…」娘：「お母さん？」母：「…」娘：「お母さんってば！聞いてる？」
example_sentences.english: Daughter: 'Mom, can I go to hang out?'Mother: '...'Daughter: 'Mom?'Mother: '...'Daughter: 'I said 'mom', are you even listening?'

example_sentences.japanese: 親：「夕飯前には家中に掃除機掛けといてね。」子供：「わかった。」３分後、親：「忘れないでね。」子供：「わかったってば！」
example_sentences.english: Parent: 'Vacuum the house before dinner, OK?'Child: 'Got it.'3 minutes later, parent: 'Don't forget, OK??'Child: 'I said I got it!'

example_sentences.japanese: 夫：「おい早くしろよ。」妻：「待ってよ、準備中なの。」夫：「早くしろってば。」妻：「あのねぇ！あなたが協力しないから、まだ準備中なのよ！！」
example_sentences.english: Husband: 'Oi, hurry it up'Wife: 'Please wait, I am in the middle of getting it ready.'Husband: 'I told you to hurry it up!'Wife: 'Listen here! Since you won't help, I am still in the middle of getting it ready!'

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒：「先生、その問題なら先週やったってば！先生、最近ちょっと疲れてるんじゃない？」
example_sentences.english: Student: 'Sensei, I told you we did that question last week! Aren't you a bit tired recently, sensei?'

example_sentences.japanese: 母：「明日は歯医者さんだから、忘れずに行くのよ？」息子：「分かってるってば！何度も言わないでよ！」
example_sentences.english: Mom: 'Because you have the dentist tomorrow, you won't forget to go, right?'Son: 'Oh my god I said I know! Don't tell me so many times!'

example_sentences.japanese: 笑っている友達に向かって：「笑わないでってば！あんな間違いをして私は恥ずかしい思いをしているのよ！」
example_sentences.english: To a laughing friend: 'I told you not to laugh! That mistake makes me feel embarrassed!'

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が飼い主を舐めている、飼い主：「アカマル、やめろ！」舐めまわされること１分後、飼い主：「やめろってば！」
example_sentences.english: A dog licking their owner, pet owner: 'Akamaru, stop!'One minute of licking later, pet owner: 'I said stop!'

example_sentences.japanese: 金太郎ってば、またエアコンつけっぱなしで家出てったよ。
example_sentences.english: That darn Kintaro, he went out with his AC still running.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたったら本当におっちょこちょいね。
example_sentences.english: Oh you, you are such a clutz aren't you.

general_translation: Even if not, Without, Don't have to
formation: Verb［ない］+ ず + ともNoun + ならずとも(1)1. なる［ない］ + ず + ともExceptions:する ￫ せずとも
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ず + ともNoun + ならずとも(1)1. なる［ない］ + ず + ともExceptions:する ￫ せずとも
explanation: A formal, hypothetical phrase, showing that even without (A) being done, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「植物は動物ならずともある種の知覚表示をしている。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Even if plants are not animals, in a way, they display perception.'

example_sentences.japanese: 昔は練習せずとも新しい曲を完璧に弾けたのに、今となってはどんだけ練習しても上手く弾けないんだよな。
example_sentences.english: I used to be able to play new music without any practice, but now I can't play well no matter how much I practice.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが今ものすごく落ち込んでいるということは聞かずともわかりますよ。
example_sentences.english: I can tell that you are very upset without even asking.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に留学せずとも、日本語を習得する方法はあるが、日本に行って勉強する方が楽しそうだから私は日本に留学したいです。
example_sentences.english: I know that there are ways to study Japanese without studying abroad in Japan, but I am going to Japan because it seems fun to study there.

example_sentences.japanese: 専門家ならずとも、彼は政治について色々と知っている。
example_sentences.english: Even though he is not an expert, he knows a lot about politics.

example_sentences.japanese: 親ならずとも子育てが大変だということは見てわかるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to be a parent to see that parenting is hard work.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週の試合の相手はあの弱いチームだから、そんなに練習せずとも良いだろう。
example_sentences.english: Next week's game is against that weak team, so we won't have to practice so much.

example_sentences.japanese: ゲーム評論：「ＲＰＧゲームファンならずとも、ウィッチャー ３に興味をひかれずにはいられません。」
example_sentences.english: Game review: 'Even if I am not an RPG fan, I cannot help but be captivated by Witcher 3.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「アメリカ人とイギリス人は他の言語をまなばずとも生きられる言語環境に居ます。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Americans and Brits are in a language environment where they can live without learning other languages.' (even if they do not learn)

example_sentences.japanese: 時代小説、瀕死の親：「わたしの身の心配などせずとも良い。我が娘よ。」
example_sentences.english: A historical novel, dying parent: 'You don't have to worry about me. My dear daughter.' (without・even if)

example_sentences.japanese: 妹：「でも、どうやってわかった？」兄：「家族だからいわずともわかる。」
example_sentences.english: Younger sister: 'But, how did you know?'Older brother: 'We are a family, so I understand you even if you don't say anything.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小学校の頃は勉強せずともテストで満点を取ることが出来ていたのになぁ〜…。
example_sentences.english: Even though I could get a perfect score without even studying when I was in primary school…

example_sentences.japanese: 親にならずともお互いが満足しているのなら、彼らに子供を勧めるのはお門違いだ。
example_sentences.english: If you're both satisfied without becoming parents, then suggesting kids to him is barking up the wrong tree.

example_sentences.japanese: 留学せずとも言語を習得できるのは百も承知だが、僕は留学したいと思っている。
example_sentences.english: I am fully aware that you can acquire a language even without studying abroad, but I still think that I want to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが子供に慣れていない事はきかずとも分かりますよ。だって表情がぎこちないんですもの。
example_sentences.english: I know that you're not used to kids without even having to ask. It's because I can tell by the silly look on your face.

example_sentences.japanese: パンデミック禍に在宅勤務が推奨されるようになってから、仕事場にいかずともできる仕事が多くある事が分かった。
example_sentences.english: Since being recommended to work from home during the pandemic, I realized that there are lots of tasks that can be done even without being at my workplace.

example_sentences.japanese: 五十年も連れ添っている妻は私が言葉にせずとも言いたい事を表情や仕草から汲み取ってくれる。
example_sentences.english: Having been wed for 50 years, even without putting it into words, my wife can grasp what I want to say from things like my mannerisms and expressions.

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりに会った友達の話、まさお：「こんな可愛い女の子とどういう関係だ？ まさかガールフレンドか？」あおしま：「まあ、あたらずとも遠からずなんだよ。我が妻だ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat with friends who met after a long time, Masao: 'What is your relationship with such a cute girl? Don't tell me she is your girlfriend?'Aoshima: 'Well... Even if you're not spot on, you are close. She's my wife.' (even if you are not on target)

general_translation: Since...(it is no wonder that), Because...(it is no wonder that), Due to...(it is no wonder that)
formation: Verb + とあって［い］Adjective + とあって［な］Adjective + （だ）+ とあってNoun + （だ）+ とあって
casual_structure: Verb + とあって［い］Adjective + とあって［な］Adjective + （だ）+ とあってNoun + （だ）+ とあって
explanation: A formal expression, implying that because (A) exists, it is no wonder that (B). (A) often expresses rarity, while (B) shows popularity.

example_sentences.japanese: いつもより講演の参加者が多いとあって、発表者はいつも以上にソワソワしています。
example_sentences.english: Since many people attended the lecture, it is no wonder that the speakers are uneasy.

example_sentences.japanese: あのグループの卒業ライブが行われるとあって、この会場は大勢のファンで溢れている。
example_sentences.english: Since a farewell concert of that group is about to take place, this venue is filled with a large number of fans.

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道は夏の間でも涼しいとあって、冬の間だけでなく夏にも多くの観光客が訪れるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Hokkaido attracts many tourists not only during winter, but also summer since it is cool there even during the summer months.

example_sentences.japanese: あの街は便利だとあって、土地の値段が高い。
example_sentences.english: Since that city is convenient, the price of land is expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: お盆の最終日とあって、高速道路だけでなく、下道もものすごく混んでいる。
example_sentences.english: Both the toll free road and the expressway are extremely crowded since it is the last day of Obon.

example_sentences.japanese: ニュースサイト：「日本で初上映とあって、大人から子どもまで多くの人が集まりました。」
example_sentences.english: News: 'Since it premiered in Japan, (it is no wonder that) many people of all ages gathered.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「この都市で唯一のイタリアンが食べれるレストランとあって、自然と大人気になった。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Since it is the only restaurant in this city where one can eat Italian cuisine, (it is no wonder that) it naturally became very popular.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はスーパーの特売日とあって、開店する三十分も前から長蛇の列が出来ています。
