example_sentences.english: Because today is a special sale at the supermarket, it is no wonder that there is already a long line 30 minutes before the store opens.

example_sentences.japanese: ニュースサイト：「 気軽に鹿などの野生動物が撮影できるとあって、大変人気の撮影スポットの一つになっています。」
example_sentences.english: News site: 'Since one can easily photograph wild animals such as deer, (it is no wonder that) it has become one of the most popular photography spots.'

example_sentences.japanese: ニュース：「今日は元日とあって、神社には初詣に来て、お賽銭をお供えする人がいっぱいです。」
example_sentences.english: News: 'Since it is the first day of the new year, (it is no wonder that) there are many people who have come to the shrine(s) for hatsumode to pay their respects and offer money.'

example_sentences.japanese: ニュース：「今日だけ無料でレベルの高い洋菓子が楽しめるとあって、客が行列を作りました。」
example_sentences.english: News: 'Since today is the only day that you can enjoy high-quality western confectionery free of charge, (it is no wonder that) customers formed a long queue.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は祝日とあって、遊園地や水族館はいつもより倍近く混んでいます。
example_sentences.english: Since today is a public holiday, it is no wonder that amusement parks and aquariums are nearly twice as crowded as usual..

example_sentences.japanese: 世界的に人気な女優が来日するとあって、空港には多くのファンが集まっている。
example_sentences.english: Due to a globally famous actress coming to Japan, it is no wonder that many people are gathering at the airport.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は大富豪の息子として育ったとあって、金銭感覚が一般人とはだいぶ違うようだ。
example_sentences.english: Because he was raised as the son of an extremely rich person, it is no wonder that his sense of money is largely different to regular people.

example_sentences.japanese: 先日テレビで紹介されたとあって、行きつけの喫茶店の予約が急に取りづらくなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Due to it being advertised on TV yesterday, it is no wonder that it has suddenly become difficult to get a reservation at my favorite coffee shop.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「沖縄は日本の他のところと比べて冬でも暖かいとあって、夏休みにとどまらず一年中日本全国から多くの人が訪れる。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Since even winters in Okinawa are mild compared to other parts of Japan, (it is no wonder that) it is visited by many people from all over the country not only in summer but all year round.'

example_sentences.japanese: 私はハンサムとあって、友達が作りやすい。
example_sentences.english: Since I am handsome, it is easy to make friends. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Not at all, By no means, Definitely not, Nothing like that, Not really
formation: Noun + でもなんでもない［な］Adjective + でもなんでもない
casual_structure: Noun + でもなんでもない［な］Adjective + でもなんでもない
polite_structure: Noun + でもなんでもないです［な］Adjective + でもなんでもないです
explanation: A strong construction, showing that something is by no means (A). It's not even (A) or even anything like (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「これは偶然でもなんでもないんです、起こるべくして起こったんです。」
example_sentences.english: 'It is not a coincidence at all. It was sure to happen.' (definitely not)

example_sentences.japanese: 俺はファンでもなんでもないよ、ただあの人が作曲した曲を聞くのが好きなだけ。
example_sentences.english: I am not a fan by any means. I just like listening to the music he produces.

example_sentences.japanese: あっ、あの人ですか？友達でもなんでもないですよ、なんかさっき急に話しかけてきたので話していただけです。
example_sentences.english: Oh, that person? They are not my friend at all. They just came up to me and started talking to me so I was just talking to them.

example_sentences.japanese: 迷惑でもなんでもないですよ、ゆっくりしていってください。
example_sentences.english: It's not bothersome at all. Please take your time.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きでもなんでもない人からそんなこと言われても全然嬉しくない。
example_sentences.english: I'm not at all happy to hear such a thing from someone I don't like or anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きでもなんでもないクラスメイトと付き合っているという噂を流されてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, a rumor that I was dating a classmate that I definitely do not like started going around.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏が誕生日でもクリスマスでもなんでもないのにペアのネックレスをプレゼントしてくれました。
example_sentences.english: Despite it not being anything like my birthday or Christmas, my boyfriend gave me a couple's necklace.

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼は‎全然天才でもなんでもない。人並み以上の努力をしているから、あれだけの結果を残せるんだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'He is not a genius by any means. He can achieve so much because he is putting in more work than anyone else.' (definitely not・not at all)

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚式の前日に私の婚約者と寝るなんて…あんなやつ、家族でもなんでもないわ。
example_sentences.english: That they slept with my fiance on the day before the wedding… That person, they are not my family at all.

example_sentences.japanese: ＡがＢをいじめている、Ａ：「ただの遊びだ・・・」Ｂ：「遊びでもなんでもないよ、ただの嫌がらせじゃないか。」
example_sentences.english: A is teasing B, A: 'I'm just playing with you...'B: 'This is definitely not a game! Aren't you just harassing me?'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話、Ａ：「ごめんね、迷惑かけちゃったよね。」Ｂ：「ううん。別に迷惑でもなんでもないよ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends, A: 'Sorry. I have caused you troubles.'B: 'Nah. There was no trouble at all.' (definitely not)

example_sentences.japanese: ＡとＢから離れた位置の人について話す、 Ａ：「あの人、誰？恋人？」Ｂ：「恋人でもなんでもない。ただの知り合い。」
example_sentences.english: A and B talk about a person some distance away, A: 'Who is that person? Girlfriend?'B: 'She is not my girlfriend at all. Just an acquaintance.' (definitely not)

example_sentences.japanese: 弟が社長になれたのは偶然でもなんでもない。人一倍の努力が実った結果です。
example_sentences.english: My little brother being able to become the company president was by no means a coincidence. It's the result of him working harder than anyone else.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の父は料理人でもなんでもないけど、独学であれだけの料理を作れるようになったんだ。
example_sentences.english: My dad is by no means a chef, but he became able to make so many dishes through self study.

example_sentences.japanese: 確かに君の事を助けたけど、別に君の支援者でもなんでもないよ。ただ、曲がった事は許せないだけさ。
example_sentences.english: Indeed it is true that I helped you, but that does not really mean that I am your supporter. I just simply can't let skewed things slide.

example_sentences.japanese: 《研究室に後輩が入る時》後輩：「お忙しいところを、すみません。」先輩：「いえ、仕事でもなんでもないです。ただの調べごとですよ。」
example_sentences.english: 《A junior enters the laboratory》Junior: 'I am sorry to bother you when you are busy.'Senior: 'No, I'm not working or anything. I'm just reading up on (articles, data).' (definitely not)

example_sentences.japanese: あいつとは別れたけど、ひどい奴だったから、悲しくもなんでもない。
example_sentences.english: I broke up with him, but since he was such an awful person, I am not sad or anything.

example_sentences.japanese: これ重くもなんでもないじゃん。
example_sentences.english: This isn't heavy at all.

general_translation: Whole, -wide, Across the, Entire, All of, With … altogether
formation: Noun + ぐるみで  Noun + ぐるみ + の + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + ぐるみで  Noun + ぐるみ + の + Noun
explanation: A grammar point implying that (B) covers the entirety of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「ともさんとは家族ぐるみの付き合いです。」
example_sentences.english: 'Our family is acquaintances with Tomo and her entire family.'

example_sentences.japanese: 会社ぐるみで違法な取引をしていたので、社員全員逮捕された。
example_sentences.english: All the employees were arrested because the entire company was doing illegal business.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼とは家族ぐるみの付き合いです。
example_sentences.english: Our family is friends with him and his whole family. (He is a family friend)

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年家族ぐるみで初詣に行きます。
example_sentences.english: I go to Hatsumode with my entire family every year.

example_sentences.japanese: 街ぐるみの治安をよくするために、町内会の人たちが毎晩パトロールをしています。
example_sentences.english: In order to improve the security of the entire town, people from the neighborhood association patrol the area every night.

example_sentences.japanese: 「長年、家族ぐるみで親しくしている友達だよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Our entire families were close friends for many years.'

example_sentences.japanese: 組織ぐるみで違法な売春宿を見逃していたと知り、組織全体に深く失望した。
example_sentences.english: Knowing that the entire organization had turned a blind eye to illegal brothels, I was deeply disappointed in the whole thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校ぐるみでイジメを隠蔽しようとした結果、社会からさらなる批判を浴びる事になった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of the whole school trying to conceal the bullying, the shower of criticism from the public grew even worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 国家ぐるみのドーピングがばれ、その国の選手の大会への出場は禁止されました。
example_sentences.english: With the uncovering of nation-wide doping, that country's athletes were banned from competing in events.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族ぐるみで付き合っていた彼が麻薬を売買していたと知り、たまげました。
example_sentences.english: Finding out that he and his entire family were selling narcotics, I was astonished.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社ぐるみの不祥事を一人の社員に押し付けて、さらに彼を自殺に追い込むなんて、なんて酷い会社なんだ！
example_sentences.english: Something like pinning a company-wide scandal on one employee and then cornering him into taking his own life in addition to that, what a cruel organization!

example_sentences.japanese: その会社の食品偽装は会社ぐるみで行われたものだ。社員一人だけに責任をおしつけるべきではない。
example_sentences.english: The false labeling of food products was a company-wide practice. A single employee should not be blamed.

example_sentences.japanese: まさか観光地として有名なあの街が地域ぐるみで工場による河川の汚染を隠蔽していたなんて、信じられないよ！
example_sentences.english: Something like that district which is famous for tourists concealing the region-wide river's pollution caused by factories, I cannot believe it!

example_sentences.japanese: 地方自治体のサイト：「街ぐるみの年中行事『ゴミ拾い』が１０月１０日（土）に行われます。」
example_sentences.english: Local government website: 'A city-wide annual event, 'Garbage Collecting' will be held on Saturday, October 10.'

example_sentences.japanese: 地方自治体のサイト：「〇〇県では、地域ぐるみで気候変動対策に取り組むことにより、ゴミの量を５０パーセント減らすことができました」
example_sentences.english: Local government website: 'In XX Prefecture we were able to reduce the amount of garbage by 50% through region-wide efforts to combat climate change.'

example_sentences.japanese: 詐欺、詐欺師：「もしもし、お祖母さん？俺、俺！」武の祖母：「武？どうしたの？」詐欺師：「うん、悪い人に身ぐるみ剥がされたんだ。お金持ってきてくれない？」
example_sentences.english: Scam, Scammer: 'Hello, Grandma? It's me!'Takeshi's grandmother: 'Takeshi? What's wrong?'Scammer: 'Yes, it's me. I was ripped off for everything I had by bad people. Could you bring me some money?'

general_translation: As soon as, Right after, Even if … still
formation: Verb［る］+ そばから + Phrase  Verb［た］+ そばから + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ そばから + Phrase  Verb［た］+ そばから + Phrase
explanation: A formal, old-fashioned structure, implying that as soon as (A), (B). From the side of (A), (B). (B) is often negative.

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車は直したそばから壊れてしまう。
example_sentences.english: My bike breaks as soon as I repair it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は約束をするそばからすぐ約束を破る。
example_sentences.english: She breaks her promises as soon as she makes them.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は注意するそばから失敗をするから、私のいうことは聞いていないんだろう。
example_sentences.english: I guess he doesn't listen to me because he makes mistakes as soon as I warn him.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンを直したそばからまた壊れてしまうから困っている。
example_sentences.english: I'm having trouble with my computer because it breaks down just as soon as I fix it.

example_sentences.japanese: 早く読みすぎると読んだそばから忘れるから、もっとゆっくり読む様にしている。
example_sentences.english: I try to read more slowly, because if I read too quickly, I forget as soon as I read it.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたって人は、「やるな」と言ったそばからやるんだから。
example_sentences.english: People like you are just… As soon as I told you not to do it, you still do it…

example_sentences.japanese: 教わったそばから同じ間違いをおかした。
example_sentences.english: I made the same mistake as soon as I learned of it.

example_sentences.japanese: ケーキが熱いから触らないように言ったそばから こいつは～。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I told him not to touch the cake because it was hot, this guy...

example_sentences.japanese: 新人育成がつらい。彼らは言ったそばからどんどん忘れてしまう。
example_sentences.english: It's hard to train new employees. As soon as I tell them something, they immediately forget it.

example_sentences.japanese: 夫はダイエットをすると言ったそばからポテトチップスを食べ始めたが、それはいつもの事である。
example_sentences.english: My husband started eating chips as soon as he said that he will start a diet, but that's the same as always.

example_sentences.japanese: バイト代が入ったそばから全て使ってしまい、後になってその事を後悔し始めた。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I received the wages for my part time job, I used the whole lot and began to regret it afterwards.

example_sentences.japanese: 「喧嘩をやめなさい」と息子たちを叱ったそばから喧嘩をするので、諦める事にしました。
example_sentences.english: Since my sons will start arguing as soon as I scold them with 'stop fighting', I decided to give up.

example_sentences.japanese: 聞いたそばから忘れてしまうなら、忘れないようにメモを取るようにしたらどうですか？
example_sentences.english: If you forget something as soon as you hear it, how about making sure to take a note in order not to forget it?

example_sentences.japanese: 模試が終わったそばから次の模試の対策を始めるなんて、あなたは学生の鑑ですね！
example_sentences.english: Something like making preparations for the next practice exam as soon as you've finished one, you're really the specimen of a student!

example_sentences.japanese: 認知症を患っている叔母はご飯を食べたそばから忘れてしまうので、一日に何回もご飯を要求してきます。
example_sentences.english: Since my auntie, who suffers from dementia, forgets as soon as she has eaten, she comes requesting food many times a day.

example_sentences.japanese: メリーさん：「夢を覚えている？」  ゆめじさん：「夢なんて起きたそばから忘れてしまうものだけど、夜中に起きてまた眠ると思い出す。」
example_sentences.english: Merry: 'Do you remember your dreams?'Yumeji: 'Dreams are something I forget as soon as I wake up, but if I wake up in the middle of the night and go back to sleep then I remember.'

example_sentences.japanese: 車の洗車を終えるそばから、雨が降ってきた。
example_sentences.english: It started to rain as soon as I was about to finish washing my car.

grammar_point: 訳（わけ）あり(訳（わけ）あって)
general_translation: ～ with reasons, Due to reasons, Defective, Problematic, Unique
formation: 訳（わけ）あり + Noun訳（わけ）あり + な + Noun訳（わけ）あり + の + Noun訳（わけ）あって + Phrase訳（わけ）あり + で + Phrase
casual_structure: 訳（わけ）あり + Noun訳（わけ）あり + な + Noun訳（わけ）あり + の + Noun訳（わけ）あって + Phrase訳（わけ）あり + で + Phrase
explanation: An expression often used to indicate that there are special circumstances that can't be stated openly, or when one is is hesitant to give detailed information.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女、過去にわけありで、なかなか人を信用できないんだって。
example_sentences.english: As she apparently has a complicated past, she can’t trust people.

example_sentences.japanese: 数量限定のわけありアウトレット品ですので、お早めにどうぞ。
example_sentences.english: There are a limited number of outlet items with minor issues, so help yourself soon.

example_sentences.japanese: この古い時計、動かないのはわけありで、中に小さな妖精が住んでるとか何とか……。
example_sentences.english: This old clock doesn’t work for some undisclosed reason. Something about a tiny fairy living inside or something…

example_sentences.japanese: 実はこのＴシャツ、洗濯すると色が変わるわけあり品。驚きのファッションアイテムだね！
example_sentences.english: Actually, this T-shirt is a unique item that changes color when you wash it. A surprising fashion item, right!

example_sentences.japanese: その笑顔の奥に、容易に触れてはならぬわけありの感情が隠されているように思えた。
example_sentences.english: On the other side of that smile, it seemed there were emotions with a complicated past behind them, which shouldn’t be lightly touched upon.

example_sentences.japanese: 当時の判断は、あくまで政治的な配慮という名のもとに下されたわけありの決定だった。
example_sentences.english: The decision made at the time was, after all, a questionable one and made solely under the guise of political considerations.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品の価格が異常に安いのは、製造過程がわけありである可能性が高い。
example_sentences.english: There is a high chance that the unusually low price of this product is due to the manufacturing process being problematic.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の辞職は、表向きは健康上の理由とされたが、内実はわけありと見る向きが多い。
example_sentences.english: Publicly, his resignation was attributed to health reasons, but many saw the truth of the matter as having more complicated reasons.

example_sentences.japanese: 節約志向が強まる中、わけあり品の市場が急成長しているのは消費者心理の変化を反映している。
example_sentences.english: As the savings-focused mindset strengthens, the rapid expansion of the market for ‘products with a reason’ reflects the change in consumer psychology.

example_sentences.japanese: 人件費削減のために行われたリストラには、労働契約上のわけありな事情が絡んでいた。
example_sentences.english: The layoffs which were carried out to reduce labor expenses involved complicated issues concerning the labor contracts.

example_sentences.japanese: わけあって、明日から海外に行きます。
example_sentences.english: Due to reasons, I’m going abroad from tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 「実は今日デートに行けなかったの、ちょっとわけありでね……ごめん。」
example_sentences.english: 'Actually, I couldn’t make it to our date today. There were some circumstances… I’m sorry.

example_sentences.japanese: わけありだのなんのって、つべこべうるさいんだよ！
example_sentences.english: Can you shut up with your endless complaints about there being issues!

example_sentences.japanese: そもそもわけあり商品なんだから、これ以上の値引きはできないよ。
example_sentences.english: Since it is a ‘product with a reason’ to begin with, it can’t be discounted any further.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは、わけあり夫婦で有名だ。
example_sentences.english: We’re famous as a couple with a complicated past.

example_sentences.japanese: わけありの商品は普通よりかなり安いことが多いから、いらなくてもつい買っちゃう。
example_sentences.english: Products with a reason are way cheaper than usual, so I tend to buy them even if I don’t need them. (Defective products are way cheaper than usual, so I tend to buy them even if I don’t need them.)

example_sentences.japanese: 最近なんでこのあたりが「訳ありの地域」って言われてるかわかってきた気がする。
example_sentences.english: Recently, I feel like I have a better grasp on why this area is known as the ‘Region with a reason’. (Recently, I feel like I have a better grasp on why this area is known as the ‘Defective Region’)

example_sentences.japanese: この会社ってなんかみんな訳ありな人だよね。
example_sentences.english: Everyone in this company is a person with a reason. (Everyone in this company has a colorful background)

example_sentences.japanese: この車はわけありな車だから、買ってすぐ壊れても修理代はすべてこっちもち。
example_sentences.english: This car has a reason, so even if it breaks immediately after purchase, I have to pay out of pocket if anything happens to it. (This car is defective/has been in an accident, so even if it breaks immediately after purchase, I have to pay out of pocket if anything happens to it)

example_sentences.japanese: わけあり商品は欠陥があっても、安いからすぐ売れることが多い。
example_sentences.english: Even if a defective product has defects, they sell fast because they are cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が住んでいるところはわけあり物件だから、東京駅から徒歩４分で２ＬＤＫだけど家賃が５万なんだよ！
example_sentences.english: The place that I am staying at is a place with reason, so the rent is only 50,000 even though it is a 2LDK that is a 4 minute walk from Tokyo station. (The place that I am staying at is a stigmatized property, so the rent is only 50,000 even though it is a 2LDK that is a 4 minute walk from Tokyo station.)

example_sentences.japanese: わけあって、明日から数日間出勤できません。
example_sentences.english: Due to reasons, I will not be able to come into work for a few days starting tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 色々とわけありで、来年から日本で生活することが決まりました。
example_sentences.english: Due to many reasons, I will be living in Japan starting next year.

general_translation: When it came to, Only when, Only after, Go as far as
formation: Verb + に至（いた）って(1)Noun + に至（いた）って(1)(1)に至（いた）り
casual_structure: Verb + に至（いた）って(1)Noun + に至（いた）って(1)(1)に至（いた）り
explanation: A grammar point showing that only when something had gone as far as (A), (B). Upon reaching the climax of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 過労で意識を失うにいたって、ようやく働きすぎたことがわかった。
example_sentences.english: Only when I collapsed due to overwork, did I finally realize that I worked too hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩に注意されるにいたって、どれだけ俺が自分勝手だったかが分かった。
example_sentences.english: It wasn't until I was warned by a senior colleague that I realized how selfish I had been.

example_sentences.japanese: 工場で大きな事故が発生するにいたって安全大会を実施する様では、この工場では事故が起こり続けます。
example_sentences.english: If a safety meeting is held only after a major accident occurs at the plant, accidents will continue to occur at this plant.

example_sentences.japanese: 糖尿病にいたって、食生活に気をつける様になった。
example_sentences.english: Only when I got diabetes, I started to watch what I ate.

example_sentences.japanese: この年にいたって会社を立ち上げるなんて、自分でもびっくりだよ。
example_sentences.english: Deciding to start a company only after reaching such an age, even I am surprised.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の祖父は肺不全にいたって、いよいよタバコを止めざるをえないことを認めた。
example_sentences.english: Only when his lungs failed, did my grandfather finally accept that he has no choice but to stop smoking.

example_sentences.japanese: 手に負えなくなったこの段階にいたってようやく緊急事態を宣言しました。
example_sentences.english: Only at this point, when things got out of hand, (did the government) finally declare a state of emergency.

example_sentences.japanese: 訴えられる事が決まるにいたってようやく、彼は自分が何をしたか気づいたようだ。
example_sentences.english: Only when the accusation was determined did he realize what he had done.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「何千ものバナナの木が枯れるにいたって、バナナ産業は初めてパナマ病の深刻さに気が付いた。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Only when thousands of banana trees died, did the banana industry realize the seriousness of the Panama disease for the first time.'

example_sentences.japanese: この年にいたって海外移住を決断するなんて、自分でも自身の決断に驚いています。
example_sentences.english: Deciding to move abroad only after reaching such an age, I myself am surprised at my decision.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は家宅捜索を受ける段にいたって、やっと自分の置かれている状況を理解したようである。
example_sentences.english: It seems that only at the point when her house had been searched that she finally understood the situation she was in.

example_sentences.japanese: 髪が抜け落ちたり白髪混じりになったりするにいたって、自分がストレスを感じている事に気づいた。
example_sentences.english: Only when things like my hair falling out and I started getting a few gray hairs did I realize that I was stressed.

example_sentences.japanese: 問題が発生するにいたって会議をするようでは、この会社が成長するとは思えません。
example_sentences.english: Since it seems like this company has meetings only after a problem springs forth, I cannot think that it is really going anywhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供をもつにいたって、初めて自分の親や世の中の親が抱える問題や苦労を理解出来るようになりました。
example_sentences.english: Only after having kids did I first realize the problems and hardships that my parents and parents all over the world bear.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「その建物は崩壊するにいたって、ようやく開発業者がどのくらい建築物の強度設計の問題を軽視したかが明らかになった。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Only when the building collapsed, did it finally become clear how much the developer neglected the issue of strength in the design of the building.'

example_sentences.japanese: パニックに襲われた私は、車のアラームが鳴るにいたってようやく、「ちがう車に入ってしまった！」ということに気がついた。
example_sentences.english: Struck with panic, only after the alarm went off, I realized that I entered the wrong car!

general_translation: Not even, Not at all, Never could have
formation: Noun + だに + しないExceptions:夢（ゆめ） + （に）+ だに + 思（おも）わない
casual_structure: Noun + だに + しないExceptions:夢（ゆめ） + （に）+ だに + 思（おも）わない
explanation: A formal particle structure, indicating that even the slightest example of (A) didn't happen.

example_sentences.japanese: そのカメレオンは外敵から身を隠すために微動だにしていません。
example_sentences.english: In order to hide itself from predators, that chameleon does not even slightly quiver.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカでこんな大きい地震が来るとは誰も予想だにしなかった。
example_sentences.english: No one could have expected such a big earthquake to happen in the United States.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が彼女と別れるなんて想像だにしなかったよ。
example_sentences.english: I would have never imagined he would leave her.

example_sentences.japanese: まさかこの年になって子供を授かるなんて思いだにしていなかった。
example_sentences.english: I would have never thought I would have a child at this age.

example_sentences.japanese: アニメのプロローグ、語り手：「あのとき、俺はあんな悲劇が待ち受けていたなんて、夢にだに思わなかった。」
example_sentences.english: Anime prologue, narrator: 'Back then, I couldn't have even dreamed that such a tragedy lay ahead.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「彼女はソファーに座ったままで、まるで本物の人形のように微動だにしない。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'She remained seated on the sofa, just like a doll, not even moving an inch.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「ビットコインがこれほどになるとは２００９年始めには誰も予想だにしなかった。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'No one could have even predicted in early 2009 that bitcoin would come this far.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「彼が心の中にこんな暗闇を抱えていたなど、勇者は夢想だにしなかった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'The hero couldn't have even dreamed that he was carrying such darkness in his heart.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「彼女の意見を一顧だにせず、彼は足の向くままに先に行った。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Without even giving a thought to her opinion, he continued on (in the direction his feet took him).'

example_sentences.japanese: まさか一年も付き合っていない彼にプロポーズされるなんて予想だにしていなかった。
example_sentences.english: Honestly, I never could have imagined that I would be proposed to by him, whom I haven't even been dating for a year.

example_sentences.japanese: 不登校の息子がまた学校に行くなんて想像だにしていなかったので、驚いています。
example_sentences.english: Because I could not even imagine that my dropout son would do something like go to school again, I am really surprised.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな平穏な村で残忍な連続殺人事件が起きるなんて、誰もが予想だにしていなかった。
example_sentences.english: That brutal serial killings like this could happen in such a peaceful town, nobody could even have imagined it.

example_sentences.japanese: 厳格で頑固な父から私たちの結婚に対して予想だにしない言葉が飛び出し、私たちは泣いて喜びました。
example_sentences.english: With words we could not even expect coming from my strict and stubborn father in relation to our marriage, we wept with happiness.

example_sentences.japanese: 確かに小さい頃から海外に住むのが夢だったが、まさか本当に自分が海外に住むとは思いだにしていなかった。
example_sentences.english: While it is indeed true that I dreamed of living abroad ever since I was a child, I honestly have not even thought that I would live overseas.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「たかぎさん『にしかたさんのことが大好きよ。』たかぎの口からは想像だにしていなかった言葉がいきなり飛び出してきた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel, Takagi-san: 'I love you, Nishikata-san.'The words I never could have imagined suddenly came out of Takagi's mouth.

general_translation: On the occasion of, While … as well, While …  (one is) at it, During, Along the way
formation: Verb［stem］+ がてらNoun + がてら,
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ がてらNoun + がてら,
explanation: A formal particle, indicating that something is being done on the same occasion as (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「帰りがてら手紙出してくるね。」
example_sentences.english: I'll post the letter on my way home as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の家に行きがてら、近くの神社にお参りに行った。
example_sentences.english: While going to my friend's house, I went to pray at the shrine nearby as well.

example_sentences.japanese: ワンちゃんの散歩がてらに、ペットショップにいってくる。
example_sentences.english: While taking my dog on a walk, I am going to go to the pet store as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動がてらに会社まで自転車で行くことにした。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of exercising, I decided to ride the bicycle to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 弟を駅から迎えがてらに、今夜の夕飯の買い物をしに行く。
example_sentences.english: I will go grocery shopping for tonight's dinner on my way to pick up my brother as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 「イノシシの散歩がてら、ちょっとコンビニまで行ってきます。」
example_sentences.english: 'While taking a walk with my pet wild boar, I will go to the convenience store as well.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「お花見がてら、公園を散歩しよう。」
example_sentences.english: 'Let's take a walk in the park while viewing the cherry blossoms as well.'

example_sentences.japanese: 回顧録：「ヒースロー空港への移動がてら、観光スポットを訪れた。」
example_sentences.english: Memoir: 'I visited some tourist attractions on my way to Heathrow Airport as well.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「じゃあ買い物がてら、紅葉を見に行かないか？」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'So, why don't we view the autumn leaves while shopping as well?'

example_sentences.japanese: 広告：「観光の後には休憩がてら立ち寄ってみてはいかがでしょうか。」
example_sentences.english: Restaurant advertisement: 'How about you drop by while taking a break after sightseeing (as well)?'

example_sentences.japanese: 帰省がてら懐かしい喫茶店やゲームセンター、よく行っていた海岸へ足を運ぶつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: I plan to make my way to a nostalgic coffee shop and game center along the way home, and the beach that I used to often go to as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動がてらバス停を二つ手前で降りて、残りの距離を早歩きで歩く事にしました。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of exercising, I decided to hop off the bus two stops before my place and quickly walk the remaining distance.

example_sentences.japanese: 気分転換のためにお散歩がてら、近所の神社に立ち寄る事にした。
example_sentences.english: For a change of pace, while taking a stroll, I decided to stop at a neighborhood shrine as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 鬱になってしまったので、療養がてら仕事を長期的に休む決断をしました。
example_sentences.english: Since I became depressed, while I was recuperating I decided to take a long-term break from work as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 不倫相手からの「仕事がてら、また家に泊まりにきたら？」というメールを夫に見られてしまった。
example_sentences.english: The message from the person that I was cheating with that said 'while you're at work, why don't you come stay at my place as well?' was unfortunately seen by my husband.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強がてら音楽を聴いていたら、いつの間にか勉強は一切せずに音楽だけ聴いていた事に気づきました。
example_sentences.english: When I was listening to music on the occasion of doing some study, I suddenly realized that I had not done any study at all, but was just listening to music.

general_translation: In order to, To, For the purpose of
formation: Verb［ない］+ ん + が + ため（に）Verb［ない］+ ん + が + ため + の + NounExceptions:する ￫ せんがため
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ん + が + ため（に）Verb［ない］+ ん + が + ため + の + NounExceptions:する ￫ せんがため
explanation: An old-fashioned phrase, implying that something is being done in order to (A). The speaker has a strong will or intent to achieve (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ソクラテス：「生きんがために食え、食わんがために生きるな」
example_sentences.english: Socrates: 'Thou shouldst eat to live; not live to eat.' (for the purpose of)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は若い頃からお金を貯めんがために、色々と我慢してきた。
example_sentences.english: In order to save up money, he has sacrificed a lot since he was young.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の両親たちは私たちの夢を叶えんがために、毎日休まずに仕事をしてきました。
example_sentences.english: In order to fulfill our dreams, my parents have worked everyday without any rest.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなことはしたくないが大会で勝たんがためのことだ。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to do such a thing, but will in order to win this competition.

example_sentences.japanese: 売れ残りの商品を売らんがための作戦を考えたが何も思いつかなかった。
example_sentences.english: I tried to come up with a strategy in order to sell the unsold goods, but came up with nothing.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「力の指輪をえんがための戦争が始まった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'The war for the purpose of acquiring the ring of power has begun.'

example_sentences.japanese: 溺れている子供をたすけんがために川に飛び込んだ人が亡くなってしまったそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the person who dove into the river to save the drowning child unfortunately passed away.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はこの世に何かをなさんがために生まれてきたはずだが、それが何かはまだ分からない。
example_sentences.english: I was bound to be born into this world for the purpose of achieving something, but I still do not know just what that is.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「その会社は不良品をうらんがために、高齢者の弱みにつけ込んだ。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'That company took advantage of the elderly in order to sell defective products.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「魔王の軍よりこの世界をすくわんがためにドワーフと人間とエルフとの協力が必要である。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'The cooperation of dwarves, humans, and elves is needed in order to save the world from the army of the Demon King.'

example_sentences.japanese: 時代小説、Ａ：「我々が失敗したら？」 Ｂ：「そうなれば、みずからの身をまもらんがため退却を余儀なくされるときがくるかもしれぬ。」
example_sentences.english: A historical novel, A: 'And what if we fail?' B: 'If that happens, the time may come when we will be forced to retreat in order to protect ourselves. '

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「それは何としても戦争を回避せんがための行動だったのは誰の目にも明らかであろう。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'It is likely obvious to everybody that that was an action taken for the purpose of avoiding the war at all costs.'

example_sentences.japanese: 長女を一流企業にいれんがために、賄賂となる金を会社に渡しました。
example_sentences.english: In order to get my eldest daughter into a first-rate company, I handed over what would amount as a bribe to the business.

example_sentences.japanese: 昇進するという目標を達成せんがために、僕は毎日上司の顔色を窺いながら働いている。
example_sentences.english: For the purpose of attaining my goal of getting a promotion, I work while trying to infer the needs of my boss on a daily basis.

example_sentences.japanese: 試合でかたんがために必死に練習をする事は大事だが、練習のし過ぎはかえって良くないですよ。
example_sentences.english: It is important to fervently train in order to win a contest, but rather training too much is not good.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は退職後にレストランを開くという夢をかなえんがために、必死に経理と料理の勉強をしています。
example_sentences.english: In order that my father's dream of opening a restaurant after his retirement can be fulfilled, he is frantically studying accounting and cooking.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は自分の作戦を成功させんがために、友達を裏切った。
example_sentences.english: She betrayed her friends in order to make her plans work.

general_translation: Regardless of (whatever … is), Irrespective of (whatever … is)
formation: Noun + (の) + いかん + に関（かか）わらず(1)(1) によらず、を問（と）わず
casual_structure: Noun + (の) + いかん + に関（かか）わらず(1)(1) によらず、を問（と）わず
explanation: A formal phrase, meaning in what way. Regardless of in what way, (A). Without questioning in what way, (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 結果いかんをとわず、この学校では努力をした生徒を褒めるようにしています。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of results, this school makes sure to praise students that put in effort.

example_sentences.japanese: 天候のいかんにかかわらず、明日のコンサートは予定通りに開催されます。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of the weather, the concert tomorrow will be held as scheduled.

example_sentences.japanese: 予約日の２４時間前であれば、理由のいかんによらず、キャンセル料を取られずにキャンセルをすることができます。
example_sentences.english: Cancellations may be made 24 hours prior to the appointment date, regardless of the reason without incurring a cancellation fee.

example_sentences.japanese: 未経験者や経験者のいかんをとわず、ここで働く前には新規研修を受けてもらいます。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you are experienced or not, we require everyone to undergo training before working here.

example_sentences.japanese: テストの形式いかんをとわず自分の力を最大限出せるように勉強しよう。
example_sentences.english: Irrespective of the test format, I shall study in order to put forward my absolute best performance.

example_sentences.japanese: これまでの経歴いかんをとわず、我が社は多様な人材を受け入れる方針だ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of your career history thus far, our company has a policy of accepting a range of talented individuals.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は勝敗いかんをとわず、全力でプレーした息子を褒め称えるつもりです。
example_sentences.english: Irrespective of winning or losing, I intend to sing the praises of my son, who played with all of his might.

example_sentences.japanese: 発信する内容のいかんをとわず、私たちは自由に発言する権利を与えられるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of the transmission contents, we ought to be given the right to voice things freely.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校の方針：「本校はプログラム及び活動などでは、宗教・国籍等のいかんをとわず、いかなる差別も許しません。」
example_sentences.english: School policy: 'The school will not discriminate regardless of religion or ethnic origin, and so on, in its programs or activities.'

example_sentences.japanese: ライセンス契約：「当社は事情のいかんにかかわらず、本品の不適切な使用によって生じたいかなる損害については責任を負いません。」
example_sentences.english: License agreement: 'The company will not be held responsible for any damage caused due to the improper usage of the product regardless of (what) the circumstances (are).'

example_sentences.japanese: 教授が「理由のいかんをとわず提出期限を過ぎたレポートは受け取らないつもりだ」と言ったから、絶対に締め切りまでに提出しないと！
example_sentences.english: Because the teacher said 'regardless of the reason, I intend not to accept any report submissions beyond the submission period', I absolutely must submit it by the deadline.

example_sentences.japanese: 確かに国籍や年齢のいかんをとわずＴＯＥＩＣを受験する事が出来ますが、あなたにはまだ早いと思います。
example_sentences.english: While it is certainly true that you may take the TOEIC regardless of things like your age or nationality, I think it is still a bit early for you.

example_sentences.japanese: 販売店の返品ポリシー：「商品到着後２週間以内であれば、理由のいかんによらず、自由に返品することが可能です。」
example_sentences.english: Return policy of a store: 'It is possible to return any product, free of charge, regardless of (what) the reason (is) if the return falls within two weeks of the delivery of the product.'

example_sentences.japanese: 試験は一部の試験科目でも合格点に達しなければ、他の試験科目の成績のいかんにかかわらず、不合格となります。
example_sentences.english: If the student does not achieve a passing mark in any part of the exam, then regardless of (what) the results of the other parts (are) the test will be considered failed.

example_sentences.japanese: 登録確認のメール：「このメッセージに返信しないようお願いいたします。返信いただいてもこちらのメールアドレスは送信専用なので内容のいかんにかかわらずお答えできません。ご了承ください。」
example_sentences.english: A registration confirmation email: 'We kindly ask you to not reply to this message. Even if you do so, this mail address is dedicated only to sending, therefore we will not be able to answer, regardless of (what) the contents of the message (are). Thank you for your understanding.'

grammar_point: う・よう + にも～ない
general_translation: Cannot... even if one wants or tries, Would like but cannot, Wants or tries but cannot
formation: Verb1［おう］ + にも + Verb1［できる］［ない］Verb［おう］ +  にも + (Reason) Phrase
casual_structure: Verb1［おう］ + にも + Verb1［できる］［ない］Verb［おう］ +  にも + (Reason) Phrase
explanation: An expression emphasizing that even if someone wants to (A), they can't. Even with the strong will or intent to (A), it can't be done.

example_sentences.japanese: 亡き妻の笑顔はわすれようにも忘れられない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot forget the smile of my late wife, even if I try to.

example_sentences.japanese: もう夜遅いから電車もバスも走ってないし、全然タクシーも通らないし、帰ろうにも帰れない。
example_sentences.english: Since it is late at night,  there aren't any trains or buses, and I haven't seen a taxi, so I can't go home even if I wanted to.

example_sentences.japanese: 色々と仕事のことで悩んでいるから、毎晩寝ようにも寝れない。
example_sentences.english: I can't sleep even if I wanted to because I am worried about a lot of things regarding work.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日出てきた釣竿を買いたいけど、高いから買おうにも買えない。
example_sentences.english: I want to buy the new fishing rod that came out yesterday, but since it is expensive, I can't buy it even if I wanted to.

example_sentences.japanese: プロジェクトについて心配するあまり、ねようにも寝られない。
example_sentences.english: I am so worried about the project that I cannot sleep even if I try.

example_sentences.japanese: 車がないのなら、運転しようにも運転できないでしょう？
example_sentences.english: If you don’t have a car, you couldn’t drive even if you wanted to, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪をひいて喉が痛すぎて、返事をしようにも出来ません。
example_sentences.english: I caught a cold, and my throat hurts so much, so I can’t reply even if try to.

example_sentences.japanese: テーマパークには行きたいですが、骨折をしていてあるこうにも歩けないのです。
example_sentences.english: I want to go to a theme park, but I broke a bone and can’t walk even if I try to.

example_sentences.japanese: 避難しようにも道が塞がっていて避難経路が確保できない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I tried to evacuate, the road is blocked so I can’t secure a route of evacuation.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が欲しいが、子供をつくろうにも相手がいないから作れない。
example_sentences.english: I want kids, but even if I do want to have them, I don’t have a partner, so I cannot.

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しいものをたべようにも、胃が小さくなってしまってあまり食べられません。
example_sentences.english: Even if I try to eat nice things, my appetite shrunk, so I unfortunately can’t eat that much.

example_sentences.japanese: 藤沼探偵：「彼が犯人だと思うけど、逮捕しようにも、証拠がないんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Detective Fujinuma: 'I think that he is the criminal, but even if I try to arrest him, I have no proof.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「今日は実家に帰るはずだったけど、ここをでようにも、こんな吹雪じゃ道が通じないから無理だ。」
example_sentences.english: I was supposed to return home today, but even if I tried to leave, it is impossible in this snow storm.

example_sentences.japanese: コメディ、語り手：「ペイン軍曹はたたかおうにも相手がいなくて困っている。とっくにすべての敵を殺したからだ。」
example_sentences.english: Comedy, narrator: 'Sergeant Pain was greatly troubled because even though he wants to fight, there is no one to fight. He already killed them all a long time ago.'

example_sentences.japanese: アクション映画、バスの運転手は警察官に：「時速が８０キロを下回るとバスに隠された爆弾が爆発するから減速しようにもできないわ。」
example_sentences.english: Action movie, the bus driver to the policeman: 'If the speed falls below 80 km/h, the bomb hidden in the bus will explode, so I cannot slow down even though I want to!'

example_sentences.japanese: 行きたくないけど、先輩に誘われたら断るに断れない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to go, but since my senpai invited me, I can't say no even if I wanted to. (Mental reason)

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯を無くしてしまったから、上司に連絡しようにもできない。
example_sentences.english: Since I lost my phone, I can't call my boss even if I wanted to. (Physical reason)

grammar_point: く + もなんともない
general_translation: Not... or anything, Not at all, Not, By no means, Definitely not, Nothing like that
formation: ［い］Adjective［く］+ もなんともない
casual_structure: ［い］Adjective［く］+ もなんともない
explanation: A strong phrase, showing that something is nothing like (A). It doesn't have the characteristic of (A), or even anything like (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「噂なんて全然しりたくもなんともないけど。」
example_sentences.english: 'I don't want to know any rumors at all.'

example_sentences.japanese: ホラー映画にしたら怖くもなんともない、むしろちょっとコメディーっぽいかも。
example_sentences.english: As a horror movie, this is not scary at all. Matter of fact, it's more like a comedy movie.

example_sentences.japanese: まだまだだな、お前のパンチを喰らっても痒くもなんともないぞ。
example_sentences.english: You still have a long way to go. Even after getting punched by you, it doesn't even itch.

example_sentences.japanese: ここで売ってるもんは全て珍しいとかって言ってるけど、実は珍しくもなんともないんだよ。他の店に行くと五千円以下で売ってるよ。
example_sentences.english: They are saying that everything they are selling is rare, but actually they are not rare at all. If you go to other stores, you can see that they sell them for under 5 thousand yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 「もうやめない？その話。おもしろくもなんともないから！」
example_sentences.english: 'Won't you stop (talking about) that topic? Because it is not interesting at all!'

example_sentences.japanese: この料理はおいしくもなんともないから、感想は何もない。
example_sentences.english: This food is not delicious or anything at all, so I don’t have any impressions.

example_sentences.japanese: かなしくもなんともないのに急に涙が出てきて混乱しています。
example_sentences.english: I am confused because, despite not being sad or anything like that, tears suddenly started pouring out.

example_sentences.japanese: みたくもなんともないテレビ番組を見たら、予想通りつまらなかった。
example_sentences.english: When I watched a TV show that I by no means wanted to watch, it was boring just I had predicted.

example_sentences.japanese: かっこよくもなんともない人にナンパされて、逆にガッカリしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Getting chatted up by a person who is not cool by any means has me feeling, on the contrary, quite disappointed.

example_sentences.japanese: はしりたくもなんともないのに、強制的に走らされてゲンナリしています。
example_sentences.english: Despite not wanting to run or anything like that, I am worn out because I was forced to.

example_sentences.japanese: 注射をされた子猫が「いたくもなんともないさ」と強がっている。
example_sentences.english: The kitten who received a vaccine is acting tough like ‘It does not hurt or anything like that at all’.

example_sentences.japanese: ホラー映画のレビュー：「ゾンビ映画にしてはこわくもなんともない。それでも面白いからハマる。」
example_sentences.english: Review of a horror movie: 'For a zombie movie, it is not scary at all. But still, one can get into it since it's interesting'

example_sentences.japanese: 「雪なんて、降ってもうれしくもなんともないよ。むしろ歩道の除雪をしないといけないから怒っているんだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Even if it snows, I am not happy at all. Rather, I am angry that I have to clear the sidewalk from snow.'

example_sentences.japanese: 東京観光、コマリ：「東京スカイツリーは本当に大きいねえ。」ヒカゲ：「私にはめずらしくもなんともないけど。初めての人は驚くよね。」
example_sentences.english: Tokyo sightseeing, Komari: 'Tokyo Skytree is really big!' Hikage: 'It's not unusual for me at all. But, I imagine that it's amazing for first-timers. '

example_sentences.japanese: ミツバが転んだ、エマ：「大丈夫？」ミツバ：「へいきだよ。」 エマ：「血、出てるよ。」 ミツバ：「でも、いたくもなんともないよ。」
example_sentences.english: Mitsuba has fallen over, Emma: 'Are you ok?'Mitsuba: 'I'm ok!'Emma: 'You're bleeding!'Mitsuba: 'But, it doesn't hurt at all.'

example_sentences.japanese: 私はジェットコースターとかが苦手だから遊園地に行きたくもなんともない。
example_sentences.english: Since I dislike roller coasters, I don't want to go to amusement parks at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のことは聞きたくもなんともない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to hear about him at all.

general_translation: Just, Even just, Even merely
formation: Verb + だに
casual_structure: Verb + だに
explanation: A formal particle structure, indicating that even the slightest amount of (A) is enough to trigger (B). Merely by (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「人間にとってはダニを食べるのは考えるだにおぞましい。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'For a human being, just thinking about eating ticks is repulsive.'

example_sentences.japanese: あんな地獄みたいな職場にまた明日も行かないとって考えるだに気が重くなる。
example_sentences.english: Even just the thought of having to go back to that hellish workplace again tomorrow makes me feel depressed.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のことを思い出すだに、悲しくなります。
example_sentences.english: Just remembering about him makes me sad.

example_sentences.japanese: 部長からもらった仕事の量を見るだに、やる気が失せる。
example_sentences.english: I lose all motivation by just looking at the amount of work my boss gave me.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「クトゥルフは見るだに正気を失ってしまうほどたいへん恐ろしい化物であるらしい。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'It is said that Cthulhu is a monster so awfully scary that one goes mad just by seeing it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「その映画のワンシーンを思い出すだに、胸が痛くなります。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Just recalling that movie scene breaks my heart.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「ただ、その事故の話を聞くだに古傷が疼く。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Just hearing a conversation about that accident makes my old wound throb with pain.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「太陽の中心の温度は想像するだに恐ろしい。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Just imagining the temperature at the center of the sun is terrifying.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「どんなことになるのか思うだに恐ろしくなる。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Just thinking about what will happen scares me.'

general_translation: Or, Either or
formation: Verb［る］(A) + なり + Verb［る］(B) + なり + するNoun (A) + （Particle(1)）+ なり + Noun (B) + （Particle(1)）+ なりNoun (A) + なり + Noun (B) + なり + （Particle(1)）Verb［る］+ なり + WH-Word + （Particle）+ なり + するNoun + （Particle(1)）+ なり + WH-Word + （Particle(1)）+ なり(1) Particles を and が cannot be used in this case
casual_structure: Verb［る］(A) + なり + Verb［る］(B) + なり + するNoun (A) + （Particle(1)）+ なり + Noun (B) + （Particle(1)）+ なりNoun (A) + なり + Noun (B) + なり + （Particle(1)）Verb［る］+ なり + WH-Word + （Particle）+ なり + するNoun + （Particle(1)）+ なり + WH-Word + （Particle(1)）+ なり(1) Particles を and が cannot be used in this case
explanation: A polite construction, indicating non-exhaustive lists of actions or things. Whether it takes the shape of (A) or (B), (C).

example_sentences.japanese: ヨーロッパなら、フランスなりイタリアなり、料理が美味しいところに行きたい。
example_sentences.english: If it’s Europe, whether it’s France or Italy, I want to go to a place with delicious food.

example_sentences.japanese: もうちょっと待機しないといけなさそうだから、タバコを吸うなり弁当食べるなりして待ってな。準備ができたら呼ぶからゆっくりしてな。
example_sentences.english: It seems like we have to wait a little longer, so why don't you go smoke some cigarettes or eat your lunch and wait. Once everything is ready, I'll let you know so take your time.

example_sentences.japanese: どうぞ受け取ってください。いらないなら売るなり捨てるなりしてもらっても結構ですので。
example_sentences.english: Please take this. If you don't want it you can sell it or throw it away.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅れるなら電話なりメールなりするのが社会人としての常識じゃないのか？！
example_sentences.english: Isn't it common sense as a member of society to call or text if you are going to be late?!

example_sentences.japanese: なんでお前はいつもそう一人でなんでも解決しようとするんだ？俺になり高橋になり相談してくれればいいのに！
example_sentences.english: Why do you always try to solve everything on your own? You should come talk to me or Takahashi!

example_sentences.japanese: 完璧な人はいない。大なり小なり欠点はあるものだ。
example_sentences.english: Nobody is perfect. To either a greater or lesser extent, we all have faults.

example_sentences.japanese: ご飯にするなり運動するなり好きにすればいいけど、早く寝なさいよ。
example_sentences.english: Do whatever you want whether it is eating or doing exercise, but please go to sleep early.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が彼氏に：「電話なり何なりで、早く連絡しなさいよ。」
example_sentences.english: Girlfriend to boyfriend: 'Contact me as soon as possible, by phone or something.'

example_sentences.japanese: お母さん：「私じゃなくて、お姉ちゃんなりお兄ちゃんなりに質問して！」
example_sentences.english: Mother: ‘Rather than me, ask your sister or brother!’

example_sentences.japanese: 上司：「具合が悪いなら、時短勤務にするなり欠席するなりしなさい。」
example_sentences.english: Boss: ‘If you’re in bad shape, please either shorten your hours or take a leave of absence.’

example_sentences.japanese: あなたには、両親なり友達なり、心から信頼できる人はいますか？
example_sentences.english: Whether it is your parents or your friends, is there anyone that you can completely trust?

example_sentences.japanese: 友達にアドバイスする：「黙ってばかりいないでよ。喧嘩するなり文句を言うなりしてみたら？」
example_sentences.english: Giving advice to a friend: 'Don't be quiet all the time! Why don't you try to argue or complain?'

example_sentences.japanese: 父親は娘に：「孤独を感じていたのなら、俺になり母さんになり電話くれればよかったのに。」
example_sentences.english: Father to daughter: 'If you were feeling lonely, you should have called me or mom…'

example_sentences.japanese: 怪我をしている友達にアドバイスする：「ケガをしてるよ！絆創膏を貼るなり包帯を巻くなりした方がいいんじゃないかな！」
example_sentences.english: Giving advice to an injured friend: 'You are injured! I think you'd better put a band-aid on or bandage it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 怒った親が子供に：「部屋を漫画本だらけにしないで！読まないものは売るなり捨てるなりして片づけなさい！」
example_sentences.english: Angry parent to a child: 'Don't scatter the manga all over the room! Either sell or throw away the things you don't read!

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、勇者が魔王に：「仲間にだけは手を出さないでください。俺を煮るなり焼くなり好きにしていい！」
example_sentences.english: A novel, Hero to Demon King: 'Please don't lay a hand on my friends! Instead, you can do whatever you like to me!' (Literally - Boil me or grill me)

general_translation: Kind of, Might, Slightly, It’s not (impossible) that, Somewhat, In some respects
formation: Verb［ない］+ （もの）+ でも(1) + ない(1)では
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ （もの）+ でも(1) + ない(1)では
explanation: A grammar point indicating that something is slightly doing (A), or that it's not impossible. It's not even that (A) isn't happening.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの考えがわからないでもないけど、反対するね。
example_sentences.english: I kind of understand what you’re thinking, but I object.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつが悪いとは思わないでもないけど、お前にも少しは非があると思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I kind of think he is in the wrong, but I think you are a little at fault too.

example_sentences.japanese: まあ、そう言われてみれば鳥に見えなくもないけど...
example_sentences.english: Well, when you put it like that, it kind of looks like a bird…

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が謝ってきたら、彼女がしたことを許す気がないでもない。
example_sentences.english: If she comes apologizing, I might forgive her for what she's done.

example_sentences.japanese: ピアノを弾くのは好きだが、ピアノのレッスンをやめようと思うことがなくもない。
example_sentences.english: I like to play the piano, but there are times when I kind of think about quitting piano lessons.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの考えが分からないものでもないけど、そういうことはあまり口に出さないほうがいいと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I kind of understand your opinion, but I don't think you should say things like that out loud.

example_sentences.japanese: パクチーはたべられないでもないけどさ、食べるとウッてなるんだよ。
example_sentences.english: It’s not that I can’t eat coriander, but if I eat it, I feel like I am gonna hurl.

example_sentences.japanese: この洋服、きられないでもないけど、やっぱりキツイなぁ〜。
example_sentences.english: These clothes, it’s not that I can’t wear them, but they really are tight.

example_sentences.japanese: トイレに行きたい気がしないでもないけど、まだ並ばなくてもいいかな…。
example_sentences.english: I kind of feel like going to the toilet, but it’s probably fine if we don’t line up yet...

example_sentences.japanese: このブランドのあのバッグは１０万円？！かえないでもないけど、勇気が出ないなぁ〜。
example_sentences.english: That bag from this brand is $1,000?! It’s not that I can’t buy it, but I can’t muster up the courage to get it.

example_sentences.japanese: 「なんとなく彼が言った話には欠陥や問題がたくさんあるような気がしないでもないが、いってくれないよりマシだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I kind of feel that there are many gaps and problems in his story, but it is better than nothing.'

example_sentences.japanese: ペトルーチオ：「ケイトは顔だけ見ると、とても美しいとかんじられないでもないんだけど・・・性格が悪い。」
example_sentences.english: Petruchio: 'When looking only at the face, Kate can seem kind of pretty, but her character is awful.'

example_sentences.japanese: お金が全てだという彼の考えが正しいとおもわないでもないが、それが事実だとしたら悲しい。
example_sentences.english: It’s not that I don’t think that his way of thinking that money is everything is correct, but assuming that is the reality, it is sad.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩：「あの雲を見ろよ。シマウマみたいに見えるぞ。」 後輩：「まあシマウマにみえないでもないですね。」
example_sentences.english: Senpai: 'Look at that cloud! It looks like a zebra.'Kouhai: 'Well, it kind of looks like a zebra.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友人に文句を言う：「最近、両親はうちの子犬に夢中だよ。まあその気持ちはわからないでもないけど。とても可愛らしいから。」
example_sentences.english: Complaining to a friend: 'Recently, my parents are all about our puppy! I kind of understand them though. It's pretty adorable.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話、ちよ：「猫が好きじゃないの？かわいくない？」 さかき：「猫はかわいいとおもわないでもないけど、噛むしひっかくしできるだけ避けるよ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends, Chiyo: 'Don't you like cats? Aren't they cute?'Sakaki: 'I think that they are kind of cute, but they bite and scratch so I try to avoid them as much as possible.'

general_translation: It is a fact that, But, Even more than, It goes without saying, Not only but also,
formation: Noun + もさることながら
casual_structure: Noun + もさることながら
explanation: A formal grammar point, highlighting that while (A) is true, (B). Even while that sort of (A) is the case, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: モナ・リザは美しい画もさることながら、やはり目を引くのは神秘的な微笑である。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that Mona Lisa is a beautiful painting, but it is the mysterious smile that attracts the attention after all.

example_sentences.japanese: あのブランドが出す商品もさることながら、マーケティングも素晴らしい。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that the products that the brand produces are amazing, but also how they market them.

example_sentences.japanese: このパソコンは機能もさることながら、デザインもいい。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that the features of this computer are good, but so is the design.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を勉強するにおいて漢字もさることながら、文法も勉強しなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to studying Japanese, it is a fact that you need to study not only kanji, but also grammar too.

example_sentences.japanese: 日頃の心がけもさることながら、今回は運が味方してくれたようだ。
example_sentences.english: Even more than my usual efforts, it would seem luck was on my side this time.

example_sentences.japanese: 見た目もさることながら性格も素晴らしい彼がモテるのは当然のことです。
example_sentences.english: It’s only natural that he’s popular, given that not only his appearance but also his personality is wonderful.

example_sentences.japanese: 歌詞もさることながらメロディーもいいのだから、この曲はやっぱり最高だ。
example_sentences.english: Even more than the lyrics, since the melody is good too, this song is really the best.

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しさもさることながら見た目も凄いこのフレンチレストランは、大人気です。
example_sentences.english: While it is a fact that the food is delicious, since the look of this French restaurant is awesome too, it’s super popular.

example_sentences.japanese: リーダーの発表は、内容がまとまっているのもさることながら、パワーポイントが見やすい。
example_sentences.english: While it’s a fact that the content of the leader’s announcement is organized, the power point is also easy to see.

example_sentences.japanese: 体の柔軟さもさることながらスタミナまであるその体操選手の演技は、圧巻である。
example_sentences.english: Even more than their flexibility, since that gymnast’s performance is also full of energy, it is superb.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を勉強するとき、熱心さもさることながら、長い目で見て一貫性も重要な要素である。
example_sentences.english: When learning Japanese, it is a fact that enthusiasm is an important factor, but in the long term - consistency too.

example_sentences.japanese: 入学試験を受けることは、当人の苦痛もさることながら、家族にも、大きな心理的負担を与えます。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that taking an entrance exam is stressful for the person concerned, but it also places a psychological burden on the family.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「だが、この国の強さは、自国の単独力量もさることながら、同盟国の多さにある。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'However, it is a fact that the strength of this country lies in its power, but it also has numerous allies.'

example_sentences.japanese: 伝記：「選手としての彼の素晴らしい才能もさることながら、何より信望や指導力が成功の要因となった。」
example_sentences.english: Biography: 'It is a fact that he has great ability as a player, but more than anything, his popularity and leadership skills were the cause of his success.'

example_sentences.japanese: 経営会議、社長：「競争が激しいからマーケティング予算を上げよう。」 部長：「マーケティングもさることながら製品品質も重要なのではないでしょうか？」
example_sentences.english: Management meeting, company president: 'The competition is intense, so we will increase the marketing budget.'Head director: 'It is a fact that marketing is important, but isn't the product quality too?'

grammar_point: ものと思（おも）っていた
general_translation: Was under the impression that, (Always) the thought used to think
formation: Verb + ものと思（おも）っていた ［い］Adjective + ものと思（おも）っていた ［な］Adjective + な + ものと思（おも）っていた Noun + の + ものと思（おも）っていた
casual_structure: Verb + ものと思（おも）っていた ［い］Adjective + ものと思（おも）っていた ［な］Adjective + な + ものと思（おも）っていた Noun + の + ものと思（おも）っていた
polite_structure: Verb + ものと思（おも）っていました ［い］Adjective + ものと思（おも）っていました ［な］Adjective + な + ものと思（おも）っていました Noun + の + ものと思（おも）っていました
explanation: A strong grammar point, expressing that someone was under the impression of (A). I had been thinking (A) was a thing.

example_sentences.japanese: てっきり漢字を学ぶのは退屈なものとおもっていた。
example_sentences.english: I was under the impression that learning kanji would be boring. (But it is not)

example_sentences.japanese: ゲートボールは老人しかやらないものとおもっていたが、最近は若者の間で流行っているらしい。
example_sentences.english: I was under the impression that gateball was something only old people played, but it seems to be popular among young people these days.

example_sentences.japanese: え...まだ晩御飯食べてないの？てっきり帰りに食べてくるものとおもっていたから、あなたの分は作ってないですよ。
example_sentences.english: What… You haven't eaten dinner yet? I was totally under the impression that you were going to grab something on the way back home, so I did not make anything for you.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の母は猫が好きではないものとおもっていたが、聞いてみたらただ猫アレルギーがあるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I was under the impression that my mother did not like cats, but after asking her, I found out that it's just that she is allergic to them.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬は怖いものとおもっていたけど、飼ってみたら思ったより優しかった。
example_sentences.english: I was under the impression that dogs were scary, but after I tried taking care of one, they turned out to be more gentle than I had thought.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんに怒られるものとおもっていたが怒られず、拍子抜けした。
example_sentences.english: I was under the impression that my mum was angry, but she wasn’t angry, so it was an anticlimax.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃、森の中で迷った。てっきりこのまま死ぬものとおもっていた。（が救われた）
example_sentences.english: When I was a child, I lost my way in the forest. I was under the impression that I would die like this. (But I was saved)

example_sentences.japanese: 面接に合格するものとおもっていたが不合格となり、愕然としている。
example_sentences.english: I was under the impression that I had passed the interview, but since I failed I am astounded.

example_sentences.japanese: 雷に打たれて死ぬものとおもっていたが、どうやら生き残ったようだ…。
example_sentences.english: I always used to think that if you got hit by lightning you would die, but it seems that they survived.

example_sentences.japanese: ワンピースは若い子しか着られないものとおもっていたが、意外と私でも着られる。
example_sentences.english: I always used to think that only young girls could wear dresses, but unexpectedly, even I can wear them.

example_sentences.japanese: 強盗に殺されるものとおもっていたが、意外にも強盗犯は傷一つすらつけてこなかった。
example_sentences.english: I was under the impression that you’d be killed when getting robbed, but unexpectedly, the robber didn’t even lay a scratch on me.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨の日はついていないものとおもっていましたが、雨の日は雨の日なりに楽しいことがあります。
example_sentences.english: I always used to think that rainy days were unlucky, but rainy days are fun in their own way.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、勇者：「ドラゴンは伝説のものとおもっていたが…｡」 小さいドラゴン：「ガオー！」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'I was under the impression that the dragons were things of legends.'Small dragon: 'Rarrrr!'

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼が拒否するものとおもっていたが、予想とは逆に彼は賛成した。
example_sentences.english: I was under the impression that he would disagree, but contrary to expectations he agreed.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「彼女が負けたなんて驚いたな。きっと勝つものとおもっていたけど。」Ｂ：「わたしもそう思ってた。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Surprisingly, she lost. I was under the impression that she would win.'B: 'I thought so too.'

general_translation: If … is not … then what is?
formation: Noun + でなくてなん + だろう(1)（か）(1)であろう
casual_structure: Noun + でなくてなん + だろう(1)（か）(1)であろう
explanation: A formal expression, showing that if something isn't (A), then what is it. If not (A), then I wonder what.

example_sentences.japanese: 注射を打った後にすぐ亡くなった…これがワクチンのせいでなくてなんだろう。
example_sentences.english: They died straight after they got a shot... If this isn’t the vaccine’s fault, then what is it?

example_sentences.japanese: あの子が新しいってだけでいじめられている。あれはパワハラでなくてなんだろう。
example_sentences.english: She is getting bullied just because she is new. If that is not power harassment, then what is?

example_sentences.japanese: 俺はこんなに夜遅くまでタダ働きをしている。俺は社畜でなくてなんだろう。
example_sentences.english: I am working late for free. If I am not a corporate slave, then what is?

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家だけ浸水しなかった。これが奇跡でなくてなんだろうか。
example_sentences.english: My house was the only one that did not get submerged. If this is not a miracle, then what is?

example_sentences.japanese: 説明欄には新品だと書いてあったのに届いた商品は傷だらけだった。これは詐欺でなくてなんだろうか。
example_sentences.english: In the description, it was written that it was brand new, but the product that arrived was covered in scratches. If this is not a scam, then what is?

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強しなかったのにテストで１００点をとるとは！天才でなくてなんだろう！
example_sentences.english: To think that despite not studying you got 100 points on the test! If that’s not genius, then what is?

example_sentences.japanese: まさか扉が勝手に開くとは…これが心霊現象でなくてなんだろうか。
example_sentences.english: To think that the door would open by itself... If this isn’t a psychic phenomenon, then what is?

example_sentences.japanese: ずっと一緒に寄り添いたいと思うこの気持ちが愛でなくてなんだろう。
example_sentences.english: If this feeling of always wanting to snuggle up close together isn’t love, then what is it?

example_sentences.japanese: 頼れる家族がいて仲のいい友達がいて愛する恋人がいて…これが幸せでなくてなんだろう。
example_sentences.english: Having a reliable family, close friends, and a partner that you love... If this isn’t happiness, then what is?

example_sentences.japanese: 炭酸水を買いに行ったのに炭酸水を買い忘れるとは…おっちょこちょいでなくてなんだろう。
example_sentences.english: To think that I went to go buy soda water but forgot to buy it... If that’s not being scatterbrained, then what is?

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「たけださんはひとり親であるばかりに昇進が見送られた。これが差別でなくてなんだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Article：Mr. Takeda has been refused promotion just because he is a single parent. If this is not discrimination, then what is?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は勉強しすぎて、結局、試験当日意識を失った。これが徒労でなくてなんだろう。
example_sentences.english: She studied so hard that she eventually collapsed on the day of the exam. If this is not wasted effort then what is? (If studying so hard that one eventually collapses on the exam day isn't wasted effort then what is?)

example_sentences.japanese: レビュー：「『遥かな町へ』という漫画を初めて読んで涙が出るほど感動した。このような漫画が傑作でなくてなんだろう？」
example_sentences.english: Review: 'When I read the manga titled 'A distant Neighborhood' for the first time, it moved me to tears. If manga like this is not a masterpiece then what is?'

example_sentences.japanese: 随筆：「もう聞こえないと言われた私の耳は人工内耳のおかげでまた聞こえるようになった。これが奇跡でなくてなんだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Essay: 'I was told that I would never hear again, but thanks to the cochlear implants I can hear once again. If this is not a miracle then what is?'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「飯がうまくて、楽しい仲間がいて、その上、近くには温泉がある。これが楽園でなくてなんだろうか？」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'There is good food, good company, and what is more, a hot spring is nearby. If this is not a paradise then what is?'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「外国での休暇の途中で、長年連絡が取れなかった幼馴染に偶然出会うなんて運命でなくてなんだろうか。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'If meeting a childhood friend you lost contact with years ago, in the middle of holidays abroad is not fate, then what is?'

general_translation: (Leaving or putting) aside, Apart
formation: Noun + はさておき(1)Phrase + かどうか(2) + はさておき(1)(1) はさておいて(2) か
casual_structure: Noun + はさておき(1)Phrase + かどうか(2) + はさておき(1)(1) はさておいて(2) か
explanation: A structure used for leaving aside the general topic of (A), and moving on. Placing (A) aside, let's move to (B).

example_sentences.japanese: それはさておき、会議の本題に移りましょう。
example_sentences.english: Putting that aside, let’s move to the main topic of the conference.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなの感想はさておき、私は美味しいと思ったよ。
example_sentences.english: Aside from everyone else's opinions, I thought that it was delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなことはさておき、仕事をちゃちゃっと終わらせて早く帰りましょうよ。
example_sentences.english: That aside, let's quickly finish work and go home.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語に自信があるかどうかはさておき、一人で行ったことのない国へ行くのには勇気がいる。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether I am confident in Japanese or not, going to a country you haven't been to alone takes some courage.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女がいるかいないかはさておき、普段から清潔にしていたほうがいいと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you have a girlfriend or not, you should be hygienic.

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談はさておき、そろそろ真面目にミーティングをしないと。
example_sentences.english: Jokes aside, we better get this meeting underway seriously.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は内容はさておき、映像のクオリティは最高でした。
example_sentences.english: Putting aside the content of this movie, the quality of the picture is superb.

example_sentences.japanese: 品質はさておき、この商品のデザインはどこよりも優れています。
example_sentences.english: Putting aside the quality, the design of this product is better than anywhere else.

example_sentences.japanese: 目が悪いことはさておき、それ以外は僕の体は完璧だと言ってもいい。
example_sentences.english: Apart from that my eyes are bad; you could say that the rest of my body is perfect.

example_sentences.japanese: サイズが大きいのはさておき、この商品には本当に沢山の機能があります。
example_sentences.english: Apart from that the size is big, this product honestly has lots of functions.

example_sentences.japanese: 大胆にデコルテが開いているのはさておき、このワンピースは私の好みのデザインだ。
example_sentences.english: Apart from that the low-cut is boldly open, this dress is the design type that I like.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲み会、仕事のことだけ話す同僚に：「仕事の話はさておき、改めて乾杯！」
example_sentences.english: Drinking party, to a co-worker, that only talks about work: 'Work talk aside, cheers!'

example_sentences.japanese: 武さん：「じゃ、エマさんは試験に合格すると思う？」 エマさん：「合格するかどうかはさておき、たくさんのことを学んでよかった。」
example_sentences.english: Takeshi: 'So, what do you think, will you pass the exam?' Ema: 'Leaving aside whether I pass or not, I am glad that I have learned a lot.'

example_sentences.japanese: たけしさん：「たなかさんが腕を折ったと聞いたんだけど・・・」 たなかさん：「そうだけど、大丈夫だよ。嫌なことはさておき、息子さん元気？」
example_sentences.english: Takeshi-san: 'I have heard that you have broken your arm...' Tanaka-san: 'Yeah, but don't worry. Putting unpleasant stuff aside, how is your son?'

example_sentences.japanese: 会社員１：「おそらく失敗するとは思いますが…」 会社員２：「細かいことはさておき、とりあえずやってみましょう。」
example_sentences.english: A company employee 1: 'I think that it will probably fail...' A company employee 2: 'Let's put minor details aside, and try it anyway!'

example_sentences.japanese: 学生１：「そういえば知ってる？トイレのはなこさんが旧校舎に出るってうわさ」 学生２：「はっはっは、誰がそんなことを。冗談はさておき、本気でこのビルには気をつけたほうがいいよ。状態が悪いから危ない。」
example_sentences.english: Student 1: 'Speaking of which, did you know? There are rumors that Hanako-san (the spirit) of the toilet appears in the old school building. Student 2: 'Hahahaha, who says that? Jokes aside, you should be careful around that building. It's dangerous because of its poor condition.'

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談はさておき、そろそろ会議を始めよう。
example_sentences.english: Jokes aside, let's start the meeting soon.

general_translation: When, Occasion, Opportunity, Time
formation: Verb + 折（おり）（に(1)）［い］Adjective + 折（おり）（に(1)）［な］Adjective + な + 折（おり）（に(1)）Noun + の + 折（おり）（に(1)）(1) には、は
casual_structure: Verb + 折（おり）（に(1)）［い］Adjective + 折（おり）（に(1)）［な］Adjective + な + 折（おり）（に(1)）Noun + の + 折（おり）（に(1)）(1) には、は
explanation: A formal, old-fashioned expression, used for highlighting usually positive occasions. On the fold of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: メール、本社の上司に：「お暇なおりにぜひ我が支店にお越しください。」
example_sentences.english: E-mail to a superior from the head office: 'Please, make sure to come to our branch when you are free.'

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの旅館にいらっしゃるおりには、事前の予約をお願いいたします。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion that you visit our ryokan, please make a reservation in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度お会いしたおりに、旅行へ行った時のお土産をお渡しします。
example_sentences.english: When the chance comes up that we meet again soon, I'll give you the present that I got when I went on a trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 卒業のおりに担任の先生に手紙を渡そうと思っている。
example_sentences.english: On the opportunity of my graduation, I am thinking that I'd like to give a letter to the teacher that was looking after me.

example_sentences.japanese: 手紙：「新春のお支度にお忙しいおりから、風邪などひかれぬようご自愛下さい。」
example_sentences.english: Letter: 'Please take care not to catch a cold at this busy time of preparations for a new year.'

example_sentences.japanese: お近くにいらっしゃるおりには、ぜひうちにご飯を食べに来てください！
example_sentences.english: On the chance that you will be close by, you’re certainly welcome to come to my place to eat!

example_sentences.japanese: 宴会をするおりには、ぜひうちの居酒屋をご利用くださいませ！
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of having a banquet gathering, you’re certainly welcome to make use of our izakaya.

example_sentences.japanese: オーストラリアへ来るおりには、ぜひカンガルーのお肉を食べてみてください。
example_sentences.english: At the opportunity of coming to Australia, certainly try eating kangaroo meat.

example_sentences.japanese: あの作家さんとお会いしたおりには、著書への愛をしっかりと伝えました。
example_sentences.english: At the opportunity of meeting that author, I properly conveyed my love for his work.

example_sentences.japanese: 両家の食事会をするおりには、ちゃんと自分で司会をしようと思っています。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of both of our families having a dinner, I will make sure to properly lead processions myself.

example_sentences.japanese: 自伝：「初めてのパリへの出張のおりにはルーヴル美術館に立ち寄った。」
example_sentences.english: Autobiography: 'On the occasion of my first trip to Paris, I stopped by the Louvre museum for a short visit.'

example_sentences.japanese: 手紙、名誉あるゲストの再招待：「北海道にいらしたおりに、是非お寄りください！」
example_sentences.english: A letter, re-invitation of a reputable guest: 'Please, make sure to drop by when you come to Hokkaido.'

example_sentences.japanese: 大学の研究室を訪ねたおりに、学生時代にお世話になった先生に挨拶をしました。
example_sentences.english: On the opportunity of visiting the university laboratory, I said hello to the teacher who looked after me during my time as a student.

example_sentences.japanese: 自伝：「京都への観光旅行のおりに、駅で偶然小学校の先生に会った。」
example_sentences.english: Autobiography: 'On the occasion of a sightseeing trip to Kyoto, I came across my elementary school teacher at the train station.'

example_sentences.japanese: 献辞：「おりに触れて相談に乗って下さった、敬愛してやまない友人、黒木智子さんに心から感謝いたします。」
example_sentences.english: Dedication: 'I am grateful from the bottom of my heart to my friend I greatly respect, Tomoko Kuroki, who has helped me wherever the occasion arose. '

general_translation: As if (to say), Seeming that
formation: Quote + とばかり（に）Noun +（だ）+ とばかり（に）
casual_structure: Quote + とばかり（に）Noun +（だ）+ とばかり（に）
explanation: A formal structure, implying that something is done as if to say (A). Just with (A) acting as the trigger, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ランナーが通り、ここぞとばかりに声援を送りました。
example_sentences.english: The runner passed, and as if to say ‘Now’s the time!’, I let out a cheer.

example_sentences.japanese: うちのわんちゃんが「待ってました」とばかりに尻尾を振って友達に飛びついた。
example_sentences.english: Our dog wagged his tail and jumped onto my friend as if to say 'I have been waiting'.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が「俺の話聞いてるか」とばかりに生徒たちを睨みつけた。
example_sentences.english: The teacher stared at the students as if to say 'Are you listening to me'.

example_sentences.japanese: 早くしろといわんばかりに上司が何回も「まだ？」って聞いてきた。
example_sentences.english: My boss repeatedly asked me, 'Are you done?' as if to say 'hurry up'.

example_sentences.japanese: つまらないといわんばかりの顔でみられたから、話すのをやめた。
example_sentences.english: They were looking at me as if they were bored, so I stopped talking.

example_sentences.japanese: 中田選手のバランスが崩れたので、斉藤選手はチャンスとばかりに中田選手の太ももを蹴った。
example_sentences.english: Since Nakata's balance was disrupted, Saito, seeing it as a chance, kicked Nakata's thigh.

example_sentences.japanese: 「おまえも黙れ」とばかりに手でテーブルを叩いた。
example_sentences.english: She slammed the table with her hand as if to say 'Silence!'.

example_sentences.japanese: 盗賊たちが待っていたとばかりに通行人を止めたのです！
example_sentences.english: As if they had been waiting, the robbers stopped the passersby!

example_sentences.japanese: 桜は、今この時を待っていたとばかりに花びらを広げています。
example_sentences.english: Seeming that they had been waiting for this time right now, the petals of the cherry blossoms spread.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長に呆れたとばかりにため息をつかれて、クビを覚悟しました。
example_sentences.english: Being sighed at by the president as if to say he was exasperated, I readied myself to be fired.

example_sentences.japanese: 殺すぞとばかりに面識のない人を突き飛ばした彼は逮捕されました。
example_sentences.english: Sending a stranger flying as if to say ‘I’ll kill you!’, he was apprehended.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題の解決は任せろとばかりにウインクをしてきた上司に恋をした。
example_sentences.english: I fell in love with my boss who winked as if to say ‘Leave solving this problem to me’.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「もうあなたとは話したくない」とばかりに彼はドアをばたんと閉めた。
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'He slammed the door as if to say "I don't want to talk with you anymore".'

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーで閉店が近づき食品などが割引される時間帯になると、主婦たちはここぞとばかりに多くの買い物をした。
example_sentences.english: As the closing time of the supermarket approached, when food and other items were discounted, the housewives did a lot of shopping as if to say, 'This is our chance!'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「洋服店に入るなり、長いことこのときを待っていたとばかりに、店員が声をかけてきた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'As soon as he entered the clothing store, the clerk approached him, as if she had been just waiting for this very moment for a long time.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「目の前で起こっていることなのに、皆信じられないとばかりに目を見開いていた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Even though it was happening right in front of them, they still looked at it with eyes wide open as if saying that they cannot believe this.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「 なかなかお目にかかれない美しい景色なので武はここぞとばかりにカメラを手にし、撮影した。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'It's a beautiful scene that you don't see very often, so Takeshi took the opportunity to grab his camera and take some pictures.'

general_translation: ~and ~and, Keep ~ing, One after another, So much, So many, One after the other
formation: Verb［る］+ わ + Verb［る］+ わ(*)(*) The same verb has to be repeated
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ わ + Verb［る］+ わ(*)(*) The same verb has to be repeated
explanation: A formal particle construction, emphasizing the speaker's astonishment about (A) happening one after the other, or to a large degree.

example_sentences.japanese: 「病院に入院してた時、いろいろ検査したらまあ、出るわ出るわ…（思った以上のことが指摘された）。」
example_sentences.english: 'When I was in the hospital, they did various tests and, well, they just kept coming up...' （the results that were worse than expected）

example_sentences.japanese: もう、昨日子供達が喧嘩して泣くわ泣くわで大変だったんだから。
example_sentences.english: Oh my god, it was so hectic yesterday because the kids got into a fight and cried so much.

example_sentences.japanese: 空き家を買ったのはいいけど、家中にはゴキブリがいるわいるわ。多分自分じゃ何もできないから業者に頼むしかなさそう。
example_sentences.english: I bought a vacant house, and that's exciting, but there are so many cockroaches all over the house. I probably won't be able to do anything myself, so I will have to call someone.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の息子なんて、部活を始めてからというもの食べるわ食べるわ、食費が心配だよ。
example_sentences.english: Ever since my son has started after school activities, he eats so much that I am worried about the cost of food.

example_sentences.japanese: あの子は医者になりたいって決めてから、毎日勉強するわするわ。
example_sentences.english: Ever since he has decided that he wants to be a doctor, he studies a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 「新婚旅行から戻ったらメールボックスには郵便物があるわあるわ、つかえてしまって引っ張ることができなかった。」
example_sentences.english: 'When we got back from our honeymoon, there was so much mail in the mailbox that it was stuck and I couldn't pull it out.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「子供が転んで泣くわ泣くわ。なだめるの大変だった。」
example_sentences.english: 'Our child fell and cried so much that it was hard to calm her down.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「先輩は面白いのなんのって喋ると笑うわ笑うわ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Senpai is so funny, that I laugh so much whenever he talks.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「ちょっとからかっただけで、あいつ怒るわ怒るわ。」
example_sentences.english: 'He gets so angry just by teasing him a bit.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「雨だろうが雪だろうが、走るわ走るわ。もう走る病気って感じだよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Whether it is rain or snow, he keeps on running. It seems that he has an incurable passion for running.'

general_translation: Even (a little), At least
formation: Noun + なりとも
casual_structure: Noun + なりとも
explanation: A very polite classical Japanese expression used to present a specific hope or condition as a bare minimum.

example_sentences.japanese: 一言なりとも、あなたの気持ちを聞かせてくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: Wouldn’t you let me hear at least a word about how you feel?

example_sentences.japanese: 会議の前に、概要なりとも共有いただけますか？
example_sentences.english: Before the meeting, would it be possible for you to share at least the general outline?

example_sentences.japanese: 詳細は後日でも構いませんが、現段階での決定事項なりとも先に教えていただけると助かります。
example_sentences.english: It’s no problem if the details come at a later date, but at this point it would be helpful if you could share at least the decisions with me.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅かれ早かれ、誰かなりとも真実に気づくときが来るだろう。
example_sentences.english: Sooner or later, at least someone will come to realize the truth.

example_sentences.japanese: 散歩がてら、近所のパン屋に立ち寄って、感想なりとも聞かせてくれたらうれしいな。
example_sentences.english: I’d be happy if, while out for your walk, you could stop by the local bakery and at least let me hear what you think.

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談なりとも、そんなこと言わないでよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is just a joke, don’t say that sort of thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 些細なことでもいいから、少しの話なりとも聞かせてよ。
example_sentences.english: It’ll be okay even if it is something trivial, just let me hear even a little of what you have to say.

example_sentences.japanese: 多少なりとも、顔を見せてくれたら、安心できたのに。
example_sentences.english: If you had shown your face, even just a little, I would have felt relieved.

example_sentences.japanese: 私なりとも、お力になれればと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I hope that, even in my own small way, I can be of some help.

example_sentences.japanese: ご意見なりともいただければ幸いです。
example_sentences.english: I would be happy to receive at least some feedback.

example_sentences.japanese: メッセージなりとも入れておいてくれたら、迎えに行けたのに。
example_sentences.english: If you’d at least left a message, I could have come to pick you up.

example_sentences.japanese: 近くまで来たなら、声なりともかけてくれてよかったのに。
example_sentences.english: If you came so close, I wish you would have at least called out to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 最後に握手なりともして別れたかった。
example_sentences.english: In the end, I wanted to part ways with at least a handshake.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ本心じゃなくても、慰めの言葉なりともかけてくれたらよかったのに。
example_sentences.english: Even if it wasn’t how you truly felt, I wish you had at least given me some words of consolation.

example_sentences.japanese: 君に迷惑をかけるぐらいなら、自分なりともできることを全部やってみるよ。
example_sentences.english: If it is to the extent that it is causing you bother then I will try and do what I can in at least my own way.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩今鹿児島にいるんですか？時間があったら、一目なりとも会いたいです！
