example_sentences.english: Senpai, you are in Kagoshima right now? If you have time I’d like to see you, even for a short time! (Slightly unnatural, but may be used for dramatic effect)

example_sentences.japanese: 母さんに一目なりとも会いたいから、夕方そっち行くね。
example_sentences.english: Hey mom, I wanna see you even if it’s brief, so I’m gonna head there this afternoon. (Slightly unnatural, but may be used for dramatic effect)

example_sentences.japanese: 多少なりとも毎日勉強することはいいことだ。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is a little, it is a good thing to study everyday.

example_sentences.japanese: このようなことは一度なりともやったことはないですが、頑張ってみます。
example_sentences.english: We have never done something like this, not even once, but we will try our best.

example_sentences.japanese: このおむつ交換ステーションのご利用の場合、お子様から一時なりともお目を離さずご利用ください。
example_sentences.english: When using this diaper changing station, please do not leave your child unattended for even a moment.

example_sentences.japanese: 急いでいるのは承知ですが、熱中症で倒れそうなので、わずかなりとも休憩をいただいてもよろしいですか。
example_sentences.english: I know you are in a hurry, but may I have a short break as I feel like I am going to collapse from heat stroke?

general_translation: Even when
formation: Verb + に至（いた）ってもNoun + に至（いた）っても
casual_structure: Verb + に至（いた）ってもNoun + に至（いた）っても
explanation: A strong phrase, implying that even when (A), (B). Even when reaching the climactic situation of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は病院に来るにいたっても、まだ治療をすることを拒否していた。
example_sentences.english: He was still refusing medical treatment, even when it came to the point of him coming to the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: あの事故に巻き込まれてから２年経つにいたっても、相手は謝罪すらもしてこない。
example_sentences.english: Even now, 2 years since I have been involved in an accident, and the other party has not even apologized.

example_sentences.japanese: 社会人になるにいたっても、まだ自分が子供だと思っている人は少なくないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even as people become a functioning member of society, there are probably a lot of people that think they are still kids.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼と別れて３年経った現在にいたっても、男の人を信用することができない。
example_sentences.english: Even now, 3 years after I broke up with him, I still have a hard time trusting men.

example_sentences.japanese: この会議は朝方にいたっても、続きそうだ。
example_sentences.english: This meeting seems like it is going to continue, even if it becomes morning.

example_sentences.japanese: これは俺が決めたことだから、どんな結果にいたっても、絶対に後悔しない！
example_sentences.english: This is something I have decided on, so I will not regret the result even if it's bad.

example_sentences.japanese: 就業時間を過ぎるにいたっても、この会議は終わりそうにありません。
example_sentences.english: Even now when work hours will pass, this meeting is showing no signs of ending.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚するにいたっても、完全にお互いを理解し合えないカップルが多い。
example_sentences.english: Many couples can't understand each other completely even when they are about to get married.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「だが、事ここにいたっても、まだ謝ることを拒否するほど頑固である」。
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'However, even when things have come to this, he is still obstinate to the point that he refuses to apologize.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「首相は政府の腐敗を暴露されるにいたっても、まだ詳細情報を隠し通そうとしていた。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Even when the corruption of the government was exposed, the prime minister still tried to hide the details.'

example_sentences.japanese: 呼吸困難に陥るにいたっても救急車を呼ばないなんて、頭がおかしいのか？！
example_sentences.english: To think that you won’t call an ambulance even now after falling into difficulty breathing. Is your brain even working?!

example_sentences.japanese: 付き合って１０年が経つにいたってもプロポーズをする勇気が出ないなんて、腰抜けだ。
example_sentences.english: Something like not being able to muster up the courage to propose even now after 10 years of dating. I am a coward.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察に尋問されるにいたっても真実を言わなかったのだから、罪が重くなるのも当然です。
example_sentences.english: Since they didn’t tell the truth even now after being interrogated by the police, it’s only natural that their crime would become worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社が破産直前の状況にいたってもなお経営陣は減給されることに首を縦に振ろうとはしない。
example_sentences.english: Even in a situation when the company is on the verge of bankruptcy, the management have still not agreed to have their salaries cut.

example_sentences.japanese: スミスさんは、事故から６年経った現在にいたっても、未だに腕の痛みを感じます。
example_sentences.english: Even now, 6 years since the accident, Mr. Smith still feels pain in his arm.

example_sentences.japanese: ハルヒさんの消失から半月以上が過ぎた今日にいたっても、彼女の行方は未だに知れない。
example_sentences.english: Even to this day, when more than half a month has passed since the disappearance of Haruhi, her whereabouts are still impossible to tell.

general_translation: And also, Also (partly) to, Also (partly) for (the purpose of), At the same time, To double as, When … also, While … as well, And as
formation: Noun + を(1) + 兼（か）ねて(1) も
casual_structure: Noun + を(1) + 兼（か）ねて(1) も
explanation: A grammar point indicating that (A) is partly done together with (B), or (B) doubles as (A). Spreading also across to (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットをかねて、スポーツジムに通っています。
example_sentences.english: I go to the gym also (partly) to lose weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動不足とストレス発散をかねて、キックボクシングジムに通っている。
example_sentences.english: I go to a kickboxing gym also partly to relieve stress and to get exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: おばあちゃんはボケ防止をかねて、毎日クロスワードパズルをしています。
example_sentences.english: My grandma does crossword puzzles also partly to prevent dementia.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強をかねて、英語の字幕なしで日本の映画をみています。
example_sentences.english: I watch Japanese movies without subtitles also partly to learn Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットをかねて、毎朝ランニングしています。
example_sentences.english: I run everyday also partly to lose weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 体調管理と節約をかねて、寝る時はエアコンを使わないようにしている。
example_sentences.english: When I sleep, I try not to use the air conditioner also partly for my health and to save money.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強をかねて、日本のゲームをしています。
example_sentences.english: I play Japanese games also (partly) to learn the language.

example_sentences.japanese: リスニングの練習をかねて、日本語の曲を聞くことにしています。
example_sentences.english: Doubling as listening practice, I decided to listen to Japanese songs.

example_sentences.japanese: 散歩をかねて隣町まで歩いて買い物に行きました。
example_sentences.english: I walked to the neighboring town to do some shopping and (partly) for a stroll as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 小遣い稼ぎをかねて趣味で同人誌を描いている。
example_sentences.english: I draw doujinshi as a hobby and also (partly) for extra money.

example_sentences.japanese: 昼食をかねて、多めの朝食を１１時に食べました。
example_sentences.english: Doubling as lunch, I had a larger breakfast at 11 o’clock.

example_sentences.japanese: 取材をかねて、ある温泉旅館へ旅行に行くことにした。
example_sentences.english: Also partly to gather material for a story, I decided to go on a trip to an inn with a hot spring.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の毎朝の日課は、情報収集をかねてＳＮＳをチェックすることである。
example_sentences.english: My every-morning routine is, doubling as information gathering, to check social media.

example_sentences.japanese: ウォーキングをかねて近所のスーパーまで買い物に行こうと思っている。
example_sentences.english: Doubling as walking, I am thinking about going to the local supermarket to do shopping.

example_sentences.japanese: ちよちゃんの誕生日が近いので、お誕生日会をかねてパーティーを行いたい。
example_sentences.english: Chiyo-chan's birthday is approaching, so I want to organize a party that will double as a birthday meet-up as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 文化祭ではクラスの出し物の宣伝をかねて衣装を着たままうろついている生徒が多い。
example_sentences.english: Also doubling as a promotion for their class productions, there are lots of students wandering around the school culture festival in costumes.

general_translation: (Why) can’t, Isn’t there, Wish that, If only
formation: Verb［できる］［ない］+ もの + （だろう）+ か
casual_structure: Verb［できる］［ない］+ もの + （だろう）+ か
polite_structure: Verb［できる］［ない］+ もの + （でしょう）+ か
explanation: A formal phrase, expressing the speaker's strong wish to do (A). I wonder if (A) is really a thing that can't be done.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットのモチベーションがもっと上がらないものだろうか。
example_sentences.english: Is there no way to raise my motivation more for my diet?

example_sentences.japanese: これはもっとシンプルにできないものか。
example_sentences.english: Can't this be made to be more simple?

example_sentences.japanese: こっちから言わないとやって貰えないものだろうか。
example_sentences.english: Can't you do it for me without me telling you to?

example_sentences.japanese: 難しいのはわかっているんですが、佐々木さんの腕でなんとかできないものでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: I am aware that it is difficult, but can't something not be done with your skills?

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事をもう少し楽にする方法はないものか。
example_sentences.english: Is there no way to make work a little easier?

example_sentences.japanese: もっと楽にお金を稼げる仕事はないものだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder if there are any jobs where I can earn money easier.

example_sentences.japanese: これよりもっと燃費がいい車はないものでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Are there no cars that have better mileage than this one?

example_sentences.japanese: 電気自動車の値段はもう少し安くできないものだろうか。
example_sentences.english: Can't electric cars's price be a bit lower?

example_sentences.japanese: 日傘はもっと畳みやすく、そして風に強くならないものだろうか。
example_sentences.english: Is there no way to make a sun umbrella that is more easily collapsible and strong against the wind?

example_sentences.japanese: 人間は食べ物を食べなくても生きるようにならないものだろうか。
example_sentences.english: If only humans could become able to live without eating food.

example_sentences.japanese: ブログ：「詐欺まがいなオンラインショップのことはどうにかならないものだろうか。」
example_sentences.english: Blog: 'Can't something be done about the fraudulent online shops?'

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語学習がもっと簡単にならないものだろうか。
example_sentences.english: Can’t Japanese study be easier?

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強嫌いの息子の成績がどうにかならないものだろうか…。
example_sentences.english: Is there no way to do something about the grades of my son who hates study?

example_sentences.japanese: みんなが満足するような法律や社会の仕組みを作れないものだろうか。
example_sentences.english: Can’t we make laws and a societal structure that makes everyone happy?

example_sentences.japanese: 伝記：「なんとかしてもっと操作しやすい携帯電話を作れないものかと、スティーブはいつも考えていた。」
example_sentences.english: Biography: 'Steven has been always thinking if there isn't some way he could make the smartphones easier to use.'

example_sentences.japanese: インタビュー：「その時、工業製品の品質を何とか上げるようにできないものかと考えました。」
example_sentences.english: Interview: 'At that time, we were thinking if there isn't some way to increase the quality of our products.'

example_sentences.japanese: 上司、部下の提案への反応：「まあ機能はするだろうね。ただちょっと気になる部分があったから、他にもっといい方法はないものかなあ...」
example_sentences.english: Superior, reacting to the subordinate proposal: 'Well, it will probably work. But there is a part that bothers me a bit. Is there no other, better way?'

example_sentences.japanese: テレビ番組、刑事ゴンロポ：「そのことは問題になります。ついては今、ここでそれに対する説明をうかがえないものでしょうか？」容疑者：「そのことでしたら隠す理由もございません。私は昨晩ずっと家におりました。」
example_sentences.english: TV show, detective Gonropo: 'This might be a problem. So, why can't I ask for an explanation about that right away?'Suspect: 'If it's this then there is nothing to hide. I have been at my house all night long. '

general_translation: I will definitely, I will certainly, Just watch, Whatever it takes, I swear, for sure
formation: Verb［て］+ みせる
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ みせる
polite_structure: Verb［て］+ みせます
explanation: A strong expression, emphasizing the speaker's intent to do (A). I will show that (A) can be done.

example_sentences.japanese: 「何があっても、必ずファンの期待にこたえてみせます！」
example_sentences.english: 'No matter what happens, I will definitely live up to my fans' expectations!'

example_sentences.japanese: お前のために、次の試合では勝ってみせる！
example_sentences.english: I will definitely win the next competition for you!

example_sentences.japanese: 来週のテストで合格してみせる！
example_sentences.english: I will definitely pass the test next week!

example_sentences.japanese: 足が痛いけど、完走してみせる！
example_sentences.english: My legs hurt, but I am definitely going to finish the race!

example_sentences.japanese: ピアニスト：「この曲を明日までにひきこなしてみせる！」
example_sentences.english: Pianist: ‘I will definitely be able to play this song well by tomorrow!’

example_sentences.japanese: 「今年こそ、必ず運転免許をとってみせるよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I will definitely get a drivers license this year!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「どんな手を使ってでも、絶対、成功してみせる！」
example_sentences.english: 'I will definitely win, no matter what it takes!'

example_sentences.japanese: 妻を喜ばせるような美味しい料理をつくってみせる！
example_sentences.english: I will make delicious food that my wife will be thankful for, just watch!

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を完璧にマスターして、日本人の友達をびっくりさせてみせる！
example_sentences.english: I will perfectly master Japanese and surprise my Japanese friends for sure!

example_sentences.japanese: 面接で良い印象を与えて、必ずこの仕事をゲットしてみせる！
example_sentences.english: I will give a good impression in the meeting and get this job whatever it takes!

example_sentences.japanese: 猫カフェに行ったら、おもちゃで沢山の猫をあやつってみせる！
example_sentences.english: When I go to a cat café, I will play with lots of cats with a toy for sure!

example_sentences.japanese: 子供：「将来は有名な俳優になって、ママとパパに良い生活をさせてみせる！」
example_sentences.english: Child: ‘In the future, I swear that I will become a famous actor and give my mom and dad a good life!’

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「必ずこの手で魔王をたおしてみせるという勇者エミリアの言葉に、わたしたちは賭けることにした。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'We decided to bet on Emilia the hero's words, that she would definitely defeat the demon king with her very own hands.'

example_sentences.japanese: 負けた後、相手を挑発する：「次こそ、必ずかってみせるぞ！あなたには負けない！」 相手：「よし、かかってこい！」
example_sentences.english: After losing, challenging the opponent: 'I will definitely win next time! I won't lose!'Opponent: 'OK! Bring it on!'

example_sentences.japanese: アニメ、 友達１：「先輩に私の気持ちを絶対きづかせてみせるわ！」 頼れる友達２：「がんばれ！」
example_sentences.english: An anime, Friend 1: 'I will definitely make senpai realize my feelings!'Supportive friend 2: 'Go for it!'

general_translation: Combined with, Coupled with, Together with
formation: Noun + が(1) + 相（あい）まって(1) と
casual_structure: Noun + が(1) + 相（あい）まって(1) と
explanation: A formal construction, highlighting when (A) and (B) are combined or coupled to create (C). (A) in association with (B), gives (C).

example_sentences.japanese: 感動的なシーンとＢＧＭがあいまって、泣かずにはいられませんでした。
example_sentences.english: The moving scene coupled with the background music made it impossible not to cry.

example_sentences.japanese: あの古い屋敷は霧とあいまって不気味な雰囲気を出しています。
example_sentences.english: That old mansion, combined with the fog, creates an eerie atmosphere.

example_sentences.japanese: ツイッターでの流行とあいまって、この漫画は若者の間ではすごく人気だ。
example_sentences.english: Combined with its popularity on Twitter, this manga is very popular among young people.

example_sentences.japanese: このステーキはシェフ特製のソースがあいまって、とても美味しい。
example_sentences.english: This steak is very tasty, coupled with the chef's special sauce.

example_sentences.japanese: クライアントのアイデアと私たちの努力があいまって、とてもいいイベントを開催することができた。
example_sentences.english: The client's ideas, combined with our efforts, resulted in us being able to host a very good event.

example_sentences.japanese: 腹痛と頭痛があいまって、まるで生きている心地がしませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Stomach pain combined with a headache made it completely uncomfortable just to live.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「夕暮れが虹とあいまって空をある種のキャンディーのように見せた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Twilight combined with a rainbow made the sky look like some sort of candy.'

example_sentences.japanese: 気温の高さと湿度の高さがあいまって、日本の夏は地獄みたいです。
example_sentences.english: The air temperature combined with the humidity in Japan makes summer like hell.

example_sentences.japanese: 値段の安さと質の良さがあいまって、この商品は売れに売れている。
example_sentences.english: The cheap price together with the good quality of this product is making it sell one after the other.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「ピーナッツバターはキュウリの酢の物とあいまって思いがけない独特な味をもたらす。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Peanut butter combined with pickled cucumber gives an unexpected, unique flavor.'

example_sentences.japanese: 飼い猫の鳴き声と仕草があいまって、その可愛さに悶絶するしかなかった。
example_sentences.english: The cuteness of my cat’s meows combined with their gestures left me with no choice but to swoon.

example_sentences.japanese: キムチのピリ辛と胡麻油の香ばしさがあいまって、このおつまみは最高である。
example_sentences.english: The light spiciness of the kimchi combined with the aroma of the sesame oil make this starter dish the best.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「電気料金が安価であることとあいまって、税額控除が電気自動車の需要の増加に寄与している。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'The tax exemptions combined with a low price of electricity contribute to the increased demand for electric cars.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「水位上昇と異常気象があいまって、それらはモルディブなどの島国では重大な脅威となっています。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'Weather anomalies combined with rising water levels are a great threat to island countries such as the Maldives.'

example_sentences.japanese: ゲームレビュー：「ペースの速いストーリー展開と個性的なキャラクターがあいまって、自然とこのゲームはＲＰＧファンの間で大きな話題となっている。」
example_sentences.english: Game review: Fast paced story development combined with unique characters naturally gained this game much attention among RPG fans.

example_sentences.japanese: 都市汚染についての記事：「盆地に不利な地理的位置と工業排ガスがあいまって家庭用空気清浄機はさらに必要となる。」
example_sentences.english: Article about city pollution: 'Industry emissions combined with the unfavorable geographical location in the basin makes house air purifiers even more necessary.'

general_translation: To not be worthy, To not be enough, To not be sufficient, To lack
formation: Verb + に足（た）りない
casual_structure: Verb + に足（た）りない
explanation: A formal structure, implying that something is not worthy of (A). It is not enough to reach (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ロジャー・キントの言葉は一つとして信じるにたりないことだ。
example_sentences.english: Not even one word of Roger Kint is worth believing.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は陰謀論者だから、あの人のいうことは信じるにたりない。
example_sentences.english: He is a conspiracy theorist so nothing he says is worth believing.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は自分を良くみせるためだったら、すぐに自分の失敗を人のせいにするから、彼は信頼するにたりない。
example_sentences.english: He will blame others for his own mistakes, just to make himself look good, so he is not worth trusting.

example_sentences.japanese: ブランド物のバッグをリサイクルショップに売りに行ったけど、買取の金額が売るにたりない金額だった。
example_sentences.english: I went to sell a designer brand bag to a secondhand store, but the purchase price was not enough for me to sell it.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな稚拙な感想文なんて、発表するにたりないですよ…。
example_sentences.english: Such a crude opinion piece is not worthy of publishing, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 自慢するにたりないテストの点数で、しょんぼりとしている。
example_sentences.english: I am feeling dejected because of a test score that is not worthy of being proud about.

example_sentences.japanese: これは因果応報というやつだから、彼女には同情するにたりません。
example_sentences.english: Because this is what you'd call karma, it is not worth sympathizing with her.

example_sentences.japanese: 信じるにたりないデタラメを信じてしまうような人が心配でならない。
example_sentences.english: I can’t help worry about the type of person that trusts rubbish that is not worthy of trusting.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の意見は気にするにたりないと思われているようで、やる気が出ない。
example_sentences.english: With my opinions seemingly thought of as not worthy of caring about, I can’t summon up the will to do anything.

example_sentences.japanese: この規則は一見取るにたりないものに見えるが実はこれには重要な理由がある。
example_sentences.english: These regulations might seem worthless at first sight, but actually, there are important reasons for them.

example_sentences.japanese: 他人から見たら取るにたりない、小さな貝にすぎないが、私にとってはあの日のお土産だ。
example_sentences.english: From another person's perspective, it is nothing but a worthless, small shell, yet for me, it is a souvenir of that day.

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「失敗など全く恐れるにたりない。なぜなら、間違えたり、失敗することは、人として成長するからである。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'The likes of failure are not worth fearing at all. It is because of mistakes, that we grow as people.'

example_sentences.japanese: 狼少年は嘘を重ねた結果、信ずるにたりないやつだと村人に思われるようになった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of his repeated lies, the boy who cried wolf has come to be regarded as untrustworthy by the villagers.

example_sentences.japanese: 現代の人類は、多忙である為、自然の美しさなどは注目するにたりないものと思って、常に無視しているきらいがある。
example_sentences.english: Due to the fast-paced life, modern humans have a tendency to ignore the beauty of nature regarding it as something that is not worth our attention.

example_sentences.japanese: 周りから見ると取るにたりない、ただのゴミだが、私にとっては大切なコレクションの一部だ。
example_sentences.english: From the perspective of the people around me, it's nothing but a worthless piece of garbage, but to me they are an important part of my collection.

example_sentences.japanese: この部品は取るに足らない物のように見えるかもしれないが、これが壊れたら、この機械は動かなくなる。
example_sentences.english: This component may seem insignificant, but if it breaks, this machine will stop working.

general_translation: Do not, Must not, Should not, Cannot (べからざる)
formation: Verb + べからずExceptions:する ￫ す(1) + べからず Verb + べからざる + Nounwhich is generally limited to: 許（ゆる）すべからざる + Noun  ありうべからざる +  Noun 欠（か）くべからざる + Noun(1) する
casual_structure: Verb + べからずExceptions:する ￫ す(1) + べからず Verb + べからざる + Nounwhich is generally limited to: 許（ゆる）すべからざる + Noun  ありうべからざる +  Noun 欠（か）くべからざる + Noun(1) する
explanation: A formal grammar point, emphasizing that (A) must not happen. It cannot be permissable that (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 空気は生きるに欠くべからざるものだ。
example_sentences.english: Air is essential to life. (Must not lack air)

example_sentences.japanese: ことわざ：「初心忘れるべからず。」
example_sentences.english: Proverb: 'Do not forget beginner's humility.'

example_sentences.japanese: この施設内ではスケートボードなどのことをするべからず。
example_sentences.english: You must not skateboard or anything similar in this facility.

example_sentences.japanese: 配達員を装って玄関のドアを開けさせるのは、許すべからざる行為だ。
example_sentences.english: Making someone open the door, by pretending to be a delivery person is an act that is not to be forgiven.

example_sentences.japanese: 吸うべからざる場所でタバコを吸っているのを見られたら、１０００円払うことになります。
example_sentences.english: If you are seen smoking in an area where you must not smoke, you will end up having to pay 1000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと稼いでいない人はご馳走など食うべからず。
example_sentences.english: Those who are not sufficiently earning should not eat treated food.

example_sentences.japanese: 池の鯉に餌をあげるべからず！鯉が増え過ぎてしまいます！
example_sentences.english: Do not feed the koi in the pond! They will multiply too much!

example_sentences.japanese: 公園の看板：「芝生にゴミ捨てるべからず」
example_sentences.english: A signboard at the park: 'Do not dump rubbish on the lawn'

example_sentences.japanese: ブログ記事：「英語で上手にフォーマルな手紙を書くための『べし・べからず』集」
example_sentences.english: Blog post: 'Dos and Don'ts for writing a formal letter in English skillfully.'

example_sentences.japanese: もろい歴史的建造物の手前の看板：「中に入るべからず」
example_sentences.english: A signboard in front of the fragile historic building: 'Do not enter inside'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「さだおさんがなにゆえそのような許すべからざる大罪を犯したのか、ゆうささんは解できなかった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Yusa-san couldn't understand why did Sadao-san commit such an unpardonable crime.' (a crime that cannot be forgiven)

example_sentences.japanese: 張り紙：「この橋は壊れています！渡るべからず！」
example_sentences.english: Poster: ‘This bridge is damaged! Do not cross!’

example_sentences.japanese: 人の名前を忘るべからず。名前を忘れるのは最大の失礼に当たる。
example_sentences.english: You must not forget people’s names. Forgetting a name is equivalent to the height of rudeness.

example_sentences.japanese: 看板：「作品に触れるべからず。触れた者は、即退場とすることにする。」
example_sentences.english: Notice board: ‘Do not touch the works. Those who do will be ejected from the premises immediately.’

example_sentences.japanese: 立ち入り禁止の場所には入るべからず。入れば恐ろしいことが待ち受けているであろう…。
example_sentences.english: You must not enter places that you are forbidden from entering. If you do, there is likely something terrible awaiting you.

example_sentences.japanese: 新年会、社長が新しい従業員に：「新しい年を迎え、諸君にひと言だけ言っておこう。『初心忘るべからず』。そうすれば真の精通への道は開けていくものだ。」
example_sentences.english: New year's party, company president to new employees: 'Greeting the new year, ladies and gentlemen, I would like to say few words. 'Do not forget beginner's humility'. That's how the road to real mastery will be open to you.'

general_translation: As if, As if it were about to, About to
formation: Verb［ない］+ ん + ばかり + にVerb［ない］+ ん + ばかり + の + Noun
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ん + ばかり + にVerb［ない］+ ん + ばかり + の + Noun
explanation: A formal construction, implying that something is about to (A). It appears that it is at the degree where only (A) could result or happen.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「われんばかりの拍手に部屋は満たされた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'As if it were about to shatter, the room filled with thunderous applause.'

example_sentences.japanese: 台風の風で、隣の空き家が崩れんばかりにギシギシ音を立てていた。
example_sentences.english: The vacant house next door was making creaking sounds as if it were to collapse because of the winds caused by the typhoon.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生は「こっちを見ろ」って言わんばかりに、机を叩いた。
example_sentences.english: The teacher slammed his desk as if to say, 'look this way'.

example_sentences.japanese: このコンサート会場は溢れんばかりのファンで埋め尽くされている。
example_sentences.english: The concert venue was filled, as if it was about to overflow with fans.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が交通事故で亡くなったってことを聞いて、私は胸が張り裂けんばかりの気持ちになって、その場から動くことができなくなった。
example_sentences.english: When I heard that he had died in a car accident, I felt as if my heart was about to tear apart (heartbroken), and I could not move.

example_sentences.japanese: あふれんばかりのこの気持ちを、どうやったら伝えられるのでしょうか…。
example_sentences.english: This feeling that is about to overflow, just how do I convey it I wonder...

example_sentences.japanese: このトリックアートを見ていたら、今にも目がまわらんばかりにフラフラしてきた。
example_sentences.english: When I looked at this trick art, I felt lightheaded as if I were about to faint at this very moment.

example_sentences.japanese: なかんばかりに口をギュッと閉じている息子が、愛おしくてしかたがありません。
example_sentences.english: How dear he looks, my son who has his mouth clenched as if he is about to cry.

example_sentences.japanese: なぐりかからんばかりに体をワナワナと震わせている彼からソッと距離をおいた。
example_sentences.english: I distance myself from him, whose body was trembling as if he was about to throw a punch.

example_sentences.japanese: かみつかんばかりに犬に吠えられてから、犬に対して苦手意識がある。
example_sentences.english: After I was barked at by a dog who seemed about to bite, I realized that I am not good with dogs.

example_sentences.japanese: 「興味ない」といわんばかりの冷たい視線に、怖気付いてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I felt dread toward their cold look as if they were about to say ‘I am not interested’.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「木橋は車の重さでおれんばかりに軋み音をたてる。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'The wooden bridge is making a creaking noise as if it were about to collapse due to the car's weight.'

example_sentences.japanese: コロ先生の最後の講演とあって、講堂が生徒であふれんばかりだった。
example_sentences.english: Since it was the last lecture of Koro-sensei, the auditorium was about to overflow with people.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「この巨大な宝石はまるで『拾ってください』といわんばかりに、燦然と光り輝いていた｡」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'The enormous jewel was shining brilliantly as if it were saying "please pick me up".'

example_sentences.japanese: 誤って犬の足を踏んでしまったとき、その犬は「これは決して忘れない」といわんばかりの顔で私を見つめた。
example_sentences.english: When I accidentally stepped on my dog's paw, she looked at me as if she were about to say 'I will never forget this'.

example_sentences.japanese: 回顧録：「１６年後、スミレに偶然出会った時、彼女は僕を知らないふりして通り過ぎた。しかし彼女は胸がいっぱいになり、喜びの涙でなきださんばかりの顔をした。」
example_sentences.english: Memoir: 'When I happened to meet Sumire sixteen years later, she passed by, pretending not to know me. However, she was filled with emotion, as if she were about to burst into tears of happiness.'

general_translation: According to, In accordance with, Based on, In line with
formation: Noun + に則（のっと）って(1)Noun (A) + に則（のっと）った(2) + Noun (B)(1)に則（のっと）り(2)に則（のっと）っての
casual_structure: Noun + に則（のっと）って(1)Noun (A) + に則（のっと）った(2) + Noun (B)(1)に則（のっと）り(2)に則（のっと）っての
explanation: A formal grammar point, showing that something is based on some long-running tradition or convention. Following along with (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 全ての犯罪者は、法にのっとって裁かれるべきである。
example_sentences.english: All criminals should be tried in accordance with the law.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は無宗教なので、宗教にのっとった式はあげたくないです。
example_sentences.english: I am not religious, so I do not want to have a ceremony based on religion.

example_sentences.japanese: どの国に行こうと、その国の法律にのっとって、生活しなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: No matter what country you go to, you must live according to the laws of that country.

example_sentences.japanese: 芸能事務所の規則にのっとって、事務所に内緒で交際を始めたアイドルがクビになった。
example_sentences.english: In accordance with the rules of the production company, the idol that began to date without notifying the company got fired.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ国のガイドラインにのっとった方法で物事を進めても、批判の声を上げる人は出てくる。
example_sentences.english: Even if things are done in accordance with national guidelines, there will still be those who will voice criticism.

example_sentences.japanese: 伝統にのっとって、和装で結婚式を行いました。
example_sentences.english: In accordance with tradition, the wedding ceremony was conducted in traditional Japanese attire.

example_sentences.japanese: 先例にのっとって全てのことをしていては、改革などできない。
example_sentences.english: If everything is always done in accordance with the initial steps, a reformation cannot happen.

example_sentences.japanese: もう古いやり方にのっとって全てのことを行うのはやめようではないか。
example_sentences.english: Isn’t conducting everything based on the old way something that we should stop already?

example_sentences.japanese: 原則にのっとって、規則を破った社員は解雇されることとなりました。
example_sentences.english: The staff member was fired, having broken a regulation in line with the precedence.

example_sentences.japanese: 求人：「交通費は企業方針にのっとり支給致します。」
example_sentences.english: Job offer: 'We cover travel expenses in accordance with the company policy.'

example_sentences.japanese: 注文のキャンセルの場合は当社規定にのっとり、１０％キャンセル手数料を請求させていただきます。
example_sentences.english: In the case of cancellation of the order, we will charge a 10% cancellation fee in accordance with the predetermined (procedures) of our company.

example_sentences.japanese: 前社長のやり方にのっとって会社を運営している彼女には賞賛の声が上がっている。
example_sentences.english: She, who is running the company in line with the previous president’s way of doing things, is raising voices of approval.

example_sentences.japanese: 伝統的なレストランの広告：「着物姿のスタッフが伝統にのっとったおもてなしをさせていただきます。」
example_sentences.english: Traditional restaurant advertisement: 'Our kimono-dressed staff will make sure to give you a warm welcome and attentive service that is in accordance with the honored tradition.'

example_sentences.japanese: 企業ウェブサイト：「弊社は個人情報保護法にのっとって、個人データの取扱いに細心の注意を払います。」
example_sentences.english: Company website: 'Our company pays close attention to handling personal data, in accordance with Personal Information Protection Law.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「たけしさんはボクシングリングで何があろうと騎士道精神にのっとって行動してきた。そのため、ボクシング界では尊敬される立場となった。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'No matter what happens, Mr. Takeshi has always acted in accordance with the spirit of chivalry in the boxing ring. For that reason, he has come to be greatly respected in the boxing world.'

general_translation: Extremely, Really, Very, As ... as one can be
formation: ［い］Adjective + 限（かぎ）り + だ［な］Adjective + な + 限（かぎ）り + だ
casual_structure: ［い］Adjective + 限（かぎ）り + だ［な］Adjective + な + 限（かぎ）り + だ
polite_structure: ［い］Adjective + 限（かぎ）り + です［な］Adjective + な + 限（かぎ）り + です
explanation: A formal phrase, expressing that something is extremely (A). The characteristic of (A) is at the limit. As (A) as can be.

example_sentences.japanese: まあ、お子さんが結婚したの？羨ましいかぎりだわ。
example_sentences.english: Oh, your child got married? I am as jealous as one could be!

example_sentences.japanese: 私のためにこんな素晴らしい送別会を開いてくれるなんて、嬉しいかぎりです。
example_sentences.english: I am very happy that you threw such an amazing farewell party for me.

example_sentences.japanese: 宝くじで一等が当たったなんて、羨ましいかぎりだ。
example_sentences.english: Something like winning first place in a lottery is very enviable.

example_sentences.japanese: 一分遅れただけで不合格にされるなんて、残念なかぎりだ。
example_sentences.english: It's very disappointing that I failed just by being a minute late.

example_sentences.japanese: 同僚にあんなことを言われて、不快なかぎりです。
example_sentences.english: I'm very offended that my colleague said something like that to me.

example_sentences.japanese: コスタリカ旅行の抽選に当たったなんて、うらやましいかぎりだよ。
example_sentences.english: Something like winning a Costa Rica trip on the lottery is very enviable.

example_sentences.japanese: 狼人間が僕の味方なんて、心強いかぎりです。
example_sentences.english: Something like having a werewolf as an ally is extremely reassuring.

example_sentences.japanese: 信頼していた子供に裏切られて、悲しいかぎりです。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely sad, having been betrayed by the child I trusted.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供を先に亡くすなんて、本当に可哀想なかぎりだ。
example_sentences.english: Something like losing a child before you die, it is as pitiable as can be.

example_sentences.japanese: 長年の研究がようやく実を結び、嬉しいかぎりです。
example_sentences.english: Having my research of many years finally bear fruit, I am as happy as can be.

example_sentences.japanese: 足を折られた同僚に：「足のことを聞きました、お気の毒なかぎりです。」
example_sentences.english: To a coworker that broke his/her leg: 'I heard about the leg. Very sorry to hear that.'

example_sentences.japanese: 来月から娘が一人暮らしを始めるなんて、寂しいかぎりだ。
example_sentences.english: To think that my daughter will start living alone from next month, I feel extremely lonely.

example_sentences.japanese: 歌手のツイッターでの投稿：「私のコンサートが中止になってしまったという連絡を頂き、残念なかぎりです。」
example_sentences.english: Post of a singer on Twitter: 'It is very disappointing to hear that my concert has been canceled.'

example_sentences.japanese: 漫画家は読者に感謝する：「私の漫画をここまで読んでくださり、嬉しいかぎりです。ありがとうございました。」
example_sentences.english: A mangaka expressing gratitude to readers: 'I am very glad that you have been reading my manga to this moment. Thank you very much.'

example_sentences.japanese: 自分を高めたいという強い意志を持って学んでいる生徒たちの姿は、教師にとって心強いかぎりだ。
example_sentences.english: Seeing pupils studying with a strong wish for improvement is very reassuring for a teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「この二人が私の娘たちです。」娘たち：「どうぞよろしく。」友達２：「まあ立派な娘さんたちですよね。頼もしいかぎりです。」
example_sentences.english: Friend1: 'These 2 are my daughters.'Daughters: 'Pleased to make your acquaintance.'Friend2: 'Oh my, what fine daughters you have. They look very promising.'

general_translation: Let alone, Much less, Needless to say, Not to mention, Not only but also
formation: Noun (A) + はおろか + Noun (B) + さえ(1)(1)も、まで、すら
casual_structure: Noun (A) + はおろか + Noun (B) + さえ(1)(1)も、まで、すら
explanation: A formal grammar point, implying much less (A), (B). Alienating the topic of (A), (B). Often negative.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ルームメイトはオムライスはおろか、おにぎりさえ作れない。」
example_sentences.english: 'My roommate cannot even make onigiri, let alone omurice.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は掃除はおろか、料理さえできない。
example_sentences.english: He can't even cook, let alone clean.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はスーパーはおろか、コンビニさえもないど田舎に住んでいる。
example_sentences.english: I live in a very rural area where there isn't a convenience store, let alone a supermarket.

example_sentences.japanese: 父はパソコンはおろか、スマホさえも使うことができない。
example_sentences.english: My father can't use a smartphone, let alone a computer.

example_sentences.japanese: 掃除機をかけることはおろか、彼はゴミ拾いさえしない。
example_sentences.english: Let alone turning on the vacuum cleaner, he won’t even pick up the trash.

example_sentences.japanese: パスタはおろかお米さえ食べるのをやめていたら痩せました。
example_sentences.english: Let alone pasta, when I stopped eating even rice, I lost weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 貴重品はおろか、身につけていた服まで奪われてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Not to mention my valuables, even the clothes off my back were stolen.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月の生活はおろか、今日でさえ生きていけるか分かりません。
example_sentences.english: Much less living this month, I am not really even sure if I can live today.

example_sentences.japanese: フランス語はおろか英語も話せないのにフランスへ行こうとしています。
example_sentences.english: Let alone French, despite not even knowing English, I am planning on going to France.

example_sentences.japanese: 「最近、痔が痛み出したなぁ。座ってるのはおろか、歩くのも痛いぞ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Recently my hemorrhoids have been so painful. It even hurts to walk, much less sit.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説： 「敵はおろか味方からも恐れられ、『バーサーカー』と言われるようになった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: Feared not only by enemies but also by her allies, she came to be called 'berserker'.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は太りすぎて、座っているときはおろか寝ている時でさえ呼吸が辛そうだ。
example_sentences.english: He is so overweight that, let alone when he is sitting, he struggles to breathe even when he is sleeping.

example_sentences.japanese: 今や都会の夜空には天の川はおろか、星すら見えなくなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Nowadays even the stars have stopped being visible in the night sky of the city, much less the Milky Way.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はアクションアドベンチャーの有名な本をシリーズで執筆したが、実は祖国はおろか、故郷すら出たことがないという。
example_sentences.english: It is said that although he wrote a famous action-adventure series, he has never left his hometown, let alone motherland.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の文字と中国語の文字の区別はおろか、ロシア語の文字との区別さえつかない人も少なくない。
example_sentences.english: There are quite a few people who cannot tell the difference between Japanese characters and Russian characters, let alone Japanese Characters and Chinese characters.

general_translation: Like, To show signs of,  To have the appearance of, To come to a (state) similar to, Somewhat, An air of,  Feels almost like
formation: Noun + めいてNoun + めいているNoun［Season］ + めいてきた​​ Noun + めいた + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + めいてNoun + めいているNoun［Season］ + めいてきた​​ Noun + めいた + Noun
polite_structure: Noun + めいてNoun + めいていますNoun［Season］ + めいてきましたNoun + めいた + Noun
explanation: A suffix showing that something is giving off the signs of (A). Very often used about natural states, such as seasons, colors, lights, or movements.

example_sentences.japanese: 脅迫めいたメールが役所に届いたそうだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems a threatening sounding email was delivered to the city office.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日までは嘘みたいに暑かったのに、やっと春めいてきた！
example_sentences.english: It has been hot until yesterday, but it's finally starting to become spring-like!

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談めいて言ったが、多分冗談だったということは気づいていないと思う。
example_sentences.english: I said it like a joke, but I don't think they understood it as a joke.

example_sentences.japanese: 皮肉めいたことを言ってしまって、相手が黙り込んでしまった。
example_sentences.english: I said something which sounded like sarcasm and the other person fell silent.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はなんか謎めいた雰囲気があるよね。
example_sentences.english: She has a somewhat mysterious vibe, doesn't she?

example_sentences.japanese: 桜も咲いてすっかり春めいてきました。
example_sentences.english: The cherry blossoms are blooming, and it starting to thoroughly show signs of being spring.

example_sentences.japanese: 作り物めいて見えるほど、平穏で美しい景色だった。
example_sentences.english: It was calm and beautiful scenery, to the point of looking man-made.

example_sentences.japanese: 色めいた彼女の表情に、思わずドキッとしました。
example_sentences.english: My heart skipped a beat when her expression showed signs of being amorous.

example_sentences.japanese: 芝居めいた彼のプレゼンには、あまり魅力を感じません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t feel any allure toward his presentation that feels almost like an act.

example_sentences.japanese: 母が「宿題しなさい」と言うときは、決まって説教めいた口調になる。
example_sentences.english: Whenever my mom tells me to do my homework, she always uses a lecture-like tone.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「いつのまにか冬は去り、かなり春めいていた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Before I knew it, it had already gotten quite spring-like.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「ともこの皮肉めいて聞こえた言葉に、ともきが黙り込んだ。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Tomoki fell silent on the words of Tomoko, which sounded like irony.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の気分を上げるため、何か冗談めいた、とるに足りない話をしようとした。
example_sentences.english: In order to improve her mood, I tried to tell a joke-like, non-serious story.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の後輩から言い訳めいた報告を長々と聞かされる、金曜日の午後６時。
example_sentences.english: It's 6 p.m. on a Friday, and I'm being made to listen to a drawn-out report from a junior colleague that sounds like an excuse.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「その知らせを聞いて彼女の顔には謎めいた微笑が浮かんでいた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Hearing the news, a somewhat mysterious smile appeared on her face.'

example_sentences.japanese: 手紙の挨拶：「九月になると空も風もだいぶ秋めいてまいりました。お変わりありませんか。」
example_sentences.english: Greetings in letter：In September, the sky and wind start to get quite autumn-like. How have you been?

general_translation: Not only A or B but every-; A, B and every-; Not only A or B but all over;  A, B both, whether A or B
formation: Noun (A) + といわず +  Noun (B) + といわず
casual_structure: Noun (A) + といわず +  Noun (B) + といわず
explanation: A formal expression, highlighting that not only (A) or (B), but all. Without saying it is (A) and without saying it is (B), (C).

example_sentences.japanese: ご飯中といわず会話中といわず携帯を手放さない娘が心配です。
example_sentences.english: Not only during food but also during conversations, I am worried about my daughter who can’t put her phone down.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は子供といわず、大人といわず、みんなに愛されている。
example_sentences.english: Not only is this movie loved by children, but also by adults.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行から帰ってきたら、タンスといわず、棚といわず、家中泥棒に物色されていた。
example_sentences.english: When I returned from my trip, the whole house had been ransacked by thieves, not only the wardrobe or the shelves.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は仕事中といわず、休憩中といわず、ずっとユーチューブを見ている。
example_sentences.english: He is always watching Youtube, not only when he is working, but also on his break.

example_sentences.japanese: 金庫の中といわず冷蔵庫の中といわず、泥棒は全てを盗んでいったらしい。
example_sentences.english: Not only the contents of the safe and the fridge, but it seems that the thieves stole and made off with everything.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供といわず女性といわず、いつでも安全に暮らせるようになればいいです。
example_sentences.english: Not only if you are a child or a woman, but everyone should be able to always live in safety.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝といわず夜といわずずっとゲームをしていたせいで生活リズムが狂ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Not only in the mornings or at night, because I was gaming all the time, my lifestyle rhythm has become screwed up.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「街灯は、はるか北の村で、夜といわず昼といわずともりつづけた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'The lights in the village far north are lit continuously, not only during day or night (but all the time).'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「勇者は戦闘後、手といわず、足といわず、満身創痍だった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'After the battle, the hero was wounded not only on his hands or feet but all over his body.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「炎は地面といわず壁といわず、無慈悲にも四方八方へと広がり続けていく。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'The flame was spreading not only on the ground or walls but mercilessly in all directions .'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「ぜなの室内は、壁といわず天井といわず、全てよそらのポスターや写真で埋め尽くされている。」
example_sentences.english: The interior of Zena's room has been plastered with posters and photographs of Yosora not only on walls and the ceiling but everywhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「新国王の名前を聞くと、一般市民といわず、貴族といわず、恐怖に震え上がった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Hearing the name of the new king, not only ordinary citizens or aristocrats (but everyone) trembled with fear.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「アンディは他の囚人に組み敷かれていて頭といわず顔といわず、身体中をめった打ちにされた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Andy was pressed down by another prisoner, and has been beaten not only on his head or face but all over the body.'

general_translation: There is a limit to, You are too ..., How …!, How … one can be!
formation: Verb + にもほどがある［い］Adjective + にも + ほどがある［な］Adjective + にも + ほどがあるNoun + にも + ほどがある
casual_structure: Verb + にもほどがある［い］Adjective + にも + ほどがある［な］Adjective + にも + ほどがあるNoun + にも + ほどがある
polite_structure: Verb + にもほどがあります［い］Adjective + にも + ほどがあります［な］Adjective + にも + ほどがありますNoun + にも + ほどがあります
explanation: An expression that is often critical of (A), implying that it has gone too far. Even in (A) there is an extent.

example_sentences.japanese: ん？熊がエイリアンを襲ったって？！嘘をつくにもほどがある！
example_sentences.english: Huh? A bear attacked an alien? There is a limit to just how much one can lie.

example_sentences.japanese: お前またぶっ倒れるまで飲み続けたの？飲み過ぎにもほどがあるよ。
example_sentences.english: You drank until you blacked out again? There is a limit to drinking too much you know.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつからまたメールがきた。また「今夜も泊めて！」だってさ。図々しいにもほどがあるって。
example_sentences.english: I got a text from him again. He said, 'Let me crash at your place again!' There is a limit to how shameless one can be.

example_sentences.japanese: 敬語使わないのは別として、先輩に向かって「お前」っていうのはどうかと思うよ。失礼にもほどがある。
example_sentences.english: Setting aside you not using keigo, I don't think you should say 'you' towards your senpai. There is a limit to how impolite you can be.

example_sentences.japanese: そういうことは相手を傷つけるかもしれないから冗談にしないほうがいいよ。冗談にもほどがある。
example_sentences.english: Things like that could hurt the other person's feelings, so you should not joke about that. There are limits to jokes too.

example_sentences.japanese: またギャンブルをしたのか…金を無駄遣いするにもほどがある。
example_sentences.english: You were gambling again? There is a limit to just how much you can pointlessly waste money.

example_sentences.japanese: ここぞという時に頼りにならないなんて、リーダー失格にもほどがある。
example_sentences.english: Something like not being reliable at just the right moment, there is a limit to just how much you can fail as a leader.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎月１０万円もコスメに使うなんて、買いすぎにもほどがあるでしょう！
example_sentences.english: Using more than 100,000 yen on cosmetics every month, there is a limit to just how much one can over-purchase.

example_sentences.japanese: 吐きそうになる料理を作れるとは…料理が下手にもほどがあります。
example_sentences.english: Something like being able to make food that makes you feel like throwing up... There is a limit to just how bad one can be at cooking.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供を作っておいて育児を放棄するなんて、無責任にもほどがあるというものだ。
example_sentences.english: To think that you would have kids and then abandon raising them, there is a limit to just how irresponsible one can be!

example_sentences.japanese: 「まったく最近の若い子って、目上の人がしゃべっているのにおしゃべりするなんて礼儀知らずにもほどがある。」
example_sentences.english: 'Seriously, youths these days, to talk when one's superior is talking, there is a limit to how mannerless one can be.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａが勝手にＢの部屋に入ってきた状況：「こんな時間に部屋に押しかけてくるなんて、いったいどういう神経しているんだ。失礼にもほどがある。」
example_sentences.english: A situation in which A entered B's room without permission: 'What a nerve, to barge into a person's room at this hour. There is a limit to how impolite you can be!'

example_sentences.japanese: 親が友達と話す：「うちの子供たちはずっと一日中二人でゲームしてるよ。起きてから何も食べずにゲーム三昧よ。不健康な生活にもほどがあるよね。」
example_sentences.english: Parent speaks with a friend: 'My children play games all day long. They wake up and without eating anything, and then they are absorbed in their games. There is a limit to how unhealthy life one can live.'

example_sentences.japanese: 自信を持ち過ぎている友達１：「遅かれ早かれノーベル賞を受賞してみせるよ。」言い過ぎへの反応をする友達２：「ノーベル賞を受賞なんて冗談にもほどがあるぞ。」
example_sentences.english: Overconfident friend1: 'Sooner or later, I will definitely win a Nobel Prize.'Friend2 who is reacting to the overstatement: 'Getting a Nobel Prize? There are limits to jokes, too.'

example_sentences.japanese: 常に迷子になってしまう方向音痴の友人へ：「高校生のくせに学校から帰る途中で道に迷うなんて方向音痴にもほどがあるよ。」
example_sentences.english: To a friend with a poor sense of direction that gets lost on daily basis: 'To get lost on the way home from school despite being a high schooler, there is a limit to how bad with directions you can be!'

example_sentences.japanese: 従業員との話、従業員１：「これは田中さんの仕事なのに私たちに全部押しつけて、自分は何もせずぶらぶらしてるとか、図々しいにもほどがあるよね。」従業員２：「そうだよね。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between employees, Employee 1: 'Even though this is Tanaka's responsibility, he has pushed it on us, and without doing anything he just walks aimlessly. There is a limit to how shameless one can be.'Employee 2: 'That's right!'

example_sentences.japanese: なんだこれは！店出せるほどの美味しさじゃん！うまいにもほどがあるだろ。
example_sentences.english: What the heck is this!? This is so good you can open a restaurant! There is a limit to how good it can be!

general_translation: Even -er than, Even more than, More than anything, More than anybody, More than ever
formation: Noun + にもまして何（なに）にもまして誰（だれ）にもましていつにもまして
casual_structure: Noun + にもまして何（なに）にもまして誰（だれ）にもましていつにもまして
explanation: A structure implying that something is more (B) than any (A). An increase from even (A) is (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 前にもまして元気になって、ようやく退院した。
example_sentences.english: I have gotten even better than before and am finally able to leave the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は去年にもまして、湿気が多い。
example_sentences.english: This year is even more humid than last year.

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと薬を飲んで体を休ませたのに、昨日にもまして腹痛がひどい。
example_sentences.english: I took the proper medication and rested my body, but my stomach ache is even worse than yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 斎藤くんは誰にもまして仕事を一生懸命やってくれるからものすごく助かっている。
example_sentences.english: Saito-kun works harder than anyone else, so he is very helpful.

example_sentences.japanese: このプロジェクトを成功させることは、何にもまして大切なんだ。
example_sentences.english: Succeeding in this project is more important than anything else.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はいつにもまして輝いている。
example_sentences.english: She is shining brighter than ever.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学に合格したという知らせに、誰にもまして父が喜びました。
example_sentences.english: Having been informed about me passing the university entrance exams, my dad was happier than anybody else.

example_sentences.japanese: 財布をなくした。それにもまして困ったのは、家の鍵をなくしたことだ。
example_sentences.english: I lost my wallet. And even more troubling than that was that I also lost the key to my house.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の花火大会は、例年にもまして豪華だったような気がします。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that this year’s fireworks festival was even more spectacular than the average year.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルの接客は、どこにもまして良いと評判になっている。
example_sentences.english: This hotel has a reputation of having better customer service than anywhere else.

example_sentences.japanese: 親として、何にもましてうちの子供が健やかに成長できるように願う。
example_sentences.english: As a parent, even more than anything else, I wish for my children to grow up healthy.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな人に応援されようとも、愛する人からの応援が何にもまして心に響きます。
example_sentences.english: No matter who encourages you, the encouragement of the ones you love resonates more in the heart than anything else.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の夏は常に蒸し暑いことで知られている。だが今年は例年にもまして湿度が高くなっている。
example_sentences.english: Summers in Japan are known for being sultry. But the humidity is even higher than average this year.

example_sentences.japanese: 全ての選手が本当に奮闘したが、はいろさんに至っては、誰にもまして情熱を燃やした。
example_sentences.english: All of the team members are making an all-out effort, but when it comes to Hairo-san, he burns with passion even more than anyone else.

example_sentences.japanese: 社会の情報化が進むにつれ、会社は従来にもましてセキュリティ上の危険にさらされるようになった。
example_sentences.english: With the informatization of the society, companies have come to be exposed to security risks even more than before.

example_sentences.japanese: 利用者は大企業が常に大量のデータ収集する時代に、これまでにもまして自分のプライバシーを気にせざるを得ない。
example_sentences.english: In this age when large companies constantly gather data, users cannot help but pay even more attention to their privacy than before.

example_sentences.japanese: 当社の成功のための重要な要素の中でいいアイデアや有能な従業員はもちろん、しかしそれにもまして大切なのは幸運であると思います。
example_sentences.english: Among the factors essential for company success, good ideas and skilled employees are important of course, however, the thing that is even more important than that is luck.

general_translation: Like crazy, Keep doing (without a second thought), Nothing but, On and on, Do … all around, To do a lot of, One after another, All over, Keep, Everything, Constantly, All the time
formation: Verb［stem］(*) + まくるVerb［て］+ Verb［て］+ Verb［stem］(*) + まくる(*) Verb has to be volitional (can be controlled by the will of a doer)
casual_structure: Verb［stem］(*) + まくるVerb［て］+ Verb［て］+ Verb［stem］(*) + まくる(*) Verb has to be volitional (can be controlled by the will of a doer)
explanation: A strong grammar point, implying that (A) is being purposely done like crazy. (A) just keeps rolling and rolling on.

example_sentences.japanese: はやせとなおとは狂ったように踊って踊っておどりまくった。
example_sentences.english: Hayase and Naoto danced like crazy.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は釣具屋でルアーを買いまくったから、来週までご飯とふりかけで我慢しなきゃいけない。
example_sentences.english: I bought a bunch of lures at the tackle shop yesterday, so I have to put up with eating rice and furikake until next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりに実家に帰って、母の料理を食べまくってるから少し太ってきた。
example_sentences.english: I have started to gain some weight because I've been eating so much of my mom's food, ever since I came to visit my family after a long time.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日はカラオケで歌いまくったから、声が全然でない。
example_sentences.english: I sang like crazy at the karaoke last night, so I lost my voice.

example_sentences.japanese: 「最近、チョコをたべまくっているからちょっと太った。」
example_sentences.english: 'I've been eating chocolate like crazy lately, so I've gained some weight.'

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りが近いから、原稿をかきまくった。
example_sentences.english: Because the deadline is close, I wrote the draft like crazy.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間さえあればはしりまくっている彼の足はたくましいです。
example_sentences.english: He, who runs like crazy so long as he has time, has strong legs.

example_sentences.japanese: ストレス発散でメイク道具をかいまくったせいで金欠になった。
example_sentences.english: Due to buying makeup goods one after the other to relieve stress, I have no money.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はシャイで、それなのに人と会うと逆にしゃべりまくってしまいます。
example_sentences.english: I am shy, although when I meet people, I unfortunately talk like crazy.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら心配だからって、電話をかけまくるのはどうかと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of how worried you are, it’s not right to just call constantly.

example_sentences.japanese: 「まさはるさんは新車購入したから毎日のりまくっているらしいよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I heard that Masaharu-san bought a new car and has been driving it all the time, every single day.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「よしこって喋るのが大好きだ。ベラベラしゃべりまくるから彼女には我慢できない。」
example_sentences.english: 'Yoshiko loves to talk. She talks nonstop, like crazy so I can't stand her.'

example_sentences.japanese: 応援中にさけびまくったせいで、喉が痛くなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Due to screaming like crazy while cheering, my throat got sore.

example_sentences.japanese: ９０年代にはあのアニメが大ヒットした。私はファンになって以来、アニメグッズをかいまくっている。
example_sentences.english: In the 90s, that anime was a big hit. I have been a fan ever since and I've been buying anime goods like crazy.

example_sentences.japanese: うざき：「ゴールデンウィーク何か用事あるの？」さくらい：「せっかくだから毎日朝から晩までゲームをやりまくりたいんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Uzaki: 'Do you have plans for the golden week? 'Sakurai: 'It's a rare opportunity, so I want to play games every day like crazy, from dusk till dawn.'

example_sentences.japanese: しゃっくりが出まくりすぎて苦しい。
example_sentences.english: I am having a hard time breathing because I am hiccuping like crazy. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: And...so, And...because, Since
formation: (A) (1)+ わ + (B) (1) + わ（で）(1) Verb［る］、［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective + だ、Noun + だ
casual_structure: (A) (1)+ わ + (B) (1) + わ（で）(1) Verb［る］、［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective + だ、Noun + だ
explanation: A formal particle construction, emphasizing what happened due to the speakers frustration about events similar to (A) happening one after the other.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今朝の通勤時は、急に雨が降ってくるわ傘は壊れるわで大変だった。」
example_sentences.english: 'I had a hard time getting to work this morning because it suddenly started raining and my umbrella broke.'

example_sentences.japanese: このアパートはボロいわ狭いわで最悪な物件だ。
example_sentences.english: This apartment sucks because it is run-down and small.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日はクライアントに怒られるわ、自分の上司に暴言吐かれるわで大変だった。
example_sentences.english: I had a bad day yesterday because my client was mad at me and because my boss yelled at me.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しく入ってきた新人はクライアントには無礼だわ、クレーム対応が下手だわで、どこから教育していいかわからない。
example_sentences.english: The newbie that just joined is rude to our clients and bad at handling complaints, so I don't know how I should train him.

example_sentences.japanese: 携帯を買ってくれたこと自体は嬉しかったんだけど、５年前のモデルだわ画面は割れているわで使い物にならなそうだったから、自分で新しい携帯を買った。
example_sentences.english: I am happy that they bought me a phone, but it was a 5 year old model and the screen was broken and didn't look like I would be able to use it, so I went ahead and bought myself a new phone.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今日はタンスに小指をぶつけるわ、道でつまずくわで、ついてなかった。」
example_sentences.english: 'I was not lucky today because I hit my little finger on the dresser and tripped on the street.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「朝から犬に吠えられるわ、鳥のウンチが頭に落ちてくるわで…（最低な一日だったわ）。」
example_sentences.english: 'The dogs barked at me in the morning and the bird pooped on my head, so... （it was a horrible day.）'

example_sentences.japanese: 「あのレストラン、料理に虫が入ってるわ、クレームいったら切れられるわで最低だったの。」
example_sentences.english: 'Speaking of that restaurant, it was the worst since they had bugs in the food, and when I complained about it, I was ignored.'

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんに怒られるわ先生にも怒られるわ、気分が悪い。
example_sentences.english: Having been gotten angry at by my mother and my teacher one after the other, I feel terrible.

example_sentences.japanese: 財布をなくすわ鍵をなくすわ、本当に自己管理が全くできていない。
example_sentences.english: Losing my wallet and losing my keys one after the other, I honestly can’t look after myself.

example_sentences.japanese: このバイトは力仕事だわ未払いの時があるわ、もうやってられません。
example_sentences.english: This part-time job is physical work and sometimes the pay is overdue, I can’t put up with it anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏に浮気されるわ友人には裏切られるわ…もう生きていたくなくなる…！
example_sentences.english: Being cheated on my boyfriend and betrayed by my friends one after the other... I’m starting to not want to live anymore...!

example_sentences.japanese: ここのレストラン、接客態度は悪いわ値段は高いわで、全くいいところがない。
example_sentences.english: The customer service at this restaurant is bad and the price is high, so there aren’t any good points.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はいつもより寒いわ風は強いわで、観光なんてしていられません。
example_sentences.english: Today is colder than usual and the wind is strong, so it’s impossible to do something like sightseeing.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は風が冷たいわ曇っているわで、観光日和ではない。
example_sentences.english: Because the wind is cold today and it’s cloudy, it’s not ideal weather for sightseeing.

example_sentences.japanese: 変な匂いがするわ湿気があるわで、このホテルの客室は最悪だ。
example_sentences.english: Because there is a strange smell and it’s humid, this hotel’s guest rooms are the worst.

example_sentences.japanese: このマットレス、硬すぎるわ小さすぎるわで、買う価値がまったくない。
example_sentences.english: Because this mattress is too hard and too small, it’s not worth buying at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達とアニメのキャラについての話、Ａ：「だって興味深いもん」Ｂ：「そのキャラがつまらないわ寒いわ退屈だわで擁護のしようもない。」
example_sentences.english: Chat with a friend about anime character, A: 'But he is interesting!.'B: 'This character is boring, dull and mind-numbing, so there's no way to defend him.'

example_sentences.japanese: あのレストランは、接客態度が最高だわご飯は美味しいわで、また行きたいの！
example_sentences.english: Because the service at that restaurant is amazing and the food is delicious, let’s go again. (Rare positive use for emphasis)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼って料理が上手だわ、仕事をちゃんとしているわで、本当に魅力的でならない。
example_sentences.english: Because he is good at cooking, and he is thorough with his work, he is so attractive I can’t stand it. (Rare positive use for emphasis)

example_sentences.japanese: ずっと付き合ってた彼女に振られるわ、両親が亡くなるわで、この一年は最悪だった。
example_sentences.english: Because I was dumped by the girl I was dating for ages, and my parents passed away, this last year was the worst.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「顔色が悪いね。」Ｂ：「そうなんだよね。昨日の夜、ルームメイトがうるさいわ、蚊にたくさんさされるわでちっとも眠れなかった。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Oh, you look pale!'B: 'Yeah, I know. I couldn't sleep at all last night because of my noisy roommate and all the mosquito bites.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は宝くじには当たるわ、長年付き合っていた彼氏にプロポーズされるわで、幸せなことが沢山あってとても嬉しい。
example_sentences.english: I am very happy this year because I won the lottery and my boyfriend of many years is going to propose to me. (Positive meaning)

general_translation: Somehow (or other)
formation: どうにか + Phrase
casual_structure: どうにか + Phrase
explanation: An adverb that expresses that a result was achieved somehow or other, despite circumstances not being ideal.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の心はすでに離れていたが、私はどうにかしてその理由を知ろうと、言葉を選びながら話しかけた。
example_sentences.english: Her heart had already left me, but endeavoring to somehow know the reason, I carefully chose my words while addressing her.

example_sentences.japanese: どうにかして敵の攻撃を回避しなければ！ このままでは私たちの方が先に滅びてしまう！
example_sentences.english: We need to somehow avoid the enemy’s attack! At this rate we’ll be destroyed first!

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の午後までにどうにか帰れたらいいんだけど・・・。
example_sentences.english: It’d be nice if I could somehow make it back by this afternoon...

example_sentences.japanese: 雨がどうにか止んでほしいと、心から願っている。
example_sentences.english: From the bottom of my heart, I wish that it would somehow stop raining.

example_sentences.japanese: 初対面の人には緊張しがちなのだが、どうにか笑顔だけは忘れないようにしている。
example_sentences.english: I tend to get nervous when I meet people for the first time, but somehow I always try to not forget to smile.

example_sentences.japanese: 途中で誰かに笑われてもかまわない。私はどうにかこの夢を形にしたいんだ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t mind if I am laughed at along the way. I want to somehow give shape to this dream.

example_sentences.japanese: どうにか付き合いたての私たちのように、関係を戻せないかな？
example_sentences.english: I wonder if we could somehow restore our relationship to how it was when we first started dating?

example_sentences.japanese: どうにか明日までに終わらせないと。
example_sentences.english: I have to somehow get this finished by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: どうにか私の作品を見ていただくことはできませんか？
example_sentences.english: Would it somehow be possible for you to take a look at my work?

example_sentences.japanese: どうにかステージの後方まで声を届けてくれないと困るよ。
example_sentences.english: It’ll be an issue if you can’t somehow project your voice to the back of the stage.

example_sentences.japanese: どうにか電車さえ動いてくれたら、実家に帰ることができるのに。
example_sentences.english: If only the trains would somehow run, then I’d be able to return home.

example_sentences.japanese: 先方にプレゼンをするまでにどうにか時間稼ぎをしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to somehow buy us some time before we do the presentation for the client.

example_sentences.japanese: 全てが崩れ去る寸前だったが、彼の一言がどうにか皆の気持ちをつなぎとめた。
example_sentences.english: Everything was on the precipice of ruin, but with a word from him, somehow everyone managed to pull it together.

example_sentences.japanese: 住民からの反対が強いという理由で、計画の見直しを迫られたが、どうにか妥協案を取りまとめた。
example_sentences.english: Due to strong opposition from residents, we were forced to change the plan. However, somehow we pulled together a compromise.

example_sentences.japanese: 理屈では説明しきれないほどの困難に直面しながらも、私はどうにか立ち止まらずに歩き続けた。
example_sentences.english: Even while confronting difficulties which were beyond logical explanation, I somehow continued walking without stopping.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなどうにか聞こえる声で話されたら何言ってるかわからないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you talk to me with a voice that I can barely hear, I won’t understand what you are trying to say.

example_sentences.japanese: 条件に不安はあったみたいだけど、どうにか説得することができた。
example_sentences.english: It appears that there were concerns about the conditions, but I was somehow able to persuade them.

example_sentences.japanese: どうにか明日までに解決しなくてはならない。
example_sentences.english: I have to solve this problem one way or another by tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな落ち込むなって、時間が経てばどうにかなるよ。
example_sentences.english: Don’t be that upset, things will work out over time.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんのこと聞いたぞ。こっちはこっちでどうにかするから、今は家族との時間を大切にしろ。
example_sentences.english: I heard about your mother. We will work things out on our end, so prioritize spending time with your family right now.

general_translation: As soon as, No sooner than, The minute
formation: Verb［る］+ や否（いな）や(1) + Phrase［た］(1)や
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ や否（いな）や(1) + Phrase［た］(1)や
explanation: A formal grammar point. Indicating that as soon as (A), (B). Although not knowing whether (A) was actually finished or not, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 教室に着くやいなやランドセルを机に置いた。
example_sentences.english: I put my backpack on the desk as soon as I arrived at the classroom.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が部屋から出てくるのを見るやいなや、空き巣が手に持っていたものを私に投げて、逃げていった。
example_sentences.english: As soon as the burglar saw me coming out of the room, he threw everything that was in his hand at me and ran away.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の顔を見るやいなや友達の犬が吠え出した。
example_sentences.english: As soon as he saw my face, my friend's dog started barking.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は席に座るやいなや「とりあえず生一つ」といった。
example_sentences.english: He said 'I'll have a beer to start' as soon as he sat down.

example_sentences.japanese: １２時を回るやいなやすぐに誕生日のメッセージを送ってくれたのは、お母さんだった。
example_sentences.english: The person who sent me a birthday message the minute it came around to midnight was my mother.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「彼があくびをするやいなや彼女もあくびが出てしまった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'As soon as he has yawned, the girl also yawned.'

example_sentences.japanese: 記事： 「警察官に気が付くやいなや急に走り出した。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'As soon as he noticed the policeman, he suddenly started to run.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「焼き立てのパンが皿に出てくるやいなやすぐに彼の口の中に消えた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'As soon as the freshly baked bread appeared on the plate, it immediately disappeared in his mouth.'

example_sentences.japanese: アイドルについての小説：「照橋さんはサングラスを外すやいなやあっという間にファンが周りに集った。」
example_sentences.english: Novel about idols: 'As soon as Teruhashi-san took off the sunglasses, in the blink of an eye, she was surrounded by fans.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は給料をもらうやいなや金を全てビンテージのオランダの家具などに使ってしまう。
example_sentences.english: As soon as she receives her salary, she spends all of it on Dutch vintage furniture.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はその子犬の顔を見るやいなや、この子を絶対に家に迎えると決心しました。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I saw that puppy’s face, I resolved to welcome him into our home no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が終わり外に出るやいなや雨が降ってきたので近くの居酒屋で雨宿りをする事にした。
example_sentences.english: Since it started to rain as soon as I finished work and went outside, I decided to wait out the rain in a local izakaya.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「その言葉を聞くやいなや彼は部屋を飛び出し、分厚い本を何冊も抱えて戻ってきた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'As soon as he heard that word, he ran out of the room, and then returned carrying some massive tomes.'

example_sentences.japanese: 我が子の帰りを心配していたその父親は、我が子の顔を見るやいなやその場で倒れてしまった。
example_sentences.english: The father who was worrying about the return of their child collapsed in place no sooner than they saw that child’s face.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「とっくの昔に亡くなっている友達からもらった、古い手紙を読み始めるやいなや感情があふれ、たちまち涙が溢れてしまった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'As soon as I started reading an old letter I received from a friend who was long gone, my feelings flooded and I suddenly dissolved into tears.'

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はＳＮＳに情報を上げるやいなや拡散されてしまうので、情報を発信する前にもう一度よく考える必要があります。
example_sentences.english: Because information spreads as soon as you put it up on social media these days, you need to think twice before sharing it.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩達が部室に入ってくるやいなや先輩達の顔色を伺い始めないといけない部活なんて、後輩にとっては居心地が悪いだろう。
example_sentences.english: Something like needing to read your senior’s mood as soon as they enter the clubroom is probably uncomfortable for juniors.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は本を開くや、寝た。
example_sentences.english: He fell asleep as soon as he opened the book.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はあの曲を聴くや、泣き始めた。
example_sentences.english: She started to cry as soon as she listened to the song.

general_translation: Because the reason is, Therefore, The present situation is like this, This is how (it is), Those are the circumstances, This is why
formation: Verb + 次第（しだい） + です
casual_structure: Verb + 次第（しだい） + です
explanation: A polite expression, stating that (A) is the reason for something. Because of the involuntary, hard to pass up situation of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: お見舞いに行く：「先生が倒れたと耳にしたため、直ぐにこちらへ伺ったしだいです。」
example_sentences.english: Enquiring about one’s health: ‘Because I heard that you collapsed, that is why I came to visit you immediately.’

example_sentences.japanese: 高速で玉突き事故があったので、遅れたしだいです。
example_sentences.english: I was late because there was an accident involving several cars on the highway.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月から、向かいの家に引っ越すことになったので、挨拶しにきたしだいです。
example_sentences.english: I came to introduce myself because we will be living in the house across from yours starting next month.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が提案してくださったプランでは予算オーバーしそうだったので、今クライアントと相談しつつ色々と調整しているしだいです。
example_sentences.english: We are now discussing with the client and making various adjustments because the plan proposed by you (senpai) seemed like it was going to go over their budget.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生：「なんで遅れたんだ？」生徒：「電車が遅延していて遅れてしまったしだいです。」
example_sentences.english: Teacher: ‘Why are you late?’ Student: ‘The reason is that the train was delayed.’

example_sentences.japanese: 部下が上司に：「吹雪の影響で列車の運行ダイヤが乱れており、出社が遅れたしだいです。」
example_sentences.english: Subordinate to boss: 'I arrived late to the office because of the blizzard and the train schedule was disrupted.'

example_sentences.japanese: 陽子：「どうして日本語の勉強をしているの？」マット：「日本にいずれ住みたいと思って勉強を始めたしだいだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Yoko: ‘Why are you studying Japanese?’ Matt: ‘The reason that I started studying is that I would like to live in Japan at some point.’

example_sentences.japanese: 辞表を提出する：「母国にいる身内が倒れたとの連絡が入ったため帰国する事にしたしだいです。」
example_sentences.english: Submitting a letter of resignation: ‘Because of receiving news that someone close to me collapsed in my home country, that is the reason why I have decided to return home.’

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の上司に招待状を送る：「今までお世話になったので、結婚式への招待状を送らせていただいたしだいです。」
example_sentences.english: Sending an invitation to a boss at work: ‘Because I have always been under your care, I am now requesting that you allow me to invite you to my wedding.’

example_sentences.japanese: 取引先への説明メール：「プロジェックトの進捗状況についてご理解頂きたく、ご連絡差し上げたしだいです。」
example_sentences.english: Explanation mail to a customer: 'I am contacting you because I would like you to know about the current state of the project.'

example_sentences.japanese: 招待客への説明メール：「万国博覧会は、台風接近のため中止にせざるを得なかったしだいです。」
example_sentences.english: Explanation mail to the invitee: 'We were obliged to cancel the World Expo because of the approaching typhoon.'

example_sentences.japanese: 保育園の先生が保護者に電話をかける：「あやかちゃんが急に発熱をしてしまったので、電話をさせていただいたしだいです。」
example_sentences.english: A teacher at a preschool phoning a guardian: ‘Because Ayaka-chan suddenly developed a fever, that is why I have called.’

example_sentences.japanese: 謝罪メール：「倉庫火災によりご注文いただいた商品の納期が遅れてしまったしだいです。心よりお詫び申し上げます。」
example_sentences.english: An apology email: 'The delivery date of the ordered products has been delayed because of a warehouse fire. We sincerely apologize.'

example_sentences.japanese: 内定状：「博士にご執筆いただきました教科書は、学生の間でとても好評です。つきましては、博士にぜひ講師としてご就任いただきたく、お願い申し上げるしだいです。」
example_sentences.english: Job offer letter: 'The textbook that you have written is very popular among the students. Therefore we would like to humbly request you to assume the position of lecturer.'

example_sentences.japanese: 同僚との会話、涼：「何をしているの？」浩介：「上司からミスを指摘されたから見直しをしているしだいだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Conversation between coworkers, Ryo: ‘What are you doing?’ Kousuke: ‘Because I was informed about a mistake from the boss, that is why I doing a reexamination.’

general_translation: I would say (about), I guess (about), It could be said that, About, At best
formation: Phrase + というところ(1) + だ(1) といったところ、ってとこ
casual_structure: Phrase + というところ(1) + だ(1) といったところ、ってとこ
polite_structure: Phrase + というところ(1) + です(1) といったところ、ってとこ
explanation: A grammar point expressing a rough estimate of what can be said. It's about the place or situation where I'd say (A). I guess (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗の原因は、過度な緊張というところでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I would say the reason for the failure was probably due to excessive nervousness.

example_sentences.japanese: これぐらいの物件だったら５０００万といったところですね。
example_sentences.english: For a property of this size, I would say it would cost something like 50 million.

example_sentences.japanese: 徒歩だと１時間といったところです。
example_sentences.english: I would say it would take an hour by walking.

example_sentences.japanese: このペースだとこの工事はあと二週間で終わるというところだ。
example_sentences.english: At this pace, I would say this construction work will be finished in about two weeks.

example_sentences.japanese: どれぐらい辛いって聞かれても...汗が出るぐらい辛いというところかな。
example_sentences.english: You are asking me how spicy it is? I would say spicy enough to make you sweat.

example_sentences.japanese: まあ順調は順調だけど、まあまあというところだ。
example_sentences.english: Well, you could say everything is going smoothly, but it's alright, I guess.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車で行けば３０分かかるけど、車なら１５分というところです。
example_sentences.english: It would take 30 minutes by train, but I would say it would take 15 minutes by car.

example_sentences.japanese: ストレスによる暴飲暴食で体重が増加したというところだと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that I would say that the reason for the weight increase was because of excessive eating and drinking due to stress.

example_sentences.japanese: はなこ：「オリビアの日本語のレベルはどうですか？」かすみ：「せいぜい平均といったところでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: Hanako: 'How are Olivia's Japanese skills?'Kasumi: 'I would say average at best.'

example_sentences.japanese: 上司：「頼んでいた仕事はどこまでおわりましたか？」部下：「７０、８０パーセントというところです。」
example_sentences.english: Boss: 'How far have you gotten on the job I asked you to do?'Subordinate: 'I would say it is about 70-80% done.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「スーパーまで行くのにどれくらいかかる？」友達２：「たぶん２０分といったところだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Friend1: 'How long will it take to get to the supermarket?'Friend2: 'I would say about 20 minutes.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達１：「小説はいつ書き上がる？」友達２：「あと４、５日といったところかしら？」
example_sentences.english: Friend1: 'When will you finish writing the novel?'Friend2: 'I would say there are about 4-5 days left.'

example_sentences.japanese: 散歩中、見た家について話すカップル、配偶者１：「この３ＬＤＫの家、だいたいいくらぐらい？どう思う？」配偶者２：「おおよそ３８９２万というところかな。」
example_sentences.english: A Couple chatting about a house they see during a walk, Spouse 1: 'About how much is this 3 bedroom house worth? What do you think?'Spouse 2: 'I would say it's worth about 38 920 000 yen.'

example_sentences.japanese: 探偵：「いつこれが起きましたか？」証人：「正確にはわかりませんが、１０−１２日前といったところではないでしょうか。」
example_sentences.english: Detective: 'When did it happen?'Witness: 'I don't know exactly, but I would say about 10-12 days ago.'

example_sentences.japanese: トレーナー：「昨日はどのくらい運動をしましたか？」会員：「２、３０分というところです。」
example_sentences.english: Trainer: ‘About how long did you exercise for yesterday?’ Member: ‘I would say 20 or 30 minutes.’

example_sentences.japanese: 校長先生：「一日に何人の保護者と面談をする事が出来る？」先生：「そうですね、四、五人というところだと思います。」
example_sentences.english: Principal: ‘How many guardians can you speak with in a day?’ Teacher: ‘Right, I think about 5 people at best.’

example_sentences.japanese: 独り言：「うーん、この量だと二人分っていうところだよなぁ…。もう少し食材を買い足すか…。」
example_sentences.english: Speaking to oneself: ‘Hmmm, if it’s about this much I guess I’d say it’s about right for 2 people. I guess I’ll buy some extra ingredients.’

example_sentences.japanese: 久留美：「隼人君って料理をするらしいよ！」陽菜：「本当に？きっと、簡単な鍋を作れるってとこだと思うけど。」
example_sentences.english: Kurumi: ‘I heard that Hayato-kun is going to cook!’ Hina: ‘Really? I think he can surely only cook a basic hotpot at best though.’

example_sentences.japanese: 主治医に妻の余命を聞いてみたところ、「運が良くてもせいぜい三年といったところでしょう」と言われてしまった。
example_sentences.english: When I asked the family physician about the amount of time my wife has left, I was told that ‘Even if she is lucky, I would say probably about 3 years’.

example_sentences.japanese: 買取となると、最低で５千円というところです。
example_sentences.english: If we were to buy this from you, I would say we would pay you at least 5 thousand yen.

general_translation: Not even one, Not a single, No (at all)
formation: 1 + Counter + たりとも + Phrase［ない］(1)(1) Verb［な］
casual_structure: 1 + Counter + たりとも + Phrase［ない］(1)(1) Verb［な］
explanation: A formal phrase, emphasizing when not even a single (A) can or will (B). The single (A) is often an extremely small amount.

example_sentences.japanese: 人間は酸素なしには１日たりとも生きられない。
example_sentences.english: Humans can not live even one day without oxygen.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなで押し入れようとしたが、一ミリたりとも動かなかったから、ユンボで押し込みました。
example_sentences.english: We all tried to push it in together, but it did not even move a millimeter, so we pushed it in using a backhoe.

example_sentences.japanese: 消防士などは一秒たりとも気を抜くことができない。
example_sentences.english: People like firefighters can't lose focus, even for a second.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は一分たりとも残業をしたくないので毎日定時に帰っています。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to work overtime even for a minute, so I go home on time every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 少したりとも油断をすると、ミスをして命を落とす恐れがあります。
example_sentences.english: If you let your guard down even a little, you could make a mistake that could cost you your life.

example_sentences.japanese: 安全や生命を脅かすものは何人たりとも許されない。
example_sentences.english: Not even one person is allowed to threaten life or security.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は沢山の仕事があるので、一分たりともぼーっとして過ごすわけにはいきません。
example_sentences.english: I have stacks of work to do today, so there’s no way I can zone out for even one minute.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「一瞬たりとも無駄にしないつもりで生きている。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'He follows his belief of wasting not even one moment in his life.'

example_sentences.japanese: 茜雫の死以来１５年経ったが、彼女を忘れたことは一度たりともなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even though 15 years have passed since the death of Senna, I have not forgotten her even one time.

example_sentences.japanese: 回顧録：「食糧不足を経験した祖母はいつも「ご飯は一粒たりとも残すな」と言ったものだ。」
example_sentences.english: Memoir: 'My grandmother, who has experienced food shortages used to say: "Do not leave even one grain of rice".'

example_sentences.japanese: 自衛隊：「救出活動は時間との戦いだ。一秒たりとも無駄には出来ないんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Self-defense force: ‘Extraction missions are a battle against the clock. You can’t even waste a single second.’

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が生徒に：「レポートの提出が遅れたら成績を下げるぞ！一秒たりとも遅れるな！」
example_sentences.english: Teacher to students: ‘If report submission is late, I will reduce your grades. Don’t be late by even a single second!’

example_sentences.japanese: 治療をしている最中は、一秒たりとも気を抜いてはいけない。その一秒が命取りになる。
example_sentences.english: In the middle of medical treatment, you can’t lose focus for even a single second. That one second could be fatal.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットの停滞期が来てしまった。この三日間、百グラムたりとも痩せる事ができていないので焦っている。
example_sentences.english: I have unfortunately reached a point of stagnation in my diet. I’m flustered because I haven’t lost even 100 grams in the last 3 days.

example_sentences.japanese: 天国で夫と再会する：「はぁ、や〜っと会えた。あなたの事を考えなかった日は一日たりともありませんでしたよ。」
example_sentences.english: Reuniting with your husband in heaven: ‘Ahh, we could finally meet. There was not a single day that I did not think about you.’

example_sentences.japanese: 水不足で悩む事が多いこの村の住民は、大事な資源である水を一滴たりとも無駄にしないそうです。
example_sentences.english: For the people of this town, who face many difficulties due to water shortage, they won’t waste even one drop of the valuable resource.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、敵役：「貴様らは全員、今日この場所で死ぬことになる。一匹たりとも逃がすつもりはない。」
example_sentences.english: A novel, the villain: 'It is decided, you all die here today. I do not intend to let even one of you escape.'

example_sentences.japanese: この洞窟へは２０年前に起きた事故以来、何人たりとも立ち入ることが許されない。
