example_sentences.english: Since the accident that occurred 20 years ago, no one has been allowed to enter this cave.

general_translation: Cannot tell, describe, say or express how, Words cannot express, Too … for words, Extremely
formation: More common pairings:Noun + といったらない(1)［い］Adjective［さ］(2) + といったらない(1)Less common pairings:Verb + といったらない(1)［な］Adjective + といったらない(1)(1)ったらない(2)［い］Adjective
casual_structure: More common pairings:Noun + といったらない(1)［い］Adjective［さ］(2) + といったらない(1)Less common pairings:Verb + といったらない(1)［な］Adjective + といったらない(1)(1)ったらない(2)［い］Adjective
polite_structure: More common pairings:Noun + といったらありません(1)［い］Adjective［さ］(2) + といったらありません(1)Less common pairings:Verb + といったらありません(1)［な］Adjective + といったらありません(1)(1)ったらありません(2)［い］Adjective
explanation: A very casual, hypothetical phrase, emphasizing that (A) made the speaker incapable of commenting about something. When it's (A), words can't express it.

example_sentences.japanese: このラーメンの美味しさったらない…。ついつい食べてしまうんだ。
example_sentences.english: Words cannot express how delicious this ramen is. I can’t stop eating it.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の人の犬は朝からうるさいといったらない。
example_sentences.english: I can't describe to you how loud my neighbor's dog is in the morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子を家で留守番させるのは心配といったらない。
example_sentences.english: I can't tell you how worried I am to let my son stay at home alone.

example_sentences.japanese: プロジェクトを終わらせた後の達成感ったらない。
example_sentences.english: I can't describe the feeling of accomplishment after finishing a project.

example_sentences.japanese: あの子の運転は危ないといったらありゃしないから、あの子と出かける時には運転させないようにしている。
example_sentences.english: I can't describe how bad her driving is. I always make sure not to let her drive when we go somewhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎では車がないとどこにもいけないから、不便といったらありゃしない。
example_sentences.english: I can't describe to you how inconvenient the countryside is. You can't go anywhere without a car.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は私の話を全然聞いてくれない。むかつくといったらありゃしない。
example_sentences.english: She does not listen to a word I say. I can't describe to you how annoyed I am.

example_sentences.japanese: 「車のタイヤが盗まれた。本当に腹が立つったらない。」
example_sentences.english: 'My car tires have been stolen. I can't tell you how angry I am!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「校長と鹿との戦いを見たときの驚きといったらないよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I can't describe my surprise at seeing a fight between the principal and a deer.'

example_sentences.japanese: メークした時の星野の変わり様といったらなかった。まるで別人のようだった。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't describe how much Hoshino has changed when she put on the makeup. She was like a different person.

example_sentences.japanese: 数年が経ったのにまだあの日の日没を覚えている。その景色の美しさといったらなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even though years have passed, I can still remember the sunset that day. I couldn't describe the beauty of the scene in words.

example_sentences.japanese: 京都の蒸し暑さといったらない。五分もしないうちに全身から汗が噴き出てきます。
example_sentences.english: Words cannot express the humidity in Kyoto. Within 5 minutes sweat will start erupting from your whole body.

example_sentences.japanese: 「最近仕事は面倒臭いったらないぞ。部長がいちいち目くじらを立てるからだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I can't tell you how bothersome my job has been recently. The head of the section is scolding me over every single little thing.'

example_sentences.japanese: あの四川ラーメンの辛さといったらない。食べてから数日間はお腹を壊してしまう。
example_sentences.english: Words cannot express the spiciness of that Szechuan ramen. After you eat it, you’ll have a stomachache for several days.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で全ての家事をこなす面倒くささったらない…あぁ、実家に戻りたいなぁ〜。
example_sentences.english: Words cannot express the bother of sorting out all the chores by yourself... Ahh, I want to return to my parents’ house.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな迷信を信じるから私と別れるっていうの？ばかばかしいったらない！！
example_sentences.english: You’re breaking up with me because of your belief in a superstition like that? I cannot tell you how idiotic that is.

example_sentences.japanese: 何年も付き合ってきた当時の彼氏からプロポーズをされた時の嬉しさと言ったらありませんでした。そしてその彼氏は今の夫です。
example_sentences.english: Words could not express my happiness of being proposed to by my then boyfriend whom I had been dating for several years. And that boyfriend is now my husband.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「歯を引っこ抜くのはどうだった？」Ｂ：「あの痛みといったらないわよ、本気で死ぬかと思ったもの。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'How was the tooth extraction?'B: 'I can't tell you how painful it is! I really thought I was going to die.'

example_sentences.japanese: その国で起きた学校での銃の乱射事件を聞いた時の悲しさったらない。犠牲になった子供達やその親御さん達の気持ちを考えるだけで涙が出てくる。
example_sentences.english: I cannot describe my sadness at the time of hearing about the random shooting incident that occurred in that country. Tears well up just thinking about the children who became victims, and their parents.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の優しさと言ったらありゃしない。
example_sentences.english: I can't describe how nice he is.

general_translation: In light of, Based on, According to, Referencing, Comparing against, In view of
formation: Noun + に照（て）らして(1)Noun (A) + に照（て）らした + Noun (B)(1)に照（て）らすと
casual_structure: Noun + に照（て）らして(1)Noun (A) + に照（て）らした + Noun (B)(1)に照（て）らすと
explanation: A grammar point indicating that something is in light of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: アルバイトをすることは学校の規則にてらして規則違反になる。
example_sentences.english: Part-time working is a violation in light of school rules.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯罪者は刑法にてらして罰せられる。
example_sentences.english: Criminals are punished in accordance with the law.

example_sentences.japanese: 母は自分の経験にてらして、こういう時はどうすればいいかをアドバイスしてくれた。
example_sentences.english: My mother advised me what to do in these situations in light of her own experience.

example_sentences.japanese: 労働基準法を守らない会社は法律にてらして罰せられるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Companies that do not comply with the labor laws should be punished in accordance with the law.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済統計にてらした強盗と窃盗事件に関する犯罪統計。
example_sentences.english: Crime statistics on burglaries and thefts in light of economic statistics.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の生活習慣にてらして罪がないことを宣言された。
example_sentences.english: In light of her everyday life (alibi), she has been declared innocent.

example_sentences.japanese: 我々の基準にてらすと、この製品を粗悪品と言う人は少なくない。
example_sentences.english: There are quite a few people that would call this product inferior in light of our standards.

example_sentences.japanese: 国内の状況にてらすと、国外からの石油の購入は必要である。
example_sentences.english: In light of the domestic situation, purchasing petrol abroad is necessary...

example_sentences.japanese: 社内規程にてらして、作業員の効率性の検証を行う。
example_sentences.english: To perform the validation of workers' efficiency in accordance with company regulations.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長の好みにてらして考えると、社長はクッキーよりもゼリーを選ぶだろう。
example_sentences.english: In light of the president’s preferences, he’ll probably choose jelly rather than cookies.

example_sentences.japanese: ２０１７年の経験にてらして価格下落は限定的であると私は考えています。
example_sentences.english: In light of the experience of 2017, I believe that price drop will be limited in scope.

example_sentences.japanese: 常に自分の基準にてらして善悪を判断する父は、多くの人からの反感を買っている。
example_sentences.english: My father, who always determines things in light of his own standards, draws a lot of opposition from others.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の経験にてらすと、彼女がこれから進もうとしている道を勧める事は出来ません。
example_sentences.english: In light of my own experiences, I cannot recommend the path that she is heading down from here.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康診断の結果にてらすと自分の体重と体脂肪率が適正範囲内に無い事が分かった。
example_sentences.english: In light of the results of my health checkup, I realized that my weight and bodyfat percentage were not within an acceptable standard.

example_sentences.japanese: 前例にてらして考えれば、社内の人と不倫行為をした人はどちらも会社を首になるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If we think in light of the previous case, the people who cheated on their partners with their coworker will probably both be fired.

example_sentences.japanese: 「恋は盲目」という諺があるように、人は恋をすると常識にてらして物事を考える事が出来なくなります。
example_sentences.english: Just like the proverb ‘love is blind’, those who fall in love become unable to think in light of common sense.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律にてらして考えてみれば彼は死刑になるはずなのに、なぜ彼の刑罰がそんなに軽くなったのだろうか…。
example_sentences.english: Despite it being clear that he ought to get the death penalty if we think in light of the law, I wonder why his punishment was so light.

general_translation: (Emphatic) if, If it is the case that, As (you wish)
formation: Noun + （だ）+ とあれば
casual_structure: Noun + （だ）+ とあれば
explanation: A formal, hypothetical construction, emphasizing that if it is the case that (A), (B). If the existing circumstance is (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 息子のためとあれば、火の中でも飛び込みます。
example_sentences.english: If it is for my son, I would even dive into a fire.

example_sentences.japanese: 状態がいいとあれば４万円ぐらいで売れると思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: If it is in good condition, I think you'd be able to sell it for 40,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: データを復元できるとあれば、いくらでも出します！
example_sentences.english: If it is for recovering my data, I would pay whatever you offer!

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩の指示とあれば従わないわけにはいけないけど、絶対私のやり方の方が効率がいいと思うのに。
example_sentences.english: It is my Senpai's orders so I have to do it, but I swear my way is a lot more efficient.

example_sentences.japanese: お前の頼みとあればやるしかないだろ。俺に任せろ。
example_sentences.english: If it is your wish, I have to do it. Leave it up to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 市民の願いとあればスーパーヒーローはいつでも出動するんだとか。
example_sentences.english: I hear that the hero would mobilize at any moment if it were the wish of the citizens.

example_sentences.japanese: 社員：「そんな会社のトップからの誘いとあれば無視できない」
example_sentences.english: Company employee: 'If it is an invitation from the head of the company, then it cannot be ignored.'

example_sentences.japanese: 母はいつも「愛する孫のためとあれば、どんな頼みも聞くわ」と言っています。
example_sentences.english: Mom always says, ‘if it is my beloved grandchild, then I would listen to any request’.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「皇帝陛下の命令とあればせざるを得ない！」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'If it is his Highness's order, then I will have no choice but to do it.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「あすの朝でも発てるか？」Ｂ：「必要とあれば（行くしかない）ね」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Are you leaving tomorrow morning?'B: 'If it is necessary (I will have no choice, but to go).'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「お願いがあって。ねえ聞いてくれる？」Ｂ：「もちろん！Ａさんの望みとあれば何でも聞いちゃうよ。なに？」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I have a request. Will you listen?'B: 'Of course. If it is your wish, I will listen to everything. What (is it)?'

example_sentences.japanese: 映画の悪役：「ふむ、それが其方の意見とあれば仕方ない。今ここで死んでもらおう。」
example_sentences.english: Movie villain: ‘Hmm, it cannot be helped if that is your opinion. I will have you die here right now.’

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルの受付係：「必要とあればアイロンとアイロン台もお貸ししますのでお申し付け下さい。」
example_sentences.english: Hotel receptionist: ‘If it is necessary, we can also lend an iron and ironing board, so please let us know.’

example_sentences.japanese: 富や権力のためとあれば身内や同僚を殺してしまうなんて、彼女はなんて冷酷なのだろう…。
example_sentences.english: Something like killing those close to you or your colleagues if it is for the sake of wealth and power, just how ruthless is she, I wonder.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、誘拐犯：「おまえの父親は、おまえのためとあれば、法外に巨額の身代金でも喜んで払うだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Novel, kidnapper: 'Your father, if it is for you, will gladly pay even an absurdly large ransom.'

example_sentences.japanese: 昇給のためには日本語能力試験の合格書がいるとあれば、それを手に入れるために必死に勉強します。
example_sentences.english: If I need a certificate of passing the JLPT in order to get a raise, then I will study with all my might to get my hands on one.

example_sentences.japanese: 生きるためとあれば、万引きを犯す人の気持ちも理解できなくはないが、まずはそのような社会を改善しなくては…！
example_sentences.english: If it is to survive, it’s not that I don’t understand the feelings of those who commit theft, but we need to improve a society like that first and foremost.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子のためとあればどれだけでも残業をする。
example_sentences.english: If it is for my son, I will do as much overtime as I have to.

general_translation: You must be very, How … you must be, I dare to say, I am sure or certain that you must be very
formation: さぞ + （かし）+ Phrase + （こと）+ だろう
casual_structure: さぞ + （かし）+ Phrase + （こと）+ だろう
polite_structure: さぞ + （かし）+ Phrase + （こと）+ でしょう(1)(1)でございましょう
explanation: A strong, formal word, highlighting that someone believes (A) to be the case. I dare say that (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「夜勤の仕事もさぞ大変だろう。」
example_sentences.english: How tough the night shift work must be!

example_sentences.japanese: あんなニコニコしている斎藤さんは初めて見た。さぞ嬉しい出来事があったんでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I had never seen Saito-san smiling like that before. He must have had something good happen to him.

example_sentences.japanese: あの一流企業で働いているなら、さぞいいところに住んでいるんでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If you work for that prestigious company, you must live in a very nice place.

example_sentences.japanese: おばあさんが急に入院されて、さぞご心配でしょう。
example_sentences.english: Your grandmother's sudden hospitalization must be very worrisome.

example_sentences.japanese: 「長旅ご苦労様です。さぞお疲れでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: You went through such a long trip. You must be very tired. (How tired you must be!)

example_sentences.japanese: 「初めての赤ちゃんのお誕生にさぞ嬉しいことでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: You must be very happy to have your first child. (How happy you must be to have your first child!)

example_sentences.japanese: 「智子は昇進が見送られて、さぞがっかりしたに違いない。」
example_sentences.english: Not getting the promotion, Satoko must be very disappointed. (How disappointed Satoko must be after not getting the promotion!)

example_sentences.japanese: 料理好きの旦那さんと結婚されて、さぞ幸せなことでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Getting married to a husband who loves cooking, how happy you must be.

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざこの国まで来て下さってありがとうございます。さぞ、疲れたことでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for coming all the way to this country. I am certain that you must be tired.

example_sentences.japanese: 硬い手紙：「ご子息様のこと、さぞご心配のことと思います。」
example_sentences.english: Formal letter: 'You must be very worried about your son.' ('How worried you must be about your son!')

example_sentences.japanese: 「家族が一生懸命働いているのに、あなただけ毎日遊んでいるだけ、さぞ楽しいでしょうね！」
example_sentences.english: 'Even though your family is working so hard, you are just having fun, how fun it must be!'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はハンサムでお金持ちでジェントルマンだ。さぞ女性からも男性からもモテるだろう。
example_sentences.english: He is handsome, rich, and a gentleman. I am certain that he is popular with both men and women.

example_sentences.japanese: 一年足らずでＴＯＥＩＣの点数を二百点も上げるなんて、さぞ懸命に勉強したに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Something like raising the score of your TOEIC by two hundred points in not even one year, I am certain that there is no mistake that you were studying with all your might.

example_sentences.japanese: 看護師として一ヶ月に十日も夜勤をこなしていると聞きました。さぞ疲れが溜まっていることと存じます。
example_sentences.english: As a nurse, I heard that you have 10 night shifts in a month. I dare to say that I am aware that you must get worn out.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの長女は以前に違法薬物や万引きなどで刑務所に入っていたそうですね。さぞ骨が折れたことと思います。
example_sentences.english: I heard that your eldest daughter has been in jail in the past due to things like illegal drugs and shoplifting. I am certain it must have been incredibly hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 詐欺にあって無一文になった姉を見て助けを差し伸べないなんて、その弟はさぞ冷酷な人に違いない。
example_sentences.english: Something like not reaching out to help your sister despite seeing her penniless after being duped, I dare say that there is no mistake that that brother is a cruel person.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに大切にしていた車を盗まれたなんて、さぞや悔しかっただろう。
example_sentences.english: You must have been so frustrated to have such a cherished car stolen.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人が彼の父だなんて、さぞかし驚いただろう。
example_sentences.english: He must have been very surprised that that man was his father.

general_translation: When it comes to, That or this … of mine, That or this darn …, That or this blasted …
formation: Noun + ときたら
casual_structure: Noun + ときたら
explanation: A very casual, hypothetical construction, used for criticizing (A). When it comes to that darn (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「義理の母ときたら私のことをぼやいてばかりよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'That mother-in-law of mine, she always complains about me!'

example_sentences.japanese: うちの息子ときたら、就職もしないで家でダラダラしている。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to my son, he is not even trying to get a job, and he is just sitting around at home.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの弟ときたら、朝から文句ばかり言ってくるから本当にうざい。
example_sentences.english: This (darn) brother of mine, he always complains to me in the morning, and it is really annoying.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の上司ときたら、自分が仕事できないくせに少しでもミスをしたらものすごく怒るからみんなから嫌われている。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to my boss, he gets super mad if you make the slightest mistake, even though he is not the best worker, so he is disliked by everyone at work.

example_sentences.japanese: 「このプリンターときたら、忙しい時に限って故障するぞ！」
example_sentences.english: 'This freaking printer of mine, it breaks only when I am busy.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「娘は真面目に勉強しているのに、息子ときたら・・・（何もやらない）」
example_sentences.english: 'Even though my daughter studies very seriously, that son of mine... (Doesn't do anything at all)'

example_sentences.japanese: 「うちの旦那ときたら、連休中うちでゴロゴロばかりで、子どもの面倒をみてくれないの。」
example_sentences.english: 'That husband of mine, he is always loafing around during the holidays and doesn't take care of children!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「隣の人ときたら、毎日、毎日、朝の６時からラジオを聞くからうるさくて眠れない。」
example_sentences.english: 'That freaking neighbor of mine, every single day he listens to radio from 6 a.m. so loud that I can't sleep.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「最近の若者ときたら・・・（年上に敬意を払っていない）」
example_sentences.english: 'When it comes to young people these days… (they do not respect their elders!)'

example_sentences.japanese: 末っ子の息子ときたら、また長男や次男におねだりをしているみたいだわ。
example_sentences.english: That youngest son of mine, it appears he is pestering his older brothers again!

example_sentences.japanese: あの子ときたら、また先生に媚びを売って内申点を稼ごうとしている。
example_sentences.english: That blasted kid. She’s trying to get grades by buttering up the teacher again.

example_sentences.japanese: 「武さんのお父さんは格好いいよ。うちときたら水を節約してとか電気を無駄使いするなとかうるさくて腹が立つ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Take, your father is so cool. When it comes to mine, he is always fussy, telling things like 'don't waste water' or 'don't waste electricity' and it pisses me off.'

example_sentences.japanese: 他の先進国には女性の議員がもっといるのに、私の国ときたらほんの少ししかいない。
example_sentences.english: There’re more female members of parliament in other countries, but my blasted country has nobody but a few.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達は結婚とか妊娠とか昇進とか人生の階段を順調に上っているのに私ときたら…。
example_sentences.english: Despite my friend rising through the stages of life smoothly with things like marriage, pregnancy, and a promotion, when it comes to me...

example_sentences.japanese: ネットが普及してからのネット上の情報ときたら、デマばかりで全く信用できません。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to information on the internet since the internet’s popularization, there’s nothing but rumors, so you can’t trust it.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の彼氏ときたら、彼女を蔑ろにして友達ばかり優先するんだよ？早く別れちゃえばいいのにさ…。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to my friend’s boyfriend, he makes light of her and always prioritizes his friends, right? She should just hurry up and break up with him...

example_sentences.japanese: 私が飼っているゴールデンレトリーバーときたら本当にやんちゃで、少し目を離せばいつも家が滅茶苦茶になっています。
example_sentences.english: That blasted Golden Retriever of mine, he’s so mischievous and as soon as I take my eyes off him even a little bit, the house gets destroyed.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの犬ときたら、家にお客さんが来るとその人に飛びつくからもっと躾をちゃんとしないといけない。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to my dog, when a guest comes to our place, he jumps on them so I need to train him properly. (To be expected)

example_sentences.japanese: カセットテープを使う機会がなくなったため、最近の若者ときたら、カセットプレイヤーが使えない子達が多い。
example_sentences.english: Since there is no opportunity to use cassette tapes, when it comes to the younger generation, there are many who do not know how to use cassette players. (Only natural)

general_translation: -like, Looking, Feeling, With an air of, To become
formation: Noun + びる［い］Adjective［い］ + びるNoun + びた + Noun［い］Adjective［い］ + びた + NounUsed with a limited set of expressions:・Common:おとなびる・おとなびた古（ふる）びたひなびた・Uncommon/sometimes used in literary language:田舎（いなか）びた物寂（ものさ）びる・Generally not used in modern language:ひねこびる神（かみ）さびるおさなびる
casual_structure: Noun + びる［い］Adjective［い］ + びるNoun + びた + Noun［い］Adjective［い］ + びた + NounUsed with a limited set of expressions:・Common:おとなびる・おとなびた古（ふる）びたひなびた・Uncommon/sometimes used in literary language:田舎（いなか）びた物寂（ものさ）びる・Generally not used in modern language:ひねこびる神（かみ）さびるおさなびる
explanation: A formal structure used for creating verbs, meaning that something is giving off the impression or air of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「くみこは年の割に大人びている。」
example_sentences.english: 'Kumiko feels mature for her age.'

example_sentences.japanese: なぜ子供は大人びた格好をしたがるのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder why kids tend to want to dress adult-like.

example_sentences.japanese: 実家で屋根裏部屋を掃除していたら、古びたアルバムが続々と出てきた。
example_sentences.english: While cleaning out the attic at my parents' house, I found a series of old-looking albums.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は幼びて見えるけど、実際は33歳らしい。
example_sentences.english: She is young-looking, but apparently she is 33 years old.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は大人びて見えるが、まだ社会のことなんて分かってないただの学生だ。
example_sentences.english: She is adult-looking, but she is actually just a student that knows nothing about the real world.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は田舎びているから好きだ。
example_sentences.english: I like this town because it is rural-like.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はどんなに治安が良くても、田舎びた町には住みたくない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how safe it is, I don't want to live in a rural-looking town.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「ヴァミリオは大人びて見えるが、純粋で、表情がわかりやすい少女なのだ。」
example_sentences.english: A novel: 'Vamirio looked mature-like, but she was a pure girl with easy-to-read facial expressions.'

example_sentences.japanese: プレミアが付いているせいでこんな古びたレコードが三十万円もするなんて…！
example_sentences.english: To think that due to it being limited, this kind of old feeling record would go for 300,000 yen...!

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「古びた木橋は足を踏み出すたびに不穏な音がした。」
example_sentences.english: A novel: 'The old-looking wooden bridge was making a disturbing noise with every step.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「そのテレビは本当に古びたものだった。まるで昭和の時代から飛び出したかのようだった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'That TV was really old-fashioned-like. As if it jumped straight out of the Showa era.'

example_sentences.japanese: 俳優：「幼びた見た目をしていることで、よく学生の役をやらされます。」
example_sentences.english: Actor: ‘I get made to take the role of a student often due to my childlike appearance.’

example_sentences.japanese: 一見するとひなびた小さな街ではあるが夏ともなると多くの観光客がこの街に来る。
example_sentences.english: At first glance, it might be a small city with a rustic feel to it, but when the summer begins, numerous tourists come.

example_sentences.japanese: この家は相当古びて見えるが、それでもその広さから一億円以上はするそうだ。
example_sentences.english: This house looks considerably old, but despite that it seems that it will go for over 100 million yen due to the spaciousness.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は仕事の都合上で都会に住んでいますが、リタイアしたら田舎びた町に引っ越すつもりです。
example_sentences.english: I am living in the city at the moment due to work circumstances, but I plan to move to rural feeling town when I retire.

example_sentences.japanese: え？！彼の年齢が三十三歳って本当？！随分と幼びて見えるから二十歳くらいだと思っていたよ！
example_sentences.english: Huh?! Is it true that he is 33 years old?! Because he has a considerable air of youth, I thought he was about 20!

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、序章：「旭丘は日がのんびりとのどかに過ぎていく、海岸沿いのひなびた雰囲気が漂う漁村だった。」
example_sentences.english: A novel, prologue: 'Asahigaoka was a coastal fishing village with a rustic feel to it, where time passed peacefully.'

example_sentences.japanese: まさにシティーガールという見た目をしている君がこんな田舎びた街で暮らしているなんて驚いたよ！
example_sentences.english: To think that you, the precise image of a city girl, would be living in a rural feeling town like this. I was surprised!

example_sentences.japanese: 陸：「なんでそんな古びた勉強机を未だに使っているのですか？」野々夏：「これはね、天国にいる母がくれたものなんだ。だから、捨てられずにいるの。」
example_sentences.english: Riku: ‘Why are you using an old looking study desk like that even now?’ Nonoka: ‘This thing, it was a present from my mother who is now in heaven. That’s why I can’t throw it out.’

general_translation: Even, Even for, Even from the perspective of, Even in the case of
formation: Noun + にしたところで(1)Less formal:Noun + にしたって(2)(1)としたところで(2)としたって
casual_structure: Noun + にしたところで(1)Less formal:Noun + にしたって(2)(1)としたところで(2)としたって
explanation: A hypothetical structure, emphasizing that even going off the situation or location of (A), the result will not be as expected. Even though (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 誰にでも欠点はある。完全な田中さんとしたって同じだ。
example_sentences.english: Everyone has faults. It is the case even for the perfect Tanaka.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩の青木さんにしたところで、上達しなければいけない箇所はある。
example_sentences.english: Even our senpai Aoki-san has areas where he can improve.

example_sentences.japanese: ノートパソコンにしたところで、Ｗｉ－Ｆｉがないと仕事ができない。
example_sentences.english: Even with a laptop, if there is no Wi-Fi I can't work.

example_sentences.japanese: １時間寝坊をしてしまったのでいくら急いだとしたところで、間に合うわけがない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I hurry, I am not going to make it because I overslept an hour.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットを始めたとしたところで、私は三日坊主だから続かないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if I go on a diet, I have a short attention span so I don't think I will be able to continue.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にしたってそんなことはしたくないけど、上司に言われたからにはするしかない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I don't want to do such a thing, my boss told me to, so I have no choice but to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 謝ったとしたって、社長は彼のことを許さないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if he apologized, the president would probably not forgive him.

example_sentences.japanese: 「え？倒産するか合併するかだって？どちらにしたって、僕にとってはマズイ事だ…。」
example_sentences.english: ‘Huh? You’re talking about either declaring bankruptcy or merging? Even in either case, for me they’re bad things...’

example_sentences.japanese: ５人の子供のお母さんにしたところで、まだまだ子育てにおいて学ぶことがあるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even in the case of it being a mother of 5, there are probably still plenty of things to learn regarding child rearing.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は非常に深刻な状態だ。天才医師のジャックにしたところで何もできない。
example_sentences.english: He is in very serious condition. Even the genius-doctor Jack cannot do anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ありがとう」や「ごめんなさい」という小さな言葉にしたって、聞く側には大きな意味を持ちます。
example_sentences.english: Even little words like ‘thank you’ and ‘I’m sorry’ hold a lot of meaning for those on the receiving end.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「ホロは賢い神だという。もっとも彼女としたところで普通人間と同じように孤独を感じる日もあるが。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Holo is said to be a wise god. However, even for her, there are days when she feels lonely like an ordinary human.'

example_sentences.japanese: 新首相は前首相を批判したが、彼にしたって国の経済を好転させられるわけではない。
example_sentences.english: The new prime minister criticized the previous one, but it does not mean that even he can change the country's economy for the better.

example_sentences.japanese: 最高の監視員にしたところでプールなどで全ての者の安全を見守るのは不可能だ。
example_sentences.english: Even for the best lifeguard, it is impossible to watch over everybody in the pool.

example_sentences.japanese: 紙の本を読む人の数はどんどん減っていくのは悲しいと思う。と言うものの、私としたところで電子書籍が日常的になった。
example_sentences.english: I think it is sad that fewer and fewer people read paper books. However, even for me, e-readers became normal.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなにあなたの教え方が上手にしたって、生徒に勉強に対するやる気がなければ意味をなしません。
example_sentences.english: No matter even how good your way of teaching is, if the students have no desire toward studying, then nothing will come of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 君がどんな高級なプレゼントを取引先に持っていくとしたところで、相手の態度は変わらないと思うけど…。
example_sentences.english: Even if you were to take the most luxurious gift imaginable to the client, I don’t think their attitude would change.

general_translation: Precisely because, Only because, Because, Due to, Only if
formation: Verb［ば］+ こそ  + Phrase［い］Adjective［ば］+ こそ + Phrase［な］Adjective + であれば + こそ + PhraseNoun + であれば + こそ + PhrasePhrase (A) + であれば + こそ + Phrase(B)
casual_structure: Verb［ば］+ こそ  + Phrase［い］Adjective［ば］+ こそ + Phrase［な］Adjective + であれば + こそ + PhraseNoun + であれば + こそ + PhrasePhrase (A) + であれば + こそ + Phrase(B)
explanation: A formal, hypothetical phrase, expressing (A) as the precise reason for (B). Similar to capitalization of a word in English

example_sentences.japanese: 悲しみがあればこそ、喜びもある。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because there is sadness, there is also happiness.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘の将来を思えばこそ、塾に通わせます。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because I am thinking about my daughter's future, I will make her attend cram school.

example_sentences.japanese: 忙しければこそ時間を効率的に使うことができるようになる。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because you are busy, you will be able to use your time more efficiently.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康であればこそ、年をとっても楽しい人生を過ごせる。
example_sentences.english: You will be able to enjoy life even if you grow old, precisely because of good health.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さな会社であればこそ、優秀な人材が必要だ。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because it is a small company, we need the best workers.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗すればこそ、成長できるのだと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that it is precisely because of failures that you are able to succeed.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強はむずかしければこそ、却ってやりがいを感じるのです。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because studying Japanese is hard, it feels all the more rewarding.

example_sentences.japanese: 両親が子どもを叱るのは子どもの幸福をかんがえればこそだ。
example_sentences.english: It is precisely because parents think of the well-being of their children that they scold them.

example_sentences.japanese: 「私たちは友達であればこそ、Ｘさんの計画に反対なんです。」
example_sentences.english: 'Precisely because we are friends, I am against your plan.'

example_sentences.japanese: 成果をアピールすればこそ、上司が私の成長に気がついてくれるのです。
example_sentences.english: It is only if my results are appealing that my boss will notice my growth.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長：「皆さんがチームの一員として協力すればこそ成功できるのです。」
example_sentences.english: Company president: 'Precisely because we work together as members of the team, we can succeed. '

example_sentences.japanese: 人間の寿命は限られている。であればこそ、人間はその命をできるだけ楽しく快適で充実して過ごそうと思う。
example_sentences.english: Human lifespan is limited. Precisely because of that, I plan to make life as enjoyable, comfortable, and fulfilling as possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 会議で批判に従った台詞：「辛辣な言葉でしょうが、わが社を心配すればこその苦言です。」
example_sentences.english: Words following criticism at a meeting: 'Those are bitter words, however, it is an honest opinion precisely due to concern for the company.'

example_sentences.japanese: 協力を依頼する：「あなたの知識があればこそ、この実験を成功させられるのです！」
example_sentences.english: Requesting cooperation: ‘It is only if we have your knowledge that we will be able to make this experiment a success.’

example_sentences.japanese: いそがしければこそメリハリを付ける事が出来ますが、常に暇だとダラダラと過ごしてしまいます。
example_sentences.english: It is only if you are busy that you can have a good life balance, but always having nothing to do will make you sluggish.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の成果をみとめてくれればこそやる気が出るのだが、この会社では誰も僕の成果を認めてくれない。
example_sentences.english: It is only if your results are recognized that you can become motivated, but nobody at this company recognizes my results.

example_sentences.japanese: 失いたくないとおもえばこそ心配になるのであって、決してあなたを束縛しようとはしていません。
example_sentences.english: It is precisely because I will become worried about not wanting to lose you that there is no way that I will try to tie you down.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな経験も命あればこそです。命を落とす危険性があることを自ら進んでしようとするなんて、私にはとてもじゃないけど理解できません。
example_sentences.english: No matter what the experience is, it’s only about having your life. So something like pressing forward myself with something that has life threatening danger is not me at all, so I don’t get it.

grammar_point: ても差（さ）し支（つか）えない
general_translation: May, Is it a bother if, Do you mind if, Is it a problem if
formation: Verb［ても］ + 差（さ）し支（つか）え + ありません(1)（か）Noun［でも］ + 差（さ）し支（つか）え + ありません(1)（か）［な］Adjective［でも］ + 差（さ）し支（つか）え + ありません(1)（か）［い］Adjective［ても］ + 差（さ）し支（つか）え + ありません(1)（か）(1) ないでしょう、ございません
casual_structure: Verb［ても］ + 差（さ）し支（つか）え + ありません(1)（か）Noun［でも］ + 差（さ）し支（つか）え + ありません(1)（か）［な］Adjective［でも］ + 差（さ）し支（つか）え + ありません(1)（か）［い］Adjective［ても］ + 差（さ）し支（つか）え + ありません(1)（か）(1) ないでしょう、ございません
explanation: A polite expression, used when asking or giving permission about something that may be a bother. (A) is a thing that may require support.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ミーティングは明後日でもさしつかえありません。」
example_sentences.english: 'I don't mind if the meeting is the day after tomorrow.'

example_sentences.japanese: ここに座ってもらってもさしつかえありません。どうぞお座りください。
example_sentences.english: I don't mind if you sat there. Please sit down.

example_sentences.japanese: お風呂は熱くてもさしつかえません。むしろ熱い方がありがたいです。
example_sentences.english: I don't mind if the bath is hot. In fact, I like hotter baths.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はまだ初心者です。下手でもさしつかえありませんか。
example_sentences.english: I am still a beginner. Do you mind if I'm not very good at it?

example_sentences.japanese: 今週はものすごく忙しいので来週でもさしつかえありませんか。
example_sentences.english: I'm extremely busy this week, so would you mind if we do it next week?

example_sentences.japanese: 電車：「ここに座ってもさしつかえありませんか？」
example_sentences.english: On a Train: 'Would it bother you if I sit here?'

example_sentences.japanese: 部下：「今日は定時に帰ってもさしつかえありませんか？」
example_sentences.english: Subordinate: ‘Is it a problem if I go home at the regular time today?’

example_sentences.japanese: 医者に：「この薬とその薬を一緒に飲んでもさしつかえないでしょうか？」
example_sentences.english: To a doctor: 'May I take that medicine together with this one?'

example_sentences.japanese: 営業担当者：「明日、お電話差し上げてもさしつかえございませんか？」クライアント：「はい、問題ありません。」
example_sentences.english: Sales representative: 'Would it bother you if I call you tomorrow?'Client: 'No problem at all.'

example_sentences.japanese: 目上の人に：「書類は宅配サービスを利用してお送りしてもさしつかえないでしょうか？」
example_sentences.english: To superior: 'Would it bother you if I send the documents using the courier service?'

example_sentences.japanese: どうせ私がいなくてもさしつかえないだろうから、次の企画は是非私抜きでやって下さい。
example_sentences.english: Seeing as though it won’t be a problem even if I am not there, please make the next plan minus me.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者：「この飲み薬は風邪の症状が治まりましたら、服用を停止してもさしつかえありません。」
example_sentences.english: Doctor: 'You may stop taking this medicine when your cold symptoms have subsided.'

example_sentences.japanese: 確かにこの職業には学歴がなくてもさしつかえないが、学歴があれば必ず役に立つだろう。
example_sentences.english: Although it is certainly true that it is not a problem even if you don’t have an academic record in this job, if you have it, it is sure to be of use.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司：「これからは会社に遅れる時、電話じゃなくてメールでもさしつかえないからね。」
example_sentences.english: Boss: ‘In the future when you will be late for work, rather than calling, it is not a problem if you just send an email.’

example_sentences.japanese: 優しい先生：「宿題の提出期限の事ですが、二、三日くらいなら遅れてもさしつかえありません。」
example_sentences.english: Kind teacher: ‘This is about the homework submission deadline, but it’s not a bother if it is two or three days late.’

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女のＳＮＳのフォロワーは三百万人を超えています。今一番人気なインフルエンサーと言ってもさしつかえないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: She has more than 3 million followers on social media. You may even say that she is the most popular influencer right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 患者：「今日は頭を洗ってもさしつかえないですか？」医師：「まだ傷口が完璧には塞がっていないので、今日と明日は我慢して下さい。」
example_sentences.english: Patient: ‘Do you mind if I wash my head today?’ Doctor: ‘Since the wound is not perfectly sealed, please hold off for today and tomorrow.’

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の大会に差し支えるので、焼肉に行くのは大会の後にしましょう。
example_sentences.english: Since it will interfere with tomorrow's tournament, let's go to the yakiniku after the tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: タバコは健康に差し支えるので、吸わないようにしています。
example_sentences.english: I do not smoke cigarettes because it is hazardous to my health.

grammar_point: には及（およ）ばない ①
general_translation: There is no need to, It is fine if you don’t, Unnecessary
formation: Verb + には及（およ）ばない［する］Verb + （する）+ には及（およ）ばない（お）+ 礼（れい） + には及（およ）ばない（ご）+ 心配（しんぱい） + には及（およ）ばないそれには及（およ）ばない
casual_structure: Verb + には及（およ）ばない［する］Verb + （する）+ には及（およ）ばない（お）+ 礼（れい） + には及（およ）ばない（ご）+ 心配（しんぱい） + には及（およ）ばないそれには及（およ）ばない
polite_structure: Verb + には及（およ）びません［する］Verb + （する）+ には及（およ）びません（お）+ 礼（れい） + には及（およ）びません（ご）+ 心配（しんぱい） + には及（およ）びませんそれには及（およ）びません
explanation: An expression implying that there is no need to (A). To not go as far as (A). It does not reach (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「待って、私も行くよ。」「いえ、それにはおよびません。」
example_sentences.english: 'Wait, I will go too!''No, there is no need for that.'

example_sentences.japanese: こちらから以前いただいたアドレスに送るので、こんな遠くまで取りに来ていただくにはおよびません。
example_sentences.english: I am going to send it to the email address you gave us last time, so there is no need to come this far to pick it up.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちの方からそちらに書類を持っていくので、こちらまでお越しいただくにはおよびません。
example_sentences.english: We will bring the documents to you, so there is no need to come here.

example_sentences.japanese: ご心配にはおよびません。これぐらいの怪我なら全然我慢できます。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to worry. This level of injury is totally bearable.

example_sentences.japanese: ここに書かれていることは皆さん既にご存じだと思いますので、ご説明にはおよびませんね。
example_sentences.english: I think everyone already knows the contents of this, so there is no need for me to explain.

example_sentences.japanese: リモートワークやオンライン会議が主流なのに、わざわざ会議の為にこちらまでお越しいただくにはおよびません。
example_sentences.english: Since remote work and online meetings are now the norm, there's really no need for you to come all the way here just for meetings.

example_sentences.japanese: はいだ：「れつこさんの顔色が悪いね。」れつこ：「ご心配にはおよびません。ただちょっと元気がないだけです。」
example_sentences.english: Haida: 'Retsuko, you are pale.'Retsuko: 'No need to worry. I am just a bit tired.'

example_sentences.japanese: 普通の人：「ありがとうございました。」偉い人：「いや、礼にはおよびません。」
example_sentences.english: Ordinary person: 'Thank you very much.'Person in high position: 'No need to thank me.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、バトラー：「気に入ったなら、何か食べるものでもお支度致しましょうか。」ゲスト：「いいえ、それにはおよびません。」
example_sentences.english: A novel, butler: 'If you would like I can make something to eat.'Guest: 'No, there is no need for that.'

example_sentences.japanese: 夫：「終電を逃しちゃったけど心配にはおよばないよ。走って帰るから！」
example_sentences.english: Husband: ‘I missed the last train, but there is no need to worry, because I’ll run home!’

example_sentences.japanese: 席を譲った人：「お礼にはおよびません。人として当たり前の事をしただけですから。」
example_sentences.english: Person who gave up their seat: ‘There is no need to thank me. I just did what any person naturally would.’

example_sentences.japanese: 夫が妻に：「心配にはおよばないよ。ただ少し血圧が高かっただけで他に異常は無いから。」
example_sentences.english: Husband to wife: ‘There’s no need to worry. My blood pressure is just a bit high, there is nothing else abnormal.’

example_sentences.japanese: 新入社員：「この会社の事でしたら説明にはおよびません。もう講習を通して全て理解しました。」
example_sentences.english: New Employee: 'When it comes to the company, I have no need for further explanations; I've already understood everything through the training sessions.'

example_sentences.japanese: セールスを断る：「その保険の事でしたら説明にはおよびません。私自身も保険会社に勤務していますので。」
example_sentences.english: Refusing sales: ‘There is no need to explain that insurance, since I myself also work at an insurance company.’

example_sentences.japanese: 申請者：「明日、書類を持って行っても差し支えありませんか？」公務員：「持って来ていただくにはおよびません。メールでも大丈夫です。」
example_sentences.english: Applicant: 'Would it be a problem if I bring the documents tomorrow?'Public servant: 'There is no need to bring them. It is ok if you send them via email.'

example_sentences.japanese: 客がお土産を差し出す、客：「いつもお世話になっているので、これ、つまらないものですが…。」会社員：「いえ、それにはおよびません。私はただ業務を全うしているだけですから。」
example_sentences.english: A customer giving a souvenir: ‘Since you’re always a help to me, here, I know it’s a bit lame...’Employee: ‘No, there is no need for that. I am just fulfilling my duties!’

example_sentences.japanese: 社員：「部長、車で本社までお送りします。空港でお待ち下さい。」部長：「わざわざ車で迎えに来るにはおよびません。近いので私がそこへ歩いていきます。」
example_sentences.english: Company employee: 'Director, I will drive you to the headquarters. Please, wait at the airport.'Head of the department: 'No need to pick me up by car. It is close, so I will walk there myself.'

example_sentences.japanese: あの有名ラーメン店には及ばないけど、ここのラーメンも結構美味しいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think the ramen here is also quite good, though not as good as that famous ramen restaurant.

example_sentences.japanese: お宅の息子さんには及ばないかもだけど、私の息子も結構上達してきたと思う。
example_sentences.english: Maybe not as good as your son, but I think my son has also improved a lot.

general_translation: In line with, Based on, In accordance with
formation: Noun + に即（そく）し(1)（て）Noun + に即（そく）した(1) + Noun(1) に則（そく）した
casual_structure: Noun + に即（そく）し(1)（て）Noun + に即（そく）した(1) + Noun(1) に則（そく）した
explanation: A formal construction, used when something in accordance with (A). In correspondence with (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 映画は実情にそくして制作されたものだ。
example_sentences.english: The movie was made in line with actual circumstances.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社のルールにそくして、副業をしてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: In line with the company's rules, you may not work a second job.

example_sentences.japanese: あの監督はちゃんと事実にそくして映画を作るから、映画を見るだけでいろいろなことが学べる。
example_sentences.english: That director makes his films in accordance with the facts, so you can learn a lot just by watching his films.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律にそくした勤務時間は週４０時間にも関わらず、あの会社は社員に週７０時間働かせている。
example_sentences.english: Work hours in line with the law is 40 hours a week, but that company makes its worker work 70 hours a week.

example_sentences.japanese: 外国人であろうと、日本にいる限り、日本の法律にそくした罰が与えられます。
example_sentences.english: No matter if you are a foreigner, as long as you are in Japan, you will be punished in line with Japanese law.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済状況にそくして課税を調整する必要がある。
example_sentences.english: There is a need to adjust taxes in line with the economic condition.

example_sentences.japanese: 役職に関わらず、ルールにそくして平等に罰せられるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of position, punishment ought to be given equally, in line with the rules.

example_sentences.japanese: 現実にそくして撮られたホラー系のドキュメンタリーほど怖いものはありません。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing scarier than horror documentaries that are shot based on true events.

example_sentences.japanese: ＭｃＲｏｎａｌｄ社とＳＦＣ社との抗争は現地の法律にそくして処理される。
example_sentences.english: The dispute between McRonald and SFC will be handled in line with local law.

example_sentences.japanese: 請願書は方針にそくして担当大臣に提出しなければならない。
example_sentences.english: The petition must be submitted to the minister in charge, in line with the policy.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い慣習に縛られずに，時代にそくした法律を制定すべきである。
example_sentences.english: The law that is in line with the time should be established without being bound to old-fashioned customs.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社方針にそくした費用補償は３０日以内にお支払いいたします。
example_sentences.english: We will pay cost compensation that is in line with company policy within 30 days.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の時代にそくして会社の方針を定めないと、社会から取り残されてしまうだろう。
example_sentences.english: If we don’t determine the company policies in line with the current generation, I dare say we’ll be left behind by society.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校の規則にそくして毎日同じ髪型、同じ制服で登校していた頃には戻りたくありません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t want to go back to the time where I had to go to school with the same uniform and the same hair every day, in line with the school regulations.

example_sentences.japanese: カーナビ：「ここで音声によるガイドは終了します。ここからも交通ルールにそくして運転をして下さい。」
example_sentences.english: Car navigation: ‘Voice guidance will now stop. Please continue to drive in accordance with the traffic rules.’

example_sentences.japanese: 事実にそくして報道するのがマスコミの仕事なのに、その会社が流す情報ときたらデタラメばっかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Despite delivering information in line with the truth being the job of mass media, that damned information that that company lets loose is nothing but garbage.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢物語を語るのは確かに楽しいけどさ、もっと現実にそくしてあらゆる事を考えないと生きていけないよ？
example_sentences.english: Speaking about wild dreams is indeed fun, but if you don’t think about everything more in line with reality, you won’t be able to live, you know?

example_sentences.japanese: この計画は現実に則していません。
example_sentences.english: This plan does not follow with reality. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: May not … but (at least), Even though not, Even if not
formation: Verb［ない］+ までも + PhraseNoun + ではない(1) + までも + Phrase(1) じゃない
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ までも + PhraseNoun + ではない(1) + までも + Phrase(1) じゃない
explanation: A grammar point highlighting that although (A) may not happen, (B). Although not even until the extent of (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: これは不可能ではないまでも、実行するのは困難である。
example_sentences.english: This may not be impossible, but carrying it out is hard.

example_sentences.japanese: この作品は名作だとは言えないまでも、なかなかいい作品だと思う。
example_sentences.english: This may not be a masterpiece, but I think that it is a pretty good piece.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯罪などは完全になくせないまでも、減らすように頑張るべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Even though it may not be possible to eliminate crime, we should try our best to reduce it.

example_sentences.japanese: プロ野球選手にはなれないまでも、プロ野球に関わる仕事をしているので満足している。
example_sentences.english: Even though I can't become a professional baseball player, I am satisfied because my job is related to professional baseball.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎週ではないまでも、娘に会えるだけ幸せだ。
example_sentences.english: I'm just happy to see my daughter, even if it's not every week.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きな仕事ができないから幸せじゃないまでも、生活費に困っていないから文句は言えない。
example_sentences.english: Even though I can't do what I love for work, I can't complain because I am not struggling with my bills.

example_sentences.japanese: クビにはしないまでも、確実にボーナスは減額するつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: Even though I may not fire you, I certainly plan on lowering your bonus at least.

example_sentences.japanese: リザ：「大谷は一番ハンサムといわないまでも、かなりカッコいい男だと思うよ。」
example_sentences.english: Riza: 'I won't say that Ooya is the most handsome, but I think he is quite a cool guy.'

example_sentences.japanese: 急速充電はバッテリーを直ちに駄目にしないまでも、性能をより速く低下させる。
example_sentences.english: Fast charging may not immediately damage the battery, but it will decrease its performance faster.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めてＪＬＰＴ Ｎ１を受験したが、合格できないまでも、せめて８０点は得点できたい。
example_sentences.english: I took the JLPT N1 exam for the first time, I may not pass, but at least I want to get 80 points.

example_sentences.japanese: この小説は「戦争と平和」と並んで傑作だとは言えないまでも、それなりに素晴らしい。
example_sentences.english: I cannot say that this novel is a masterpiece on par with 'War and Peace', but it is brilliant in its own way.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察：「犯人の名前は覚えていないまでも、顔や体の特徴だけでも覚えていませんか？」
example_sentences.english: Police: ‘Even though you may not remember the perpetrator’s name, you don’t at least remember their face or particular features, do you?’

example_sentences.japanese: エベレストの頂上までは辿り着けないまでも、８合目までは何としてでも登るつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: Even though I may not make it to the summit of Everest, I plan to climb at least as far as the 8th marker.

example_sentences.japanese: ファンタジー小説：「勇者えみりあを仲間にしないまでも、一度は会ってみたらどうですか？」
example_sentences.english: Fantasy novel: 'You may not make hero Emilia into an ally, but what about meeting her at least once?'

example_sentences.japanese: 母親からの賛成は得られないまでも、私の決定に対する反感を無くす事なら出来るでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I may not be able to get my mother’s approval, but I can probably get rid of her animosity regarding my decision.

example_sentences.japanese: 母親が息子に：「毎日とは言わないまでも、週に二日から三日くらいは家事をしてくれない？」
example_sentences.english: Mother to son: ‘I may not say every day, but could you at least do the chores from twice to three times a week for me?’

example_sentences.japanese: 女性同士の愚痴：「私たちにムダ毛を処理しろって言うなら、完璧は求めないまでも、男性にも少しはムダ毛を処理してほしいわよね。」
example_sentences.english: Girls’ complaints: ‘If they’re going to tell us to get rid of unwanted hair, even though I may not demand perfection, I want men to at least get rid of their unwanted hair a little.’

example_sentences.japanese: 人種や性別による差別を全て無くす事は出来ないまでも、この問題の深刻さを皆に認知してもらう事なら出来るに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Even though we may not be able to completely get rid of discrimination based on gender or race, there is no mistake that we can at least get everyone to acknowledge this problem’s gravity.

general_translation: Ignoring, Disregarding, Despite
formation: Noun + をよそにPhrase + の + をよそに
casual_structure: Noun + をよそにPhrase + の + をよそに
explanation: A formal construction used when doing (B), despite the situation of (A). Making (A) another place, (B). Often critical of (B).

example_sentences.japanese: メアリーと武は親の反対をよそに一緒になった。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring objections from their parents, Mary and Takeshi got together.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は親の心配をよそに、毎晩夜遅くまで友達と遊んでいる。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring his parent's worries, he hangs out with his friends every night until late at night.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長は社員の反対をよそに、仕事の効率を上げるために休憩所を撤去した。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring objections from his workers, the president got rid of the break room in order to increase efficiency.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は周囲の視線をよそに、コンビニの店員に暴言を吐き続けていた。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring the eyes of those around him, he continued to lash out on the convenience store worker.

example_sentences.japanese: 母の心配をよそに、彼は商船の船員になった。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring his mother's worries, he has become a merchant seaman.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は泣いている子猫をよそに、そのまま猫を置き去りにして行ったのです。
example_sentences.english: Disregarding that it was a crying kitten, he completely abandoned it and went like that.

example_sentences.japanese: ピーターは周りの忠告をよそに、ＭＭＯＲＰＧゲームばかりすることを存分に楽しんだ。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring the advice of those close to him, Peter does nothing but play MMORPG games to his heart's content.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちがその衝撃的な言葉の意味をまだ飲み込めてないのをよそに彼女は説明を続けた。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring that we still haven't digested the meaning of her shocking remark, she continued the explanation.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は両親の心配をよそに都内での一人暮らし生活を謳歌しているようだ。
example_sentences.english: Disregarding her parents’ concerns, she seems to be reveling in the fact that she is living alone in the city center.

example_sentences.japanese: 浪人生活で苦しんでいる僕をよそに、友達たちは毎日楽しそうな生活を送っています。
example_sentences.english: Despite that I am struggling with my jobless life, my friends are  leading a fun life every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 地域住民の反対の声をよそに、自治体が空港建設の計画を進めている。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring the voices of opposition, the local government carries forward the plan of airport construction.

example_sentences.japanese: 豪雨の天気予報をよそに傘を持たずに家を出た兄がずぶ濡れで帰ってきました。
example_sentences.english: Disregarding the forecast of heavy rain, my brother left the house without an umbrella and returned home soaking wet.

example_sentences.japanese: 幸原さんは仲間の学生や教師の期待をよそに、学校を中退し、気の向くままに旅に出た。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Yukihara, ignoring the expectations of his fellow students and teachers, dropped out of school and embarked on a journey at his fancy.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済的に苦しんでいる多くの国民をよそに贅沢三昧をしている政治家がいるなんて、許せません。
example_sentences.english: Disregarding the many citizens struggling economically, the fact that there are politicians that are living lavishly is something that I can’t let slide.

example_sentences.japanese: 周囲の視線をよそに駅の構内でイチャイチャしているカップルを見て良い気分になる人はいないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Disregarding being in the line of sight of those around them, I doubt there are any people that enjoy seeing couples make out within the train station premises.

example_sentences.japanese: 妊娠と出産で心身にダメージを負った私をよそに毎週同僚と飲みに行く夫をみて、長年の愛が一瞬で冷めてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring me, who has suffered mental and physical stress with pregnancy and birth, seeing my husband go off and drink with his colleagues every week has made my long love for him instantly wear off.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は両親の反対をよそに、彼と結婚することにした。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring my parents' objections, I decided to marry him. (Unnatural Japanese)

grammar_point: に限（かぎ）ったことではない
general_translation: Not limited to, Not restricted to, Not only
formation: Noun + に限（かぎ）ったことではない
casual_structure: Noun + に限（かぎ）ったことではない
polite_structure: Noun + に限（かぎ）ったことではありません
explanation: An expression used to say that something is not a thing that is restricted to (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 浮気をするのは男性にかぎったことではない。
example_sentences.english: Cheating is not something that is limited to men.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近の若者は挨拶ができないと言われているが、若者にかぎったことではない。
example_sentences.english: It is said that young people these days can't greet people, but it is not limited to young people.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日にかぎったことではないが、なんか仕事する気にならない。
example_sentences.english: It is not limited to today, but for some reason I don't feel like working.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法が難しいのは日本語にかぎったことではない。
example_sentences.english: Grammar being difficult is not something that is limited to Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震が頻繁に起きるのは日本にかぎったことではありません。
example_sentences.english: Frequently occuring earthquakes are not something that is limited to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 不幸が連続して起こるのは自分にかぎったことではないと信じている。
example_sentences.english: I believe that successive misfortunes are not something that is limited to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 子犬にメロメロになるのは女の子にかぎったことではない。父もメロメロだ。
example_sentences.english: Being infatuated with puppies is not something that is limited to girls. My father is infatuated too.

example_sentences.japanese: 松岡さんが宿題を忘れるのは今日にかぎったことではない。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Matsuoka forgetting to do his homework was not limited only to today.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットが上手くいかないのはあなたにかぎったことではなく、多くの人が悩むことです。
example_sentences.english: A diet not going well is something that is not restricted to you, but rather something that many people struggle with.

example_sentences.japanese: オレオレ詐欺で騙されるのはお年寄りにかぎったことではない。大人も騙される。
example_sentences.english: It is not only the elderly who are deceived by the 'ore ore' scam. Adults are too.

example_sentences.japanese: 言語を学ぶのは、子供にかぎったことではない。大人も言語が学べる。
example_sentences.english: Learning a language is not restricted to children. Adults are able to learn languages too.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯罪に遭うのは警戒を怠った人にかぎったことではなく、誰にでもあり得ることである。
example_sentences.english: Running into a criminal is not something that is limited to people that lack vigilance, but rather something that is possible to happen to anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 敬語は何も日本語にかぎったことではない。他言語にもあるか、または過去にあった。
example_sentences.english: Honorifics are not restricted to Japanese at all. Other languages also have it, or had it in the past.

example_sentences.japanese: アルコール依存症で家庭が壊れるのは我が家にかぎったことではなく、多くの家庭でそれが起こっています。
example_sentences.english: A fractured household due to alcohol addiction is not something that is limited to my home, but rather something that occurs in many households.

example_sentences.japanese: 科学者によると、少子化はなにも日本にかぎったことではないとのこと。すべての先進国における問題だそうだ。
example_sentences.english: According to scientists, the declining birthrate is not limited to Japan at all. It seems that it is a problem in all developed countries.

example_sentences.japanese: うつ病は人間にかぎったことではない。動物でもうつ病と診断されることがある。
example_sentences.english: Depression is not limited to humans. Even animals can be diagnosed with depression.

grammar_point: とは比（くら）べものにならない
general_translation: Nothing compared to, Cannot be compared to, Much more, Way better, Above comparison (beyond comparison), Far greater than
formation: Noun + とは比（くら）べものにならない
casual_structure: Noun + とは比（くら）べものにならない
polite_structure: Noun + とは比（くら）べものになりません
explanation: An emphatic expression used to make a comparison by saying that there isn't a comparable thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の絵画など須ノ宮さんのとはくらべものにならない。
example_sentences.english: My paintings are nothing compared to Sunomiya's.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ社の作る部品はいいが、Ｂ社の作る部品とはくらべものにならない。
example_sentences.english: Parts made by Company A are good, but they are not comparable to the parts made by Company B.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんのスパゲティーとはくらべものにならないが、ここのシェフが作るやつはなかなか美味しい。
example_sentences.english: The spaghetti prepared by the chef here is quite good, but it is nothing compared to the spaghetti my mother makes.

example_sentences.japanese: 岐阜は寒いが、北海道とはくらべものにはならない。
example_sentences.english: Gifu is cold, but it is nothing compared to Hokkaido.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の地震の多さはオーストラリアとはくらべものにならない。
example_sentences.english: The amount of Japan’s earthquakes is beyond comparison to Australia.

example_sentences.japanese: 光の速さでも、この宇宙の大きさとはくらべものにならない。
example_sentences.english: Even the speed of light is nothing when compared to the size of the universe.

example_sentences.japanese: この寿司は悪くはないが良質の寿司とはくらべものにならない。
example_sentences.english: This sushi is not bad, but it is nothing compared to good quality sushi.

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道は寒いといえどもシベリアとはくらべものにならないと思う。
example_sentences.english: Even though Hokkaido is cold, I think it is nothing when compared to Siberia.

example_sentences.japanese: 私もコスメが好きですが、コスメマニアの橋本さんとはくらべものになりません。
example_sentences.english: I like cosmetics, but it’s nothing compared to Hashimoto-san, the cosmetic freak.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホのパフォーマンスは当時とはくらべものにならないほど上がってます。
example_sentences.english: The performance of smartphones has improved to a degree that is beyond comparison to back then.

example_sentences.japanese: 確かにお金に余裕はある方だが、富豪たちとはくらべものにならない。
example_sentences.english: While it is true that I am on the having-excess-money side of things, it’s nothing compared to the wealthy.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパー火山の噴火の被害は他の火山とはくらべものにならないとされます。
example_sentences.english: It is considered that the damage from a supervolcano eruption is beyond comparison to other volcanoes.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は少し贅沢をしましたが、浪費癖のある祖母とはくらべものになりません。
example_sentences.english: I was a bit extravagant today, but it’s nothing compared to my grandma who has wasteful habits.

example_sentences.japanese: 上手にピアノを弾くことができたが、プロの演奏を聴いてプロとはくらべものにならないと思い知った。
example_sentences.english: I can play the piano well, but after hearing a pro play, I realized that I am nothing compared to them.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さん：「もちろんこのウイスキーも美味しいけど、やっぱりあの高級なやつとはくらべものにならないな〜。」
example_sentences.english: Father: ‘Of course, this whiskey is tasty, but yeah, it’s nothing compared to that high-class one.’

example_sentences.japanese: 自分で作るご飯もいいけど、誰かに作ってもらうご飯とはくらべものになりません。
example_sentences.english: Making your own food is good, but it doesn’t compare to the food that you have someone make for you.

general_translation: Without regard for, Ignoring, Without concern for
formation: Noun + を顧（かえり）みずNoun + も顧（かえり）みず
casual_structure: Noun + を顧（かえり）みずNoun + も顧（かえり）みず
explanation: A stiff expression used to describe acting without regard for the risks or negative consequences.

example_sentences.japanese: 命の危険をかえりみず高所で作業を続けた建設作業員たちの努力は称賛されるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: The efforts of the construction workers who continued working at high altitudes without regard for the danger to their lives should be praised.

example_sentences.japanese: 徹夜した後の眠さをかえりみず友人の相談に乗った。
example_sentences.english: Without regard for my sleepiness after pulling an all-nighter, I listened to my friend's problems.

example_sentences.japanese: お隣さんは、台風をかえりみず車の掃除をしている。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring the typhoon, my neighbor is cleaning their car.

example_sentences.japanese: 環境への影響をかえりみず新たな工場を次々と建てていくのはよくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not good to build new factories one after another without concern for the environmental impact.

example_sentences.japanese: 怖さをかえりみず、闘牛と一騎打ちをしたあの経験は今でも鮮明に覚えている。
example_sentences.english: I still vividly remember that experience of fighting a bull one-on-one without regard for the fear.

example_sentences.japanese: 月曜日から５連勤なのをかえりみず、日曜の朝方５時まで飲むなんて、どうかしていると思う。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring the fact that you have to work five days straight from Monday, then drinking until 5 AM on Sunday morning is crazy, I think.

example_sentences.japanese: 義兄が警官なのをかえりみず旦那は薬物を止めようとしません。
example_sentences.english: Without regard for the fact that his brother-in-law is a police officer, my husband won't try to stop using drugs.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は世間の批判をかえりみず、自分の信念を貫いた。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring public criticism, he stuck to his beliefs.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は、家族の心配をかえりみず海外赴任を決意したかと思ったら、たったの２日で日本に帰ってきた。
example_sentences.english: Just when I thought my daughter had decided to take an overseas assignment without concern for the family's concerns, she returned to Japan in just two days.

example_sentences.japanese: 個人的利益をかえりみず、社会全体のために行動したあの人は日本の歴史に名を刻むだろう。
example_sentences.english: That person who acted for the sake of society as a whole, without regard for personal gain, will surely carve their name into Japanese history.

example_sentences.japanese: 社会的立場をかえりみず、真実を公表した記者の勇気は非常に価値がある。
example_sentences.english: The courage of the reporter who published the truth, without concern for their social standing, is extremely valuable.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は自分がメタボと診断されたのをかえりみず、毎日揚げ物やスイーツなどの高カロリーな食事をしている。
example_sentences.english: Ignoring the fact that he was diagnosed with 'metabolic syndrome', he eats high-calorie meals like fried foods and sweets every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は危険を顧みず、見知らぬ人を助けた。
example_sentences.english: He helped a stranger, regardless of the danger.

example_sentences.japanese: 消防隊員は自らの犠牲を顧みず、炎の中へ飛び込んでいった。
example_sentences.english: The firefighters jumped into the flames, regardless of their own sacrifice.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は家族の反対を顧みず、ホームレスの男性と結婚をした。
example_sentences.english: My older sister married a homeless man, despite her family's opposition.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は周りの目を気にしないで自由に生きている。
example_sentences.english: She lives freely without worrying about the opinions of those around her.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は世間の批判も顧みずその計画を実行した。
example_sentences.english: She executed that plan, despite even public criticism.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は昨日の失言を省みて反省した。
example_sentences.english: I reflected on my slip of the tongue yesterday and felt regret.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生を顧みると、多くの人に支えられてきたと感じる。
example_sentences.english: When I look back on my life, I feel that I have been supported by many people.

general_translation: Unbecoming of, Unworthy of, Not proper for, Should not, Must not, Cannot
formation: Noun (A) + にある(1) + まじき + Noun (B)許すまじき + Noun(1)としてある
casual_structure: Noun (A) + にある(1) + まじき + Noun (B)許すまじき + Noun(1)としてある
explanation: A formal, old-fashioned expression, showing that something is unbecoming of (A), or must not (A). (A) is judged as improper, so (B).

example_sentences.japanese: リヒャルトは王としてあるまじき汚名を着せられ、やがて廃位された。
example_sentences.english: Richard was tarred with the stigma unbecoming of the position of the king and was eventually dethroned.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒に手を挙げることは先生にあるまじき行為だ。
example_sentences.english: Raising your hand to a student is unbecoming of a teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は飲酒運転という警察官にあるまじき行動をし、クビになった。
example_sentences.english: He was fired for drunk driving, an unbecoming behavior for a police officer.

example_sentences.japanese: 先日、斉藤首相は総理としてあるまじき発言をし、SNSで炎上している。
example_sentences.english: Recently, Prime Minister Saito has been under fire on social media for making comments that are unbecoming of a prime minister.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は医師としてあるまじきミスをしてしまい、医師免許を剥奪された。
example_sentences.english: He made a mistake that was unbecoming of a physician and was stripped of his medical license.

example_sentences.japanese: 煽り運転のようなゆるすまじき行為をした場合、免許は取り消しになります。
example_sentences.english: If you commit unforgivable acts such as tailgating, your license will be revoked.

example_sentences.japanese: 言うまでもないが、公金横領など政治家としてあるまじき行為だ。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying, but something like misappropriation of public funds is an act unbecoming of a statesman.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻を下げるような発言をするなんて、夫にあるまじき行為だ。
example_sentences.english: Something like saying remarks that bring down his wife, it is behavior that is unbecoming of a husband.

example_sentences.japanese: 戦場から離脱することは武士にあるまじき行為と咎められ、罰せられた。
example_sentences.english: Fleeing from the battlefield was condemned as unbecoming of a warrior and punished.

example_sentences.japanese: ララティーナは貴族にあるまじき態度で、甘やかされた子供のようなふるまいをした。
example_sentences.english: Lalatina behaved in a manner unbecoming of a noble, like a spoiled child.

example_sentences.japanese: ニュースの主題：「看護師としてあるまじき行動」高齢患者から５００万円詐取
example_sentences.english: News title: 'Behavior unbecoming of a nurse': Fraud of 5000000 yen from an elderly patient

example_sentences.japanese: 医療費を多く請求する為に必要ではない治療を行うなんて医師にあるまじき行為です。
example_sentences.english: Something like administering unnecessary treatments in order to raise the medical costs, it is behavior that is not proper for a doctor.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は生徒と関係を持つという先生としてあるまじき事をしたために懲戒処分となった。
example_sentences.english: Due to that she had relations with a student that was unbecoming of a teacher, she was subjected to judicial punishment.

example_sentences.japanese: 思い通りにいかない度に園児に対して暴力を振るうなんて、保育士としてゆるすまじき行為です。（許す）
example_sentences.english: Something like getting abusive with kindergarteners every time something does not go right, it is behavior that must not be forgiven as a childcare worker.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲み歩いたせいで次の日の会社に遅刻するなんて、社会人としてあるまじき行動だ。
example_sentences.english: To think that he would be late to work the next day due to going bar hopping, it is behavior that is unbecoming of a functioning member of society.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「深く考えず勝手に好きなことをいうのは普通の人にとっては許せるかもしれないが、外交官にとってはゆるすまじき悪行だったのだ。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Saying whatever one wants, without thinking deeply might be allowed for an ordinary person, but for a diplomat, it is a misdeed that cannot be forgiven.'

general_translation: Utmost, Height of, Extreme, Heartiest, Such a, Very, really, Completely, Deeply
formation: Noun + の + 至（いた）り + だ
casual_structure: Noun + の + 至（いた）り + だ
polite_structure: Noun + の + 至（いた）り + です
explanation: A formal grammar point, used to express the utmost height of (A). The climax of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 演説：「特別賞を受賞することになり、光栄のいたりです。」
example_sentences.english: Speech: 'Receiving the special reward is an extreme honor.'

example_sentences.japanese: ここ４年間色々と教えていただき、恐縮のいたりです。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely grateful for the many things you have taught me over the last four years.

example_sentences.japanese: このような大切な式に、こんな私を招待してくださったことは光栄のいたりです。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely honored that you invited me to such an important ceremony.

example_sentences.japanese: 色々とアドバイスをしていただいて、感謝のいたりです。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely grateful for all the advice you have given me.

example_sentences.japanese: 「このような小さな誤りに気づくのに数日もかかるとは、赤面のいたりです。」
example_sentences.english: 'I am extremely ashamed that it took a few days to notice such a simple mistake.'

example_sentences.japanese: 演説：「たいそうな品をいただき、恐縮のいたりです。」
example_sentences.english: Speech: 'We are extremely grateful for your generous gift.'

example_sentences.japanese: インタビュー：「ファンや映画評論家の皆さまから肯定的なレビューをいただき、感激のいたりです」
example_sentences.english: Interview: 'We are extremely moved by the positive reviews we have received from fans and film critics.'

example_sentences.japanese: 伝記：「若気のいたりで、給料の良い仕事を辞めて独立開業した。」
example_sentences.english: Biography: 'Due to an extreme moment of youthful indiscretion, I had quit a well-paid job and started an independent business.'

example_sentences.japanese: 演説：「講演者として本会議に招待してくださったことは、光栄のいたりでございます。」
example_sentences.english: Speech: 'As a speaker, being invited to this conference is an extreme honor.'

example_sentences.japanese: 演説、他の企業の代表者：「この機会に、御社の新支社が設けられたことは、ご同慶のいたりに存じます。」
example_sentences.english: Speech, the representative of another company: 'On this occasion, I would like to offer my heartiest congratulations on establishing your company's new branch.'

example_sentences.japanese: こんな賞を私がいただけるなんて、光栄のいたりでございます。
example_sentences.english: That I would receive a prize such as this is the utmost of honors.

example_sentences.japanese: まさかこんな初歩的なミスを犯してしまうとは…恐縮のいたりです。
example_sentences.english: To think that I would make such a rudimentary mistake. You have my utmost apologies.

example_sentences.japanese: ファン：「あなたのファンになって１０年目です。お会い出来るなんて感激のいたりです。」
example_sentences.english: Fan: ‘This is my 10th year of being your fan. I am deeply grateful for being able to meet.’

example_sentences.japanese: 歌手：「君みたいな素敵な人に応援して頂けて、こちらこそ感謝のいたりだよ。これからもよろしくね。」
example_sentences.english: Singer: ‘Having a person as wonderful as you cheering me on, I should be the one to say that I am deeply grateful. Please continue to cheer for me!’

example_sentences.japanese: 若気のいたりで自分の心と体を大切に出来なかった日もあるが、別に後悔はしていない。
example_sentences.english: In the height of my youth there were days that I didn’t take care of my mind or my body, but I don’t really regret it.

example_sentences.japanese: 部下が上司に：「こんな私みたいな人の事を褒めて頂き、恐縮のいたりです。これからも精進して参ります。」
example_sentences.english: Subordinate to their boss: ‘You have my utmost gratefulness for praising a person such as me. I will continue to give it my all from now on.’

example_sentences.japanese: 上司が部下に：「昨日は合コンでお会いしてしまうとは赤面のいたりだよ。どうかこの事は二人だけの秘密に…。」
example_sentences.english: Boss to their subordinate: ‘It was the height of embarrassment seeing you yesterday at the mixer. If you could somehow keep this between just you and I…’

example_sentences.japanese: 大学生の頃は若気のいたりでたくさん悪いことをしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I did a lot of bad things when I was in college, due to an extreme moment of youthful indiscretion.

general_translation: Lives up to, Truly to …’s name, Worthy of, Not dishonor, Not putting to shame, Measure to
formation: Noun + に恥（は）じないNoun + に恥（は）じない + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + に恥（は）じないNoun + に恥（は）じない + Noun
polite_structure: Noun + に恥（は）じませんNoun + に恥（は）じません + Noun
explanation: A grammar point highlighting that something lives up to (A). (B) which does not dishonor (A).

example_sentences.japanese: サハラ砂漠の名にはじない天候だ。
example_sentences.english: It is a weather that lives up to the name of the Sahara desert.

example_sentences.japanese: あの大学のバスケチームは日本一という名にはじない強さだ。
example_sentences.english: That university's basketball team's strength lives up to its name of being the best in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本代表の名にはじないよう、ベストを尽くします。
example_sentences.english: I will do my best to live up to the name of a representative of Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の名にはじないよう、精一杯頑張ります。
example_sentences.english: I will do my best to live up to the name of the company.

example_sentences.japanese: 店のウェブサイト：「当店は８０年培った信頼と伝統にはじないサービスをご提供致します。」
example_sentences.english: Shop's website: 'Our shop provides services that live up to the trust and the tradition we have built over 80 years .'

example_sentences.japanese: 昇格する演説：「ブランド名にはじないよう、精一杯努めさせていただきます。」
example_sentences.english: Being promoted speech: 'I will work as hard as I can to live up to the brand's name.'

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルのウェブサイト：「五つ星ホテルの名にはじないサービスをお客様に提供しております。」
example_sentences.english: Hotel's website: 'We provide a service for our guests that lives up to the name of a five star hotel.'

example_sentences.japanese: 受賞の演説：「この賞にはじないよう、これからも最善を尽くすつもりです。」
example_sentences.english: Receiving award speech: 'I intend to continue doing my best to live up to this award.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「このラーメンはさすが沖縄最高のラーメンという名にはじない味だ！」
example_sentences.english: 'As expected, the taste of this ramen lives up to being named the best ramen in Okinawa.'

example_sentences.japanese: 恩師にはじないように立派に活躍したいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: In order to not put shame on my mentor, I want to excel in my performance.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京の名にはじないオリンピックが出来たのかと聞かれれば、首を傾げてしまう。
example_sentences.english: If I was asked whether Tokyo was able to put on an Olympics that was worthy of its name, I’d unfortunately have second thoughts.

example_sentences.japanese: 歌舞伎役者：「父の名にはじないよう精一杯頑張っていく所存ですので、宜しくお願いします。」
example_sentences.english: Kabuki performer: ‘Since I intend to live up to my father’s name and give it my all, I beg your cooperation.’

example_sentences.japanese: 古くからの伝統にはじないよう、このレストランでは最高の料理を提供しております。
example_sentences.english: In a way that is worthy of the old traditions dating back into the past, this restaurant serves up the best food.

example_sentences.japanese: 神にはじないように生きていきたいが、人間とは誰もが一度や二度、間違いを犯すものである。
example_sentences.english: I want to live in a way that is worthy of God, but humans are things that make one or two mistakes.

example_sentences.japanese: 水泳部の部長の独り言：「本当は後輩にはじないような記録を出したかったんだけど…。」
example_sentences.english: The mumblings of the swimming club manager: ‘I really wanted to deliver a record that would not put shame to my juniors but...’

example_sentences.japanese: 他人の期待を裏切ってしまうのはしょうがないけれど、せめて自分にはじない生き方をしたいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: It can’t be helped if I betray the expectations of others, but I at least want to live in a way that is true to myself.

general_translation: Ended up not, Did not (in the end), Never did
formation: Verb［ない］+ ず + じまい
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ず + じまい
explanation: A strong construction indicating regret that something unfortunately did not happen. (A) never came about.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「結局、やらずじまいで新学期になっちゃったよ。」Ｂ：「なにをやらなかったの？」Ａ：「夏休みの宿題…」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I ended up not doing it, and the new school term started.'B: 'What did you not do?'A: 'The summer homework...'

example_sentences.japanese: マウンテンバイクを買ったが、使わずじまいで売ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I bought a mountain bike, but I ended up selling it without using it.

example_sentences.japanese: コンサートのチケットを買ったが、色々とやることがあって行かずじまいだった。
example_sentences.english: I bought the ticket to the concert, but I had a lot on my plate so I ended up not going.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で使うために電子辞書を持っていったが、持ち運ぶのが面倒だったから結局使わずじまいだった。
example_sentences.english: I brought my electronic dictionary to Japan to use it there, but I ended up not using it because it was a pain to carry it.

example_sentences.japanese: 「宇崎さんと映画館に行こうと思っていたけど、仕事から手が離せなくて結局いけずじまいだった。」
example_sentences.english: 'I planned to go to the cinema with Uzaki, but I couldn't get away from work, so I ended up not going.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「事故の原因について調べようとしたが、ついにわからずじまいだった。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'I tried to investigate the cause of the accident, but I ended up not discovering anything.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「最新の愛Ｐｈｏｎｅを買おうとストアに１０時間並んだのに、自分の番が来る頃には欲しい色がもう売り切れていて結局かえずじまいだった。」
example_sentences.english: 'I stood for 10 hours in line to buy the new 愛Phone, but when my turn came, it turned out that the color I wanted had already sold out, so I ended up not buying it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「日本語の教科書をたくさん買ったけど、結局つかわずじまいだった。」
example_sentences.english: 'I bought lots of Japanese textbooks, but I ended up not using them.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「神社に初詣に行きたかったのですが、天気が悪くていかずじまいでした。」
example_sentences.english: 'I wanted to go for the first shrine visit of the new year, but the weather was bad and I ended up not going.'

example_sentences.japanese: 伝えたかったことをつたえずじまいで元カノと別れたことを後悔しています。
example_sentences.english: I ended up not conveying what I wanted to, and regret that I broke up with my ex girlfriend.

example_sentences.japanese: 戦争に行ってあえずじまいになってしまった夫婦の話を聞き、涙が止まりませんでした。
example_sentences.english: After hearing the story of going to war and the married couple ending up never meeting again, my tears wouldn’t stop.

example_sentences.japanese: 忙しい事を理由に友達からの誘いを断り続けていたら、結局あそべずじまいになってしまった。
example_sentences.english: When I continued to decline my friend’s invitations with the reason of being busy, we never did end up hanging out.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年こそ彼氏とバレンタインデーを過ごす計画だったのに、結局彼氏はつくれずじまい、友達と過ごす事になった。
example_sentences.english: Despite planning to spend time with my boyfriend this valentines day, in the end he never did plan anything, and hung out with his friends.

example_sentences.japanese: 突然転校してしまい仲直りできずじまいだった旧友と５年ぶりに再会し、仲直りをすることが出来ました。
example_sentences.english: After suddenly transferring schools without ending up making amends with my old friend, we saw each other for the first time in 5 years and were able to make up.

example_sentences.japanese: リストラされてしまったせいで家賃も水道代も電気代もはらえずじまいなので、直にホームレスになるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Since I ended up not being able to pay my electricity, rent, or water bills due to being downsized, I’m probably on the verge of becoming homeless.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度こそはダイエットをするって決めたのに、今日もうんどうせずじまいで一日が終わってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Despite deciding to really get fit this time, even today ended up with me not doing any exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きな子に告白せずじまいで、高校を卒業してしまった。
example_sentences.english: I ended up graduating highschool without confessing my feelings to the girl I liked.

general_translation: If you ask, In … opinion, According to
formation: Noun + に言（い）わせれば(1)(1) に言（い）わせると、に言（い）わせたら
casual_structure: Noun + に言（い）わせれば(1)(1) に言（い）わせると、に言（い）わせたら
explanation: A hypothetical phrase, indicating that in the opinion of (A), (B). If (A) were to be asked, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 私にいわせればあなたが買ったスマホは不良品だよ。もう３回も壊れたんだから！
example_sentences.english: If you ask me, the smartphone you bought is a defective product. It has fallen apart 3 times already!

example_sentences.japanese: 専門家にいわせれば、もっと早い対応をするべきだったそうです。
example_sentences.english: According to a specialist, we should have dealt with it earlier.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にいわせれば５キロを２５分で走るのは簡単だ。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me, running 5km in 25 minutes is easy.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はあのパーソナルトレーナーは厳しすぎると思ったが、彼にいわせれば優しすぎるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I thought that that personal trainer was too strict, but according to him, he is apparently too nice.

example_sentences.japanese: 私からいわせれば、なんでそんなことして許されると思ったのかがわからない。
example_sentences.english: In my opinion, I don't know why they thought they would be forgiven after doing such a thing.

example_sentences.japanese: ドイツ側にいわせればオーストラリア企業は初めは経済協力に反対していたという。
example_sentences.english: According to the German side, the Australian companies were opposed to cooperation from the beginning.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の観点からすれば、結果は失敗とみなされるかもしれないが、少なくとも私にいわせれば、完全な失敗というわけではない。
example_sentences.english: From the company's point of view, the results might be considered a failure, but it does not mean it was a complete failure, at least if you ask me.

example_sentences.japanese: 君にとっては面白いのだろうが、私にいわせれば、ただの無礼にしかすぎない。
example_sentences.english: For you it might be funny, but if you ask me, it is just rude.

example_sentences.japanese: 武田さんにいわせれば、最近の若者はまったくお年寄りを敬わないとのこと。
example_sentences.english: According to Mr. Takeda, youth these days do not respect their elders at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の冷蔵庫が壊れた：「新しい冷蔵庫を買うことができるかもしれないが、俺にいわせれば、修理したほうがいいと思う。」
example_sentences.english: A friend's refrigerator broke: 'You could buy a new refrigerator, but if you ask me, I think it's better to fix it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 専業主婦になった母にいわせれば、自分で稼げないことは結構なストレスになるのだとか。
example_sentences.english: If you ask my mom, who became a housewife, she says stuff like that not earning her own money is stressful.

example_sentences.japanese: 大学院まで進学した父にいわせると、大学に進学するに越した事はないそうです。
