example_sentences.english: If you ask my dad, who went through graduate school, nothing compares to getting into university.

example_sentences.japanese: 女性関係で散々痛い目に遭ってきた彼にいわせれば、付き合う事に利点なんて無いとのこと。
example_sentences.english: If you ask him, who’s had various unfortunate experiences with relationships with women, there is no benefit at all with relationships.

example_sentences.japanese: ホテルの受付係にいわせると、私たちがこの宿を予約出来たのは本当にラッキーだったようだ。
example_sentences.english: According to the receptionist, it seems that we were really lucky to get a reservation at this hotel.

example_sentences.japanese: お年寄り：「私にいわせれば、５０歳なんてまだまだ赤ちゃんみたいなものよ。挑戦する事を恐れないでね。」
example_sentences.english: Elderly person: ‘In my opinion, being 50 years old is still like being a baby. Don’t be afraid to take on challenges.’

example_sentences.japanese: 最近の若者はファストファッションを好みますが、母にいわせるとそれらのファッションは安っぽく見えるそうです。
example_sentences.english: Young people prefer fast fashion, but if you ask my mom, it seems that she thinks it looks cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者である私にいわせれば、タバコも酒も薬物もただ単に体に害を及ぼすものであって、かっこよくとも何ともない。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me as a doctor, tobacco and alcohol and drugs are nothing more than things that will cause your body harm, and aren’t even cool.

general_translation: Cannot tell, describe, say, express or find words for how, Words cannot express, Too … for words, Extremely
formation: More common patterns:Noun + たら(1) + ありゃしない(2)［い］Adjective［さ］(3) + たら(1) + ありゃしない(2)Less common patterns:Verb + たら(1) + ありゃしない(2)［な］Adjective + たら(1) + ありゃしない(2)(1) といったら(2) ありはしない(3)［い］Adjective
casual_structure: More common patterns:Noun + たら(1) + ありゃしない(2)［い］Adjective［さ］(3) + たら(1) + ありゃしない(2)Less common patterns:Verb + たら(1) + ありゃしない(2)［な］Adjective + たら(1) + ありゃしない(2)(1) といったら(2) ありはしない(3)［い］Adjective
explanation: A very casual, hypothetical structure, emphasizing that (A) cannot be described. When it's (A), there's nothing to be said. Only used negatively.

example_sentences.japanese: 「凹凸の多い地形は走りにくいといったらありはしない。」
example_sentences.english: 'I cannot tell you how difficult it is to run on uneven terrain.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「犬を飼ったのに世話をしないなんて、無責任ったらありゃしない。」
example_sentences.english: 'I cannot tell you how irresponsible it is to keep a dog but not take care of it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 上司：「君は毎日毎日、会社に遅刻して来て。見苦しいったらありゃしないぞ。」
example_sentences.english: Boss: 'You are late for work every single day. I can't tell you how unseemly it is!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「さだおさんの企業が倒産してからの元従業員の連中の態度といったらありゃしない。」
example_sentences.english: 'I cannot express the attitude of Sadao's former employees after his company went bankrupt.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「昨晩遅くに帰宅したルームメイトに起こされた。腹がたつったらありゃしない。」
example_sentences.english: 'I was awoken by my roommate who returned home late last night. I can't tell you how angry I am.'

example_sentences.japanese: 厳しいおばあさん：「大人のくせにそんな態度！全くみっともないったらありゃしないのよ。」
example_sentences.english: Strict grandmother: 'You are an adult, and you are acting like that. I can't express how disgraceful it is!'

general_translation: Due to, Since, On account of, Because
formation: Verb + こととてVerb［ない］+ ぬ(1) + こととてNoun + の + こととて(1) ない
casual_structure: Verb + こととてVerb［ない］+ ぬ(1) + こととてNoun + の + こととて(1) ない
explanation: A formal, old-fashioned, particle-based expression, meaning on account of (A), (B). Even when (A)'s the thing, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 時代劇、Ａ：「あなたのお父さんによろしくお伝えください。」Ｂ：「お父さんは遥か昔に亡くなりました。」Ａ：「そうでしたか。知らぬこととて、失礼をお許しください。」
example_sentences.english: A period drama, A: 'Please, send my greetings to your father.'B: 'My father passed away long ago.'A: 'Is that so? Please, forgive my rudeness due to my lack of knowledge.'

example_sentences.japanese: あの事件は２０年前に起こったこととて、世間からは忘れられているだろう。
example_sentences.english: Due to that incident happening 20 years ago, it probably has been forgotten by the public.

example_sentences.japanese: 商品についてあまり知らぬこととて、お客様の信頼を失ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Due to me lacking knowledge about the product, I unfortunately lost credibility.

example_sentences.japanese: 新人のこととて、まだ分からないことがたくさんありますが、これからよろしくお願いいたします。
example_sentences.english: Since I am still new, there are many things I don't know, but please take good care of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 突然のこととて、前の車を避けきれませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Due to it being a sudden event, I was not able to avoid the car in front of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い手紙：「取り込み中のこととてご迷惑をおかけしましたがなにとぞご寛容のほどお願い申し上げます。」
example_sentences.english: Old letter: 'I have caused you a lot of trouble due to being busy, but I would kindly ask for your understanding.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「仕事になれぬこととて間違いをしてしまいました。申し訳ございません。」
example_sentences.english: 'I made a mistake due to not being accustomed to the work. For that I am awfully sorry.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「田舎のこととて年齢や学年に関係なく生徒が勉強する教室が１教室だけしかなかった。」
example_sentences.english: Since it was the countryside, there was only one classroom where school children studied, regardless of their age or grade.

example_sentences.japanese: 「子供がやったこととて、親としてお詫び申し上げます。」
example_sentences.english: 'Since my child did it, I would like to apologize as their parent.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「春の最中のこととて、早咲きの花のかすかな香りが漂っていた、肌に心地よいそよ風が吹いた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Since it was mid-spring, the pleasant soft wind that carried a faint aroma of flowers blew.'

example_sentences.japanese: 耳が生まれつき悪いこととて、さっきの話がほとんど聞き取れなかったのです…。
example_sentences.english: On account of my ears being bad since birth, I couldn’t catch most of the conversation from a moment ago...

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒：「集会で話すのは初めてのこととて、声が震えるほどに緊張をしております。」
example_sentences.english: Student: ‘Due to it being my first time speaking at an assembly, I am so nervous that my voice is shaking.’

example_sentences.japanese: 電話対応をする従業員：「すみませんが、その件を扱う担当者が席を外しているとのこととて、後で掛け直させて下さい。」
example_sentences.english: Staff member answering a phone call: ‘I do apologize, but on account of the person responsible for handling that case being away, please allow me to call you back later.’

example_sentences.japanese: 刑事：「お前はあの時、何をしていたんだ？」ある男：「そんなの昔のこととて、覚えているわけがないだろ。」
example_sentences.english: Detective: ‘What were you doing at that time? A certain man: ‘On account of that being in the past, there’s no way I remember it, right?’

example_sentences.japanese: 店員に相談をする：「彼氏が出来たのは初めてのこととて、何をプレゼントするべきなのか分からないんです…。」
example_sentences.english: Discussing with a staff member: ‘Due to it being my first time getting a boyfriend, I have no idea what I ought to get as a present.’

example_sentences.japanese: プロポーズされた女性：「突然のこととて、まだ考えが整理出来ていないのです。お返事まで時間を下さい。」
example_sentences.english: A woman that has been proposed to: ‘On account of the suddenness, I haven’t been able to get my thoughts together. Please give me some time until I answer.’

example_sentences.japanese: 上司が後輩のミスを庇う：「なにせ新人なもので…慣れないこととてミスをしてしまったようです。私からも謝らせて下さい。」
example_sentences.english: A boss covering for their junior’s mistake: ‘In any case it’s a newbie thing… It seems like the error is on account of them not being used to it. Please let me apologize on my behalf as well.’

general_translation: Completely, Entirely, All in, Nothing but, A real streak of, Without exception, Jet
formation: Noun + ずくめNoun (A) + ずくめ + の + Noun (B)
casual_structure: Noun + ずくめNoun (A) + ずくめ + の + Noun (B)
explanation: A suffix highlighting that something is completely (A), or nothing but (A). Exhaustively (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞の見出し：「６月猛暑記録ずくめ」
example_sentences.english: Newspaper headline: 'June - A Heatwave full of Temperature Records'

example_sentences.japanese: 今月も仕事ずくめになりそうだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like I'm going to be doing nothing but work again this month.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は嫌なことずくめで全然楽しくない。
example_sentences.english: I'm not having the best time right now, because nothing but bad things are happening.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は黒ずくめの男たちに誘拐された。
example_sentences.english: He was kidnapped by men covered in black.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察への電話：「もしもし、家の前に黒ずくめの車が何台も止まっているんで今から言う住所まできてもらってもいいですか。」
example_sentences.english: Calling the cops: Hello, there are several jet black cars parked in front of my house, so could you please come to the address I'm about to tell you?

example_sentences.japanese: 規制は必要であるが規則ずくめで窒息しそうな社会は強圧的ではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: Regulations are needed, but isn't a society that is about to suffocate with nothing but restrictions overbearing ?

example_sentences.japanese: ２０２０年は異例ずくめの大変な年でしたが何とか乗り切りました。
example_sentences.english: 2020 was a very challenging year full of irregularities, but we somehow got through it.

example_sentences.japanese: ツイッターの投稿：「朝から晩まで、ごちそうずくめで結婚を祝う。」
example_sentences.english: Twitter post: 'We are celebrating the marriage with nothing but delicacies from morning till night.'

example_sentences.japanese: 黒ずくめのスーツに身を包んだ男はベンチに座り、逆さに持った新聞を読むふりをしていた。
example_sentences.english: A man dressed in a completely black suit was sitting on a bench and pretending to read a newspaper that was upside down.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は妹が生まれたし大学に受かったし朝からいいことずくめで、万々歳だ。
example_sentences.english: Today calls for celebration, because nothing but good things have been happening since the morning, like my younger sister being born, and my acceptance to university.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供：「野菜ずくめのこの料理なんて美味しくなさそうで食べたくないよ！」
example_sentences.english: Child: ‘This food is nothing but vegetables and doesn’t seem tasty so I don’t wanna eat it!’

example_sentences.japanese: 独り言：「最近は良い事ずくめだから、そろそろ悪い事が起こりそう…。」
example_sentences.english: Mumblings: ‘It’s been nothing but good things recently, so it seems like something bad is about to happen…’

example_sentences.japanese: 新記録ずくめの大会を会場で観戦する事が出来て、とても嬉しいです。
example_sentences.english: Since I was able to spectate an event that had a real streak of new records, I am really thrilled!

example_sentences.japanese: 映画のナレーター：「彼女の幸せずくめの毎日はここで終わりを告げました…。」
example_sentences.english: Movie narrator: ‘It announced to her that her days of nothing but happiness were over.’

example_sentences.japanese: 父は働きずくめの今の生活に不満は無いと言っていたが、絶対に少しはあるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: Although dad was saying that he has no grievances with his current lifestyle of nothing but work, he absolutely has at least some.’

example_sentences.japanese: 同僚の高橋さんは全身ブランドずくめですが、一体そんなお金はどこから湧いているのでしょう…。
example_sentences.english: My colleague Takahashi-san is covered from head to toe in branded clothes without exception, but where the heck does the money sprout up from for that…’

example_sentences.japanese: 会社員：「残業ずくめの毎日なんて、もう沢山だ！こんな会社さっさと辞めないと、絶対に精神が病んでしまう…！」
example_sentences.english: Company employee: ‘Something like having nothing but overtime work every day, I am at my wits end! If I don’t quit this company straight away my mental health is going to deteriorate...!’

example_sentences.japanese: 国づくしの偉い人が集まった。
example_sentences.english: Great people from all sorts of countries gathered.

grammar_point: には及（およ）ばない ②
general_translation: To be no match (for), To not compare (with), To fall short (of), To not reach, Cannot win with, To be out of reach (for), To not be on par (with)
formation: Noun + には(1) + 及（およ）ばないSet expression:Noun + の足元（あしもと）にも及（およ）ばない(1) に
casual_structure: Noun + には(1) + 及（およ）ばないSet expression:Noun + の足元（あしもと）にも及（およ）ばない(1) に
polite_structure: Noun + には(1) + 及（およ）びませんSet expression:Noun + の足元（あしもと）にも及（およ）びません(1) に
explanation: A phrase expressing that something falls short of (A), or is no match for it. To not go as far as (A). It does not reach (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 言うまでもなく真作にはおよばないでしょうが、いい贋作です。
example_sentences.english: Needless to say, it is no match for the original. Even still, it is a good forgery.

example_sentences.japanese: この海は沖縄の海にはおよばないが、結構綺麗だ。
example_sentences.english: This beach is no match for the beaches in Okinawa, but it is quite beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: あの一流レストランの味にはおよばないが、かなり似ている。
example_sentences.english: The taste is no match for that top-notch restaurant, but it is very similar.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はものすごくギターが上手いが、布袋寅泰にはおよばない。
example_sentences.english: He is very good at playing the guitar, but he is no match for Hotei Tomoyasu.

example_sentences.japanese: どれだけ頑張っても、青木先輩のあしもとにはおよばない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how hard I try, I am no match for Aoki senpai.

example_sentences.japanese: 「物理学では、とてもアルバートにはおよばない。」
example_sentences.english: 'I am no match for Albert in physics.'

example_sentences.japanese: 続編は立派なものの、明らかに最初の映画にはおよばない。
example_sentences.english: Even though the sequel is splendid, it is clearly not on par with the first movie.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「はるこの嗅覚は、犬にはおよばないが、普通の人間のよりはるかにすぐれている。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Haruko's sense of smell was no match for a dog's. However, it was far better than an ordinary human's.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「どんなに練習してもさいたま先生の足元にはおよばない。」
example_sentences.english: 'No matter how much I train, I am no match for Saitama-sensei.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「メアリーは外国人なのに日本語が上手だよね。」Ｂ：「それに漢字学習にかけては誰もメアリーにもおよばないと思う。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Mary's Japanese is good for a foreigner!'B: 'What's more, I believe that when it comes to kanji knowledge, no one is a match for her.'

example_sentences.japanese: 弟子：「私の技なんて、もちろん師匠の技のクオリティにはおよびません…。」
example_sentences.english: Apprentice: ‘This technique is, of course, a technique that falls short of my master’s.’

example_sentences.japanese: 化学の知識で言えば両親にはおよばないが、英語の知識だったら勝てるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: If we speak in terms of chemistry knowledge, I am no match for my parents, but as for English knowledge, I would surely win.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の洞察力なんて、長年に渡って刑事をしている彼女の洞察力にはおよびません。
example_sentences.english: My power of discernment is nothing compared to her power of discernment, as she has spent many years as a detective.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘：「母さんの作る料理にはおよばないけどさ、私の料理もなかなか上手でしょ？」
example_sentences.english: Daughter: ‘It’s nothing compared to my mother’s cooking, but my cooking is pretty good too, right?’

example_sentences.japanese: アニメや漫画の知識について比べるとしたら、誰も彼にはおよばないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If we were to compare against him in terms of knowledge of anime and manga, then nobody’s a match for him.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼には生まれながらにしてバイオリンの才能がある。どんなに練習しても彼の腕にはおよばないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if we assume that he was a violin genius from birth, I’d be no match for him no matter how hard I practiced.

example_sentences.japanese: 節約家として知られる社内の川上さんにはおよびませんが、私もそれなりに節約術を持ち合わせています。
example_sentences.english: I cannot compare with Kawakami-san, who is known within the company as being frugal, but I am also somewhat of a thrifty person.

general_translation: Although, But, Although I say, Although it is said, Having said that
formation: Verb + とは言（い）うものの + Phrase［い］Adjective + とは言う（い）ものの + Phrase［な］Adjective + （だ）+ とは言（い）うものの +  PhraseNoun + （だ）+ とは言（い）うものの + PhrasePhrase (A)。とは言（い）うものの + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Verb + とは言（い）うものの + Phrase［い］Adjective + とは言う（い）ものの + Phrase［な］Adjective + （だ）+ とは言（い）うものの +  PhraseNoun + （だ）+ とは言（い）うものの + PhrasePhrase (A)。とは言（い）うものの + Phrase (B)
explanation: A formal conjunction-particle based phrase, used for highlighting that although (A) is a fact, (B) contradicts it. While having said (A), (B)

example_sentences.japanese: 数学は時間の無駄だとはいうものの、やはり基本を知る価値だってある。
example_sentences.english: Although it is said that math is a waste of time, actually, learning the basics still has its value.

example_sentences.japanese: なんでも頑張れば必ずできるようになるとはいうものの、どれだけ頑張ってもできないことはある。
example_sentences.english: Although it is said that you will be able to do something if you try your best, there are things that can't be done no matter how much you try.

example_sentences.japanese: 今働いている会社の給料はいいとはいうものの、お金を使う時間がない。
example_sentences.english: Although the pay at my current company is good, I don't have any time to use my money.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホは便利だというものの、使い方がわからないとスマホの便利さをしれきれない。
example_sentences.english: Although it is said that smartphones are useful, if you don't know how to use them, you can't fully appreciate their usefulness.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は学生だというものの、バイトばかりしていて勉強についていけていない。
example_sentences.english: Although he is a student, he is falling behind with his studies because he works a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はホラー作家として知られているとはいうものの、傑作と言えるものは１９８２年に出版された犯罪小説だ。
example_sentences.english: Although he is known as a horror author, what can be called his masterpiece is actually a crime novel that was published in 1982.

example_sentences.japanese: チェコの「ストラホフ・スタジアム」は「世界最大のスポーツスタジアム」とはいうものの、実際にはスポーツ目的にはほとんど使われていない。
example_sentences.english: Although the Czech 'Strahov Stadium' is said to be the 'world's largest sports stadium', in practice it is hardly used for sports purposes.

example_sentences.japanese: このカフェは人気が高いとはいうものの、実際には知る人ぞ知る所だ。
example_sentences.english: Although I say that this coffeehouse is popular, actually that's limited to the people that know the place.

example_sentences.japanese: それは「人工知能」とはいうものの、まだ「知能」というよりも「コンピューター」に近いものだ。
example_sentences.english: Although that is called 'artificial intelligence', it is still closer to a 'computer' than actual 'intelligence'.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は亡くなったと一般に信じられていた。とはいうものの、実際には公の生活から引退しただけだった。
example_sentences.english: She was widely believed to have been dead. Having said that, in actuality she had simply retired from public life.

example_sentences.japanese: 死後の世界などないとはいうものの、あると信じたっていいとも思う。
example_sentences.english: Although it is said that there is no life after death, even if you believe in it, I think that’s fine.

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーは体に良いとはいうものの、飲み過ぎると却って体に悪くなってしまいます。
example_sentences.english: Although it is said that coffee is good for the body, if you drink too much of it, it would inversely be bad for you.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘は結婚式なんてお金の無駄だとはいうものの、本当はしたいと思っているはずだ。
example_sentences.english: Although you could say that my daughter thinks that the wedding ceremony is a waste of money, I think that she surely wants to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 運命は既に決まっているとはいうものの、僕は自分で自分の運命を切り開いていきたいです。
example_sentences.english: Although it is said that fate is already decided, I want to determine my own fate.

example_sentences.japanese: 「接客業ではお客様が第一」とはいうものの、お客さん側にも少しは礼儀をわきまえて欲しいものだ。
example_sentences.english: Although it is said that ‘In the customer service industry, the customer is always right’, I want at least some of that politeness to stem from the customer’s side as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 恋愛とは違って友情は一生続くものだとはいうものの、続かない友情だっていくらでもあると思います。
example_sentences.english: Although it is said that, unlike romance, friendship lasts forever, I think that there are even friendships that don’t last.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は「もう熱も下がったし大丈夫だ」とはいうものの、大事を取ってもう少し入院しておいて欲しいのが本音である。
example_sentences.english: Although dad is saying ‘My fever has already gone down, it’s fine’, my real opinion is that I want him to stay in the hospital just a little bit longer to play it safe.

general_translation: As soon as, No sooner than, The instant that, No sooner had
formation: Verb［る］(1) + が早（はや）いか + Phrase［た］(1) Verb［た］
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + が早（はや）いか + Phrase［た］(1) Verb［た］
explanation: A formal construction, showing that (B) happened as soon as (A). Often expressing habitual actions. As (A) finished or even sooner, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんがケーキを焼き上げるがはやいか、お父さんが食べ始めた。
example_sentences.english: As soon as mom had baked the cake, dad started eating it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は彼が書いた手紙を読むがはやいか、悲しさのあまりで泣き始めた。
example_sentences.english: As soon as she read the letter from her boyfriend, she started to cry out of sadness.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は食卓に座るがはやいか、並べてあった夕食を吸い込むように食い上げた。
example_sentences.english: As soon as my son sat at the dining table, he ate all the food that was out as if he sucked them up.

example_sentences.japanese: 木村くんはアラームが鳴ったがはやいか、スヌーズボタンを押した。
example_sentences.english: As soon as the alarm went off, Kimura-kun pressed the snooze button.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察官は犯人を見つけたがはやいか、犯人に飛びつき手錠をかけた。
example_sentences.english: As soon as the police officer saw the suspect, he jumped onto him and handcuffed him.

example_sentences.japanese: 黒ずくめの男は探偵を見つけたがはやいか、疾風のごとく駆け出した。
example_sentences.english: As soon as the man dressed completely in black noticed the detective, he dashed off like the wind.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜、幼い魔法使いが窓を開けるがはやいか、白フクロウが飛び込んできた。
example_sentences.english: At night, as soon as the young wizard opened the window, a white owl flew in.

example_sentences.japanese: 自動ドアが開くがはやいか、まもなく人々は電車に乗り込んだ。
example_sentences.english: As soon as the automatic doors opened, people promptly entered the train.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「田中は目が覚めたがはやいかベッドから飛び起きた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'As soon as Tanaka opened his eyes, he jumped out of bed.'

example_sentences.japanese: あやめは兵士たちの姿が目に入るがはやいか、いきなりそばの畑に逃げ込んでしまった。
example_sentences.english: As soon as the soldiers' silhouettes came into sight, Ayame ran away into a nearby field.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんは日陰から日向に出るがはやいか日傘をさしました。
example_sentences.english: No sooner had my mother stepped from the shade into the sunlight than she put up her sun umbrella.

example_sentences.japanese:
デパートが開店するがはやいか
、一斉に大勢の客が店の中へ入って行きました。
example_sentences.english: No sooner had the shop opened than, all at once in huge numbers, customers entered.

example_sentences.japanese:
授業の終了を告げるチャイムが鳴るがはやいか
、生徒たちは教室を足速に去っていった。
example_sentences.english: No sooner had the chime rung signalling the end of class than the students fled the classroom with haste.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は家に帰ってきてランドセルを玄関に置くがはやいか、また家を出ていった。
example_sentences.english: No sooner had my son returned home and placed his school bag in the entrance than he left the house again.

example_sentences.japanese: ベッドに入るがはやいか寝てしまう人は、疲れが溜まり過ぎていると言われています。
example_sentences.english: It is said that people that fall asleep as soon as they get into bed have accumulated too much fatigue.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼の事を一目見るがはやいか恋に落ちてしまい、猛烈なアプローチを始めました。
example_sentences.english: No sooner had I laid eyes on him than I fell in love and approached him fervently.

example_sentences.japanese: その母親は娘の裁判で娘が無罪だと言い渡されるがはやいか、大粒の涙を流し始めた。
example_sentences.english: No sooner had a verdict of not-guilty been passed down in her trial than that girl’s mother started weeping in huge tears.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が止むが早いか、出かけるつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: As soon as the rain stops, I am planning to go out. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 俺は毎日家に荷物を置くが早いか、友達の家に行く。
example_sentences.english: I go to my friends house as soon as I drop my stuff off at home, everyday. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Not hard to, Not difficult to, Easy to, Is obvious that
formation: Most common pattern:想像（そうぞう） + （する）+ に難（かた）くないLess common patterns:予想（よそう） + （する）+ に難（かた）くない察（さっ）する + に難（かた）くない理解（りかい） + （する）+ に難（かた）くない推測（すいそく） + （する）+ に難（かた）くない
casual_structure: Most common pattern:想像（そうぞう） + （する）+ に難（かた）くないLess common patterns:予想（よそう） + （する）+ に難（かた）くない察（さっ）する + に難（かた）くない理解（りかい） + （する）+ に難（かた）くない推測（すいそく） + （する）+ に難（かた）くない
polite_structure: Most common pattern:想像（そうぞう） + （する）+ に難（かた）くありませんLess common patterns:予想（よそう） + （する）+ に難（かた）くありません察（さっ）する + に難（かた）くありません理解（りかい） + （する）+ に難（かた）くありません推測（すいそく） + （する）+ に難（かた）くありません
explanation: A formal phrase, implying that (A) is not hard. Usually about imagining or predicting something. There's no difficulty in (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ピラミッドが、古代人に畏敬の念を抱かせたであろうことは、想像にかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to imagine the awe that the pyramids likely inspired in the ancients.

example_sentences.japanese: そう言う叱り方は子供にいい影響を与えないだろうことは想像にかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to imagine that scolding children like that would not have a positive effect on the child.

example_sentences.japanese: このプロジェクトを中止したら多くの人に迷惑がかかることは予想にかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to guess that canceling this project would end up inconveniencing a lot of people.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供を亡くした親たちの気持ちは理解にかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not difficult to understand the feelings of parents who have lost their children.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機が墜落すれば乗客に何が起こるかは察するにかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to guess what happens to passengers when an airplane crashes.

example_sentences.japanese: その日の悲惨な出来事が、大いに影響していただろうことは想像にかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to imagine that the tragic events of that day likely affected her greatly.

example_sentences.japanese: 暴力に満ちているこのゲームが９０年代に論争を巻き起こした理由は理解にかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to understand the reason why this game that is filled with violence caused controversy in the '90s.

example_sentences.japanese: バスの運転手がいかに大きな責任を背負っているか、想像にかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to imagine how much responsibility a bus driver shoulders.

example_sentences.japanese: 安全対策の手抜きが今回の悲劇につながったことは予想にかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to guess that neglecting the safety procedures led to this tragedy.

example_sentences.japanese: この暑さの中、外で働いている人の苦難は想像にかたくありません。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to imagine the suffering of the people working outside in this heat.

example_sentences.japanese: マイノリティとしてこの国で生活をするその難しさは理解にかたくありません。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to comprehend the difficulty of living in this country as a minority.

example_sentences.japanese: 新人のミスを全部あなたが一人で背負っていたなんて、その重荷を察するにかたくない。
example_sentences.english: Taking all of the blame for that newbie’s mistake, it is not hard to imagine the burden.

example_sentences.japanese: 難病や障害を患っている生徒に勉強を教える事が簡単ではない事は想像するにかたくありません。
example_sentences.english: It is not hard to imagine that it is not easy to teach students with chronic diseases and impairments.

example_sentences.japanese: 母親に育児の負担がかかる事を当然だと考えているこの世の中で子育てをする母親の苦労は理解にかたくない。
example_sentences.english: It is easy to understand the struggle of mothers raising children in this world where the burden of child rearing falls on the mother.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の人種、そして性別による差別の経験談を聞けば、その人生の過酷さを察するにかたくない。
example_sentences.english: Hearing about her experiences with discrimination due to race and gender, It is not hard to fathom the harshness of her life.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金を納める義務を怠った事が明るみに出れば、議員の辞職に追い込まれる事は想像にかたくありません。
example_sentences.english: If the negligence of tax payment were to come to light, it is not hard to imagine that the parliament members would be forced to resign.

general_translation: Don’t know about it, Maybe it would or might be possible for
formation: Most common pattern:Noun + なら(1) + いざ知（し）らずLess common patterns:Verb + （の）+ なら(1) + いざ知（し）らず［い］Adjective + （の）+ なら(1) + いざ知（し）らずNoun + であれば(2) + いざ知（し）らずNoun + は + いざ知（し）らず(1) ならば(2) だったら
casual_structure: Most common pattern:Noun + なら(1) + いざ知（し）らずLess common patterns:Verb + （の）+ なら(1) + いざ知（し）らず［い］Adjective + （の）+ なら(1) + いざ知（し）らずNoun + であれば(2) + いざ知（し）らずNoun + は + いざ知（し）らず(1) ならば(2) だったら
explanation: An old-fashioned, hypothetical, formal grammar point, highlighting that one doesn't know about (A), but (B). If it's (A), well, I don't know.

example_sentences.japanese: １万円は社会人ならいざしらず、小学生にとっては想像を絶する金額だ。
example_sentences.english: I don't know about working adults, but for children, 10 000 yen is an unimaginable amount of money.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚式かなんかに出席するならいざしらず、友達の家に行くだけなんだからスーツなんて着ていかなくてもいいんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: I don't know if you're going to a wedding or something, but since you're just going to your friend's house, you probably don't have to wear a suit.

example_sentences.japanese: １５分待つならいざしらず、いくら友達でも３０分以上待つのは無理だ。
example_sentences.english: It may be possible for me to wait for 15 minutes, but I won’t be able to wait more than 30 minutes, no matter how good of a friend they are.

example_sentences.japanese: 経験豊富で仕事が上手ならいざしらず、まだ始めたばかりの子にこの仕事を任せるのはかわいそうすぎますよ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about people that have a lot of experience and are good at their jobs, but I feel bad giving such work to a person that just started.

example_sentences.japanese: 平日ならいざしらず、連休中に遊園地などのようなところに行く人は多いだろう。
example_sentences.english: I don't know about weekdays, but I’m sure that there are a lot of people that go to places like amusement parks during holidays.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいのならいざしらず、前のモデルはよく勝手に電源が落ちたからあまり売れなかったらしい。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about the new ones, but the older models didn’t sell well because they would turn off on their own.

example_sentences.japanese: １００年前ならいざしらず、現代のこの国においては情報へのアクセスは容易になっているからそのようなことを誰でも知っているはずだ。
example_sentences.english: I don't know about 100 years ago, but in modern times, since access to information is widespread in this country, everybody should know something like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 「運動は不健康だからしない」と最近よく聞く。プロのスポーツ選手ならいざしらず、一般の人ならば、運動は有益である。
example_sentences.english: Recently, I often hear that 'exercising is unhealthy, so I don't do it'. I don't know about professional athletes, but for ordinary people exercising is beneficial.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「子供の頃、ここでザリガニを釣ったものだ。」 Ｂ：「昔ならいざしらず、現代では川が汚染されているから​​無理です。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'When I was a child, I used to catch crayfish here.'B 'I don't know about how it was in the past, but nowadays the river is polluted, so it's impossible.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「自分一人で衣装を着て楽しむのならいざしらず、人前にコスプレ姿で出るのは私にとっては不可能に近いです。」
example_sentences.english: 'It might be possible to wear the costume by myself for fun, but when it comes to going out in public dressed in cosplay, then it's nigh on impossible!

example_sentences.japanese: 若い子ならいざしらず、３０歳の大人にはそんな事は許されない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know about small children, but for 30 year-old adults, something like that is unacceptable.

example_sentences.japanese: 体が弱いのならいざしらず、そうでないならこの階段なんてどうってことないはずだ。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know if my body is weak, but if that’s not the case then this staircase wouldn’t be an issue at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達ならいざしらず、妻なら僕が多少太っても全てを愛してくれるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about a friend, but if it were my wife, then she’d surely love me even if I was somewhat fat.

example_sentences.japanese: １０年前ならいざしらず、現代ではＳＮＳを介して人と知り合う事は一般的です。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about 10 years ago, but in the current era, connecting with people through social media is commonplace.

example_sentences.japanese: 神様や仏様ならいざしらず、この世に生きている人は皆、未来を予測出来ません。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about God or Buddha, but there is no one living in this world that can predict the future.

example_sentences.japanese: 命を預かるという責任があるならいざしらず、そうでないならペットを飼うべきではない。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about the responsibility of being put in charge of something’s life, but if that’s not the case, then one ought not own a pet.

example_sentences.japanese: 一軒家ならいざしらず、そんなにドタバタする運動はアパートやマンションでは不可能です。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about a standalone house, but that sort of noisy exercise is not possible in an apartment or unit.

example_sentences.japanese: 数千円のスニーカーならいざしらず、一万円を超えるようなスニーカーを買う時には失敗は許されない。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about if it is a pair of sneakers for a few thousand yen, but you can’t get it wrong when buying a pair of sneakers that is over 10,000 yen.

example_sentences.japanese: 大昔ならいざしらず、現代では詐欺についてよくテレビやインターネットで話題になっているから、詐欺の手口も年々と進化していってる。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about the past, but nowadays, scams are often talked about on TV and the internet today, so scam tactics are evolving year by year.

example_sentences.japanese: 神ならいざしらず、俺みたいなやつにはああいうことをする奴たちを許すことなどできない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know about the gods, but it is very hard for a person like me to forgive people that do things like that.

example_sentences.japanese: ６０年前はいざしらず、今では喫煙する人が減ってきている。
example_sentences.english: I don’t know about 60 years ago, but nowadays, there are less people that smoke.

general_translation: Cannot help feeling, Cannot but, Cannot hold back
formation: Noun + を禁（きん）じ得（え）ないVerb + の + を禁（きん）じ得（え）ない
casual_structure: Noun + を禁（きん）じ得（え）ないVerb + の + を禁（きん）じ得（え）ない
polite_structure: Noun + を禁（きん）じ得（え）ませんVerb + の + を禁（きん）じ得（え）ません
explanation: A formal structure, expressing that (A) cannot be helped or stopped. Forbidding (A) cannot be gained.

example_sentences.japanese: この生徒たちは流暢な日本語でニュースについて議論していたが、彼らは二年前から日本語を勉強し始めたと聞いて、驚きをきんじえなかった。
example_sentences.english: I could not help being surprised, hearing that these students who were discussing the news in fluent Japanese, had started studying it two years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めて広島にある平和記念資料館に行ったとき、涙をこらえるのをきんじえなかった。
example_sentences.english: I could not hold back my tears when I went to the peace museum in Hiroshima for the first time.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が生まれたが、いい父親になれるか不安をきんじえない。
example_sentences.english: I have a son, but I can't stop worrying about whether I will be a good father.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金を国民のためではなく自分たちのためだけに使う政治家に怒りをきんじえない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot help but be outraged at politicians who spend taxpayers' money only on themselves and not on the people.

example_sentences.japanese: この不況の中、政治家が自分の給与を上げるとの報道を耳にし、怒りをきんじえません。
example_sentences.english: I cannot help but feel anger upon hearing the news that the politicians raised their salaries during this time of recession.

example_sentences.japanese: 伝記：「戦争がこの地方にもたらした破壊を見て、涙をきんじえなかった。」
example_sentences.english: Biography: 'I could not hold back tears after seeing the destruction that the war brought upon this area.'

example_sentences.japanese: 長い年月の後、互いに抱き合った姿に、喜びをきんじえない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot help but feel joy at seeing those two embracing one another after all these years.

example_sentences.japanese: 全てを失った地震の被害者に同情の念をきんじえない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot help feeling compassion for the victims of the earthquake, who lost everything.

example_sentences.japanese: 伝記：「 初めて『クトゥルフの呼び声』を読んだ時、鳥肌が立つのをきんじえなかった。」
example_sentences.english: Biography: 'I could not help getting goosebumps when I read 'Call of Cthulhu' for the first time.'

example_sentences.japanese: ブログのコメント：「面白すぎて草をきんじえない。」
example_sentences.english: Blog comment: 'It is so funny that I can't hold back laughter.'

example_sentences.japanese: ドラゴンを目の前にして絶望をきんじえない人はいないだろう。
example_sentences.english: There probably isn’t a person that couldn’t help but feel despair when faced with a dragon.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに美しい人が本当はおじさんだったと知り、驚きをきんじえなかった。
example_sentences.english: Finding out that a person that beautiful was actually an old guy, I couldn’t help feeling surprised.

example_sentences.japanese: 防犯カメラを見て１０分前までこの家に泥棒がいたと知り、恐怖をきんじえなかった。
example_sentences.english: Looking at the security camera and seeing that there was a thief in this house until 10 minutes ago, I couldn’t help feeling terror.

example_sentences.japanese: 元担任の先生が未成年の生徒に対して好意を抱いていたと知り、嫌悪感をきんじえません。
example_sentences.english: Finding out that my former homeroom teacher held feelings toward an underage student, I can't help but feel disgusted.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに凶悪な犯罪を犯した人がたったの二十年で刑務所を出たなんて、驚きをきんじえない。
example_sentences.english: A person getting out of jail after only 20 years after having committed such a heinous crime, I cannot help feeling shocked.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の若者にとって、子育てはおろか結婚でさえ経済的に難しくなっていると聞き、絶望をきんじえません。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but feel despair that for the young people of today, not to mention raising children, but even with marriage, it is getting difficult economically.

example_sentences.japanese: 普段は真面目で強面の上司がまさかこんなに面白いジョークを言えるなんて、笑いをきんじえない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but laugh after hearing my boss, who is usually serious and has a stern demeanor, tell a joke this funny.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はあのシーンを見て涙を禁じ得ないようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems like he was not able to hold back his tears when he saw that scene. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: In the name of, Using the excuse of, To use as a pretext of, Under the guise or pretense of
formation: Noun + にかこつけてVerb + の(1) + にかこつけて(1) こと
casual_structure: Noun + にかこつけてVerb + の(1) + にかこつけて(1) こと
explanation: A structure indicating that something is being done with the excuse of (A), or under the pretense of (A). Consigning it as (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 「花子ったら部活動にかこつけて、部室に潜り込んでひとり遊んでばかりいるよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Speaking of Hanako, she sneaks into the club room under the pretense of club activity and just lazes around.'

example_sentences.japanese: 病院に行くというのにかこつけて仕事を休んだ。
example_sentences.english: I took a day off work under the pretense of going to the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の家に忘れ物をしたというのにかこつけて彼のところにもう一度行く。
example_sentences.english: I will go to his place again under the pretense that I left something at his place.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はいつも何かにかこつけて僕の家に来ようとする。本当にやめてほしい。
example_sentences.english: She always tries to come to my place under the pretense of something. I really want her to stop.

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪にかこつけて、授業を休んで一日中テレビを見ながらダラダラしていた。
example_sentences.english: Using the pretext of a cold, I skipped class and loafed around and watched TV all day.

example_sentences.japanese: 人（私も含めて）はお菓子が大好きで何かにかこつけていつも買ってしまうのではないだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I think that people (myself included) love sweets and will always buy them under some pretext.

example_sentences.japanese: 武田：「田中さんったら出張にかこつけてパリを観光するつもりね。」田中さん：「いやいや、そんなこと。」
example_sentences.english: Takeda: 'Tanaka-san, you're planning to go sightseeing in Paris using the pretense of a business trip, aren't you?'Tanaka: 'No no, nothing like that.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「あすかさんと会いたいけどどうしたらいい？」 Ｂ：「プリントを渡すというのにかこつけて家に行ったらどう？」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I want to meet with Asuka, but what should I do?'B: 'How about going to her house under the pretext of intending to give her printouts?'

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪にかこつけて、仕事を休んで一日中コーラを飲んだりゲームをしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Using the pretext of a cold, he took some time off work, drank coke, and played games all day long.

example_sentences.japanese: 姉の見舞いにかこつけて実家に帰った。そして、仲違いしていた両親と仲直りすることができた。
example_sentences.english: Under the pretext of visiting my ill sister, I returned home. And I was able to reconcile with my parents, whom I had been at odds with.

example_sentences.japanese:
誕生日祝いという名目にかこつけて
、私たちは五つ星の温泉旅館に泊まりました。
example_sentences.english: Using the excuse of a birthday celebration, we stayed at a 5-star onsen resort.

example_sentences.japanese: 留学にかこつけて外国人の彼女をゲットしようとした友達は撃沈して帰ってきました。
example_sentences.english: Using the excuse of studying abroad, my friend who tried to get a foreign girlfriend crashed and burned, and then returned home.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が父に：「アドバイスにかこつけて過去の栄光について語るの、やめてくれない？」
example_sentences.english: A son to his father: ‘Could you please stop talking about your past glories under the pretense of advice?’

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏はクリスマスとかバレンタインデーとかにかこつけて物をねだってくるから困ります。
example_sentences.english: My boyfriend pesters me for things in the name of Christmas and Valentine’s day, so it’s a bother.

example_sentences.japanese: 同僚に忠告する：「あの上司は酒に酔った勢いにかこつけて口説こうとしてくるから、気をつけてね。」
example_sentences.english: Advising a colleague: ‘That boss uses the excuse of being merrily drunk in order to come making advances, so be careful.’

example_sentences.japanese: 暴徒化したデモにかこつけて近辺の店から商品を盗もうとするなんて、奴らはなんて卑怯なんだ！
example_sentences.english: Something like stealing products from surrounding shops under the pretext of what had turned into a riot, they’re such cowards.

example_sentences.japanese: 独り言：「私ったら、家族の誕生日や友達の誕生日、結婚記念日とか色々なイベントにかこつけてケーキを買っちゃうんだから…。」
example_sentences.english: Talking to oneself: ‘Oh me…, always buying cake under the pretense of various events like my family or friends’ birthdays and wedding anniversaries.’

example_sentences.japanese: 靴ひもを結ぶのにかこつけて落ちていた財布をこっそりと拾った。
example_sentences.english: I sneakily picked up the wallet that was on the ground, labeling it as tying my shoelace.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつは出張にかこつけて、また釣りに行っているに違いない。
example_sentences.english: I bet he has gone fishing again, consigning it as a business trip.

general_translation: Depending on the way, Depending on how
formation: Verb［stem］+ ようによっては + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ ようによっては + Phrase
explanation: An expression showing that depending on the manner in which someone does (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: このドレスの色はみようによっては「青と黒」か「白と金」に見えるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Depending on how you look at it, the color of this dress may seem like it's 'blue and black' or 'white and gold'.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は見ようによってはコメディーだと感じる人もいるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Some people may see this movie as a comedy film, depending on how they watch it.

example_sentences.japanese: ４５分で行けるはずだけど、混みようによっては１時間半かかることもあり得るから明日は少し早く家を出よう。
example_sentences.english: We should be able to get there in 45 minutes, but depending on how congested the road is, it could take an hour and a half, so let’s leave a bit early tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに安全な機械であっても使いようによってはとても危険になることもある。
example_sentences.english: No matter how safe a machine is, it could become very dangerous depending on how you use it.

example_sentences.japanese: 「結構です」はききようによっては肯定にでも否定にでもどちらにでも受け取れる。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the way you hear it, '結構です' can be taken either as affirmation or denial.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済危機は、一見絶望しかないように見えるが、かんがえようによっては素晴らしい機会とも言えるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: The economic crisis may seem to be nothing but despair. However, depending on the way you think about it, it might also be called a great opportunity.

example_sentences.japanese: 確かに、この大きな目のクモは、みようによっては可愛いらしいと言えなくもない。
example_sentences.english: Needless to say, depending on the way you look at this big-eyed spider, it can kind of be called adorable.

example_sentences.japanese: このツイートはよみようによっては皮肉にも取れるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the way you read this tweet, you could take it as irony, right!?

example_sentences.japanese: この試合はやりようによっては勝てるんじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Depending on how we play this match, we can probably win.

example_sentences.japanese: かんがえようによっては、上司の厳しさは私のためを思っているとも言える。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the way you think, I could say that my boss’ strictness can be thought of as being for my benefit.

example_sentences.japanese: 上司に「はたらきようによっては一ヶ月で１００万円くらい稼げるよ。」と言われ、やる気が出た。
example_sentences.english: I was told ‘Depending on the way you work, you can earn up to $10,000 a month’ by my boss, so I got fired up.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が経営するカフェは資金も人員も限られているが、やりようによっては上手くやれる。
example_sentences.english: The cafe that I manage is limited in funds and personnel, but depending on the way we do things, it can go well.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強はやりようによっては、少ない時間・少ない努力でも力をつける事が出来ます。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the way you study, you can make progress with even little effort or little time.

example_sentences.japanese: ソーシャルメディア上での営業は、つかいようによっては良くも悪くも、どちらにもなり得ります。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to social media enterprises, it can either go good or bad depending on the way it is used.

example_sentences.japanese: 独り言：「僕は彼女に振られて、仕事も失って、どん底にいるけれど、かんがえようによっては、これは人生を変えるチャンスだ！」
example_sentences.english: Talking to oneself: ‘I was dumped by my girlfriend, lost my job, and am at rock bottom, but depending on the way you think about it, this is a chance to change my life!’

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は正直すぎて相手の気分を害してしまう事もしばしばあるが、つかいようによっては営業に向いているかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: He frequently wrecks the mood of his clients due to being too straightforward, but depending on the way we use him, he may be suited to sales.

example_sentences.japanese: この絵は見方によっては奇麗な女性かウサギに見える。
example_sentences.english: Depending on how you look at this picture, it may look like a beautiful lady or a rabbit.

general_translation: No (doubt or hope), There is no way, It is impossible, Not a hope in hell
formation: Verb + べくもないExceptions:［する］Verb + す(1) + べくもない(1) する
casual_structure: Verb + べくもないExceptions:［する］Verb + す(1) + べくもない(1) する
polite_structure: Verb + べくもありませんExceptions:［する］Verb + す(1) + べくもありません(1) する
explanation: A formal construction, indicating that there is no hope of (A). It would not even be permissable that (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「戦力差は歴然としているゆえ、まともな勝負は望むべくもない。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Since the difference in strength is clear, there is no hope of a decent match.'

example_sentences.japanese: 自分が作ったパスタはあの有名シェフが作るパスタと比べるべくもないが、結構おいしいと思う。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to compare the pasta I made with the one made by that famous chef, but I think mine is quite tasty.

example_sentences.japanese: あの顔を見てみろ、あいつが彼を殺したという事は疑うべくもない。
example_sentences.english: Look at that face, there is no doubt that they are the one that killed him.

example_sentences.japanese: 私自身が先生になるまでは、先生の大変さなど知るべくもなかった。
example_sentences.english: Until I became a teacher myself, I could never have known how hard it is to be a teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら頑張ったところで、絵は写真にはおよぶべくもないのである。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much one tries, a drawing is no match for a photograph.

example_sentences.japanese: 地球温暖化は人間活動と直接関係があるということは疑うべくもない。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that global warming is directly linked to human influence.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「今回、彼は危害を免れたにせよ、そのように運転を続けていては将来は彼に何事が起りかねぬかは、知るべくもない。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Even though he escaped injury this time, there is no way to know what might happen to him in the future if he continues driving like that.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「この真正直な少年に、嘘をつくなど望むべくもない。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'There's not a hope in hell that this honest boy would lie.'

example_sentences.japanese: 田中先生の作品は傑作と比べるべくもないが、それなりに素晴らしいものがある。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to compare Tanaka's works to masterpieces, but they are wonderful in their own respect.

example_sentences.japanese: ボーナスの増額なんて、この不況の中では望むべくもない。
example_sentences.english: Something like an increase in bonuses, in the midst of this sorry state there’s not a hope in hell.

example_sentences.japanese: たった二年くらい一生懸命練習したところで、プロの腕に敵うべくもありません。
example_sentences.english: There’s not a hope in hell that you’d reach a professional level of skill with just 2 years of practicing your hardest.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長や取締役がどんな話をしていたのかなど、平社員の我々が知るべくもありません。
example_sentences.english: For run-of-the-mill employees like us, it is impossible to know what kind of conversations the president or board members have.

example_sentences.japanese: 若い頃は貧乏だったので将来を考えるべくもなく必死に生きていたが、今なら少しは考える余裕がある。
example_sentences.english: I was poor in my youth, so I was flat out staying alive and it was impossible to think about the future, but now I have at least a little bit of room to think.

example_sentences.japanese: 千年以上前に建てられたこの建物を保護する価値があることに対しては、疑うべくもありません。
example_sentences.english: There is no way that you could doubt the worth of preserving this building that was constructed more than a thousand years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 広告に反応する：「サプリを飲むだけで体重がガクンと落ちるだって？そんな都合の良過ぎる事、望むべくもないよ。」
example_sentences.english: Reacting to an ad: ‘By just drinking a supplement your weight can drastically decrease they say? There is not a hope in hell of a situation being so good.’

example_sentences.japanese: あの中古車販売店が詐欺まがいなことをやっていたということは、否定するべくもない事実だ。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that that used car dealership was doing something that could be considered as a scam.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな解決策では問題が解決すべくもない。
example_sentences.english: There is no way that we can solve the problem with such a solution.

general_translation: For …(is the best), When it comes to, Concerning
formation: Phrase + ときたら
casual_structure: Phrase + ときたら
explanation: A hypothetical construction, used for raising a topic and giving thoughts on it. When it comes to topic (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 「田中さんがクビになったと聞いたよ。」「毎日遅刻ときたらクビになるのは当然でしょ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I heard Mr. Tanaka got fired.''No wonder he would get fired when he was late every day.'

example_sentences.japanese: 夏ときたらやっぱりキンキンに冷えたビールですよ！
example_sentences.english: When it comes to summer, as expected, a cold beer is the best!

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い日ときたら、鍋でしょう。
example_sentences.english: For a cold day, hot pots (is the best), don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: パワハラときたら大問題になるのは当然でしょう。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to power harassment, of course it is going to become a huge problem.

example_sentences.japanese: ドーナツときたらやっぱり牛乳でしょ！
example_sentences.english: For donuts, as expected, it's gotta be milk, right?

example_sentences.japanese: テストで毎回０点を取っているときたら、お母さんが怒らないわけがない。
example_sentences.english: When you get a zero on every test, there's no way your mother won't get angry.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑い日ときたら、やっぱり麦茶よね。
example_sentences.english: For a hot day, as expected, there's nothing like barley tea, right?

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに曇っているときたら、雨が降らないはずがない。
example_sentences.english: When it is so cloudy, it is impossible for it not to rain.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ときたら、やっぱりコーヒーしか無いですね。
example_sentences.english: For morning, as expected, only coffee (is a good match), right?

example_sentences.japanese: 暑い夏ときたら、絶対にプールでしょ！
example_sentences.english: When it comes to the heat in summer, it’s gotta be the pool!

example_sentences.japanese: ガトーショコラときたら、あの美味しいケーキ屋さんのに限ります。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to gateau chocolate, there’s nothing better than that cake shop's.

example_sentences.japanese: 数学の先生ときたら、あの有名講師の田中先生だ。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to math teachers, it’s gotta be the famous lecturer Mr. Tanaka.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬ときたら鍋だと思っていたが、彼にとってのそれはミカンらしい。
example_sentences.english: I thought that there was nothing better than nabe when it comes to winter, but for him it’s apparently mandarin.

example_sentences.japanese: ジュエリーブランドときたらティファニーだと言う彼女は、お金持ちに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Since she says that there is nothing better than Tiffany when it comes to jewellery brands, there is no mistaking that she is rich

example_sentences.japanese: バラエティ番組の司会者ときたら、あの女性をおいて他にはいないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: When it comes to variety show hosts, there is nobody better than that lady.

example_sentences.japanese: 合コンがしたいんだって？合コンときたら、あの合コンマスターの林君に頼るのがいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You wanna go to a mixer? When it comes to mixers you should leave it up to Hayashi-kun, the mixer master.

general_translation: Assuming, Supposing, (Interpret) as, On the assumption, Regarding, Considering
formation: Verb + ものとして［い］Adjective + ものとして［な］Adjective + な(1) + ものとしてNoun + である + ものとして(1) である
casual_structure: Verb + ものとして［い］Adjective + ものとして［な］Adjective + な(1) + ものとしてNoun + である + ものとして(1) である
explanation: An expression used for making suppositions. Treating it as a thing that is (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: これ以上討議しても進展は見込めないものとして、これをもって会議はお開きとします。
example_sentences.english: Considering no further progress can be made in the discussion, with this the meeting is closed.

example_sentences.japanese: もう一時間もたつので、出席しないものとして会議を始めましょう。
example_sentences.english: It’s already been an hour, so let’s assume that they are not attending and start the meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなが参加できるものとして計画を立てましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let’s make a plan on the assumption that everyone would be able to attend.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日のテストは難しいものとして勉強したが、実際に受けてみたら全然余裕だった。
example_sentences.english: I studied for yesterday’s test with the assumption that it was going to be difficult, but when it came to actually taking the test, it was easy.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のアイデアは不可能なものとして、誰も彼のアイデアを取り入れようとしなかった。
example_sentences.english: No one even considered implementing his idea on the assumption that it was impossible.

example_sentences.japanese: 講師：「ご質問等はありますか？ない場合は理解したものとして今日はここまでです。」
example_sentences.english: Lecturer: 'Do you have any questions? If not, I will assume that you understood, and that will be all for today.'

example_sentences.japanese: 大学のサイト：「先生からの連絡は一度掲示された内容については１週間後、全学生に伝達されたものとして扱います。」
example_sentences.english: University website: 'Once posted, communications from the teacher will be assumed to have been delivered to all students after one week.'

example_sentences.japanese: 格闘技においては選手は畳やマットを３回叩くと降参したものとして、試合の決着がつく。
example_sentences.english: In martial arts, a match will be regarded as forfeited when a fighter strikes the tatami or mat three times.

example_sentences.japanese: しかしながら、市長は、住民の心配事を、ありえないものとして、却下しました。
example_sentences.english: However, the mayor dismissed the residents' worries, supposing they were improbable.

example_sentences.japanese: 政府は、経済が成長し続けるものとして計画を立てていた。
example_sentences.english: The government had based its plans on the assumption that the economy would continue to grow.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の説明はありえないとして、聞き流されました。
example_sentences.english: His explanation was seen as impossible, and was dismissed.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の説明はありえないものとして、聞き流されました。
example_sentences.english: His explanation was assumed to be something which was impossible, and therefore dismissed. (Slightly more verbose, creating a feeling of stiffness or formality)

general_translation: On the premise of
formation: Noun + を前提（ぜんてい）に(1)Verb + こと + を前提（ぜんてい）に(1)(1) として、にして
casual_structure: Noun + を前提（ぜんてい）に(1)Verb + こと + を前提（ぜんてい）に(1)(1) として、にして
explanation: An expression that shows that action or goal (B) is based on the prior assumption of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは、結婚をぜんていに付き合っている。
example_sentences.english: We are dating on the premise of marriage.

example_sentences.japanese: このパソコンは仕事場で使われることをぜんていに作られているので、ゲームなどには向いていないです。
example_sentences.english: This computer was made on the premise that it would be used in the workplace, so it is not suitable for games.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘さんとは結婚をぜんていにお付き合いをさせていただいています。
example_sentences.english: I am dating your daughter on the premise of marriage.

example_sentences.japanese: この車はレースをするということをぜんていに改造されているため公道では運転できません。
example_sentences.english: This car was customized on the premise of racing, so you can’t drive it on public roads.

example_sentences.japanese: 名前を出さないということをぜんていにして、労基に上司のパワハラなどを通報した。
example_sentences.english: On the premise that they don’t make my name known, I reported to the Labor standards inspection office about my boss harassing me.

example_sentences.japanese: このアパートは、一人で住むことをぜんていとして作られているので、キッチンとお風呂場は小さいです。
example_sentences.english: This apartment was built on the premise that only one person will live here, so the kitchen and the bathroom is small.

example_sentences.japanese: 元々、 一人で住むことをぜんていにこの家を建てたから、時が経ったらちょっと狭くなった。
example_sentences.english: The house was originally built on the premise that I would live there by myself, so it turned out to be a little small over time.

example_sentences.japanese: 原価見積は、建材の価格が緩やかに上昇することをぜんていに計算されます。
example_sentences.english: Cost estimates are calculated on the premise of a slow increase in the price of building materials.

example_sentences.japanese: 多くの家庭用ゲーム機を所有している人はゲームが終わったら売ることをぜんていにそのゲームを買っている。
example_sentences.english: Many console owners purchase games based on the premise that they will sell them after finishing.

example_sentences.japanese: 本教科書は、文法に関する知識があることをぜんていに書かれています。
example_sentences.english: This textbook was written on the premise that you have an understanding of basic grammar.

example_sentences.japanese: 当社の製品は長期使用をぜんていに設計されています。
example_sentences.english: Our products are engineered on the premise of long-term use.

general_translation: Won't get away without, Won't get off without, Have to, Have no choice but to, Can’t not
formation: Verb[ない] + ずには + すまないVerb[ない] + では + すまないException:する→せずにはすまない
casual_structure: Verb[ない] + ずには + すまないVerb[ない] + では + すまないException:する→せずにはすまない
explanation: A somewhat old-fashioned expression, indicating that someone cannot get away with not doing (A). It will not come to an end with (A) not being done.

example_sentences.japanese: 重要な会議だから、まにあわないではすまない。
example_sentences.english: It's an important meeting, so I won't get away without making it on time.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに迷惑をかけてしまったんだから、謝らずにはすまないだろう。
example_sentences.english: I caused so much trouble, so I won’t get away without apologizing.

example_sentences.japanese: 取引先のお偉いさんに飲みに誘われたから、行かずにはすまない。
example_sentences.english: A high-ranking business partner invited me out for a drink, so I have no choice but to go.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の先輩からの電話は出ずにはすまない。
example_sentences.english: I have no choice but to answer phone calls from my senpai from work.

example_sentences.japanese: やばい、田中君のゲーム機を壊してしまった。これは、弁償せずにはすまないな。
example_sentences.english: Oh shoot, I broke Tanaka-kun’s gaming console. I won't get away without paying him back.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が大切にしていた釣竿を折ってしまった。謝らないではすまない。
example_sentences.english: I accidentally broke a fishing rod my father took great care of. I won’t get away without apologizing.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金は払わないではすまない。
example_sentences.english: You can’t get away without paying taxes.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は相談もなく重要な道具を廃棄した。首にならずにはすまないだろう。
example_sentences.english: He has scrapped an important tool without consultation. He won't get off without being fired.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は子犬を助けるためとはいえ、無断で車の窓を破った。罰をうけずにはすまないだろう。
example_sentences.english: I broke the window of the car without permission, even though I was trying to save a puppy. I won't get away unpunished.

example_sentences.japanese: この深刻な問題は難しいので、上司にはなさずにはすまないだろう。
example_sentences.english: I have no choice but to talk to my boss about it, since it is a serious problem.

example_sentences.japanese: 大人なのだから、しらずではすまないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Since you are an adult, you won't get by without knowing it.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当は僕がミスをしたのに、彼がかばってくれたんだ。彼にはあやまらずにはすまない。
example_sentences.english: Even though I made a mistake, he covered for me. I won't get away without apologizing.

general_translation: Cannot bear to, Cannot stand to, Too much to, Cannot go on doing, Cannot tolerate
formation: Verb + に堪（た）えないAdverb + に堪（た）えない
casual_structure: Verb + に堪（た）えないAdverb + に堪（た）えない
explanation: An expression showing that (A) is something that cannot be withstood or tolerated. Cannot bear (A).

example_sentences.japanese: くりやまさんの歌声は酷すぎて聞くにたえなかった。
example_sentences.english: Kuriyama-san's singing voice was so terrible that I couldn't bear to listen.

example_sentences.japanese: この本には過激な表現がありすぎるので、読むにたえない。
example_sentences.english: There are too many graphic expressions in this book that I can’t bear to read it.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事の環境がひどすぎて続けるにたえない。
example_sentences.english: The working conditions are so bad that I cannot bear to continue.

example_sentences.japanese: あの映画に出ている役者さんみんなが大根役者だったので、見るにたえなかったです。
example_sentences.english: Since all the actors that were in that movie were bad actors, I couldn’t bear to watch it.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんの話はいつも人の悪口ばかり言っているので、聞くにたえない。
example_sentences.english: I can’t tolerate listening to Tanaka-san because he is always talking ill about others.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんの所有物を壊してお客さんをだますなんて怒りにたえない。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely outraged that they destroyed their customers’ property and lied to them.

example_sentences.japanese: このホラー映画には正視にたえない、すごく残虐なシーンが多い。
example_sentences.english: In this horror movie, there are so many brutal scenes that I cannot bear to watch it.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、新聞で悪いニュースばかりが続いているから読むにたえない。
example_sentences.english: With all the bad news in the newspaper lately, I cannot bear to read it.

example_sentences.japanese: 嘘をついてばかりいる政治家のインタビューはもう聞くにたえない。
example_sentences.english: I can't tolerate listening to interviews with politicians who tell nothing but lies.

example_sentences.japanese: 中二病のころ撮った写真は恥ずかしすぎて見るにたえないから消した。
example_sentences.english: The photos I took when I was in my 'look at me' stage were so embarrassing that I couldn't bear to look at them, so I deleted them.

example_sentences.japanese: この漫画は内容がとてもよく、大人でも読むに堪える。
example_sentences.english: This manga is worth reading, even for an adult, because it is well written.

example_sentences.japanese: やっと公開するに堪える音楽ができました！
example_sentences.english: I have finally made a song that is worth publishing!

general_translation: Ends up, Finally, In the end, (Unfortunately) As a result, This is what happened, To come about, To wind up
formation: Verb[る] + 始末（しまつ）だこの始末（しまつ）だ
casual_structure: Verb[る] + 始末（しまつ）だこの始末（しまつ）だ
explanation: A strong construction, showing the unfavorable result of (A). From start to finish it all wound up as (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 武田さんは小さな声で職場でハラスメントを受けたことを伝えてきて、しまいに大きな声で泣き出すしまつだ。
example_sentences.english: Takeda-san quietly told me that she was being harassed at work, and wound up crying out loud.

example_sentences.japanese: あんだけダブルチェックをするように言ったのに、このしまつだ。
example_sentences.english: I told him so many times to double check, but this is the result.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなで祭りに行くつもりだったのに、みんながドタキャンするから、結局一人で行くしまつだ。
example_sentences.english: We were supposed to go to the festival together, but everyone canceled suddenly, so I ended up going alone.

example_sentences.japanese: その客は店中をぐちゃぐちゃにしたあげく、何も買わないで帰るしまつだ。
example_sentences.english: After messing up the whole store, they ended up leaving without buying anything.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつは、自分が起こしたミスなのに、謝るどころか私のせいにするしまつだ。
example_sentences.english: Even though it was a mistake that he had made, far from apologizing, he ended up blaming me!

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく友達と海へ行く計画を立てたのに、田中は大事な用があって行けないとか、武田もシフトが入ってたとかで、結局私一人だけで行くしまつだ。
example_sentences.english: Even though I went out of my way to plan this trip to the beach with friends, Tanaka said that he had something important to do and couldn't go, while Takeda said that he had a shift. So I ended up going all by myself.

example_sentences.japanese: 武田：「山田さん、顔色が悪いですけど・・・」山田：「夜遅くまでゲームをしていたので、おかげでこのしまつだ。」
example_sentences.english: Takeda: 'Yamada-san, you don't look so good...'Yamada : 'I was playing video games until late at night, and this is the result.'

example_sentences.japanese: 田中には二度と仕事は頼まないぞ。納期は守らないし仕上がりも悪かったのに、言い訳ばかりならべて。最後には追加の料金を払えと言い出すしまつだ。
example_sentences.english: I'll never ask Tanaka to work for me again. He can't meet deadlines, his workmanship is poor, and he only gives excuse after excuse. In the end he told me to pay an additional fee.

example_sentences.japanese: プロジェクトを期限内に終えることができなくて、上司の逆鱗に触れてしまうしまつだ。
example_sentences.english: I couldn't finish the project on time, and I wound up infuriating my boss.

example_sentences.japanese: 重い買い物袋が破れて中身が地面に落ちたところ：「下から抱えなかったら、このしまつだ。」
example_sentences.english: After a heavy shopping bag has just ripped, and the contents fell out: 'This is what comes about when you don't hold it from the bottom.'

general_translation: If you were to do, If you try to, If … happens, Should there be
formation: Verb[volitional] + ものなら/もんなら + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb[volitional] + ものなら/もんなら + Phrase
explanation: A strong hypothetical phrase, meaning that should (A) happen, (B). If it's the thing which is (A), without a doubt (B). (B) is negative.

example_sentences.japanese: しのぶさんはとても血を恐れている。万が一、一滴でも血を見ようものなら気絶してしまうはずだ。
example_sentences.english: Shinobu is completely terrified of blood. If she were to see even one drop of it by chance, she would faint for sure.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の誕生日を忘れようものなら、一日中機嫌が悪くなる。
example_sentences.english: If you were to forget her birthday, she would be in a bad mood all day.

example_sentences.japanese: このレポートを出し忘れようものなら、今までの努力が水の泡だ。
example_sentences.english: All of our efforts would be worth nothing, if I happen to forget to submit this paper.

example_sentences.japanese: 以前同じようなことで炎上したから、また似たようなことで炎上しようものならこの業界から干されるに違いない。
example_sentences.english: Since we went under fire with something similar before, if we go under fire for something similar again, I am sure we would be sidelined from this industry.

example_sentences.japanese: ブラッド・ピットに出逢おうものなら、死んでしまう。
example_sentences.english: If I were to run into Brad Pitt, I would die.

example_sentences.japanese: 秘密を打ち明けようものなら、彼女はすぐに他の奴らにしゃべってしまうだろう。
example_sentences.english: If you happen to tell her a secret, she will quickly spill it to others.

example_sentences.japanese: 万が一このプロジェクトが失敗しようものなら、我々は終わりだ。
example_sentences.english: If this project were to fail, we'd be finished.

example_sentences.japanese: うっかり彼のお菓子を食べようものなら、きっと、ものすごく彼にしかられるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: If you were to go and eat his sweets, you would be scolded for sure.

example_sentences.japanese: これは大変デリケートな機械だからもし少しでも力を入れようものなら壊れるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: It's a very delicate device, so if we were to put even the slightest pressure on it, it may break.

general_translation: In stark contrast, In comparison, On the other hand, While, In sharp contrast
formation: Noun＋にひきかえ［な］Adjective＋な・である＋の＋にひきかえ［い］Adjective＋の＋にひきかえVerb＋の＋にひきかえPhrase (A)。それにひきかえ、Noun は＋Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Noun＋にひきかえ［な］Adjective＋な・である＋の＋にひきかえ［い］Adjective＋の＋にひきかえVerb＋の＋にひきかえPhrase (A)。それにひきかえ、Noun は＋Phrase (B)
explanation: A strong expression, implying that (B) is in sharp contrast to (A). Pulling right back from (A) and changing views, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 母親の友達の息子さんは、弁護士として立派に働いているのにひきかえ、僕は・・・。
example_sentences.english: In stark contrast to my mother's friend's son, who is working prominently as a lawyer, I am… (still a permanent part-timer)

example_sentences.japanese: 周りの人たちはどんどん就職していっているのにひきかえ、俺はまだ面接さえしていない。
example_sentences.english: In stark contrast to the people around me, who are getting jobs, I haven’t even gone to an interview.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの娘は頭がいいのにひきかえ、うちの長男はゲームばかりして全然勉強をしようともしない。
example_sentences.english: In stark contrast to my daughter, who is smart, all my eldest son wants to do is play videogames and won’t even try to study.

example_sentences.japanese: 親戚の全員が裕福なのにひきかえ、なぜか私の家族だけが貧乏。
example_sentences.english: In stark contrast to all my relatives, who are wealthy, my family is poor for some reason.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年の夏にひきかえ、今年の夏はえげつなく暑い。
example_sentences.english: In stark contrast to summer last year, summer this year is extremely hot.

example_sentences.japanese: 周りの子たちを見てみなさいよ！みんな来年から大学よ！それにひきかえ、あんたったら。。。
example_sentences.english: Look at the kids around you! They are all going to college starting next year! In stark contrast to that you…

example_sentences.japanese: 姉は積極的で活発な性格にひきかえ、弟の健太郎はとても無気力だ。
example_sentences.english: In stark contrast to the elder sister's lively personality, the younger brother, Kentaro, is very apathetic.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は優秀な成績をおさめている。それにひきかえ妹の方は遊んでばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: The elder brother has excellent grades. In stark contrast to that, the younger sister is just mucking around.

example_sentences.japanese: 前回のテストにひきかえ今回のテストは難しい。
example_sentences.english: In stark contrast to the previous test, this one is hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 隣の家の猫は痩せていて頭がいいのにひきかえうちの猫はぐうたらしてばかりだなあ。
example_sentences.english: In stark contrast to the neighbor's cat, which is skinny and smart, our cat is just loafing around.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の服はかっこいい。それにひきかえ私の彼氏の服は、なんてダサいのだ。
example_sentences.english: His clothes are cool. In stark contrast to that, how uncool my boyfriend's clothes are.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は寒いのに引き換え、昼になったら暖かくなるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: In stark contrast to it being cold right now, it would probably get warmer at noon. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: If… then it is all in vain, It's done, It is useless, No point, It is a waste, That's it, It is all gone,
formation: Verb [たら] + それまでだVerb [ば] + それまでだ
casual_structure: Verb [たら] + それまでだVerb [ば] + それまでだ
explanation: A hypothetical phrase, implying that something is in vain if it is (A). If it goes until (A), then that is all there is.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「毎日毎日勉強していてとても疲れてるんだ。大学を中退したい…。」Ｂ：「でも、もう３年生だよ！あきらめてしまったらそれまでだよ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I'm studying every single day, I am so tired. I want to drop out of college...'B: 'But you're already in your third year! If you give up then it's all in vain.'

example_sentences.japanese: やっとここまでたどり着いた。ここでミスを犯せばそれまでだ。
example_sentences.english: We finally got to this point. If we make a mistake then it’s all in vain.

example_sentences.japanese: もう少し我慢をしろ！ここで見つかったらそれまでだ。
example_sentences.english: Have a little more patience! If they find you here, that's it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らに訴えられたらそれまでだ。
example_sentences.english: If they sue us, that's it.

example_sentences.japanese: このことが外部に漏れればそれまでだ。
example_sentences.english: If this information gets leaked, then it’s all in vain.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに大きな家でも、誰も住まなければそれまでだ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how big the house is, if no one lives there then it's all in vain.

example_sentences.japanese: この内定を受諾することに興味がないだけと言えばそれまでだが、もういちどよく考えて決めたほうがいいだろうな。こんなチャンスは二度とないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you say that you are not interested in accepting this offer then there is no point (in discussing further), but I think you'd better think it over once again and then decide. You won't get a second chance like this.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットしている友達へ：「頑張って運動しても毎日食べ過ぎたらそれまでだよ。」
example_sentences.english: To a friend who is dieting: 'Even if you do your best exercising, if you eat too much every day then it's all in vain.'

example_sentences.japanese: スパイ映画：「敵に発見されたらそれまでだ。」
example_sentences.english: Spy movie: 'If we are discovered then it's all in vain.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が日本語能力試験に一回で合格したのは彼女が才能に溢れているからと言ってしまえばそれまでだが、実は彼女も努力をしたんだよ。
example_sentences.english: If you say that she passed the JLPT on the first try because she is overflowing with talent then that is the end of the discussion, but the truth is that she also put forth an effort.

example_sentences.japanese: 不可能だと言われればそれまでだ。せめて一回でもいいから試してみよう。
example_sentences.english: If you say it's impossible, that's the end of the story. Let’s at least give it a try, even if it's just once.

general_translation: How to put it, How shall I put it, How should I put it, Or perhaps, Or maybe, Call it … or
formation: AといおうかBといおうか + (Phrase)where A and B can be Noun, い [Adjective], な [Adjective] or Verb
casual_structure: AといおうかBといおうか + (Phrase)where A and B can be Noun, い [Adjective], な [Adjective] or Verb
explanation: An expression used when the speaker is uncertain about how to put (A), or how to phrase (A). Shall I say it's (A).

example_sentences.japanese: この前、電車を乗り違えてしまったんだ。僕はそのとき、自分でもこんなドジをして、面白いといおうか、困っているといおうか…とにかく忘れられない思い出になったよ。
example_sentences.english: I took the wrong train the other day. I made such a blunder at that time, how shall I put it, it was funny? or perhaps troubling?... Anyway, it turned into an unforgettable memory.

example_sentences.japanese: また彼女に誕生日を忘れられたんだ。あきれているといおうか、傷ついたといおうか、よくわからない。毎年のことだから慣れてきたけど…。
example_sentences.english: My girlfriend forgot my birthday again. How shall I put it, I don’t know whether I am disappointed or sad. Well, this happens every year so I’m starting to get used to it…

example_sentences.japanese: あいつの運転は荒いといおうか、危ないといおうか、とにかくあいつが運転する車には乗りたくない。
example_sentences.english: How shall I put it, his driving is rough, perhaps dangerous, either way I don't want to get in a car operated by him.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の体を使ってお客さんの車を守ろうとするなんて、バカといおうか、真面目すぎるといおうか分からない。
example_sentences.english: How shall I put it, I don't know whether to call him stupid or too serious for trying to protect a customer's car with his own body.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいとこといおうか、ハトコといおうか、私もどういう関係かはわからないけど親戚だということはわかっている。
example_sentences.english: How shall I put it, I don’t know if he is my cousin or my second cousin. I don’t know how we are related, but I know that we are relatives.

example_sentences.japanese: お前は努力が足りないといおうか、才能がないといおうか…。（俺にはお前がこの仕事に向いていないと思う）
example_sentences.english: How shall I put it, you aren’t trying hard enough, or perhaps you are not talented… (I think that you are not suited for this job)

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「プチチーズってなんですか。」Ｂ：「クラッカーといおうか、チーズとのスナックといおうか…（うーん、的確な言葉が思い浮かばないなぁ）」
example_sentences.english: A: 'What is Puchi cheese?'B: 'How shall I put it, a cracker, or perhaps a snack with cheese... (well, I can't think of the right word)'

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼女は誰ですか？」「彼の元カノといおうか友達といおうか複雑ですよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Who is she?''How shall I put it, his ex-girlfriend, or perhaps his friend, it's complicated.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は穏やかといおうか、のんびりといおうか、何事につけてもゆっくりしている。
example_sentences.english: How shall I put it, he is calm or perhaps relaxed, he takes his time with everything.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう一人暮らしを始めたのに、寂しいといおうか嬉しいといおうか、よくわからない。
example_sentences.english: I finally started living alone, and how shall I put it, I don't really know if I am lonely or happy.

example_sentences.japanese: プライドが高いといおうか何といおうか、彼女は他人の手助けをいつも断る。
example_sentences.english: How shall I put it, she is prideful or whatever - she always refuses assistance from others.

general_translation: Will definitely, Will certainly, Bound to, Not fail to
formation: Verb [ない-stem] + ずには + おかないVerb [ない] + では + おかないException:する→せずにはおかないVerb [Negative] + では + おかない
casual_structure: Verb [ない-stem] + ずには + おかないVerb [ない] + では + おかないException:する→せずにはおかないVerb [Negative] + では + おかない
explanation: A strong construction, implying that someone will definitely do (A). I will not set it aside with (A) not being done.

example_sentences.japanese: 小説、勇者：「どんな手段を用いても、かならず魔王をたおさずにはおかない。」
example_sentences.english: Novel, Hero: 'No matter what it takes, I will not fail to defeat the Demon Lord!'

example_sentences.japanese: あんなひどいことをした人だから、警察も捕まえずにはおかないだろう。
example_sentences.english: I am sure the police will not fail to arrest that person, since they did something so horrible.

example_sentences.japanese: メディアにも取り上げられたから、警察も調査をせずにはおかない。
example_sentences.english: Since it was covered by the media, the police will certainly investigate.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなことをされたのだから、お客さんも訴えないではおかないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Since they did such a thing to the customers, they would certainly sue them.

example_sentences.japanese: この犬は３０キロになるから、躾に力を入れないではおかない。
example_sentences.english: Since this dog will become 30kg, I will not fail to train him.

example_sentences.japanese: 「私はきっと彼に同じ手で仕返しをしないではおかない。」
example_sentences.english: 'I won't fail to pay him back in his own coin.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「警察はすべての悪者に必ず罰をあたえずにはおかない。」
example_sentences.english: 'The police will not fail to punish all the wicked people.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼はまた私との約束をすっぽかした。絶対に彼に『ごめんなさい』といわせずにはおかない。」
example_sentences.english: 'He skipped our appointment again. I won't fail to get him to say "I'm sorry".'

example_sentences.japanese: 小説：「探偵は『この残虐行為の責任者を訴追せずにはおかない』と意を決する。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'The detective resolved himself, "I won't fail to bring the person responsible for this atrocity to justice".'

example_sentences.japanese: あの人のスピーチは聞く人を感動させずにはおかない。
example_sentences.english: That person’s speech will not fail to move the audience.

general_translation: As of (the end of), (Starting) from, (No longer) after, By (the), Ending with
formation: Noun + を限（かぎ）りにNoun + 限（かぎ）りで
casual_structure: Noun + を限（かぎ）りにNoun + 限（かぎ）りで
explanation: A construction highlighting the end of (A), after which a significant change often happens. To the limit of (A). As of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの事情により、明日をかぎりに店を閉店させていただくことになりました。長年ご利用いただき誠にありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: Due to personal reasons, we have decided to close the store as of tomorrow. Thank you very much for your patronage over the years.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月をかぎりに、海外に引っ越すことになりました。今までいろいろとお世話になりました。
example_sentences.english: As of this month, I will be moving abroad. Thank you so much for everything.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月行われるコンサートをかぎりにＳＵＭ４１は解散することを決めたそうです。
example_sentences.english: SUM41 has decided to disband after the concert next month.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日をかぎりに閉店致します。当店は１９７２年に開業し、４９年にわたり現在の場所で営業してまいりました。
example_sentences.english: We will close as of tomorrow. This store opened in 1972 and has been operating at our current location for 49 years.

example_sentences.japanese: 異動、公務員：「今週かぎりで、現在の職務から離れることになりました。」
example_sentences.english: Changes in personnel, civil servant: 'I will be leaving my current position as of this week.'

example_sentences.japanese: 同僚との話：「今月かぎりで田中さんは退職するつもりって聞いたけど、本当か？」
example_sentences.english: Conversation between coworkers: 'I heard that Tanaka is planning to resign as of this month, but is that true?'

example_sentences.japanese: 今回をかぎりに武田先生は人前では演奏しません。
example_sentences.english: Takeda-sensei will not perform in public as of now.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の夜は息子が声を限りに泣いていたから大変だったよ。
example_sentences.english: It was tough last night because my son was crying to the limit of his voice (crying as loud as he could).

general_translation: It's unbearable when, It'd be unbearable if, I can't stand it when, I couldn’t stand it if
formation: Verb［られる］［て］＋ては(1)＋かなわない［い］Adjective［い］＋くては(1)＋かなわない［な］Adjective＋では(2)＋かなわないNoun＋では(2)＋かなわない(1) ちゃ(2)じゃ
casual_structure: Verb［られる］［て］＋ては(1)＋かなわない［い］Adjective［い］＋くては(1)＋かなわない［な］Adjective＋では(2)＋かなわないNoun＋では(2)＋かなわない(1) ちゃ(2)じゃ
polite_structure: Verb［られる］［て］＋ては(1)＋かないません［い］Adjective［い］＋くては(1)＋かないません［な］Adjective＋では(2)＋かないませんNoun＋では(2)＋かないません(1) ちゃ(2)じゃ
explanation: A somewhat old-fashioned grammar point, expressing that it is unbearable when (A). I cannot face it when (A).

example_sentences.japanese: こうさむくてはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: It's unbearable when it's cold like this.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日充電器を忘れてはかなわないから、今のうちに鞄に入れておこう。
example_sentences.english: It’d be unbearable if I forgot my charger tomorrow, so I am going to put it in my bag right now.

example_sentences.japanese: こう頭が痛くてはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: It’s unbearable when my head aches like this.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子に竿を折られてはかなわないから、手が届かないところに置いておこう。
example_sentences.english: It’d be unbearable if my son breaks my fishing rod, so I am going to put it out of reach.

example_sentences.japanese: 今繁忙期だしこんな時にやめられてはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: It’d be unbearable if they quit during peak season.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車で隣に座っている人がくさくてはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: It is unbearable when the person sitting next to you on the train smells.

example_sentences.japanese: そうあやふやではかなわない。
example_sentences.english: It’s unbearable when you are vague like that.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨にふられてはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: I can't stand getting rained on.

example_sentences.japanese: 上の部屋の人がうるさくてはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: It's unbearable when the people upstairs are noisy.

example_sentences.japanese: 話をしている時、非常識なひとに邪魔されてはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: It's unbearable when I am interrupted by a thoughtless person when I am speaking.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日こんなにむしあつくてはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: It's unbearable when it is so humid every day like this.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日勉強させられてばかりではかなわない。
example_sentences.english: It's unbearable when I am just studying every single day.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字とくると彼女にはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: She is no match for me when it comes to kanji.
